title: build(process): merge-ready skill in the repo, deterministic merge planner, collaborator rule
body:
## What changed

- `.claude/skills/merge-ready/SKILL.md`: the maintainer's local merge-ready skill, ported step for step (preconditions, collect, plan, ask in groups, wave 1, wave 2 one at a time, after-merge sweeps, report, one gate per batch). Every planner call is `cargo xtask merge-plan ...`; no home-directory path. Safety rules kept: the user decides, never merge an unapproved PR, never `gh pr review --approve`, merge commits only, fork branches are not deleted, stacked children retargeted first, refresh only the PR that is next in the batch.
- Planner (`xtask/src/merge_plan*.rs`): every order choice is a named total order ending in the PR number (`wave1_pick_key`, `order_key`, `wave2_key`, `shared_first`); repeated PR numbers resolve by (number, head); a shared-history pair keyed either way round reads the same; the simulated-commit cache is a `BTreeMap`. The plan prints the full base sha and each PR's head sha. New `--json` (waves, order, per-PR kind, conflicted files, shas, `after`). Rendering moved to `merge_plan_out.rs` (files stay under 400 lines).
- Scope change from the maintainer (question dialog, 2026-11-12: "Any collaborator review counts", "Both collaborators" may merge; chat: "everyone counts. everyone needs to get merged, mkinney and i are coolaboration across the world on the same code base"): markers and `merge-ready` labels count when made by a collaborator (push permission), not only the owner; any collaborator's session runs `/merge-ready` and merges, cuts/tags stay with the maintainer; non-collaborators' PRs still wait for the user. Updated in AGENTS.md (the #1227 rule kept as "Superseded since 2026-11-12, later the same day"), review-prs, resolve-conflicts, PR-reviewer and the new skill. `xtask` reads no marker author, so no code change there.
- AGENTS.md also names `/merge-ready` as how a batch is run (in "Outside PRs are reviewed"). `PROCESS_VERSION` 31 -> 32.

## Parity with the reference planner (`plan_merge_order.py`)

| Behaviour | Status |
|---|---|
| Stack ordering (child's base is parent's branch, or parent head is an ancestor) | same |
| Shared unmerged history: fewer own commits first | same; a tie now goes explicitly to the lower number (as the reference's `<=` on sorted numbers) |
| Wave-1 selection (fewest live rivals, fewest paths) | same, with the number as last key, as the reference |
| Merge order: docs first, hot files last, small before large | same, number last |
| Wave-2 order and kinds (clean after wave 1 / mechanical / by hand) | same |
| GitHub-only conflict = `plain refresh` (git clean, GitHub CONFLICTING, several merge bases) | same |
| UNKNOWN mergeable: 6 x 5 s retries, then a WARNING line, planned as git says | same |
| Octopus merge in `--delta` = NEW CODE | same |
| `--delta` classes SAME / MECHANICAL / DELTA / NEW CODE | same |
| Base sha | differs: printed in full (reference printed 8 chars) so two runs compare |
| Head shas, `--json` | new (reference had no head shas; its `--json` had no per-PR sha or kind) |
| Scratch refs `refs/merge-plan/N` | differs: deleted after the run (the reference left them) |
| Reference was Python | differs: Rust, so it runs on every OS with the workspace and is unit-tested without git |

## How tested

- `cargo test -p xtask`: 88 passed. Pinning tests in `xtask/src/merge_plan_det_tests.rs`: `shuffled_input_gives_the_identical_plan` (an 8-PR fixture with docs, hot, stacked, pair clashes, base conflict, shared history, GitHub-only and UNKNOWN; 23 input orders; plan, text and JSON all identical), `a_repeated_pr_number_resolves_the_same_way_in_either_order`, `wave1_tie_on_rivals_and_paths_goes_to_the_lower_number`, `wave1_fewer_rivals_beats_fewer_paths_and_number`, `wave1_fewer_paths_beats_the_number`, `merge_order_is_docs_then_cool_then_hot_then_small_then_number`, `wave2_order_is_parents_then_fewest_files_then_number`, `shared_history_tie_goes_to_the_lower_number_and_either_key_direction_reads_the_same`, `unknown_list_is_in_number_order_whatever_the_input_order`, `output_names_the_base_and_every_head`, `json_escapes_quotes_backslashes_and_control_characters`. No real git in the unit tests.
- `cargo clippy -p xtask --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean. `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main`: green on the first run.
- Planner run twice each against live PRs (read-only, it only fetches): `cargo xtask merge-plan 1319 1314 1311 1310` printed the identical plan both times (base 4ea96bd5; wave 1 #1319, #1314; wave 2 #1310 by hand in `xtask/src/main.rs`, #1311 mechanical on `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION`). `--label merge-ready`: the first run (base 8e9489e2) planned #1134 alone; by the time of the paired runs no open PR carried the label, and both runs gave the same clean "no matching open PRs" error. Main moved between those runs, which is why the base sha is printed.

## Not exercised

The skill was not run end to end on a real merge. `--json` with `--delta` is not defined (`--delta` prints its class as text).

## Process announcement for #681

`PROCESS_VERSION 32` · PR #<this> · the merge-ready skill is now in the repo (`.claude/skills/merge-ready/`) and `cargo xtask merge-plan` is deterministic with head shas and `--json`; **this reverses PROCESS_VERSION 31's "only the owner's reviews count"**: a review marker or `merge-ready` label now counts when a collaborator (push permission) made it, and any collaborator's session may merge PRs that meet the rule (cuts and tags stay with the maintainer); non-collaborators' markers still do not count. A fork must pull the process files (`AGENTS.md`, `.claude/agents`, `.claude/skills`, `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION`, `xtask`).

Effort: medium. No `push`, `pull_request` or `schedule` trigger added.

Changelog: none

Fixes #1320

title: fix(verify): the mid-turn sweep reads the whole turn, not five poses
body:
Fork synced at v0.18.0.

## What changed

Reach law (c3), the mid-turn sweep, read the band stack's column at 4 path stations x 5 turn fractions. Between them a holder or shank could cross uncut stock with no `SweepHit` (#1313).

It now reads the whole reachable set, by construction:

- New module `crates/sim/src/verify/turn_cells.rs`. Per band, one *cell* per tip chord and per interval of the turn. A cell is the convex hull of law (c)'s column at the interval's two end poses, grown by a proven sag, with its bottom at the lower end bottom less the sag.
- The sag bound: the letters lerp and bend the axis no faster than their own sweep, so inside a cell the axis strays from the chord of its end axes by at most `(sweep in the cell)^2 / 8`; times the band's reach above the tip. The cell count keeps it at 0.001 mm or less, capped at 64 cells per band (a 90 degree turn at 150 mm reach then overstates by 0.011 mm, still conservative).
- The tip's travel is not sampled either: the hull is clipped against the tip chord exactly, the bottom rides the chord's Z, and the flutes' kerf excuses a column only for the tip positions that stand over it.
- `sweep.rs` asks a cell one question (`bottom_over`); the column memo and the worst-offender rule are unchanged. `midpose::pose` became `pub(super)` to share the letter lerp.

A refusal is the safe side here: the new reading is a superset of the old one at every pose and station the old grid read.

## How tested

- `crates/sim/tests/midturn_swept_band.rs` - `a_holder_crossing_a_stock_post_between_two_sampled_poses_is_convicted`: a holder 100 mm up the stack swings through a stock post between the 20 and 40 degree samples of an 80 degree turn. Run against main's `sweep.rs` it reports nothing; here it reports `SweepHit { at: 0 }`. Its twin `a_turn_that_stops_short_of_the_post_stays_clean` keeps a clear swing clean.
- `verify::turn_cells::tests::no_band_position_of_a_random_turn_lies_outside_the_cells` - the issue's brute-force probe: 240 random turns (A and B up to +-85 degrees, a third also in C), 5,076,000 band positions (the true cylinder's surface and law (c)'s own column, 9 path stations x 25 turn fractions). Zero outside the cells, in XY and in Z. The old grid misses 272,961 of the same positions.
- Three more unit tests: the sag bound at a wall, the kerf following the tip, degenerate bands and non-finite letters.
- Quick gate `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: sim, motion and app suites green (48 gate-mapped suites, every existing mid-turn test, no assertion edited). `cargo clippy -p camcraft-sim --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean.

## Not exercised

- The release lanes (`--ignored`, the big posed fixtures) were not run, so false convictions on real 5-axis programs are not measured. In the debug suites there are none.
- Verify time on a large posed program was not measured. A small turn needs fewer cells than the old 20 states per band; a large one up to 64.
- The overhang backstop (stock hidden under a ledge) still asks the old 4 x 5 grid: filed as #1316.

Decision note: `docs/decisions/1313-midturn-swept-band.md`.

Changelog: Verify's mid-turn sweep (law c3) reads every pose and tip position of a turn instead of five sampled poses, so a holder or shank crossing stock between samples is reported
Effort: max (not escalated)

Fixes #1313

title: fix(sim): verify refuses a non-finite or zero tool axis and normalises a scaled one
body:
## What changed

`verify` passes the path through one door before any law runs (`crates/sim/src/verify/axis_door.rs`, new; wired in `verify/engine.rs`):

- An axis with a **non-finite** component, **zero length**, or a length that **overflows** is refused by name with `Warning::NonFinite { at }`. The NonFinite law now covers `axis` as well as `from`/`to`; its text now reads "non-finite coordinate or tool axis". The refused axis is kept as stated, so each law's own guard still fires. For example, the radial rapid law's conviction of a zero pose stands.
- A **finite, non-unit** axis (`|a|²` more than 1e-12 off 1) is **normalised once** in a copy that every law reads.
- Already-unit axes pass bit for bit through a borrowed `Cow`: no copy, and no existing verdict or golden moves.

Decision record: `docs/decisions/1312-verify-axis-refusal.md`. The reachability search the issue asks for is on the issue: no generator, CL import or MCP path emits such an axis, so the issue stays P3.

## How tested

- Pinning tests in `crates/sim/tests/axis_door.rs` (new, 5 tests). Four of them fail on main and pass here:
  - `a_non_finite_axis_is_refused_by_name`: reproduction 1, `[1e-12, 0, inf]` and others.
  - `a_scaled_axis_is_judged_as_its_unit_direction`: reproduction 2, the 7x axis at 2e-9 rad keeps its `ShankHit`.
  - `a_zero_or_overflowing_axis_is_refused_by_name`
  - `one_bad_axis_refuses_only_its_own_move`
- Unit tests in `verify::axis_door::tests` (2).
- `radial_rapids::a_rapid_on_a_pose_that_is_no_direction_convicts_itself`: its exact assertion now also expects the added `NonFinite { at: 0 }`. The `RapidInStock` conviction is unchanged.
- Quick-gate plan (`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`): every sim suite whose gate map names `sim::verify` plus the sim lib, 272 tests, all green on the final head. Motion `real_tip` and `solid_law` green. The 47 mapped app suites ran green (533 s) on the first variant of the door, which dropped a refused axis to upright. That gate run was VOID only because I edited files during it. The final variant differs only for refused axes, which no app suite feeds verify (grep-checked).
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-sim --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

## Not exercised

- The mapped app suites were not re-run on the final head. See above for why.
- The other public law entries the post gate calls directly (`bands_vs_fixtures`, `rapids_vs_fixtures_spindle`) do not go through the door. The search found no path that feeds them a bad axis.
- Release-lane heavy tests were not run.

Changelog: Verify refuses a move whose tool axis is non-finite or of zero length, and judges a non-unit axis by its unit direction (#1312)

Effort: high (no escalation)

Fork synced at upstream/main 53a52f88 (branch cut from upstream/main).

Fixes #1312

title: feat(ui,app): an async file picker opens models and projects in the browser
body:
Part of #31, the app and UI on wasm. This slice adds an **async file picker**, so a model or a project can be opened in the browser build. Until now every picker there answered "cancelled".

Fork synced at v0.18.0. The branch merges `upstream/main` (53a52f88) so that it diffs clean against `main`.

## What changed
- **`crates/ui/src/file_pick.rs`** (new): the browser picker. On wasm32, `open()` makes an `<input type=file>` whose `accept` comes from the dialog's filters, clicks it and returns at once. When the user has chosen, the file's name and bytes go into a thread-local inbox, and the next frame is woken through the egui context, which `shell_web` registers.
  - Files over 256 MiB (`BROWSER_READ_LIMIT`) are refused by name before they are read. A failed allocation in wasm aborts the tab.
  - The input and its change closure are held in one slot until the next pick, not `forget`ed, so a cancelled picker does not leak.
  - The inbox, `accept_attr` and `too_big` are plain Rust on every target.
- **`crates/ui/src/state_picked.rs`** (new):
  - `open_model_dialog` / `open_project_dialog`: rfd's synchronous dialog on native (unchanged), the async picker on wasm32.
  - Each frame, `drain_actions` turns every inbox entry into a `CommandKind::OpenPicked`. A model goes through `ImportModel::from_bytes` and `finish_import`: one undo step, and a same-named model is an update. A project goes through `project::open_noted`.
  - A failed read, a refused import, or a project that is not text or not JSON is said on the status line ("import refused: …" / "open failed: …") and changes nothing.
- **`crates/app/src/commands/import_model.rs`**: `ImportModel::from_bytes(file_name, data, budget)`. It shares the path import's laws through `checked_budget`: IGES and unknown extensions refused, the STEP budget's bounds. It adds the `MAX_FILE_BYTES` cap and the finite-mesh gate. `geometry::import::parse_model_graded_within` is now `pub`.
- **`crates/ui/src/state.rs`**:
  - Two new `CommandKind` arms route to the functions above.
  - The model and project dialogs' filters are factored out (`mesh_dialog`, `project_dialog`) so both pickers ask with the same ones.
  - `open_project_path`'s reset is factored out as `reset_for_open`, so the bytes open retires the old document the same way. Behaviour is unchanged.
- No dependency added. The picker uses `eframe::web_sys` features that eframe already enables (`HtmlInputElement`, `File`, `FileList`, `Blob`).
- Decisions: `docs/decisions/31-wasm-file-picker.md`.

## How tested
- Pinning tests:
  - `crates/app/tests/import_bytes.rs`:
    - `picked_bytes_import_like_the_same_file_from_disk`: the same name, mesh and fidelity as the disk import, for STL, OBJ and STEP.
    - `picked_bytes_are_refused_by_name_never_a_panic`: IGES, an unknown extension, no extension, empty or corrupt files of each format, and a budget given for a non-STEP file.
  - `crates/ui/src/file_pick_tests.rs`:
    - `a_picked_model_imports_through_the_undoable_command`
    - `a_picked_file_that_cannot_be_used_is_refused_by_name`
    - `a_picked_project_opens_in_place_of_the_document`
    - `the_browser_picker_accepts_the_dialogs_extensions`
    - `a_file_over_the_browser_read_limit_is_refused_before_it_is_read`
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: green. The app suites (lib, import_bytes, large_models, model_fidelity, step_*, stock_export, bore_facet_sagitta) passed in 21 s. The ui suites (lib, boundary, boundary_picks, feedback, fixtures, gpu_render, machine, models, operations, shell, theme_files) passed in 19 s.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean (native, macOS).
- **wasm check**: `web/build-app-wasm.sh` passed on macOS, using the official rustc 1.99.1 with the wasm32 std and Homebrew LLVM's clang for the wasi C.
  - It linked `camcraft-cli.wasm` and `camcraft_ui.wasm`, ran wasm-bindgen 0.2.129 and laid out `target/web`. The shim answers all nine WASI imports.
  - camcraft-ui raised no warnings.
  - `web/check-app-page.sh target/web` passed.
  - The script needed two local workarounds, which are not part of this PR: a GNU-`sed -i` shim, and a bash-3.2 empty-array fix for `"${PROFILE_ARGS[@]}"` under `set -u` (line 104). As shipped, the script does not run on stock macOS bash/sed. Worth a small follow-up.

## Not exercised - browser hand check needed
- **The picker was not run in a browser.** It needs a hand check: serve `target/web`, then use File > Open model on an STL, OBJ and STEP file and File > Open project on a `.camproj`. Also check that cancel does nothing and that a file over 256 MiB is refused on the status line.
- The input is clicked from the egui frame (requestAnimationFrame), not from the DOM click handler itself. Browsers allow this within the click's transient user activation. That is the main thing to confirm by hand, Safari included.
- Still owed on #31 (see the decisions file):
  - Save, Save As and Post in the browser, which need a download.
  - The other pickers: fixture import, machine, post, theme and tool library.
  - Dropped files.
  - Inline playback, a WebGPU run, the in-browser CI job, console diagnostics for the app crate, and the shell.rs split.

Changelog: The browser build opens models (STL, OBJ, STEP) and projects through an async file picker (#31).
Effort: high (no escalation)

Refs #31

title: test(post): move the probe and arc post suites out of app on recorded input
body:
Slice 2 of #926. Slice 1 was PR #1002 (the recorded edge-case streams and the per-`.cps` script suites). This PR moves the ten app suites named in the issue to `crates/post/tests`. They used app only to generate a toolpath before posting it; now they read recorded input instead.

## What changed
- **Moved to `crates/post/tests`:** `fanuc_post`, `probe_dialects`, `probe_guard`, `probe_report`, `probe_tormach`, `inverted_probe`, `arc_planes`, `inverted_equivalence`, `inverted_post`, and the posting half of `vertical_arc_entry`. Their helpers `inverted_support/` and `macro_b/` moved with them.
- **Recorded inputs (`crates/post/tests/recorded/inputs/`):**
  - 28 probe `.cnc` streams, one per distinct (cycle, dump) pair the old tests built.
  - 5 probe paths as `.cl`. `cl::text` carries no touches, so `probe_guard`'s "every GUARD is a positioning feed of the path" law needs the path and the stream side by side.
  - 3 contour `.cl` paths for `vertical_arc_entry`.
  - The inverted-axis fixture stream.
- **Generator-side guards.** Each one compares byte for byte and rewrites the file with `WRITE_GOLDEN=1`:
  - App's `recorded_post_streams` (slice 1's guard suite) guards the probe streams and paths, generated by `motion::probing::probe_cycle` and `post::dump`. App is still the only crate that sees both motion and post. Its new `every_recorded_input_has_a_generator` fails on any file in `inputs/` that nothing writes.
  - `crates/motion/tests/vertical_arc_entry.rs` is the generator half: true arcs, tangency, the oblique note and verify. It also guards the three contour recordings.
  - Post's `inverted_post` guards `inverted_probe.cnc`. App's `inverted_axis_display` reads that file, so app no longer carries a copy of `inverted_support`.
- **Stays in app:** the `ArcDto` project-file test, now in `float_roundtrip`, as the #919 research said.
- **Goldens:** they stay in `crates/app/tests/golden/` (the post suites use `recorded::app_golden`), because other app suites and xtask read them. **No golden changed.** One home for the goldens is #919's sub-issue 6.
- **xtask:** the asset and gate-map unit tests named `fanuc_post` / `arc_planes` as app suites. They now read every crate's `<crate> suites` step. **PROCESS_VERSION 33.** A fork pulls the process files as usual; nothing else is needed.
- Decisions: `docs/decisions/926-recorded-app-post-tests.md`.

## Done means
- **The 10 tests run outside app from recorded input:** yes. The one `ArcDto` test stays in app by design (it tests the project file).
- **No new dependency between crates:** none. No `Cargo.toml` changed.
- **Each recorded file has a generator-side test that fails when it goes stale:** yes. I checked this by appending a line to a recording (`every_recorded_probe_stream_is_current` failed and named the file) and by adding an orphan file (`every_recorded_input_has_a_generator` failed).

## Test counts
- Before: 79 `#[test]`s in the ten files.
- After: those 79 still run; 78 are in post and the `ArcDto` test is in app `float_roundtrip`. Post gains 1 new guard.
- New guard tests: post `inverted_post::the_recorded_inverted_probe_stream_is_current`; app `every_recorded_probe_stream_is_current`, `every_recorded_probe_path_is_current` and `every_recorded_input_has_a_generator`.
- Motion `vertical_arc_entry` holds 3 generator-half tests, under the same names as the originals.
- Golden asserts are unchanged.

## How tested
- The quick gate passes on head 9338316c (`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`): post suites (all 29), motion `vertical_arc_entry` (3 fns), app `float_roundtrip` / `inverted_axis_display` / `recorded_post_streams`, and the xtask unit tests (76).
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app --tests -- -D warnings` is clean. It compiles every app test, which confirms no app suite still uses the moved helpers.

## Not exercised
- Batch and release tiers.
- `fanuc_post`'s "hair under zero" probe case was posted from a serialized stream before this PR as well, so its recording is byte-identical to the zero-edge one (the stream is in microns). I kept it as its own file and noted this in the test.

## Overlap
- PR #1034 (#995, a probe section starts no coolant) touches probe posting. If it changes a probe stream or golden, whichever PR merges second regenerates with `WRITE_GOLDEN=1`.

Fork synced at v0.18.0; branch carries upstream/main merged (process files at upstream's PROCESS_VERSION before this bump).

Changelog: none (test-only move)
Effort: high (no escalation)

Fixes #926

title: fix(xtask): select and run directory test suites
body:
## Summary

- Discover conventional Cargo directory integration targets (`tests/<suite>/main.rs`) alongside flat suites, following declared modules rather than treating neighboring support files as independent targets.
- Keep quick changes scoped to their owning suite and to qualified changed test functions when precise. Check both preimage and postimage hunk spans; structural, missing-preimage and conditional-source changes fall back conservatively.
- Run named directory tests through `gate test`, preserving nested/inline/`#[path]` qualification, duplicate leaf names and ignored/heavy selection. Documentation mentioning `#[ignore]` does not turn an ordinary test into a heavy test.
- Isolate real Cargo fixture outputs by source-root identity. Increment `PROCESS_VERSION` from 30 to 31 and record the decision in `docs/decisions/927-directory-test-suites.md`.

## Validation

Used the repository-permitted targeted alternative: the touched xtask test binary plus touched-crate all-target Clippy.

- `cargo test -p xtask -- --nocapture`: **73 passed, 0 failed, 0 ignored**.
- Five real Cargo directory-suite selections executed nonzero counts: default **1**, nested **1**, comment-brace module **1**, duplicate leaf names **2**, aliased module path **1**. Three independent fixtures have distinct source roots, targets and executable paths; sequential selections of one unchanged fixture intentionally reuse its binary.
- `cargo clippy -p xtask --all-targets -- -D warnings`: passed.
- Focused `rustfmt --check --edition 2024 --config skip_children=true` on the eight changed implementation/new-test modules: passed. Three legacy test-adapter initializers retain their existing formatting; diff whitespace checks pass.
- Sequential independent review of the complete contribution and correction delta: no remaining actionable findings. Regressions include `documented_ignore_examples_are_not_ignore_attributes` and `quick_checks_old_and_new_hunk_sides_without_widening_in_test_edits`.

Validation ran on native Windows against the exact final committed tree. No application/full/release suite, other-platform run, test migration or hosted workflow was requested or executed.

## Readings and scope

Current repository AGENTS/README/work-issue rules, Cargo Book package layout, rustc Book test filtering, and #919's linked research. This implements only the directory-suite prerequisite, not #919's test consolidation or crate moves. No dependency or workflow changes.

Effort: medium
Changelog: xtask recognizes directory test suites and keeps quick and named test selection scoped to their qualified tests.

Fixes #927

title: docs(mcp): camcraft-mcp skill lists set_tool_cutter_params; a drawn neck feeds the checks
body:
Docs for the camcraft-mcp skill (`.claude/skills/camcraft-mcp/SKILL.md`), the rest of #1013 after PR #1024 (`Refs #1013`) landed the first two drawn-cutter rows.

title: fix(sim): crossing law reads a shared vertex a rounding apart as a touch
body:
Fork synced at v0.18.0 (branch cut from upstream main 0757563d; not stacked on #1134, which carries `needs-rework`).

## What changed

The verifier's crossing law (a) read orientation signs exactly, so two moves meeting at one vertex reached twice, a rounding apart, could read as a proper crossing and hold the post with `Warning::Crossing`.

- `crates/sim/src/verify/laws.rs`: new `pub const CROSSING_TOUCH: f64 = 1e-9` (mm), documented (f64 rounding at 1e4 mm is ~2e-12 mm; cutting tolerances are microns), re-exported as `camcraft_sim::verify::CROSSING_TOUCH`. New `proper_cross_touch`: `proper_cross` with a chord end that stands within `CROSSING_TOUCH` of one of the other chord's **end points** read as on that chord's line (orientation 0, a touch). The test is a point-to-point distance (`hypot`), not a raw cross-product magnitude, so it does not scale with chord length.
- `crates/sim/src/verify/crossing.rs`: law (a)'s pair predicate asks `proper_cross_touch`. `proper_cross` itself is unchanged, so `dist2_segs` and the arc-wall law keep the exact predicate.
- Doc comment and decision file say the law is the reference: the planner's `guard::crosses` (#1048, PR #1134's `TOUCH`) should use or match this constant and this end-point reading.

**Why end points, not the line (as #1129's text proposed).** The #1134 review showed that excusing an end within `TOUCH` of the other chord's *line* hides a real pass-through: a walk crossing a chord at a vertex 0.5 pm off its interior makes both of its chords there read as touches. That review said #1129 must not port that test to the verifier. Every case the issue names is a shared vertex, so the end-point reading fixes them and keeps that probe reported. Recorded in `docs/decisions/1129-crossing-tolerance.md`.

## How tested

Pins, `crates/sim/tests/crossing_touch.rs` (each checks the bucketed law against the all-pairs reference):
- `a_shared_vertex_a_rounding_apart_does_not_warn`: a joint 1e-12 mm apart in 16 directions, origins 0 / 37.25 / 1000 mm, chords 1 um / 0.5 / 20 / 1000 mm. Each scale asserts the old exact test tripped on at least one jitter. This test fails with the old predicate (checked).
- `a_crossing_a_micron_through_still_warns`: same scales, B starting 1 um short of A's end and 1 um below its line (a quarter chord for the 1 um chord).
- `a_walk_through_a_chord_at_a_vertex_a_picometre_off_its_line_still_warns`: the #1134 review's probe, vertex at -0.5 / +0.5 pm, at y 0 and 1000 mm.
- `collinear_overlaps_keep_their_reading`: partly overlapping collinear chords at 4 angles and 3 scales give the exact-sign verdict; an exact retrace stays no crossing.
- `a_joint_just_past_the_touch_keeps_the_exact_reading`: at 2e-9 mm the exact verdict is kept, so the edge itself is pinned.

Gate (macOS arm64, debug):
- `cargo test -p camcraft-sim`: lib and all 58 test binaries green (incl. `crossing_touch` 5, `crossing_buckets` 3).
- `camcraft-app`: `verify` 21 (2 ignored), `golden_cl` 25, `verify_arc_reading` 7, `carried_verify` 8, `warned_moves` 2, `operations` 117 (6 ignored), `solid_law_goldens` 5, `shoulder_adaptive` 3, `trochoid_op` 5, `pocket3d_hsm` 1 (1 ignored): all pass.
- `cargo test -p camcraft-motion --lib adaptive`: 26 passed, 1 ignored.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

No existing verify test or golden changed verdict.

## Not exercised

- The planner side: `motion` `adaptive::guard` is untouched. PR #1134 should adopt `CROSSING_TOUCH` and the end-point reading when it is reworked.
- The release `--ignored` heavy lanes and the UI suites were not run.
- Residual, same in kind as before: two walks crossing in an X exactly through a shared vertex were never reported by the exact-sign law; this extends that reading to a vertex a picometre apart. No new class of miss.

Changelog: The verifier's crossing law no longer holds the post when two moves share a vertex a rounding apart (within 1e-9 mm); a real crossing, including a pass-through at a vertex near another chord's interior, still blocks (#1129).

Effort: high (no escalation)

Fixes #1129

title: fix(sim): the posed fixture sweep reads a band as a flat-ended cylinder
body:
Fork synced at v0.18.0 (cut from upstream/main 0757563d).

## What changed

The posed sweep of fixture laws (c2)/(d2) (`crates/sim/src/verify/posed_steel.rs`) placed each band of a leaning tool stack as a capsule. A capsule's caps reach one whole band radius past each band end, so an r 15 holder standing 0.5 mm over a clamp was convicted `FixtureHit` at any lean at all.

A box the capsule reaches is now read a second time against the band as the flat-ended cylinder it is (`flat_band_clear`):

- per interval: the tip chord `p0..p1` swept exactly + the cylinder `lo..hi`, radius `r`, about the midpoint pose + a ball of `pad = bulge + swing * hypot(max(|lo|,|hi|), r)`;
- fixed steel under a rotary: that set carried by the midpoint turn and grown by `dth * (rho_max + r + pad)`, `rho_max` over the parallelogram's four corners;
- cleared only on a GJK proof of a separating plane wider than `pad + FIXTURE_HIT_TOL` (`fixture_mesh::band_clear_of_box`: the mesh law's existing `SweptBand`/`Boxed` supports and `gjk::separated`, pointed at a fixture box).

This is the enclosure `verify/mesh_posed.rs` already proves for the fixture mesh law; the box law now reads the same geometry. Leaning by θ the rim reaches R sin θ past the end plane, not R, and the verdict turns at the lean where the true band touches.

## Why it is still conservative

- Both enclosures contain the swept band (proof in the module header and in `docs/decisions/1305-posed-band-cylinder.md`); a box is struck only when both reach it, so nothing the true band touches can be cleared.
- The cylinder's swing arm is `hypot(hi, r)` (the rim's distance from the tip), not the capsule's centreline arm `|hi|`.
- "Clear" is only the supporting-hyperplane bound over exact support mappings. Non-finite input, a zero axis, a degenerate rotary or an exhausted search is "not proven": the capsule's hit stands.
- Every verdict that was clear is clear by the same arithmetic (the capsule still runs first); only capsule hits can change. No golden moved.

## Tests

New, `crates/sim/src/verify/posed_steel_tests.rs` (unit, on `posed_hits` / `sweep`):

- `a_holder_just_over_a_clamp_is_clear_at_a_small_real_lean` - the issue's evidence case (r 15 holder, clamp top 0.5 mm under it): clear from 1e-7 to 1.5 degrees (0.01 degrees included).
- `the_holder_is_struck_once_its_rim_really_reaches_the_clamp` - convicted as `Holder` from 2.2 degrees.
- `the_verdict_turns_once_and_at_the_true_touching_lean` - 1000 leans, 0.005 to 5 degrees: the verdict flips exactly once, within 0.006 degrees of the analytic touching lean (2.130 degrees).
- `a_fixed_clamp_under_the_stood_up_holder_is_clear_at_any_lean` - machine frame, clear at 29.5 and struck at 30.5.
- `steel_at_any_point_of_the_true_leaning_band_is_struck` - the property: 4800 specks of steel at sampled points of the true band (rims and end faces weighted) on moves whose pose swings, path frame and under a rotary, all struck.
- `a_non_finite_band_or_box_is_never_proven_clear`.

New, `crates/sim/tests/posed_band_cylinder.rs` (public laws): fixed clamp under a rotary clear at any lean / convicted when it reaches into the holder (`bands_vs_workholding`, `rapids_vs_workholding`); a 5 degree lean still convicts through `bands_vs_fixtures`.

Mutation checks (not committed): dropping the swing term from `pad` fails the property test; removing the second reading fails the three clearance tests.

## Gate (final head e15b633e)

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: green - sim suites (lib + 20 binaries, `posed_band_cylinder` among them), motion (`real_tip`, `solid_law`), app (46 binaries); 3 steps, 0 failed, 3.4 min.
- By hand: `posed_fixture` 7/7, `posed_fixture_midpose` 3/3, `stock_posed` 3/3, `fixture_mesh` 9/9 (1 ignored, release lane).
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

## Not exercised / known limits

- **`main` has neither #938 nor #1303.** PR #973 (`UPRIGHT_TILT_RAD`) is open and #1303 is open with no branch pushed, so this is built on `upstream/main` alone and `crates/sim/tests/tilt_tolerance.rs` does not exist here. In the path frame, law (c2) also runs its own column enclosure (`stack_span::band_struck`), which still drops a leaning band by its whole radius - that is #1303. Until it merges, `bands_vs_fixtures` on the evidence case is still convicted at 0.01 degrees by the column, not by the sweep. The sweep's verdict is pinned directly, and end to end where the sweep alone decides (fixed steel under a rotary).
- PR #973 changes one line of `posed_steel.rs` (`is_vertical` -> `is_upright`), away from these hunks; whichever merges second should merge cleanly.
- A move whose pose CHANGES keeps the swing ball (`swing * hypot(hi, r)`, intervals of 0.5 mm of far-end travel): continuous, but wider than a constant-pose move's reading.
- `mesh_posed.rs` already sweeps flat-ended bands (read in full). `probe.rs` was skimmed, not audited; unchanged.
- No release-lane (`--ignored`) suites were run.

Changelog: The posed fixture sweep reads each band of a leaning tool as the flat-ended cylinder it is, so a holder just over a clamp is no longer reported as a fixture hit at a small tilt (#1305)

Effort: max (no escalation)

Fixes #1305

title: fix(sim): a tilted band's column dips by the rim's exact R·sin θ
body:
**Stacked on #973** (branch `issue/938-tilt-tolerance` @ 9b01def4, which already carries current `main`). This PR's own change is the single commit de1d8641; until #973 merges the diff against `main` also shows #973's commits. Fork synced at v0.18.0.

## What changed

Since #938 a pose within 1e-9 rad is judged upright. Just above it the reach laws took the tilted column, which stood each band's bottom one **whole radius** under its foot. An r 12 holder 5 mm clear of a part was clean at 1e-9 rad and `ShankHit { part: true }` at 2e-9 rad or 0.01 degrees.

The tilted column now dips by the rim's exact `R·sin θ`. One helper, `verify::tilt_band::lean` (new module `crates/sim/src/verify/tilt_band.rs`), builds the column; the four copies of the formula are gone. Consumers:

| Law | File | Was | Now |
|---|---|---|---|
| (c) reach vs rest material | `reach.rs` | bottom `- R` | bottom `- R·sin θ` |
| (c3) mid-turn sweep | `sweep.rs` | bottom `- R` | bottom `- R·sin θ` |
| (c2) fixture band column | `stack_span.rs` | z planes `-/+ R` | `-/+ R·sin θ` |
| (d2) tilted rapid, flute column | `laws.rs` | z planes `-/+ R` | `-/+ R·sin θ` |

The column's centre and radius are the sums they were. Every upright branch is untouched. The posed capsule sweep, the mesh-steel law, the solid law and the contact law place the real pose and do not share this column; they are not changed.

## Derivation (full text in `docs/decisions/1303-tilt-band-dip.md`)

A band is the cylinder of radius R about the unit axis `a` (tilted θ off +Z) between axial stations `above` and `above + len`: points `tip + s·a + ρ·w`, `0 <= ρ <= R`, `w` a unit vector square to `a`.

- **z.** Write +Z as `cos θ·a + sin θ·h` with `h` unit and square to `a`. Then `w·Z = sin θ·(w·h)`, at most `sin θ`, reached at the rim point `w = ±h`. The axial part `s·az` is linear, so its extremes are the two ends. Lowest point: `tip.z + min(above·az, (above+len)·az) - R·sin θ`; highest: `max(..) + R·sin θ`. Both ends are in the `min`/`max`, so the band's own height is included.
- **Sideways** (unchanged): `s·a` stays within `len/2·sin θ` of the mid-station's foot and the disc adds R or less, so radius `R + len/2·sin θ` about `mid·(ax, ay)` holds it.

**Never under.** `rim_sine` = `min(1, max(h, h/|a|))`, `h = hypot(ax, ay)`: the sine itself for a unit axis, the larger reading for an axis off unit length, and 1 (the old whole radius) for a zero or non-finite axis. Never more than the old reading, never less than the true dip.

## Verdicts and goldens that moved

- Tilted moves only, toward clean only, and only where the old extra depth (between `R·sin θ` and `R`) was what met the material.
- `crates/sim/tests/tilt_tolerance.rs` (#938's pins): `a_tilt_just_above_the_tolerance_is_still_judged_tilted` expected the r 15 holder 5 mm over the stock to convict at 1.01e-9 rad and 0.001 degrees. That was the cliff. It is now `a_tilt_just_above_the_tolerance_reads_like_upright_and_a_real_dip_convicts` (clean at both, convicted at 20 degrees where the rim is 1.9 mm into the stock). `a_leaning_shank_and_holder_report_one_shank_hit_per_move` moved its tilt to 20 degrees so the holder group still convicts beside the shank group.
- No golden, no posted output, no other existing test changed.

## How tested

Pins (new):
- `crates/app/tests/tilt_band_dip.rs`, on the `beside_wall` plate:
  - `a_small_tilt_of_a_holder_standing_clear_over_the_part_no_longer_convicts` - 1e-9, 2e-9 rad, 0.01 and 1 degree clean;
  - `a_tilt_that_brings_the_rim_into_the_part_still_convicts` - 0.4 degrees clean (rim 0.016 mm clear), 0.6, 1, 2, 5, 10, 30, 60 degrees `ShankHit { part: true }`;
  - `the_verdict_is_monotone_in_the_tilt_across_the_upright_tolerance` - 20 tilts from 0 to 60 degrees, clean then convicted, never back, turning between 0.4 and 0.6 degrees;
  - `the_mid_turn_sweep_dips_by_the_rim_too` - law (c3).
- `verify::tilt_band` unit tests: a 4000-case property (random tilt 0..180 degrees, azimuth, R, foot, length; every sampled band point inside the column, and the column's planes reached by the samples), the limits, the unreadable-axis fallback, and the (c2) column read directly.

Mutation check, by hand: the whole radius (old reading) fails all four app pins; half the dip (an under-read) fails the conviction pins and the property test.

Gate on de1d8641, local:
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: sim suites ok, motion suites ok, app suites ok (190 s), 0 failed.
- `cargo test -p camcraft-sim`: 59 binaries ok, 486 passed, 0 failed.
- app `tilt_band_dip`, `tool_body_bands`, `tool_body_judged`, `sim_tool_body`, `verify`, `posed_contact`, `rotary_verify`, `solid_law`, `solid_law_goldens`: 76 passed, 0 failed.
- motion `multiaxis`, `multiaxis_avoid`, `multiaxis_rough`, `swarf_pose_continuity`, `swarf_reentry`, `pivot5d`: 33 passed, 0 failed.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

## Not exercised / known

- Batch and release tiers and the `--ignored` heavy lanes were not run.
- The fixture verdict on a posed move is still the OR of the column and the posed capsule sweep, whose capsules reach a whole radius past each band end. A clamp just under a holder is still convicted on any tilt above the tolerance (`the_fixture_band_law_reads_noise_as_upright_and_a_real_tilt_as_tilted` is unchanged). Filed as #1305.
- Law (c3) still samples the turn (4 stations x 5 pose fractions). The decision file argues the sampled bottoms bound the in-between ones in z; that argument is not pinned by a test.
- No hands-on check in the GUI or on a machine.

Effort: max (no escalation)

Changelog: A tilted tool's holder and shank bands are enclosed by the rim's exact dip (R·sin θ) instead of the whole radius, so a small commanded tilt no longer reports a false shank or fixture-column collision (#1303)

Fixes #1303

title: fix(sim): a shipped build ignores CAMCRAFT_CARRY_ENGINE; a field-engine verdict names its engine
body:
Fork synced at v0.18.0 (cut from upstream/main 0757563d).

## What changed
- **A shipped build ignores `CAMCRAFT_CARRY_ENGINE`.** The switch (#637) is honoured only where `CARRY_ENGINE_SWITCH_HONOURED = cfg!(debug_assertions)` holds (dev and test profiles); a release build never reads the variable and always carries stock on the column engine. The read is now the pure `engine_from_switch(value, honoured)` (`crates/app/src/stock_sim_held.rs`, re-exported as `stock_sim::carry_engine_from_switch`). This was the only reader of the variable.
- **A field-engine verdict names its engine, never silently.** New `stock_sim::carry_engine_note()`: `None` on the column engine, else "carried stock judged by the field engine (band N, development switch CAMCRAFT_CARRY_ENGINE), not the shipped column engine". It rides the post gate's visible, non-blocking line (`posting::sim_clause` -> post result, status line, G-code header), the setup sheet's `SIM:` line (`setup_sheet::simulate_verdict`) and the GUI Deviate readout (`crates/ui/src/actions.rs`).
- On the column engine nothing changes: no golden, no shipped verdict text moves.
- Decision recorded in `docs/decisions/1168-carry-engine-switch.md`: `debug_assertions` chosen over `cfg(test)` (integration tests link the lib without it, so the carried suites could no longer be run whole on the field arm) and over a cargo feature (a build change, plus `--features` on every field-arm run). No Cargo.toml change. The agreement lane is unaffected: it selects engines per call tree with `with_carry_engine`, in release too.

## Tests
Pinning tests (`crates/app/tests/carried_engine_agreement.rs`, default lane):
- `a_shipped_build_ignores_the_carry_engine_switch` - `engine_from_switch(_, honoured = false)` is the column engine for `field`, ` FIELD `, `column`, empty and unset; honoured, `field` selects the field engine; `CARRY_ENGINE_SWITCH_HONOURED == cfg!(debug_assertions)`.
- `a_verdict_the_field_engine_judged_names_the_engine` - on a carried two-setup document, `sim_clause` and `simulate_verdict` name the field engine (and the switch) under `with_carry_engine(FIELD)`, and add nothing on the column engine.

Gate on the final head (f8a8ff8d), Linux:
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: app suites + ui suites ok, 949 passed, 0 failed (4.1 min).
- `carried_engine_agreement` 3 passed, 1 ignored (heavy lane, untouched); `setup_carry` 9/9, `rest_across_setups` 7/7, `carried_verify` 8/8, `carried_fixtures_cache` 6/6.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

Not exercised: a real `--release` build run with the variable set (the release behaviour is pinned through the pure gate function and the `cfg!` constant); the heavy `--ignored` agreement lane; macOS/Windows; the GUI readout by hand. `crates/ui/src/actions.rs` is now 403 lines (was 400).

title: fix(thread): start the thread mill's feed at the operation's R plane
body:
Stacked on #1219 (on #1137, #1045, #1005). Retarget to `main` before #1219 merges.

Fork synced at v0.18.0.

## What changed

- **Kernel** (`camcraft-motion`, `machining2d::thread_mill`): `ThreadParams` gains `r_z: Option<f64>`, the R plane. Each feature's rapid stops at `max(R, the ride's run-out)` and the feed down the axis (or beside the boss) starts there; the ride climbs back to it at feed before the link rapid. `None` is the #894 ride, so every existing kernel golden is byte-identical. An R plane below a feature's top, above the link plane, or not finite is refused by name.
- **App** (`thread_op::kernel_params`): passes the resolved `top_z` ("R plane (feed starts here)") as `r_z`, for internal and external threads.
- **Door** (new `operation::thread_r_plane`): a fixed `top_z` below a listed hole's or boss's top is refused when the operation is created, edited or re-tooled. A referenced height resolves at generate, where the kernel asks. The door's R check runs after the tool and feature laws, so their refusals keep their own wording.
- **Stock law** (`thread_r_plane::judge`, called at generate before the #992/#985 way-in laws): every vertical rapid down is read in the prior grid over the mill's full disc. Stock above the rapid's end is refused by name with the stock height and the fix ("raise the R plane (feed starts here) to z ... or above, or machine that stock away"). An unknown prior or an unreadable disc is left to the way-in laws, which already refuse both by name.
- Decision record: `docs/decisions/1212-thread-r-plane.md`. It covers how the default is seeded: unchanged, Top of Model, and every golden fixture already states R on the feature top.

## Tests (pinning)

- Kernel: `machining2d::thread_tests::the_ride_rapids_to_the_r_plane_and_starts_its_feed_there` (internal and external; an R on the top equals the #894 ride move for move), `an_r_plane_under_a_top_or_over_the_link_plane_is_refused_by_name`.
- Golden (new): `golden_cl::thread_mill_raised_r_plane_matches_golden` -> `tests/golden/thread_mill_raised_r_plane.cl` (R 2 mm over the tops of two holes). **No existing golden moved.**
- App: `thread_entry::the_operations_r_plane_is_where_the_rapid_stops_and_the_feed_starts` (generates, verifies clean, posts through the gate), `an_r_plane_under_the_holes_top_is_refused_when_the_operation_is_made`, `an_r_plane_that_ends_the_rapid_in_the_stock_left_ahead_is_refused_by_name`. Unit: `operation::thread_r_plane::tests::*` (door, stock law).

title: fix(app): judge a tap's cutting moves at its thread's core in the op verify
body:
Fork synced at v0.18.0 (cut from upstream/main 0757563d).

### What changed

The second half of #266. @austin62jake's PR #713 (merged) made the program sim sweep a Tap-kind tool at its thread's core (`tool_law::cutting_radius`, ISO 724 basic minor diameter, `d/2 - 0.5413 p`). As their PR noted, a tap on a tap-drill hole still did not post: the op's own verify convicted the tap's feed in and out (`move 1/2 cuts past the finish surface`) because its tangency and solid laws read the full major diameter against the hole wall.

- New `operation::tap_core` (`acquit`, `core_tool`): for a Z drill cycle with a Tap-kind tool, generate re-runs the same cutting laws (`verify_bodies` + the containment solid law) with the tap cut to its core, and drops each `Gouge` that the core run does not also raise.
- Only `Gouge` is re-read. Rapids, shank, holder and fixture verdicts keep the full diameter (a tap must never rapid into its thread band). It can only remove convictions, never add one; a pitch with no core leaves the full verdict standing.
- Out of scope, unchanged (full diameter, over-reports only): the helical thread mill (`Thread` op), cross holes, tilted (3+2) taps.
- Decision record: `docs/decisions/266-tap-core-verify.md`.

Credit: the rule (`cutting_radius`), the sim half and the `tap_sim.rs` fixtures are @austin62jake's (#271 / #713); this PR builds on them. No code of theirs is re-committed here, since it is already on main.

### Readings (M6 x 1 catalog tap, block with a blind square hole)

| Case | Op verify before | Op verify after | Program sim |
|---|---|---|---|
| Ø5 hole (tap drill) | Gouge at moves 1, 2 (blocks post) | no blocking warning | clean |
| Ø4.6 hole (under D1 4.917) | gouge | gouge | gouge |
| Ø0.5 slit (no pilot) | gouge | gouge | - |
| Ø5 hole, tap 3 mm past the floor | gouge | gouge | gouge |
| Ø6 drill in Ø5 hole | gouge | gouge (unchanged) | - |

### Pinning tests (`crates/app/tests/tap_sim.rs`)

- `a_tap_in_a_tap_drill_hole_carries_no_blocking_warning` - fails on main (Gouge at moves 1 and 2), passes with the fix.
- Guards: `a_tap_in_a_hole_under_its_minor_diameter_is_still_convicted`, `a_tap_deeper_than_its_hole_is_still_convicted`, `a_tap_with_no_hole_under_it_is_still_convicted`, `a_drill_at_its_own_diameter_keeps_the_full_verdict`; austin62jake's two sim tests still pass.

### How tested (Linux)

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` on head 74c5ba8b: app suites (lib + 131 suites incl. `tap_sim`, `solid_law_goldens`, `drill_prior`, `posting`, `tapping_mode`, `verify`-adjacent) ok in 639 s, ui suites (boundary_picks, edge_loop_pick, feedback, machine, operations) ok in 114 s; 0 failed.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `tap_sim` alone: 7 passed. The new pinning test reproduced on main as `Gouge { at: 1 }`, `Gouge { at: 2 }` before the fix.

Goldens: no golden file changed (paths are untouched; only warnings are re-read). `solid_law_goldens` (tapped hole modelled at the major diameter) unaffected.

### Not exercised

- Through the GUI / `camcraft-cli mcp` post end to end (the post gate reads exactly these warnings plus the program sim, both pinned).
- Thread mill, tilted frames, Windows/macOS.

Changelog: A tap on a hole modelled at tap-drill size no longer carries false "cuts past the finish surface" warnings, so it posts (#266)

Effort: high (no escalation)

Fixes #266

title: fix(ui): no console window on Windows double-click
body:
Fork synced at v0.18.0 (cut from upstream/main 0757563d).

**What changed.** `crates/ui/src/main.rs` gets `#![cfg_attr(windows, windows_subsystem = "windows")]` (debug and release), so a double-click opens no console. On Windows `main` first calls `AttachConsole(ATTACH_PARENT_PROCESS)` via a one-line `unsafe extern "system"` kernel32 declaration (edition 2024), result ignored, so a terminal launch still shows tracing/stderr output and a double-click (no parent console) just fails the call harmlessly. No new dependency: windows-sys is only transitive, using it directly would add a Cargo.toml entry. title: feat(finish3d): land model - fill closed openings on the drive surface
body:
Fork synced at v0.18.0 (cut from upstream/main 37482923).

## What changed

A 3D Finish option, **Fill openings** (`fill_openings`, mm, off by default), for the land case in #1196: the finish flies over bolt holes and small pockets at their rim instead of diving down their walls.

**The fill rule** (`crates/motion/src/finishing3d/fill.rs`, new):
- Sample the model's top-down height field on a grid (cell = width/12, coarsened to at most 4M cells; a width too fine for the model at that cap is refused by name). Cells over no facet read as the model's lowest Z.
- Grey-scale morphological closing with a flat disk of the stated diameter (Serra 1982; Soille 2003). A cell raised by more than the finish tolerance is an opening cell.
- A connected group is filled only when it is **closed**: none of it on the grid border, and every bordering cell is material standing at the lid's level (within one cell's 45-degree rise + tol). Slots or valleys that run out to an edge, or a lid that would spill over a lower rim, are never filled.
- Lids (horizontal rectangles at the closed height, never below the surface) cover the group plus its neighbour ring.

**Safety:** the drive facets are the model's facets, unchanged and first, plus lids, so a path planned on them can rise but never bite the model deeper. Only the path is planned on the lids. The verifier still gets `material.facets` (the real model), so a gouge under a lid is still caught. The path gets a `land: N closed opening(s) narrower than W mm filled at their rim and flown over, not cut ...` note.

**Plumbing:** `OpParams::Finish3D.fill_openings: Option<f64>` (undoable through `EditOperationParams`; sanity refuses a non-finite or non-positive width at the door). The optional `fill_openings` file key is absent when None. The MCP params door carries it (`edit_operation {"fill_openings": 5.0}`). The stamp digest gets bytes only when a width is set. There's a "Fill openings" field on the 3D Finish page. Geodesic + fill is refused by name, because the lids would be new open boundary for its march. There's no project-file version bump: an older reader ignores the key and cuts the model itself, which is a valid finish, not an unsafe one. The reasoning is in `docs/decisions/1196-finish3d-land-fill.md`.

**Option off is byte-identical:** no file key, no digest bytes, and the generators get `&material.facets` as before. No goldens moved.

## Tests
- `crates/motion/tests/finish3d_land.rs` (new):
  - `land_finish_flies_over_the_bolt_holes_and_verifies_on_the_real_plate`: a 40x20x8 plate with two 3.4 mm through holes and a 3 mm ball. Waterline and Parallel with fill on: no tip inside a hole below the top. The deepest ball bite measured on the REAL plate is within tol. The same path sunk 0.5 mm is caught on the real plate. The raster crosses the mouths at the top with fill on and doesn't with it off.
  - `a_blind_pocket_is_lidded_and_a_gouge_into_its_floor_is_convicted`: off dives to the pocket floor and on never does. A plunge planted through the lid into the pocket floor is caught on the real model.
  - `an_opening_wider_than_the_width_or_open_to_the_edge_is_not_filled`: a 3 mm width doesn't fill a 3.4 mm hole (output is exactly the model), and an edge-to-edge slot stays open.
  - `nonsense_widths_are_refused_by_name`: 0, negative, NaN, inf, a too-fine width and an empty model.
- `crates/app/tests/operations.rs` `finish3d_fill_openings_lands_over_a_pocket_and_verifies_on_the_model`: end to end through `GenerateOperation`. Off rides the pocket floor. On never descends, status Ok (the real-model verify is clean), and the land note is present. A negative width is refused at `CreateOperation`.
- `crates/app/tests/mcp.rs` `fill_openings_rides_the_params_door_and_undoes`: off by default, set over MCP, 0 refused, generate ok, and undo restores off.
- Quick gate (`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`) on the final head: green on 0754f88c (motion 190 s, app 599 s, ui 74 s; 0 failed). Clippy `-D warnings` is clean on motion, app and ui.

## Not exercised
- The reporter's STEP part (not attached). The fixtures are square-hole plates.
- The finish3d heavy (`--ignored`) envelope lane: no existing generator changed, and the fill is opt-in.
- The UI field is only compile-checked. No snapshot PNGs changed.

Changelog: 3D Finish can fill closed holes and pockets narrower than a stated width on the planned surface ("Fill openings"), flying over them as a land finish while the verifier still judges the real model (#1196)

Effort: high (no escalation)

Fixes #1196

title: docs(site): search box in the docs header
body:
Fork synced at v0.18.0.

## What changed

- `site/config.toml`: `build_search_index = true` with a `[search]` block: `index_format = "elasticlunr_javascript"` (so the index is `search_index.en.js`), title, description and path indexed, body indexed truncated to 2000 characters.
- `site/templates/base.html`: a search form in the header. It loads `vendor/elasticlunr.min.js` and `search_index.<default_language>.js` with `get_url`, then a small inline script. Results are a dropdown under the box, built with `textContent` (no `innerHTML`). Keyboard: Down from the box enters the results, Up/Down move between them, Enter follows the first result on submit, Escape closes and returns focus to the box. Result links are the URLs Zola builds from `base_url`, so the base path is carried and no host is hard-coded.
- `site/static/vendor/elasticlunr.min.js` is elasticlunr 0.9.5 from the npm tarball, unmodified, with its MIT licence in `site/static/vendor/elasticlunr.LICENSE.txt`. No third-party service at run time.
- `site/static/style.css`: search styles in the existing tokens (`--bg`, `--card`, `--line`, `--fg`, `--muted`, `--accent`), so the dropdown follows the dark theme; under 600px the box takes the full header row.
- `site/README.md`: a short note on search and `vendor/`.
- `docs/decisions/1245-site-search.md`: the decisions taken unattended.

No `.github/` change: the existing `zola build` in the `site` job picks up the config, so the maintainer does not need to touch the workflow.

## How tested

- Zola 0.23.6 (`brew install zola`, the version pinned in `release.yml`).
- `zola build --base-url https://neotech.github.io/Camcraft` in `site/`: builds; `public/search_index.en.js` (195 KB) and `public/vendor/elasticlunr.min.js` exist; the index's document URLs use the Pages base path.
- `zola serve --port 1111` (base_url `http://127.0.0.1:1111`): `GET /` and `/guide/setups/` include the search box and both script tags; `GET /vendor/elasticlunr.min.js` returns 200 (17827 bytes); `GET /search_index.en.js` returns 200 (175688 bytes) and its links use the local base.
- Index queries run in Node against the built files (elasticlunr loaded from `vendor/`, the index from `search_index.en.js`, the same calls the inline script makes):
  - `refused` → 7 hits (first: "Reading a refusal").
  - `WCS` → 1 hit ("Setups").
  - `adaptive` → 1 hit ("Operations").
  - a nonsense term → 0 hits.

No Rust code changed, so no cargo gate was run.

## Not exercised

- The dropdown in a real browser: keyboard flow, focus and Escape behaviour, and the phone-width and dark-mode looks were not checked visually. The logic was checked only through the index queries above.
- The Pages deploy itself; the `site` job's `zola build` with the release base URL was not run in CI.
- Pages with no body text (their excerpt falls back to the description) were not reviewed one by one.

Fixes #1245

title: feat(vise): self-centering grip jaw - a step the stock sits on
body:
Fork synced at v0.18.0 (cut from upstream/main 37482923).

## What changed
- `vise::SelfCentering` gains `grip_depth` / `grip_width` (mm, 0 = off): a grip jaw, a step cut into each jaw's inside top edge. The jaw profile walks down the face to the ledge, in along it, down to the floor; the frame's z = 0 is the ledge (the floor the part sits on), so the vise body drops by `jaw_height - grip_depth`. Fit and an in-place `SetVise` edit both keep the stock seated on the ledge; the fixture/collision laws, stock simulation and the post gate read the stepped mesh.
- Law (`check_grip`, refused by name at command creation): both figures or neither; finite, non-negative; depth < jaw height; width < jaw thickness; opening > 2 x width (ledges would meet under the stock); dovetail lip and grip step not both ("a dovetail or a grip jaw, not both").
- `ViseParams::seat_height()` / `SelfCentering::seat()`.
- Project: two optional keys on the `self_centering` object, written only when non-zero; older files read as no step and a stepless vise writes byte for byte as before. No project version move.
- Dialog: "Grip step depth" / "Grip step width" rows with tooltips (dovetail rows get one too); the fit line says the stock sits on the grip steps and how far above the vise floor.
- MCP: `add_builtin_vise` / `set_vise` `dimensions` take `grip_depth` / `grip_width`; the vise view reports them.
- Decision: `docs/decisions/1274-grip-jaw.md`.

## Tests
- `crates/app/tests/self_centering_grip_jaw.rs` (new): `the_grip_jaw_carries_the_step_and_its_seat_is_the_frame_origin` (volume, bounds, steel/air at ledge and jaw), `bad_grip_figures_are_refused_by_name`, `a_grip_vise_seats_the_stock_on_the_ledge` (vise sits 12 mm lower than bed-seated for a 3 mm step on a 15 mm jaw), `the_fixture_law_judges_the_stepped_jaw` (face pass at z 9.5 struck by bed-seated jaws, clear on the grip step; pass at z 1 into the step blocks the post), `an_older_vise_key_reads_and_writes_unchanged_and_a_grip_round_trips` (old key byte for byte; save/reload; undo/redo).
- `crates/app/tests/mcp_self_centering_vise.rs`: grip dims through `set_vise`, refusals named, undo count.
- `crates/ui/src/egui_app/fixture_self_centering_tests.rs`: grip rows present for self-centering only; `a_grip_jaw_seats_the_stock_on_its_steps_and_places_in_one_step` (structural; no snapshot PNGs).
- Quick gate (`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`) and clippy `-D warnings` on app/ui on the final head f0e63454: green (app suites 18 s, ui suites 83 s; 0 failed); clippy clean.

## Not exercised
- Posed (tilted) grip vises in the 5-axis fixture laws beyond the shared mesh path; setup sheet (it does not state jaw forms).
- An older build re-editing a grip vise would drop the step (it keeps the saved facets until edited) - noted in the decision file.

Changelog: Self-centering vises get an optional grip jaw - a step (depth, width) on each jaw's inside top edge that the stock sits on; the fixture checks judge the stepped jaw (#1274)
Effort: high (no escalation)

Fixes #1274

title: fix(post): refuse by name a post that does not serve its setup's machine kind
body:
## What changed

A post now writes only for what its setup's machine can run (#1232):

- **Kind door** (`crates/app/src/posting_serves.rs`, wired into `post_setup`/`post_script`, `post_mounts`/`post_mounts_script`, `post_per_op`/`post_per_op_script` - so the GUI, script verb and MCP `post` get it too): a mount whose post does not serve its machine's kind is refused by name (setup, ops, post, machine, kind) before anything is written. Shipped posts are judged by the picker's law (`post_serves`); a user's script by its `capabilities` mask (`work_voice`).
- **Section door** (maintainer's decision, 2026-11-12, "Refuse it"): a section that turns the work - a turning op or an on-centre drill, as `lathe_voice::voice_of` reads it - posts only through a turning post (`work_voice` = `WorkSpindle`). Through a milling post it is refused by name, on a mill-turn as on a lathe. Milling and C-axis sections on a mill-turn still post through a milling post. The shipped Mill-turn machine's default post is unchanged.
- ~27 lathe tests in 14 suites were themselves posting through the Fanuc mill post (this bug); they now select Fanuc Lathe. `lathe_cross_drill`: the generate-only tests stay on the plain lathe; only the posting test uses a mill-turn. `lathe_work_spindle`: the on-centre drill on a mill-turn through the Fanuc mill post is now refused. `lathe_stroke`: the built-in Mill-turn turning job selects Fanuc Lathe.

## Pinning tests

- `post_serves_kind`: `an_own_milling_post_on_a_lathe_setup_is_refused_by_name`, `a_lathe_program_through_a_milling_post_is_refused_on_every_single_file_path`, `a_mill_setup_on_a_lathe_post_is_refused_and_the_lathe_on_its_lathe_post_still_posts`, `an_edm_mount_refuses_a_cutting_program_by_name`, `a_turning_section_on_a_mill_turn_through_a_milling_post_is_refused_by_name` (Haas own post and Fanuc document post, on post_mounts, post_per_op and post_setup; nothing written; a turning post serves it).
- `lathe_workholding_mill_post`: `a_mill_turn_facing_op_through_a_milling_post_is_refused_and_held_to_the_chuck` (was "posts at the chuck limit"; now refused by name at the limit too - stricter). `a_mill_turn_milling_section_through_a_milling_post_is_not_judged` and the kind x dialect x section walk still pass (milling section on a mill-turn through Fanuc/Haas posts).
- No golden, recorded post stream or snapshot touched: a lathe on a lathe post, a mill, and C-axis sections post byte-identical.

## How tested

`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` on the final head, plus `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` on head d1fec88a: whole app crate (shared `tests/common/bore.rs` maps quick to every suite) 2313 passed, 0 failed, 20 ignored (heavy lane); clippy clean.

## Not exercised

The `crates/ui` suites (UI code untouched), the release-tier heavy lanes, MCP/script end to end (they call the gated entry points). Not addressed here (review notes, non-blocking): the undeclared-script hint to settle with #1213, a label for a script handed by path, a builtin-mask agreement unit test, the `lathe_workholding_kinds` test name.

Fork synced at v0.18.0.

Changelog: A post now refuses by name a setup whose machine kind it does not serve, and a turning section (turning op or on-centre drill) through a milling post on a lathe or mill-turn; existing documents with a lathe or mill-turn turning op on the default Fanuc post now refuse until a turning post is picked (#1232).

title: docs(site): keyboard shortcut and mouse reference
body:
Fork synced at v0.18.0 (cut from upstream/main 37482923fc858b4ba3c4c600504020ef2489f1b0).

## What changed

- New guide page `site/content/guide/keyboard-and-mouse.md` (weight 7): every keyboard shortcut and mouse gesture bound in `crates/ui`, with Windows/Linux and macOS columns. Egui's `command` modifier is Cmd on macOS. Pick modifiers use the physical Control key on every platform.
- `site/content/guide/first-run.md`: one paragraph linking to the new page.
- Docs only. No Rust, no snapshot, no test changes.

## Verified rows (source)

Keyboard, `crates/ui/src/egui_app/panes.rs` `shortcuts()`:
- New Ctrl/Cmd+N, Open model Ctrl/Cmd+O, Open project Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+O, Save +S, Save As +Shift+S, Post +P: gated by `cmd && !typing`.
- Quit Ctrl/Cmd+Q (same block). macOS Cmd+Q also via `egui_app/os_quit.rs`.
- Undo Ctrl/Cmd+Z (no shift/alt). Redo Ctrl/Cmd+Y or +Shift+Y. Not gated by typing.
- Copy operation Ctrl/Cmd+C (needs a selected operation), Paste Ctrl/Cmd+V: `cmd && !typing`.
- Delete key (`Key::Delete`), gated by `!typing`. On a Mac this is Fn+Delete (forward delete) - not checked on hardware.
- F frames all (`!typing && !cmd && !alt`). Bare P toggles perspective/ortho (same guard).
- Enter commits a typed value: `egui_app/op_page.rs:83`, `egui_app/step_budget_row.rs:24`.

Viewport mouse, `egui_app/shell.rs` (~L415-520) and `interact.rs`:
- Left drag past `CLICK_TRAVEL_PX` (4 px) orbits; middle drag orbits.
- Right drag pans. Right click with no movement does nothing; the viewport has no context menu.
- Mouse wheel and `smooth_scroll_delta` dolly toward the cursor (`cam.dolly_cursor`). Two-finger scroll is the same path on a trackpad.
- Pinch (`zoom_delta`) is read only in `egui_app/tool_body_page.rs`, not in the viewport: listed under Not bound yet.
- Left click (release within 4 px) picks through `interact::pick_at`; a miss clears the model selection (`pick_model`).
- ViewCube: `egui_app/viewcube.rs` `click()` orients the view on a cube hit, and runs nav buttons.

Picking modifiers, `interact.rs` `Mods` (`ctrl` = physical Control), `edge_pick.rs`, `feature_click.rs`, `boundary_draft.rs`:
- Feature pick: plain replaces; Ctrl or Shift appends (`feature_click.rs:191`). Adding an already-picked face or vertex is refused with "already selected" (`interact.rs` `queue_feature_pick`).
- Edge mode: Ctrl toggles one edge (removes it when already picked), Shift takes the whole face loop, Alt one segment (`feature_click.rs` `ask`, `edge_pick.rs`).
- Boundary: Ctrl toggles, Shift closes around the face loop, plain replaces (`boundary_draft::PickMods`).
- Box-select: no code path (no marquee in `crates/ui`). Not bound.

Right-click, `egui_app/browser_pane.rs` (`hit.menu`), `tree_menu.rs`, `fixture_menu.rs`, `egui_app/panes.rs` (L1066 pin, L1454 error line), `painted.rs`:
- Operation row: operation menu. Model row: fixture menu. Setup Operations row: Paste. Ribbon cell: pin/unpin. Error line: Copy message.

## Not bound yet

Listed on the page under "Not bound yet": box-select, a Run shortcut, shortcuts for Paths/Simulate/Deviate and the Setup groups, Ctrl/Cmd+A outside a text field, pinch-zoom in the viewport, Ctrl/Shift/Alt drag pan, arrow keys, Escape to close dialogs (comments mention it; no Escape handler exists), middle-click alone.

## Mac checks not done

- No Mac available: Control-click on macOS is reported as a secondary (right) click by the OS (the PR #1242 description says so). The page says "not checked on a Mac" for that and for two-finger click/drag pan.
- Fn+Delete as the forward-delete key: assumed from egui's key mapping, not verified on hardware.

## Pick modifier note

PR #1242 (`fix(ui): pick add-to-selection uses the platform command modifier`) moves add-to-selection from Ctrl to the command modifier (Cmd on macOS). The page documents main's current behaviour and has a note on it.

## Gate

Docs-only: no test binary touched, so no quick gate run. `zola` is not on PATH in this environment, so `zola check` was not run; the internal links were checked by hand (`@/guide/keyboard-and-mouse.md` resolves to the new file; the `#not-bound-yet` anchor matches the heading).

title: test(machine): pin that a machine switch is judged again at the post
body:
## What changed

This PR adds tests and a decision record. It changes no product code.

Issue #1241 asked whether a toolpath generated and cleared on machine A can post on machine B without being checked against B. A remount happens two ways: through the setup's own machine (`SetSetupMachine`) or through the document's machine (`LoadMachine`), which the setup follows. The new suite `crates/app/tests/machine_switch.rs` traces both.

**Result: only the display is stale. No path posts on B without being checked.** For every law the post checks the cached path again, against the machine the op's setup mounts now:

| Law (path made on A, mounted on B) | Op status after the switch | Gate / post on B |
|---|---|---|
| Travel (B: +/-10 mm) | Ok | refused: `machine TightMill: ... Face1: move N reaches ... the stroke is -10.000..10.000` |
| Spindle max rpm (B: 1000) | Ok | refused: `Face1: tool EM-0400-2FL runs ... above the machine's 1000` |
| Rotary (tilt-head to VMC 3-axis, leaning pocket) | Ok | refused: `P: move N tilts the tool; ... states no tilting rotary` |
| Machine kind (mill to Lathe) | Ok | refused: `Face1: a ... operation cannot run on its setup's ... machine` |

Every refusal writes no file. The same results hold through each switch route (setup and document), after undo (A is back and the program posts), after redo, and after save and reopen.

The op still reads Ok after a switch on purpose. This is the M2.3 "roomy-one" law: machine limits and workholding feed the post's live gate and are never part of the op stamp. It is pinned by `fixtures.rs::workholding_never_stales_a_fresh_toolpath` ("loading a machine must not re-generate the program"). M3.2 B once tried a machine digest term in the stamp and reverted it. So the issue's "Done means" is met by its "or the issue records why it need not" branch. `docs/decisions/1241-machine-switch-live-gate.md` records the decision, the options I dropped (stamping the machine identity, or only the fields generation reads), and what it would cost to change if the maintainer wants a switch to show ops as stale.

## How tested

- Pinning tests, `crates/app/tests/machine_switch.rs` (6):
  - `a_setups_new_machine_judges_stroke_and_spindle_at_the_post`
  - `the_documents_new_machine_judges_stroke_and_spindle_at_the_post`
  - `a_setups_new_machine_without_the_rotary_refuses_the_lean`
  - `the_documents_new_machine_without_the_rotary_refuses_the_lean`

title: fix(ui): pick add-to-selection uses the platform command modifier
body:
Fork synced at v0.18.0 (cut from upstream/main 7580cd21).

## What changed

Edge and feature picks added to the selection on Ctrl. On macOS Control is the secondary (right) click, so a Mac user could not Ctrl+click to add an edge chain to an operation's picks, while the keyboard shortcuts already use the command modifier.

- `interact::Mods.ctrl` is renamed to `Mods.command`. It is built from egui's `modifiers.command` (Cmd on macOS, Ctrl elsewhere) through a new `From<egui::Modifiers>` impl, which the shell now uses.
- Pick add/toggle reads `mods.command`: `edge_pick::queue_edge_pick`, `interact::queue_boundary_pick` (boundary toggle), `feature_click::click` (feature add), and the `ui.input` conversion in `egui_app/shell.rs`.
- Shift keeps its meaning exactly (add in feature modes, whole loop in Edge mode, close in boundary mode).
- Windows/Linux: egui sets `command` whenever Ctrl is held, so behaviour is unchanged there.
- UI hint strings are not touched (#1239).
- Decision recorded in `docs/decisions/1238-pick-command-modifier.md`.

## Tests

Pinning test: `the_command_modifier_from_egui_toggles_and_control_alone_does_not` (crates/ui/tests/edge_loop_pick.rs). It converts `egui::Modifiers::COMMAND`, Shift and Control-alone, asserts Control alone does not add on macOS, and that the command modifier toggles an edge in.

Updated, still green: `command_click_toggles_one_edge_in_and_out` (was ctrl), and the boundary_picks CTRL constant is now CMD (`command: true`). Shift tests unchanged.

- `cargo test -p camcraft-ui --test edge_loop_pick --test boundary_picks`: all pass.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` on the final head: ok (ui lib, boundary, boundary_picks, edge_loop_pick, operations, theme_files).

## Not exercised

- No Mac was used. The macOS behaviour rests on egui's `command` mapping and the converted-`Modifiers` test; it was not run on hardware.
- The feature-mode add path in `feature_click::click` is changed but has no direct test (the function is `pub(crate)`); it is covered only by the rename compiling and the existing suites staying green.

Changelog: fix: edge and feature pick add-to-selection uses the platform command modifier (Cmd on macOS, Ctrl elsewhere); Control alone no longer adds on macOS (#1238)

title: fix(verify): a polygon declared at its corner circle earns no full rim credit
body:
Stacked on #1228 (base it on main once #1228 merges; this branch carries #1228's two commits).
Fork synced at v0.18.0.

## What changed
- #1228 credits a facet edge its whole chord dip when both of its ends lie on a declared hole rim. That left a gap: a hole that is really a coarse polygon, declared or recognized at its corner circle, kept the full credit on its flats. A drill cycle's own rim (tool diameter / 2) left the same gap.
- `crates/sim/src/verify/solid_index.rs` (`on_rim`): a rim chord now also has to dip at most `RIM_SAG_MAX` (0.05 mm) inside its circle, `r - sqrt(r^2 - l^2/4)`.
  - A deeper chord counts as a polygon's flat. It gets the 0.01 mm mesh credit, like every off-rim edge.
  - An octagon on r 5 (flats 0.38 mm deep) or a 16-gon on r 5 (0.096 mm) now convicts against a drill, bore or thread of the corner-circle size.
- The fix sits in the verifier rather than the recognizer. The hole list is editable data, and the drill's own rim bypasses the recognizer, so the verifier is the one gate every path goes through.
- Decision: `docs/decisions/1231-rim-sagitta-bound.md` (it also lists what was dropped: inscribed-radius declaration, the STEP `ReducedFidelity` chord, the surface type, a segment-count rule).

## Tests
- New in `crates/app/tests/hole_wall_chord.rs`:
  - `a_polygon_declared_at_its_corner_circle_still_convicts_on_its_flats`: 8-gon and 16-gon on r 5, rim declared at r 5; a drill, bore orbit and thread helix each convict. It fails with the bound removed (checked).
  - `a_small_tessellated_round_hole_keeps_its_rim_credit`: 16-gon r 2 (0.038 mm), a matched 4 mm drill on its rim is clean.
- Quick gate `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/issue/1217-chord-dip-excuse` on the final head: green (sim lib, midmove_pose, posed_rapids, motion solid_law, app hole_wall_chord, probe_reach, real_tip_contour, tool_body_drill_probe).
- Also run by hand, all green:
  - app `solid_law_goldens` (drill_plate, tap_plate), `golden_cl`, `bore_facet_sagitta`, `solid_law`, `conformance`, `fanuc_post`;
  - `operations` drill tests, including `drill_op_recognizes_from_the_model_then_machines_clean`.
- Clippy `-D warnings` on camcraft-sim and camcraft-app (all targets): clean.
- No golden or snapshot changed.

## Not exercised
- Real coarse STL exports: any round hole that dips more than 0.05 mm is now judged as a polygon. That is a refusal, not a pass.
- The batch and release tiers.

Changelog: Verify: a polygonal hole declared or drilled at its corner circle no longer has its flats excused; a chord counts as round-hole tessellation only when it dips at most 0.05 mm (#1231)
