title: fix(verify): hole-wall chord-dip excuse only on a declared rim, never a polygon's flats
body:
Fork synced at v0.18.0 (cut from upstream/main 12a6dcbf).

## What changed
The containment kinds' hole-wall excuse (`swept::chord_dip`, read by `solid_index` under `SolidLaw::hole_walls`) used to credit every facet chord's full dip into the swept disc. That let a coarse polygon hole's flats be cut silently. It now judges each facet edge on its own:
- **An edge with both ends on a declared rim circle** (within `RIM_TOL` = `DEV_TOL`, 0.01 mm, in XY, on an upright move) is a chord of the round wall that the region judges exactly. It keeps its whole dip.
- **Any other edge** is credited at most `HOLE_CHORD_CREDIT` = `DEV_TOL`, 0.01 mm. That is the mesh tolerance, and the same value #1099 uses for its thread grant.
- **Where the rims come from:** `generate::contain_into` builds them from the op's `holes` (Drill, Bore, Thread), using each hole's circle. A drill cycle also gets its own diameter at the hole centre, because a drill or tap cuts its own size there (the `tap_plate` case). They are passed through the new `verify::solid_hits_rims` and `verify::HoleRim`.
- **Callers without rims:** `solid_hits` keeps its signature and passes no rims, so the cross-drill and probe laws get only the 0.01 mm credit. Their suites are green.
- **The issue's case now convicts:** the octagon's corners at r 5 are on no declared rim (the thread was declared at r 4.4), so its flats are judged and the cut is a Gouge.

**Why not a bare 0.01 mm cap.** That was the first commit on this branch. It false-gouged pinned round holes: `drill_op_recognizes_from_the_model_then_machines_clean` (a 16-gon r 2 that dips 0.038 mm), plus the `drill_plate` and `tap_plate` goldens (32-gons). It would have done the same on every coarse STL drilled hole.

**Residual, stated in `docs/decisions/1217-chord-dip-credit.md`.** A hole declared or recognized at a polygon's own corner circle is still excused on its flats, because the declaration says it is round. Only the recognizer could tell the two apart.

**Interaction with #1099 (open, #1071):** the two PRs touch different files and both use the 0.01 mm credit. This PR's constant is private and named `HOLE_CHORD_CREDIT`, so it does not collide with #1099's `verify::CHORD_CREDIT`.

## Tests
- New `crates/app/tests/hole_wall_chord.rs` (the first and third fail under the old full credit; the second passes both before and after):
  - `a_coarse_polygon_holes_flats_cut_by_a_containment_kind_convict`: an octagon and a 16-gon (corners on r 5), cut out to r 5 by a bore orbit and a thread-mill helix with the rim declared at r 4.4 or with no rim, and by a drill with no rim. Each is a Gouge.
  - `a_full_fidelity_round_hole_stays_clean_for_every_containment_kind`: a 96-gon hole stays clean for the drill, bore and helix, with or without its rim.
  - `a_coarse_round_hole_is_excused_only_on_its_declared_rim`: a 32-gon at r 5 stays clean on its declared rim (drill and bore). A drill gouges when the rim is declared at r 4.4.
- `solid_law_goldens`: its `contain_law` harness now passes the drill cycle's rims, as `contain_into` does. **No golden files changed.**
- Quick gate (`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`) on the final head: **green** (sim 12 s, motion 4 s, 76 app suites 334 s).
- Also run by hand on the final head: 32 containment-related app suites, including `golden_cl`, `solid_law`, `solid_law_goldens`, `operations`, `coarse_contain`, `drilling_cross*` and `tap_sim`. All green.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- No snapshot PNGs changed.

## Not exercised
- The release-lane `--ignored` heavy suites.
- The issue's Thread reproduction through the full op path (`#1071`'s `thread_mill_rim` fixture lives on #1099's branch). It is pinned at the `solid_hits_rims` seam with the same declared-r 4.4 octagon geometry.
- Tilted (non-upright) containment moves: they read no world-XY rim and get only the capped credit. That is stricter, never looser.

Changelog: The containment kinds' (drill, bore, thread) solid law no longer excuses a cut into a polygonal hole's flats: a hole-wall chord's full dip is excused only on a declared hole rim, any other at most 0.01 mm (#1217)

Effort: high (no escalation)

title: build(process): refresh a conflicting PR only at merge time; merge-plan planner
body:
Process change (#1221, P4, effort:high). Branch synced from `origin/main` at 7a5816cf. The five points of the issue, in order.

## What changed

1. **Refresh only at merge time.** AGENTS.md: new rule "Refresh only at merge time" (the maintainer's words quoted, 2026-11-12). A conflicting PR carries `conflicts` and is otherwise left alone. The start-of-session contributor refresh is marked superseded (quote kept). `resolve-conflicts` contributor mode is the merge-time tool; its maintainer `check` asks an author only for a PR in the batch about to merge, and never for others. `review-prs` 2b and `PR-reviewer` follow.
2. **Planner in the repo.** `cargo xtask merge-plan <PR>...`, `--label <name>`, `--delta <PR> --reviewed <sha>` (plus `--repo`, `--remote`, `--base`). Pure ordering in `xtask/src/merge_plan.rs` (waves, stacks, shared history, the trial callback); pure delta classes in `xtask/src/merge_delta.rs`; git/gh side in `xtask/src/merge_plan_git.rs` (`gh pr list`, `git fetch`, `git merge-tree --write-tree`, `git commit-tree`, `git show --remerge-diff`; nothing checked out, built or pushed). Unit tests in `xtask/src/merge_plan_tests.rs`. One deliberate difference from the reference script: a child whose parent was deferred in wave 1 is deferred too (the reference would have merged it and pulled the parent's changes in silently). Pinned by `three_way_clash_defers_the_merge_and_its_child`.
3. **A clean merge of main keeps its review.** AGENTS.md section of that name. `--delta` says SAME (only merges of main, empty remerge-diff: review and `merge-ready` stand, no agent) or MECHANICAL (hand edits only in settled files: read by the merging session); DELTA gets a delta review, NEW CODE/Rewritten a full one. The draft rule in AGENTS.md gets the one exception: a clean merge of main keeps the ready flag; any other merge still turns it back into a draft. `review-prs` step 1 skips a head whose new commits are SAME; `PR-reviewer` skip check does the same.
4. **Only the owner's reviews count** (#1207, "No, only ours count"). `review-prs` step 1 query reads markers only from comments/reviews whose author is the owner (`gh repo view NeoTech/Camcraft --json owner`). `merge-ready` without an owner marker for the PR (current head, or an earlier head that `--delta` says SAME/MECHANICAL) is removed with a one-line comment. `PR-reviewer` skip check and `resolve-conflicts check` filter on the author too. AGENTS.md "Outside PRs are reviewed" names the rule.
5. **One gate per batch.** AGENTS.md "Fixes are tested in the background": one batch-tier gate per merge batch, not per merge.

Also: `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION` 30 to 31. Decision note: `docs/decisions/1221-merge-time-refresh.md`.

**PROCESS_VERSION 31** - what changed: refresh of conflicting PRs only at merge time (no start-of-session refreshes); the merge-order planner (`cargo xtask merge-plan`); clean merges of main keep their review; only the owner's markers and `merge-ready` count.
What a fork must do: stop the start-of-session contributor refreshes; stop marking and labelling your own PRs (the owner's account does that); pull the process files:
`git checkout upstream/main -- AGENTS.md .claude/agents .claude/skills .claude/PROCESS_VERSION xtask .cargo/config.toml scripts/gate.ps1 scripts/gate.sh scripts/release.ps1 scripts/collect-decisions.ps1 scripts/collect-decisions.sh`
(the announcement on #681 is made by the merging session when this merges.)

## How tested

- `cargo test -p xtask --bin xtask merge` : 16 passed, 0 failed. Names: `independent_prs_form_one_wave_docs_first_then_cool_then_hot`, `base_conflict_is_refreshed_after_wave_one_and_is_clean_then`, `pair_clash_on_mechanical_files_is_a_mechanical_refresh`, `code_conflict_after_wave_one_is_by_hand`, `stacked_child_merges_after_its_parent_even_when_it_is_docs_only`, `child_of_a_deferred_parent_is_deferred_too`, `shared_history_puts_the_side_with_fewer_own_commits_first`, `three_way_clash_defers_the_merge_and_its_child`, `render_names_both_waves`, `mechanical_is_the_settled_files_and_snapshots`, and the six `delta_*` tests.
- Quick gate `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main`: green on the first run (xtask unit tests, 6 s).
- `cargo clippy -p xtask --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

title: test: trace a setup's own machine and post to the posted files
body:
## What changed

This PR is test-only. It traces a setup's own machine and post from the pick to the bytes in the posted files (#1224), on top of the #1206 UI pins already in this PR. No product code changed.

Fixture (app): Setup1 follows the document, which mounts **machine A** (the shipped VMC 3-axis) and **post A** (the built-in Fanuc). Setup2 owns **machine B** (the shipped Tormach 770M, a 10000 rpm spindle) and **post B** (Siemens 840D). Each setup cuts its own box: Setup1 has Face1a then Face1b at G54, Setup2 has Face2 at G55. The tests check dialect markers, not only file counts. Fanuc files carry `%`, `O0001 (<machine>)` and `M30`. Siemens files carry `; <machine>`, `N10 G17 G710` and `M2`. Each header names its own machine.

- `crates/app/tests/setup_mount_trace.rs` (new, 6 tests)
- `crates/app/tests/mcp_setup_mount_trace.rs` (new, 1 test)
- `crates/app/tests/setup_mounts_post.rs`: two edge tests. One is `#[ignore = "#1232: ..."]`.
- `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests/setup_mount_pages.rs`: the #1206 two-mount pin now also posts through the shell's own `PostProgramFile` command. It reads both files from disk and checks Fanuc on the VMC and Haas on the tilt head, each holding only its own setup's work.
- `docs/decisions/1224-setup-mount-trace.md`

## Failing rows (filed, not fixed here)

- **#1232 (P1)**, row 7: a lathe setup's turning operation, posted through the setup's own milling post (Haas), is written as a milling program (`G17`, `T2 M6`, `G43 H2`, `S3000 M3`, facing as `Y` moves at `X0`). It should be refused. Pinned by `an_own_milling_post_on_a_lathe_setup_is_refused_by_name` (ignored).
- **#1233 (P5)**, the MCP half of row 1: no MCP tool sets a setup's own post, so the MCP leg covers the machine pick only. The post pick is pinned app-side.

## Trace table

| Row | Test (path) | Result |
|---|---|---|
| 1 Stored | `each_mount_file_is_its_own_post_machine_ops_and_work_offset` (app `setup_mount_trace.rs`, new): the document, Setup1 and Setup2 each hold their own machine and post. UI: `the_setup_machine_page_takes_its_own_machine`, `the_setup_post_page_takes_its_own_post_through_the_picker`, `the_setup_machine_page_picks_its_own_machine_from_the_library` (ui `setup_mount_pages.rs`, #1206). MCP: `a_setups_own_machine_picked_over_mcp_reaches_its_own_posted_file_and_undoes` (app `mcp_setup_mount_trace.rs`, new) and existing `setups_declare_activate_and_post_their_own_word` (app `mcp_setup.rs`) | pass. The MCP post pick has no tool: #1233 |
| 2 Generated (other setup active) | `each_mount_file_is_its_own_post_machine_ops_and_work_offset` (new: Setup1's operations are generated with Setup2 active, and the reverse). Existing: `an_inactive_setups_op_generates_on_its_own_machine_without_activation` (mill/lathe kind law, `setup_mounts_post.rs`), `two_setups_on_different_machines_are_judged_on_their_own_and_the_ribbon_follows_the_active` (`setup_mount.rs`), `the_z_stroke_cap_reads_the_ops_own_setups_machine_not_the_active_one` (`fixture_route.rs`) | pass |
| 3 Verified / simulated | New: `a_spindle_limit_is_judged_on_each_ops_own_machine_from_either_active_setup` (12000 rpm refused on machine B only, naming Face2, nothing written) and `a_rotary_index_swing_is_judged_on_each_ops_own_machine` (a work-turning A with no nose height refuses only the ops of the setup that mounts it). Existing: `a_travel_limit_is_judged_on_the_ops_own_machine_only` (`setup_mounts_post.rs`), `the_struck_check_judges_each_op_on_its_own_setups_spindle` (`fixture_ux.rs`), the lathe file's `G50 S12000` from its own machine (`a_mill_and_a_lathe_post_two_files_each_byte_identical_to_posting_it_alone`), workholding rpm per setup (`lathe_workholding_rpm.rs`) | pass |
| 4 Posted | `each_mount_file_is_its_own_post_machine_ops_and_work_offset` (new): two files `_01_Setup1.nc` and `_02_Setup2.nc`. Each is in its own dialect and names its own machine. Each holds only its own operations in order (Face1a before Face1b) at its own work offset (G54 / G55). The bytes are the same whichever setup is active. UI: `each_setup_picks_its_own_machine_and_post_and_posts_one_file_per_mount` (extended: shell Post command, dialect asserts) | pass |
| 5 Follow the document | `the_document_mount_moves_only_the_following_setup_and_untick_follows_again` (new): a new document machine and post (Tilt-head 5-axis, Haas) change Setup1's file and leave every byte of Setup2's. Unticking Setup2's own post, then its own machine, makes it follow the document (one file at the end). Each untick is one undo step back to the earlier output | pass |
| 6 Round trip | `two_mounts_round_trip_byte_identical_and_undo_redo_restores_each_output` (new): save, reopen, post gives byte-identical files. Undo and redo of the machine pick and of the post pick each restore the earlier output. Existing: `a_setups_own_machine_and_post_round_trip_and_undo` (`setup_mount.rs`), `the_script_post_writes_one_file_per_mount` (`setup_mounts_post.rs`) | pass |
| 7 Edges | `the_same_own_mount_is_one_file_and_half_a_mount_is_two` (new): both setups owning machine B and post B give one file through Siemens for machine B with G54 and G55, as `program_mounts` groups. An own machine with a followed post gives two Fanuc files. The reverse gives one machine in two dialects. `an_own_lathe_post_on_a_mill_setup_is_refused_by_name` (new, `setup_mounts_post.rs`): refused (#1190 door), nothing written. `an_own_milling_post_on_a_lathe_setup_is_refused_by_name` (new, ignored) | **lathe setup + milling post: FAILS, #1232**. The rest pass |

## How tested

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main`: green on the first run. It ran app `mcp_setup_mount_trace` and `setup_mount_trace` (new suites), `setup_mounts_post::an_own_lathe_post_on_a_mill_setup_is_refused_by_name`, the ui lib unit tests, and ui `boundary`, `boundary_picks` and `theme_files`.
- Each new test was also run by name: `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test setup_mount_trace` (6 passed), `--test mcp_setup_mount_trace` (1 passed), `--test setup_mounts_post -- an_own_ --include-ignored` (the #1232 pin fails as filed), and `cargo test -p camcraft-ui --lib -- setup_mount_pages` (4 passed).
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --test setup_mount_trace --test mcp_setup_mount_trace --test setup_mounts_post -- -D warnings` and `cargo clippy -p camcraft-ui --lib --tests -- -D warnings`: clean.

## What was not exercised

- No posted file was run on a real control or a control simulator. The dialect checks are text markers.
- Nothing was looked at on screen. The UI leg drives clicks headlessly.
- The single-file post of a lathe document whose document post is a milling dialect was not run. #1232 says it is very likely the same path.
- A user's own `.cps` as a setup's own post was not traced.

title: fix(sim): the hole-wall excuse measures a facet about its hole's axis, so a tool cutting into a flat is a gouge
body:
## What changed

The containment kinds' hole-wall excuse in the solid law (drill, bore, thread mill, cross drill) read a facet by its **corners** against the **tool's own disc** (`swept.rs` `chord_dip`). If every vertex stood outside the tool, the facet was forgiven its edges' dip into it. That bound grows as the tool shrinks against the hole. Every flat whose corners lie on the hole circle (an octagon, a D-bore, a square) passes inside that circle along its middle, and a cut there got no blocking warning.

Now:
- The operation names its holes' axes: `verify::solid_hits_walled(path, facets, cutter, law, &[HoleAxis])`. `generate::contain_into` passes the op's Drill/Bore/Thread holes, and `cross_part` passes the cross holes' lines. `solid_hits` is unchanged for every other caller. With no holes named, nothing is excused.
- New `crates/sim/src/verify/hole_wall.rs`. A facet is excused only when it is a **round wall** of one of those holes. Its sagitta about the hole axis must be at most `WALL_SAG` = 0.05 mm. The sagitta is the nearest vertex's radius less the facet's **nearest approach** to the axis (point-to-segment, or point-in-triangle, in the plane square to the axis).
- The excuse granted is the smaller of that sagitta and the old edge-dip bound, so the law can only convict more than before, never less.
- A facet with any non-finite coordinate excuses nothing. So does a facet over the axis, or a hole axis that is not along the move's tool axis (`Frame::axis_xy`).
- `chord_dip` is removed. The decisions are in `docs/decisions/1205-hole-wall-nearest-point.md`: why a cap is needed on top of the nearest-point reading, why 0.05 mm, and what was dropped.

Why there is a cap: an octagon *is* an inscribed polygon of its corners' circle, with a 0.38 mm sagitta on r 5. So a nearest-point measurement alone still excuses a cut to its corners. Only a stated bound on what counts as tessellation tells a coarse circle from a flat. That is the issue's "passes inside the circle by more than the stated tolerance convicts".

## Probe readings (before = main's rule, after = this PR; the same build with the old rule toggled by a throwaway switch, since removed)

| Case (plate, blind hole, corners on the circle) | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Thread mill 6 mm p1, declared r 4.4 (major 4.94), octagon on r 5: solid law | **0** gouges | 38 |
| same, D-bore (96-gon r 5, flat chord at Y 4) | **0** | 22 |
| same, 32-gon at the major circle (the thread's own round wall) | 0 | 0 |
| Bore EM-0600 at r 5, octagon on r 5 (0.38 mm into each flat): op verdict | **0** | 10 |
| Bore at r 5, D-bore | **0** | 4 |
| Bore at r 5, 32-gon on r 5 (0.024 mm sagitta, past the 0.01 tolerance) | 0 | 0 |
| Bore at r 4.6, octagon on r 5 (inside the 4.62 flats) | 0 | 0 |
| Bore at r 5, 23-gon (sagitta 0.0466, under the cap) | 0 | 0 |
| Bore at r 5, 22-gon (sagitta 0.0509, over the cap) | 0 | 10 |
| Drill DR-0600, octagon on r 3 (flats at 2.77) | **0** | 1 |
| Drill DR-0600, 32-gon on r 3 | 0 | 0 |

Thread note: on main, a model-sourced **Thread op** is already refused by its region law (the helix cuts past the declared minor circle by design; that is #1071, which PR #1099 grants). So the op-level probe gives 52 blocking warnings before and after. The reviewer's 0 was read on #1099's tree. The thread rows above therefore judge the generator's own helix with the solid law alone, as `contain_into` runs it. That is the verdict that stands once #1099 lifts the region law.

## Tests

- New `crates/app/tests/hole_wall_flats.rs` (4 tests):
  - `a_thread_mill_cutting_into_an_octagons_flats_is_a_gouge`: the reviewer's probe, plus the D-bore and the round-wall control.
  - `a_bore_or_drill_into_an_octagons_flats_is_a_gouge`
  - `a_round_tool_in_a_finely_faceted_round_hole_still_verifies_clean`
  - `the_wall_excuse_ends_at_its_stated_sagitta`: the boundary pin, 23-gon clean / 22-gon convicts on r 5.
- New unit tests in `hole_wall.rs`: `a_chord_reads_its_own_sagitta_about_the_axis` and `a_facet_over_the_axis_or_unreadable_is_never_round` (NaN and infinite input excuse nothing).
- `solid_law_goldens`' `contain_law` now names the holes it drills (it called the law with `hole_walls: true` and no holes, which now excuses nothing). Its verdicts are unchanged: all 14 goldens clean, and the drill/peck/tap 32-gon goldens still need, and keep, the excuse.
- Kept green without loosening anything: `bore_facet_sagitta` (2/2) and `bore_entry`.
- Full `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` on the final head 6637e92c: green, 8.1 min. The sim lib plus 19 sim suites, motion `real_tip`/`solid_law`, the app lib plus 75 app suites: 950 passed, 0 failed, 12 ignored.
- By hand on the same head: `bore_facet_sagitta`, `golden_cl`, `conformance`, `tap_sim`, `mill2d_c`, `drill_prior_kinds`, `drilling_cross_box`, `drilling_cross_holder`: 57 passed, 0 failed. Before cleanup I also ran `bore_entry`, `verify`, `solid_law`, `solid_law_goldens`, `coarse_contain`, `drilling_*`, `operations` and more on identical logic, all green. (There is no `coarse_rims` suite on main.)
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-sim --all-targets -D warnings` is clean. `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --lib --test hole_wall_flats --test solid_law_goldens -D warnings` is clean.

## Goldens

No golden file moves: no `.cl`, `.nc` or snapshot PNG is touched, and `golden_cl` is green. I instrumented the old rule over the touched suites (throwaway, removed). Every excuse the old rule granted in `solid_law_goldens` (3326), `drilling_cross` (15595) and `operations` (574) is still granted.

The one newly convicted fixture is `tap_sim::a_tap_in_a_hole_modelled_at_tap_drill_size_is_not_a_gouge`:
- Its hole is a **square** of half-width 2.5 under an M6 tap.
- The generator's contain law sweeps the tap at its full r 3, which is 0.5 mm into each flat. The old rule excused that only because the square's corners (r 3.54) stand outside the tap.
- The test asserts only the program sim's verdict (core-radius tap, #266), so it still passes. The op's generator verdict now carries a blocking Gouge.
- This matches main on a *round* tap-drill hole, where the contain law already convicts the tap's full radius (the hole's vertices are inside the tap, so no excuse applied). The square was the bug's case, not a different law.

## Not exercised

- A tilted cross hole through a coarse wall: `drilling_cross*` suites pass, and the axis-in-frame mapping is covered only by them.
- A 4th/5th-axis posed Drill/Bore whose tool axis is not the hole axis: there the excuse now stands down (stricter).
- Real STEP/STL parts beyond `Milling-test.step`. A hole imported coarser than 0.05 mm sagitta (e.g. a 16-gon on r 5) now convicts as a false gouge, which is the safe side, as with #864.

## Overlap with PR #1099

This PR changes `solid.rs`, `solid_index.rs`, `mod.rs`, `contact.rs` and `rapids_posed.rs` (the `hits` signature: the `hole_walls: bool` parameter became the hole-axis slice `walls`). PR #1099 also changes them: it adds a `bores` parameter to the same `hits` and a `solid_hits_threaded` beside `solid_hits`, and `generate.rs` `contain_into`. Whichever merges second needs a careful keep-both on those lines. `swept.rs` `chord_dip` is gone: #1099's call to it becomes `hole_wall::wall_excuse`. #1099's own vertex-based measurements (`thread_bore.rs` `wall_radius`, `material_source.rs` `major_rims`) are left to that PR's review, which asks for this same nearest-point rule.

Changelog: The verifier no longer excuses a drill, bore, thread mill or cross drill cutting into the flats of a hole whose corners lie on its circle (an octagon, a D-bore, a square); only a round wall's own tessellation, up to 0.05 mm, is forgiven (#1205).

Effort: high (no escalation). Fork synced at v0.18.0 (process files at PROCESS_VERSION 29); branched from upstream/main 62a2c93a.

Fixes #1205

title: fix(post): an undeclared post script posts only C sections on a lathe or mill-turn
body:
Fork synced at v0.18.0.

## What changed
- `app::lathe_voice::at_post` (the #1190 door) reads the script's dialect through main's `post::dialect::work_voice` (#1174) - no second parse of `capabilities`:
  - `WorkSpindle` (mask has the turning bit): the door fires for every operation, as before.
  - `ToolSpindle` (mask 1 alone): passes, as before.
  - **`Undeclared`** (no mask naming 1 or 2: absent, 0, 4, a string, negative, non-finite): on a setup whose machine has a work spindle (lathe or mill-turn), the door refuses **every section except a C-axis live-tool section** (`voice_of` == `LiveTool`). That covers milling sections (a turning post would open them on the work spindle) *and* sections that turn the work (a turning kind, an on-centre Drill): only a turning post may post those (maintainer, 2026-11-12, #1232 / PR #1265), an unstated script is not known to be one, and a user's milling post without the line would post them as milling (tool change, `S M3`, the work standing still). The refusal says the script has no `capabilities` line and what to add (`capabilities = 1;` mill, `= 2;` turning), and for a turning section why. On a mill or with no machine an undeclared script passes, as before.
- `at_post` takes the script's name for the refusal (`Option<&str>`): the per-mount post (`posting_mounts.rs`) and the per-op post (`posting_per_op.rs`) pass the setup post's registry name or path from `script_of`; the single-file `post_script` and an explicit script for all mounts pass `None` ("the post script").
- `setup_workholding::work_speed`: the `(Undeclared, Some(_))` arm is unchanged; its stale comment now says what the door does.
- Decision recorded in `docs/decisions/1199-undeclared-dialect.md`: option (b) of the issue, with the stricter undeclared rule, a cell-by-cell table, the residual case (an undeclared *lathe* script on a mill / no-machine doc meets no door; not covered by #1265 either) and what was dropped.

Behaviour change for users: a user's own script without `capabilities`, posting anything but a C-axis section on a lathe or mill-turn setup, is refused by name with the one-line fix. Every shipped post states its mask, so no shipped post, golden or registry pairing changes.

title: feat(ui): WCS page applies its origin from the footer beside Close, and says where the origin is
body:
#870: a Makera Z1 user cut air on their first program because they hadn't understood where the origin was. Then it "took a while to find out how to actually save the setting, as the 'set origin' button is crammed next to a lot of other options".

Fork synced at v0.18.0, PROCESS_VERSION 29; merged with upstream main at 62a2c93a.

## What changed

- **Set origin in the footer.** The WCS page's apply button leaves the page body (where it shared a row with *Level*, among the quarter turns) and moves into the property pane's fixed footer, beside *Close* (`egui_app::wcs_footer`). Every other page keeps its plain *Close*.
- **Pending edits are flagged.** While the typed X/Y/Z or angles differ from the placed WCS, the footer shows **Origin not applied** in the warning ink.
  - The position is compared to 1e-9 mm. The angles are compared as rotations, so yaw 360 is not an edit. A non-finite field reads as pending.
  - The drafts survive a close and reopen, so closing loses nothing silently. Closing does not apply them either.
- **The origin in words.** A new pure module, `app::setup_origin`, places the origin against the box the page anchors on (the stock box, else the model's bounds).
  - A point on one of the 27 anchor points is named, e.g. `top of stock, front-left corner`, `top of stock, centre` or `mid-height of stock, front edge, centred`.
  - Any other point is given as signed distances from the box's left side, front and top, so it never claims a corner it is not on.
  - The WCS page states it under its heading: `G54 origin: top of stock, front-left corner (X0 Y0 Z0)`. The setup sheet gains an `origin:` line under the WCS numbers.
- **Viewport marker:** the WCS axis triad already marks the origin; nothing was added.
- **Docs:** `docs/user-guide/work-origin.md`, a short page on where the origin is shown and how to change it.
- Decision record: `docs/decisions/870-wcs-set-origin-footer.md`.

**Overlap with #759** (@mkinney, open draft, `conflicts`): it splits the WCS page body out of `pages.rs` into `wcs_page.rs` and keeps its own *Set Origin* in the quarter-turn rows. This PR touches the page body in one place only, removing that button. The new code lives in its own files (`wcs_footer.rs`, `setup_origin.rs`). Whichever lands second drops the body button and calls `wcs_footer::origin_line` from the page.

## How it was tested

New pinning tests:
- `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests/wcs_footer.rs` (structural: painted text, AccessKit labels, coarse placement):
  - `the_page_says_where_the_origin_is_in_words`
  - `set_origin_sits_in_the_footer_beside_close_and_nowhere_else`: one row, Set origin before Close, below the page body, exactly one apply button, no flag on a fresh page.
  - `a_typed_origin_is_flagged_until_set_origin_applies_it`: the flag appears, a click on Set origin places the typed X and clears it, and yaw 360 does not raise it.
- `app::setup_origin` unit tests: `every_anchor_point_is_named`, `a_point_off_the_anchors_is_given_as_distances_never_as_a_corner`, `a_non_finite_origin_or_box_says_so`.
- `crates/app/tests/setup_wcs.rs`: `the_setup_sheet_says_where_the_origin_is_in_words` (corner, centre, off-anchor).

Two existing ui tests got a taller window, 1280 x 900 instead of 720. The new origin line makes the WCS page one to two rows taller, and at 720 px the bottom of the page scrolls under the footer. The page scrolls; nothing is lost.
- `one_wcs::the_wcs_page_shows_the_work_offset_dropdown_and_no_setups_page_pointer`: its bottom note was out of view.
- `origin_page_shows_the_anchor_grid_and_arms_pick_mode`: its SE cell click missed.

Gates on 8b850a18:
- `cargo test -p camcraft-ui` (CWD `crates/ui`): all green. The lib has 596 passed and 5 ignored; every integration binary passes.
- App suites that read the setup sheet or the WCS: `setup_wcs`, `setup_sheet`, `rotated_wcs`, `setup_align`, `program_entry`, `inverted_axis_display`, `setup_stock_source`: all pass. `cargo test -p camcraft-app --lib setup_origin`: 3 passed.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- No snapshot PNG touched.

## Not exercised

- Not looked at in the running app. The layout is pinned structurally only.
- On a rotated or aligned setup (#326), "left" and "front" are the world box's, as the anchor grid's compass names already are.
- The release-lane pixel snapshots were not run. If one frames the WCS page, it moves at the cut's regeneration.

Changelog: WCS page: Set origin sits in the footer beside Close, unapplied edits are flagged, and the page and setup sheet say where the origin is in words ("top of stock, front-left corner") (#870)

Effort: medium (the issue's label). Not escalated.

Fixes #870

title: feat(edm): sinker side burn - a lateral electrode move that burns one wall out by a stated amount
body:
**Stacked on #1166** (#544, `issue/544-sinker-orbits`), which stacks on #1131 (#541) → #560 (#531) → #551 (#530). Retarget it to `main` once its parents merge. Fork synced at v0.18.0 (process files at PROCESS_VERSION 17).

## What changed
- **New op kind, Sinker Side Burn** (`OpType::SinkerSideBurn`, stored id 42, appended; file key `sinker_side_burn`). Its params are `SinkerSideBurnOp { burn: SinkerBurnOp, direction, amount, undersize }`:
  - The burn's plunge is #541's struct, embedded whole, with the op's **own** condition. It takes no orbit; an orbit is refused by name.
  - Then one lateral Feed of `amount` along +X, -X, +Y or -Y at the floor, the same Feed back to the burn point, and the rapid retract.
  - #541's door (`sinker::check`) and condition read (`sinker_op::condition_gap_as`) are reused, not copied.
- **Allowance law** (`motion::sinker_side`): `allowance = undersize - gap`. Refused by name:
  - a move past the allowance ("... toward +X burns into the part - the side's allowance is 0.150 (undersize 0.200 less spark gap 0.050)");
  - a gap the undersize can't honour;
  - a non-finite, zero or negative amount;
  - a bad undersize;
  - an orbit.
- **Validated at command creation** (`gates::sinker_gate`, on CreateOperation, PasteOperation, EditOperationParams and ChangeOperationKind, ahead of `is_sane` so the refusal is by name):
  - always: the structural refusals above;
  - once a condition is named on a sinker EDM: an unknown condition, the gap against the undersize, and the allowance.

  An unnamed condition stays a draft (the ribbon's seed) and is refused at generation. Generation, the staleness stamp and the sim plan re-run the whole law (`sinker_side_op::side_gap`). A machine that later re-states a wider gap therefore refuses the stored op by name.
- The stock sim sweeps every move with the existing box atom. No new sim law.
- **MCP:** through the params JSON door (`add_operation` / `edit_operation` with `direction` / `amount` / `undersize`). `list_operation_types` lists the kind. No new command, so no new MCP tool.
- **UI:** only the minimal rows on the existing sinker page's Passes tab (wall, amount, undersize, in place of the orbit rows), plus the contour glyph for its row. The full pages are #548's. No snapshot PNG was touched.
- **Files:** an appended DTO variant (the burn's keys flattened, plus the three side keys). Old files load unchanged.
- Decision record: `docs/decisions/545-sinker-side-burn.md`.

## How tested
- `crates/app/tests/sinker_side.rs` (new):
  - `a_side_burn_moves_the_faced_wall_by_its_amount_in_the_sim`: for each of the four directions, at a 0.05 column grid:
    - the faced wall stands at electrode + gap + amount: the column centre just inside it is burned to the floor and **the next column out is untouched**;
    - the far wall and the walls across the move stay at the plunge's gap;
    - the program verdict reports 0 gouge cells.
  - `a_lateral_move_past_the_allowance_is_refused_by_name`:
    - refused at creation: a move past the allowance, past the undersize, a gap past the undersize, an unknown condition, a NaN/inf/negative/zero amount, a bad undersize;
    - at the allowance exactly, the op is admitted; an edit past it is refused;
    - after a remount with a wider gap, generation refuses by name and the op is left unchanged.
  - `an_undersize_overstated_against_the_part_is_convicted_by_the_stock_sim`: the part's cavity lacks the claimed undersize, so the sim reports a gouge.
  - `the_side_burn_round_trips_the_file_and_rides_the_mcp_params_door`: save and load, then `list_operation_types`, add, generate, an edit past the allowance refused, edit, undo.
  - `sinker_side_burn_matches_golden`: new golden `crates/app/tests/golden/sinker_side_burn.cl`, read by hand. Rapid to (12.5, -7.5, 25), plunge to Z 14.05 (floor 14 + gap 0.05), lateral -Y 0.15 to Y -7.65, back to -7.5, rapid to Z 25. Five moves.
- Unit tests in `motion::sinker_side`: `sinker_side_moves_along_its_axis_by_the_amount_and_back` and `sinker_side_refuses_past_the_allowance_by_name`.
- `ribbon` (the last kind is now SinkerSideBurn) and `coarse_laws` (SinkerSideBurn is a stated refusal on a reduced model, like SinkerBurn).
- Gate: `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` on 7bdd2505. Tools, post, sim, motion and ui suites, and every app integration binary, were green. That includes coarse_laws, sinker_burn, sinker_orbit, sinker_side, edm_machine, edm_conditions, golden_cl, project_roundtrip, operations, ribbon and mcp. The app lib's `operation::tests::stamp_follows_every_input` failed on the kind count (42 -> 43); b8191744 bumps the pin, and `cargo test -p camcraft-app --lib` is green on the final head (138 passed). `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean.

## Not exercised
- Not exercised on a real EDM control: the conditions are synthetic.
- Posting waits on #542 (the sinker post). This PR emits no new PARAM.
- No wear compensation (#546) and no electrode generation (#547).

Changelog: Sinker EDM side burn: a lateral electrode move burns one wall out by a stated amount, bounded by the op's own undersize less its condition's spark gap; a move into the part is refused by name (#545)
Effort: high

Fixes #545

title: fix(turning): read a lathe holder body on the holder's own side of the axis
body:
Fork synced at v0.18.0 (branch cut from upstream/main 7e3c75f9).

## What changed

The holder law (#369) read a lathe body point at `|X + x|`, with `X` signed along the path's signed meridian (`SignedMeridian`). That frame takes its + side from the path's **first** off-axis point, which need not be the side the holder stands on. Take a rear tool that starts a hair past centre: every later tip is at X < 0 of that frame, and the body was read mirrored through the axis. A lip reaching the part was judged clear, and a clear body was judged to cross the axis.

- New `crates/app/src/operation/turning_holder_side.rs`: `sided` gives the holder's side as a property of the whole path, read from its moves' meridian pieces. A rigid holder never flips mid-path, so the side is the one the path reaches farthest on. The other side may hold only a past-centre overrun of at most `PAST_CENTRE` = 2.5 mm, as in a face pass cleaning the centre pip, while the far side reaches beyond twice it. A path on both sides beyond that, or whose far side stays under 5 mm while the near side is off the axis, is refused by name: "the lathe holder body cannot be judged: the path stands on both sides of the spindle axis ...". A round XY arc about the axis (a thread's half-turn, whose ends alternate onto the antipode) tells no side: it is left out of the reading and read at |rho| on the holder's side.
- `turning_holder::judge` reads `Reach::radii(side * X)`. On the + side the call is `radii(x)` exactly as before, so it is byte-identical. `body_axes`, which draws the body (#1038), flips its radial by the same side, so the drawn holder is still the judged one.
- `camcraft-tools::lathe_holder`: the docs now state that X is signed along the holder's own +x, which is away from the axis on the holder's side, front or rear post alike.

**Which signed X the generators produce.** Every turning generator places its straight moves' tips at `Frame::point(rho >= 0, ..)`, and a face pass runs to `rho = 0` at most. Threading is the exception: its half-turn arcs end on `Frame::antipode`, at -rho, by construction - so the side is read with those round arcs left out, and they are read at |rho| (as `kerf_of` already does). Every other generated tip is at X >= 0 of its own frame and reads as before. No turning op today carries a straight-move tip at X < 0, so the defect was latent and the issue stays P2, not re-rated P0. This is stated in the pinning tests and in `docs/decisions/1102-lathe-body-signed-reach.md`.

**UI/MCP wording.** Main has no "+x points away from the spindle axis" text. That text is in #1043, and under this law it is now true as written. No wording change was needed here.

**Expected merge with #1043 / #1061.** This PR touches only the reach reading in `turning_holder.rs` (a `side` field on `Scene`, one `sided_pieces` call in `judge` and one in `body_axes`, and the `radii` argument), plus a new module. Merging either way should be additive.

## How tested

- `operation::turning_holder_side::tests::the_side_is_where_the_path_reaches_and_a_past_centre_overrun_keeps_it`: front paths are +1, a face run 0.4 past centre keeps +1, and a rear path starting 0.5 past centre is -1. Both-sides paths are refused by name, and so are a near side off the axis with a far side under 5 mm (`[2, -3]`) and a non-finite radius.
- `operation::turning_holder_side::tests::a_rear_tool_past_centre_is_read_on_its_own_side_like_its_front_mirror`: this runs `judge` end to end. A rear tool (tip at X -8) whose body lip reaches the part is convicted, and the same tool with an outward body passes. Both match the front mirror at X +8. A face start 0.4 past centre reads on the front side. A both-sides path is refused.
- `operation::turning_holder_side::tests::a_thread_pass_winding_through_the_antipode_is_judged_not_refused`: a thread-kernel-shaped pass (six ccw half-turn arcs about the axis alternating +5.5/-5.5) judges `Ok` with an outward body and convicts a reaching one, front and rear mirror alike (the first cut refused it as both sides).
- `operation::turning_holder_side::tests::the_drawn_body_flips_its_radial_with_the_holder_side`: `body_axes` returns the negated radial for a rear path, the frame's own for a front one, and draws a thread pass on its approach's side.
- Mutation check: with the old `radii(x)` reading put back, the rear pin fails (`Ok([])` against `Ok([(1, true)])`), which is the missed strike.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` on the final head 569f09b9 (upstream/main merged in, review findings fixed): green (app suites, the 130-suite gate map of `app::operation` plus `--lib`, and the ui suites; 0 failed, 9.8 min). `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-tools --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

## Not exercised

- A real rear-turret machine definition, because none exists. Also the GUI drawing of a flipped body (the `body_axes` flip is not pinned by its own test).
- No golden or snapshot changes.

Changelog: The lathe holder law reads a holder body on its own side of the spindle axis for a tip at either signed X, and refuses by name a path that stands on both sides (#1102)

Effort: high (no escalation)

Fixes #1102

title: feat(edm): sinker orbit patterns (circular, vector, planetary) as explicit moves
body:
**Stacked on #1131** (M5's #541, sinker burn to depth, branch `issue/541-sinker-burn-depth`). Retarget to `main` before #1131 merges. Fork synced at v0.18.0 (process files at PROCESS_VERSION 17).

## What changed

A Sinker Burn can now **orbit at the burn floor** after the plunge. The orbit is circular, vector or planetary, and it is expanded into explicit Feed chords (#290 D3), so the 3-axis stock sim's box atom (#541) verifies every move that would post. Corner joins are included, under the same laws as #541's burns.

- `motion::sinker_orbit` (new) holds the pattern geometry.
  - circular: out along +X to the radius, then one full circle;
  - vector: out to the radius and back along N evenly spaced directions from +X;
  - planetary: an Archimedean spiral from 0 to the radius over N turns, closed by a full circle.
  - Every vertex is on or inside the stated radius (an ulp-past rounding is pulled back in), so no chord overshoots it. Chords keep a sagitta of 0.001 mm or less. Their count is a multiple of 4, so the ±X/±Y directions are vertices and a rectangular electrode's walls move out by exactly the radius. The counts are bounded (vectors 1..=72, turns 1..=20), so an orbit cannot balloon into a hang.
- `motion::sinker::burn_to_depth` runs the orbit at the tip Z at the servo feed and returns to the centre before the rapid retract. With `orbit: None` the plain plunge's CL and params digest are unchanged.
- `SinkerBurnOp.orbit: Option<SinkerOrbit>` is an additive field and file key (`orbit: { kind, radius, vectors, turns }`), so old files load. It is edited through `CreateOperation` / `EditOperationParams`. MCP reaches it through the existing params JSON door (`add_operation` / `edit_operation`, `"orbit": null` drops it). There is no new command, so there is no new MCP tool. The minimal sinker page gets Orbit / radius / vectors / turns rows on Passes.
- **Machine law** (`sinker_op::orbit_law`, #290 D6), refused by name at generation:
  - `machine X lists no vector orbit under edm.orbits ...`
  - `machine X states no maximum orbit radius (edm.max_orbit_radius) ...` (absent is not unlimited)
  - `the circular orbit radius 0.600 exceeds machine X's maximum orbit radius 0.500`
  - The job and the staleness stamp read it through `burn_gap`, so a re-stated orbit list or maximum marks the op stale. A garbled orbit is refused at the door (`is_sane`).
- **No schema change.** `edm.orbits[]` and `edm.max_orbit_radius` already exist in the `.mch` edm section from #530 (on this base), and #1141's post reads the same fields. They are read as they are. This PR emits no `EdmOrbit` PARAM: the orbit posts as its explicit moves, and a canned word on top would be a double orbit (D3's later item).
- Decisions: `docs/decisions/544-sinker-orbits.md`.

## How tested

- `crates/app/tests/sinker_orbit.rs` (new, 6 tests):
  - `sinker_orbit_circular_matches_golden`: golden `tests/golden/sinker_orbit_circular.cl`, which I read. It has the plunge to Z 14.050, out to +0.200 X, 32 CCW chords on the r = 0.2 circle back to +X, a return to the centre, and the retract. Max excursion is 0.200.
  - `a_circular_orbit_widens_the_simulated_cavity_by_its_radius`: on the simulated stock (0.05 cell), the cavity floor reaches electrode + gap + radius on ±X and ±Y, and the next column out stands untouched. The same burn without the orbit stops one radius short. The furthest move is the radius exactly.
  - `every_orbit_pattern_stays_in_its_radius_and_verifies_clean`: all three patterns stay inside the radius with chords only, and `simulate_document` finds 0 gouge cells in the orbit-sized cavity.
  - `an_orbit_wider_than_the_parts_cavity_is_convicted_by_the_stock_sim`
  - `an_unlisted_pattern_and_an_over_radius_orbit_are_refused_by_name`: also covers the unstated maximum (refused), radius == max (admitted), and the garbled-orbit door.
  - `the_orbit_round_trips_the_file_and_rides_the_mcp_params_door`: file round trip, MCP add, an over-max edit refused at generate, undo, an unlisted pattern refused, `orbit: null` back to a plunge.
- `motion::sinker_orbit` unit tests: every pattern for radii 0.0005..12 is inside its radius and closes on the centre; the chord tolerance holds and the axis directions are vertices; garbled numbers are refused by name.
- `sinker_burn.rs` (#541) is unchanged apart from `orbit: None` in its literals, and its golden is byte-identical.
- Gate: the full `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` on head `49904407` ran tools, post, sim, motion, app and ui: 3437 passed, 1 failed. The failure is `coarse_laws::every_kind_is_either_judged_or_refused_for_a_stated_reason_on_a_reduced_model` ("SinkerBurn is judged while a tolerance is left"). It is **pre-existing on the #1131 base**: I reproduced it on the base tree without this commit. `fidelity_law.rs` refuses `Section::Sinker`, but the test's `refused` list has no `SinkerBurn`. This PR touches neither file. It belongs to #1131.
- The sinker suites (`sinker_burn`, `sinker_orbit`), `edm_machine`, `edm_conditions`, `golden_cl` and `project_roundtrip` are green. `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -D warnings` is clean.

## Not exercised

- **Not exercised on a real EDM control.** The fixtures are synthetic: an invented condition, invented orbit words and an invented 0.5 mm maximum.
- Posting waits on #542 (#1141). That post refuses arcs, and how it treats the lateral orbit chords has not been checked here. The post script is untouched.
- The stock view / playback (field eye) still refuses an electrode by name (#541), so the orbit is judged by the program verdict's column engine only.
- The minimal sinker page gains orbit rows; #548's full pages (PR #1165) will need them carried over.
- Interaction with #543's undersize (PR #1136) and #546's wear compensation was not exercised. Both touch the same op, and whichever merges second may need a small merge.

Changelog: Sinker Burn orbits (circular, vector, planetary) at the burn floor, expanded into explicit moves the stock sim verifies; a pattern the machine does not list, or a radius past its stated maximum, is refused by name (#544, PR #1166)

Effort: high (no escalation)

Fixes #544

title: fix(post): doosan-dnm index writes A only for a stated A rotary
body:
Fork synced at v0.18.0 (branch cut from upstream/main 7e3c75f9, which includes #1092).

## What changed
- `assets/posts/doosan-dnm.cps`, non-RTCP indexing path in `tilt()` only: the A word is now written through #1092's `angleWord("A", ...)`, and `missingLetter` runs first. A turning letter the machine does not state is refused by name ("indexed move commands A - the machine states no A rotary"), and no word is posted. A stated C that turns is refused by name too ("indexed move commands C - this dialect's indexing path writes only an A rotary"). Before this change that path dropped C silently.
- On a machine that states A, the output is byte-identical: `angleWord` is `w()`, which is `"A" + fu(v)` for the finite angle `tilt()` already requires.
- Other direct rotary-letter writers: there are none left. Doosan's probe macro `ax + fu(pos)` writes only X/Y/Z, and fanuc.cps's non-RTCP path refuses every tilt.
- The edit stays inside the indexing block, so it merges additively with the open doosan-dnm PRs #961, #981 and #1034 (coolant, units and probe coolant, in other sections).
- Decision: `docs/decisions/1155-doosan-index-a-word.md`.

## How tested
- Pinning test `doosan_dnm_post::doosan_dnm_index_names_only_a_stated_rotary` (app). It checks three things. An A index on a machine with no rotaries is refused by name, with no A word. A turning C on millturn.mch (states C, non-RTCP) is refused by name, with no C word. On the shipped doosan-dnm.mch the motion lines are exactly `M11 / G00 X0 Y0 Z10 A90 / M10 / G01 X50 Y0 Z-1 F400`. I confirmed it fails on the upstream script: no warning, and the A word was posted.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: green. It ran only the changed test, because .cps is not gate-mapped.
- By hand: every `camcraft-post` suite passed (all `script_*`, recorded_streams, cycle_hop, post_engine, vendor_mch_cli). These app suites passed: doosan_dnm_post 9, fanuc_post 12, fourth_axis_pose 9, conformance 6, tilt 8, rotary_verify 9, probe_spindle_stop 2, post_unit_word 5, recorded_post_streams 2.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --test doosan_dnm_post -- -D warnings`: clean.
- No golden moved.

## Not exercised
- No real Doosan control was used.
- C indexing on a C table is refused for now, not implemented.

Changelog: doosan-dnm post refuses by name an indexed move that turns a rotary the machine does not state (or a turning C, which the indexing path never wrote) instead of posting an A word the control lacks or silently dropping C (#1155)

Effort: high (no escalation)

Fixes #1155

title: feat(edm): sinker electrode wear compensation in Z
body:
**Stacked on #1131** (#541 sinker burn to depth, branch `issue/541-sinker-burn-depth`), which is itself stacked on #560 (#531 EDM condition table), stacked on #551 (#530 EDM machine kinds). The chain is #551 -> #560 -> #1131 -> this PR. Until those merge, their commits show here; this PR adds one commit on top of #1131's head. Fork synced at v0.18.0.

## What changed
- **A wear rate per condition.** `edm.conditions[]` gains an optional `wear`: the electrode's axial wear rate, as mm of electrode lost per mm burned (dimensionless, not unit-scaled). `parse_mch` (so `LoadMachine` and the project reader) and `Edm::is_sane` refuse a rate that is not a finite ratio in [0, 1), by name ("... is not an axial wear rate ..."). No rate ships with any machine; rates are user data (#290 D4).
- **A measured wear and a layer step on the op.** `SinkerBurnOp` gains `layer`, `wear_lost` and `wear_over`. A wear measured between burns (length lost over depth burned) wins over the condition's rate. With neither stated, the burn is **not compensated**: the path note and the op page say `electrode wear: not compensated (no wear rate stated)`. `CreateOperation` / `EditOperationParams` (and the project reader) refuse a measured rate of 1 or more, a half-stated or non-finite measurement, and a non-positive layer step, all by name, through a new `OpParams::named_refusal` door that runs ahead of the generic "not usable".
- **Compensation in Z** (`crates/motion/src/sinker_wear.rs`, `burn_compensated`). The burn is fed in layers. Each layer's tip is programmed `rate * d` deeper, where `d` is how far that layer's nominal floor lies below the work top. Every move is re-checked against the bound: the stated floor plus the gap, minus `rate` times the stated depth. A move past it is refused as over-deep, by name. All of #541's refusals still apply. The electrode-length law now reads the deeper, compensated tip. With no rate and no layer step, the moves are exactly #541's (pinned).
- **The stock sim judges the worn electrode.** `plan_program` maps each programmed tip back to where the worn electrode burns (`worn_tip`, the exact inverse of the compensation). A compensated burn to the cavity's own floor therefore reads 0 gouge cells, and a nominal floor past the model is still convicted.
- **Staleness.** The op digest adds the layer step and the measured wear, and the stamp adds the condition's rate, each only when stated. Existing digests do not change.
- **File, MCP, UI.** The three op keys are additive and optional: older files load unchanged and write no new keys. MCP drives them through the existing params JSON door (`add_operation` / `edit_operation`). No new command or tool was needed, and a test pins this. The Sinker Burn page's Passes tab gains Layer step, Measured wear and Measured over, plus the compensation status line.
- Decisions: `docs/decisions/546-sinker-wear-comp.md`.

## How tested
- New suite `crates/app/tests/sinker_wear.rs`:
  - `sinker_wear_layers_match_golden`: golden `crates/app/tests/golden/sinker_wear_layers.cl`. I read it: three 2 mm layers at rate 0.02, gap 0.05, with tips at Z 18.010, 15.970 and 13.930 (that is 18.05 - 0.04, 16.05 - 0.08 and 14.05 - 0.12).
  - `a_condition_wear_rate_deepens_each_layer_and_the_sim_judges_it_clean`
  - `a_missing_wear_rate_shows_not_compensated`
  - `a_bad_wear_rate_is_refused_by_name`: machine file and op commands.
  - `a_measured_wear_wins_over_the_condition_and_round_trips_the_file`: includes an older file with no new keys.
  - `the_wear_fields_ride_the_mcp_params_door`
- Unit tests in `motion::sinker_wear`: wear off equals the plain burn, per-layer deepening plus its inverse, and refusals of the rate, step and reach.
- `crates/app/tests/sinker_burn.rs`: the op literal gains the three new `None` fields; no assertion changed.
- Gate: `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` on this head (b0e121ce), 24.3 min. The tools, post, sim, motion and ui suites pass. In the app suites, every binary passes except one test, and that test **fails on #1131's own head too**: I ran it alone on `origin/issue/541-sinker-burn-depth`, and this PR doesn't change it:
  - `coarse_laws::every_kind_is_either_judged_or_refused_for_a_stated_reason_on_a_reduced_model`: "SinkerBurn is judged while a tolerance is left". The fidelity law refuses a Sinker Burn on a reduced-fidelity model, but the test expects it to be judged.
  The fix belongs on #1131. The sinker_burn, sinker_wear, edm_machine, edm_conditions, golden_cl and project_roundtrip suites pass. `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean.

## Not exercised
- **Not exercised on a real EDM control** (#290 D10). The conditions and wear rates are synthetic fixtures.
- Wear is axial only; corner and side wear are not modelled. No orbit (#544), no multi-electrode undersize logic (#543), and no sinker post (#542). Layers are a stepped plunge with no retract between them.
- The field-arm stock view still refuses an electrode program (as in #541).

Changelog: Sinker EDM: electrode wear compensation in Z - a stated axial wear rate (per condition in the machine file, or measured on the op) deepens each burn layer by the wear it states, bounded and refused by name past it; with no rate the burn says "not compensated" (#546)

Effort: high (no escalation)

Fixes #546

title: feat(sinker): generate an electrode from a cavity's picked faces
body:
Stacked on #1136 (→ #1131 → #560 → #551). Fork synced at v0.18.0. Until those merge, this PR's diff against `main` includes theirs; its own change is the last commit.

## What changed

A sinker EDM electrode is generated from the picked faces of a part's cavity - its level floor and every vertical wall standing on it - and added to the document as #541's electrode tool, in one undo step.

- **`motion::sinker_cavity::cavity_of`** (pure, no world) reads a face set as one cavity. Each face is checked on its own (finite, in range, planar, non-zero area, closed boundary), classed by its outward normal, and the walls are matched to the floor's outer ring edge by edge: a wall stands on a floor edge when one of its edges lies on it at floor height and its normal points into the floor. Every floor edge must be covered end to end.
- **`motion::sinker_electrode::derive`** offsets the outline inward by `undersize + orbit` with the geometry crate's polygon offset (`geo2d::Region::offset_sharp`, Clipper2) and extends the electrode a stated stub above the cavity's mouth. The sizes are the arithmetic `cavity - 2 x inset`; the offset polygon must agree within 10 nm or the derivation refuses.
- **`standing_in`** clips the part's facets against the cavity's column above the floor: a boss, a rib or an overhang in the electrode's way refuses the electrode with the spot.
- **`operation::sinker_faces`** resolves the picks (the one pick rule, #692; outward normals by the facets' winding) and reads a condition's undersize by id through #531's door.
- **`commands::ElectrodeFromFaces`** is the undoable command (its write and inverse are `AddTool`'s). **MCP: `electrode_from_faces`** runs it; its reply carries a `burn` object that `add_operation`'s `params` takes as is.

## Rectangular cavities only, for now

The stock sim burns an electrode with #541's box atom: an axis-aligned rectangular face. So only a cavity whose outline is an axis-aligned rectangle yields an electrode. A rounded corner, a rotated rectangle, an L, a curved wall, a drafted wall or a stepped floor is refused by name, and the refusal names the follow-up: **#1152** (a sim atom and a tool record for an electrode body). The offset outline is already computed and carried on the result for it.

Orbit (#544) is not merged: an optional orbit radius is accepted and taken off the electrode, and the tool's answer says so. Until #544 changes #543's size law, a Sinker Burn judges such an electrode without its orbit.

## Refusals, each by name

Empty face set · a face with a non-finite or out-of-range coordinate · a zero-area or degenerate face · an open loop (a boundary that does not close) · a curved (welded) or non-planar wall · a leaning (drafted) wall or tilted floor · a face looking down · no floor · two floors (faces from different cavities, or a stepped cavity) · only the floor · a wall of another cavity (stands on none of the floor's edges, reaches below it, or faces away) · walls that do not close around the floor · a self-intersecting outline · a non-rectangular cavity (#1152) · an inset that consumes the cavity · a garbled undersize, orbit, stub or pickup · picks on different models, on no part, a stale id, a chain or a vertex · an open, inside-out or non-manifold body · the part standing in the cavity's column · a taken or reserved tool name.

## How tested

Run one by one (`cargo test -p <crate> ... -- --exact` style), debug:

- `camcraft-motion --lib sinker_electrode` (7 tests): `a_rectangular_cavitys_faces_yield_its_electrode`, `a_cavity_reads_whatever_the_winding_split_or_order`, `every_degenerate_face_set_is_refused_by_its_own_name`, `a_cavity_the_box_atom_cannot_burn_is_refused_by_name`, `the_model_standing_in_the_cavitys_column_is_found`, and the seeded fuzz: `fuzz_a_damaged_cavity_is_always_refused_by_name_never_a_panic` (6000 sound cavities, each then damaged one of 20 named ways and required to refuse by that name) and `fuzz_garbage_faces_never_panic_and_never_answer_a_nonsense_electrode` (20000 garbage face sets with NaN, infinities, `f64::MAX`, denormals).
- `camcraft-app --test sinker_electrode` (8 tests): `a_pockets_faces_yield_an_electrode_that_burns_that_pocket_in_the_sim` (the generated rough leaves stock and gouges nothing, the generated finish leaves the program verdict clean), `the_verdict_convicts_the_generated_electrode_burned_off_its_point` (the contrast: 1 mm off centre gouges), `the_electrode_is_one_undo_step_and_its_name_is_checked`, `the_condition_door_reads_the_undersize_or_refuses_by_name`, `a_face_set_that_is_no_single_cavity_is_refused_by_name`, `faces_from_different_cavities_are_refused_by_name`, `a_boss_in_the_cavity_is_in_the_electrodes_way`, `a_rounded_pocket_is_refused_by_name_until_the_sim_burns_a_body`.
- `camcraft-app --test sinker_electrode_mcp`: `the_electrode_is_generated_and_burned_over_mcp_with_the_gui_commands`.

The fuzz found one hole while this was written: a denormal stub vanished into the depth, giving an electrode no longer than its cavity. The stub now has a floor (1 micron) and the length is checked against the depth.

Gate (local, debug, head `c93678aa`):
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo test -p camcraft-motion --lib`: 205 passed, 0 failed, 1 ignored.
- `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test sinker_electrode --test sinker_electrode_mcp --test sinker_burn --test sinker_undersize --test mcp --test mcp_pick --test mcp_pockets --test mcp_order --test commands_undo --test tool_law --test pocket_recognition --test edm_conditions --test edm_machine`: 109 passed, 0 failed.

## What was not exercised

- **Not exercised on a real EDM control.** Synthetic conditions and parts built in code only (#290 D10).
- No GUI entry: the sinker pages are #548's; the command is what its button will run.
- The full quick-gate plan (every suite whose gate map names `app::commands` / `app::operation` / `app::mcp`, about 190 app binaries and 7 ui suites) was not run; the change is additive (new modules, one appended tool-table row, no existing function edited), and the suites named above were run instead.
- The `camcraft-mcp` skill's tool table is a process file and is not touched here (`tools/list` is the live registry).
- STEP-imported parts: the fixtures are meshes built in code. A wall that is off vertical by more than a millionth is refused as leaning.

Decisions: `docs/decisions/547-electrode-from-faces.md`.

Changelog: Sinker EDM: an electrode is generated from the picked faces of a part's cavity (its floor and walls), offset inward by the undersize and extended to a holder stub - `ElectrodeFromFaces`, MCP `electrode_from_faces`; rectangular cavities only, every other face set refused by name (#547)

Effort: max (not escalated)

Fixes #547

title: fix(app): the program sim, setup sheet, tool list and cutting data know a tool-less wire cut
body:
**Stacked on #1123** (issue #532, the Wire Contour op; itself on #560, #551). Until those merge, this PR's diff also shows their commits. The commit for this issue is the last one on the branch. Retarget or merge after #1123.

Fork synced at v0.18.0 (process files at PROCESS_VERSION 17).

## What changed

A Wire Contour mounts no library tool (#532), so its `Operation::tool` is the empty word. Each reader changed below checks `KindInfo::mounts_tool()` and nothing else: no kind matches, no "is the name empty" checks. A milling op whose tool was deleted still mounts a tool, so it is refused or listed exactly as before. Each surface has a pinning test for that too.

| Surface | Before | Now |
|---|---|---|
| Program stock sim (`stock_sim.rs` plan walk, new `stock_sim_wire.rs`) | `Die1: tool  is not in the library` | `plan_program` leaves the wire cut out of the plan, the same way the probe and torch arms do. `simulate_document` refuses by name: `Die1: a wire cut is verified by the wire laws, not the stock sim`. The post gate shows this as its non-blocking "not judged" line, and the setup sheet's sim line says "SIM: not judged - ...". |
| Setup sheet, op row (`setup_sheet/operations.rs`) | empty TOOL cell | TOOL cell `cond C110`, and under the row `CONDITION C110  WIRE D 0.250  GAP 0.040`, read through `wire_op::condition_of` (the door generation uses). A condition the machine no longer states prints `! wire condition: <refusal>`. |
| Setup sheet, tool table (`setup_sheet/tools.rs`) | `(tool '' is no longer in the document)` | No change in this file: it reads `tool_list::for_setup`, which no longer has the row. A wire setup prints "(no tools in this setup)". |
| Tool list / export (`tool_list.rs`, `tool_list_export.rs`) | a row for tool `""` | No row. A wire EDM has no tool table. The export reads the same rows, so no change was needed in it. |
| Cutting data (`cutting.rs`, found in the audit) | `tool  is not in the library` | `a Wire Contour mounts no library tool - its cut is the machine's EDM condition, and the cutting-data table speaks for milling tools only` |

`stock_sim.rs` gets only three touches, to keep the later merge with #1140 a keep-both: the `#[path]` module line, a 3-line skip arm, and one call line. The file was already 421 lines before this PR (now 428). The new logic is in `stock_sim_wire.rs` rather than added to it.

Why refuse the verdict instead of only skipping the cut: judging the uncut stock would report rest material wherever the wire cut through, which is a wrong answer. A program that mixes a wire EDM setup with a mill setup is already refused by the carry law (two machines), so no gouge verdict is lost today. Decisions: `docs/decisions/1110-wire-tool-readers.md`.

## Audit of the other `op.tool` readers

| File | Verdict on a wire cut | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `cutting.rs` | **fixed** (above) | `suggest` looked the empty name up as a library tool. |
| `fixture_struck.rs` (`op_hits`) | fine | No tool means `Ok(vec![])` (no hits). This file is display only (it tints the struck fixture) and feeds no post. A wire cut's workholding verdicts belong to the wire laws (#534). A milling op with a lost tool is still refused at the post by `tool_gate::tool_problem_of`. |
| `fixture_carried.rs` (`carried_fixture_problems`) | fine | No tool means `tool_r = 0.0`, which is only the carry lattice's sizing radius. The fixture-in-carried-body check still runs on the carried body. |
| `operation/footprint.rs` | fine | Only the `Face` arm reads the tool. A Wire Contour takes the `_ => Some(region)` arm, so its footprint is its profile region. |
| `posting_index_swing.rs` | fine | A wire EDM states no work A axis, so `work_a` is `None` and the loop `continue`s before the tool is read. The post refuses a wire cut by name first anyway (`op_streams`, #532). |

title: feat(edm): Wire Contour skim passes - per-pass condition, offset and direction
body:
Stacked on #1139 (on #1123, #560, #551). Fork synced at v0.18.0.

Expected merges: retarget to `main` after #1139 merges. #1143 (Wire UI, also on #1139) touches `crates/ui/src/egui_app/wire_page.rs`; this PR changes one line there (the op destructure gains `..`), so a trivial conflict at most. #534 (verify) and #1109 (open profile) on #1123 are not touched.

## What changed

The Wire Contour gains skim passes: a rough pass, then N skims, each naming its own machine condition (and so its own offset, wire radius + that condition's gap), with an optional direction reversal per skim.

- `operation::WireContourOp.skims: Vec<WireSkim { condition, reverse }>`; file / MCP JSON `skims: [{ condition, reverse? }]`, absent when empty (rough-only files and goldens unchanged). Edits ride `EditOperationParams` (undoable) and the existing MCP params door.
- Command door (`wire_op::condition_of`): every skim's condition resolved through #531's door, refused by name when it names none or the machine does not state it; then `motion::wire_edm::check_passes`: a pass nearer the profile than the finishing (last) pass ("would cut past the finished profile", rough included), a skim farther out than the pass before it ("would cut only air"), a skim condition with another wire diameter ("one threading cuts every pass with one wire").
- Generator: `motion::wire_edm::wire_passes` (new `skims.rs`) runs #532's single-pass generator per pass at its own offset, every law at that offset; each pass leads in from the threading point and back; a reversed skim walks clockwise. No skims is `wire_contour` exactly.
- Stamp digests each skim's condition numbers and direction (writes nothing for no skims - no stored stamp moves).
- Post stream (`posting_wire`): a mid-section `PARAM EdmCondition <skim id>` before each skim's first move (after each return to the threading point); a path that does not return once per pass is refused.
- `wire-iso.cps`: a condition that arrives with the wire threaded is the next skim's - `(SKIM n)`, the condition select and `comp_off` again at its first move; the wire stays threaded.
- Decision record: `docs/decisions/538-wire-skims.md`.

## How tested

- New golden `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/wire-iso/wire_contour_punch_skims.nc` (rough C110 + skim S21 + reversed skim S31 on #533's synthetic fixture): three distinct offsets (X-20.165 / -20.145 / -20.135), three condition selects, one thread, one cut.
- `wire_post`: `a_rough_and_two_skims_post_three_offsets_and_condition_selects`, `no_skims_is_the_rough_program_and_json_unchanged`, `skims_edit_undo_and_round_trip`, `each_skim_refusal_is_named_at_the_door`; the existing `the_punch_contour_posts_its_golden_through_the_gate` passes with #533's golden unchanged (no golden moved).
- `camcraft-motion` unit: `skims_cut_their_own_offsets_and_none_is_the_single_pass`, `skim_laws_refuse_by_name`.
- `wire_contour` suite (all 7) green; `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/issue/533-wire-iso-post` on head 0e96ca1c: motion, app (every suite - the new golden is shared input) and ui suites, 0 failed (12.4 min). `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean.

## Not exercised

- No real EDM control (D10): the fixture's conditions and codes are synthetic (three synthetic conditions S21, S31, W20 added to it).

title: feat(sim): wire EDM 2.5D verification - kerf, threading and slug laws block the post
body:
Stacked on #1139 (on #1123, #560, #551) - this diff shows their commits until they merge; merge #551, #560, #1123, #1139 first. Fork synced at v0.18.0. Not exercised on a real EDM control.

**Integration with #1139 (#533 wire post).** `issue/533-wire-iso-post` is merged into this branch (`8cd0aff6`), keeping both sides: `posting_wire.rs` holds #533's Wire Contour stream and this PR's wire clause, mounted once in `posting.rs` as `wire` with the clause re-exported; `wire_contour.rs` asserts the combined truth (the note points at the wire laws, and the wire cut streams with its condition). With a real wire post underneath, the verdict now stands between a judged cut and NC text: `wire_post::the_wire_laws_stand_between_the_cut_and_its_nc_text` (`3e852d68`) posts the clean punch through `wire-iso.cps` to #533's golden (unchanged, byte-identical) and refuses a die whose kerf burns the plate by name (`Die1: wire gouge: the kerf of move ...`), writing no NC file.

## What changed

Wire EDM verification of a 2-axis cut (#534, part of #290 D7). Every finding blocks the post; nothing is a warning.

**Laws** - `crates/sim/src/verify/wire/` (pure 2D, `judge(&WireJob) -> WireVerdict`):
- **Kerf law (gouge).** Each move's segment must stay at least the kerf offset (wire radius + spark gap, from the condition) from the product's section, and must not stand in it, at every judged height. The first move that breaks it is named with its depth, the spot, the height and how many moves gouge. The check uses exact point-to-segment distance, not an area threshold.
- **Threading law.** The start hole must be stated, the path must start at it, and the product must stand clear of it by the kerf offset at every height through the full stock height. Each failure is refused by name.
- **Slug law.** The kerf (the offset disc swept along the whole path, `Region::sweep`) is taken out of the material section (stock and part), and the connected pieces inside the cut's filled outline are the ones freed. A die whose freed piece holds part material ("the part drops") is refused, and so is a punch whose freed pieces hold none ("only waste drops"). A cut that frees nothing is refused too.
- **What "the part" is, by the stated side.** For a punch it is the model. For a die it is the model when the start hole stands outside it (a die plate with the opening as its hole). When the start hole stands inside the model, the model is the opening (#532's whole-model die) and the stock around it is the product.

**Gate** - `crates/app`:
- `operation/wire_verify.rs` gathers the inputs live, at the post. That is the cached path, the condition's offset, the side and start, and the part and stock sliced at both ends of the span the wire passes plus about every 2 mm between (at most 9 heights). The span covers the op's planes, the part and the stock, whichever reaches farthest.
- `posting_wire.rs` adds the wire clause to `verification_report`, beside the plasma clause. Every finding is a blocking problem. The not-judged line says the 3D stock sim did not run for the wire, and names the piece each cut frees: "Die1 frees 7xx mm² near X0 Y0 (waste)" or "Punch1 frees ... (the part)".
- A wire cut taken from the stock, or one with no path, is refused by name at the gate.
- The machine check's wire note no longer says verification is not built. It now points to the post's wire laws, and the one assertion in `wire_contour.rs` that read the old note was updated to match.

Decisions in `docs/decisions/534-wire-verify.md`. They cover: judged live at the post, the whole height the wire passes, exact distance rather than area, the product reading per side, threading clearance = the kerf offset, slug connectivity, and no capture/tab law until #539.

## How tested

- `camcraft-sim` lib, `verify::wire::tests` (5): `a_correct_punch_passes_and_drops_the_punch`, `a_correct_die_passes_whether_the_model_is_the_opening_or_the_plate`, `a_kerf_into_the_part_is_a_gouge_naming_the_move`, `a_missing_moved_or_crowded_start_hole_is_refused`, `the_slug_is_read_for_the_stated_side` (a punch stated on a die plate's hole, a die stated on a punch outline, and a die plate with no stock).
- `camcraft-app` `wire_verify` (3), through the commands and the gate: `a_correct_die_and_a_correct_punch_pass_and_name_the_piece_they_free`, `a_kerf_into_the_part_blocks_the_post_naming_the_move` (a 12 mm opening model in a 20 mm plate, so above the opening the wire burns the plate), `a_missing_start_hole_blocks_the_post`.
- `wire_contour` (7) still green, with the machine note's assertion updated.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/issue/532-wire-contour` on the final head `82bf9b54`: **green**, 4 steps and 0 failed (sim 19 s, motion 9 s, app 602 s for the whole suite list including `wire_contour` and `wire_verify`, ui 90 s).
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- After merging #1139: `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/issue/533-wire-iso-post` on head `3e852d68`: **green**, 4 steps, 0 failed (sim 12 s, motion 4 s, app 522 s incl. `wire_post` 5, `wire_contour` 7, `wire_verify` 3, ui 86 s); clippy -D warnings on sim/app clean.

## Not exercised

- **Not exercised on a real EDM control.** The condition is synthetic, and nothing was cut.
- On this PR alone (without #1139) there is no wire post; the integration above is what puts the verdict in front of NC text.
- Taper (#536): the laws read straight, vertical, unposed moves and refuse anything else by name. The ruled surface between planes is not judged.
- Capture/tabs (#539, D6): a correct slug passes and is named on the report line. An unsupported slug is not refused, because no capture parameter exists yet.
- A pre-drilled start hole's diameter is not modelled (the op states a point). "Too small" means the product stands within the kerf offset of the threading point.
- Only the op's source model is judged. Another model on the same setup that stands in the wire's column is not checked.
- A selection-sourced (picked-edge) wire cut was not tested through the gate.

Changelog: Wire EDM: a Wire Contour is verified at the post in 2.5D: a kerf into the part (naming the move), a missing or crowded start hole, and a slug on the wrong side (die vs punch) or a cut that frees nothing each block the post by name, and the report names the piece each cut frees (#534)

Effort: high (not escalated)

Fixes #534
