title: refactor(sim): the app holders carry stock as CarriedStock, on either engine
body:
Step E3 of #637: the app's stock holders carry stock through one engine-agnostic type, so a carried program can run on the field engine. The column engine stays the default, call for call - no shipped verdict, golden or stamp changes.

## Design answers (full text in `docs/decisions/637-carried-stock-holders.md` and the [issue comment](https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/issues/637#issuecomment-6815368088))

1. **Representation:** a transformed query frame, never a re-sample (the bake before a cut is a re-index on the origin-locked lattice). New here: the field arm builds its solid in the stock lattice's own frame (corner at the origin), so every verdict column is a field cell centre.
2. **Floor:** the lower end of the column's one material interval (`column_span`). A column cut through used to read back as air (`-inf`), which a verdict reads as "nothing to judge". It now reads the stock's own extent (top at the stock's floor, floor at the stock's top, both finite), so the column stays empty and the verdict convicts it.
3. **Clip:** the column law as a solid - the body minus the half-infinite prism above the entered stock's top over its footprint - not a plain intersection, which would delete material standing beside the new block (less material than the column engine reports).
4. **Agreement lane:** sim pins in the quick lane, an app heavy lane over the three carried suites' fixtures, and a per-thread engine switch so one process reads both.

## What changed

- **camcraft-sim:** `CarriedStock` (`Column(Body)` | `Field(Box<FieldBody>)`) in `stock_sim/carried.rs`: `carry`, `simulate`, `clip_under`, `into_body`, `deviate`. `FieldBody::body` (`carried_read.rs`) reads the field back onto the column `Body`, so `deviate`, `display`, `volume` and `bounds` are the column carry's own code on both arms. `clip_columns_under` is the clip loop moved out of the app.
- **camcraft-app:** `stock_sim_held.rs` holds `Held` (`Plain(Stock)` | `Carried(CarriedStock)`), `first_body` and the engine switch (`stock_sim::with_carry_engine`, `carry_engine`, env `CAMCRAFT_CARRY_ENGINE=field`). `stock_sim_carry::walk` / `judge` / `incoming_body`, `simulate_document`, `rest/across::sweep`, `rest::prior_state` and `rest::PriorPlan` go through it. The carried-body cache key takes the engine on the field arm only (the column key is unchanged).
- A cylinder stock is refused by name on the field arm (`FIELD_CARRY_SHAPE_REFUSAL`): its mesh is an inscribed polygon and would hold less than the column engine's disc at the rim.
- Old project files: nothing persisted changes.

## Tests

- `crates/sim/tests/carried_stock.rs` (6, quick lane): a block off the cell pitch on both arms - uncut, cut, carried through all 8 lattice turns and cut again, two carries with a cut between, the clip under a block and a round (then flipped and cut), a cut-through column convicted on both arms before and after a flip, degenerate field blocks refused.
- `crates/app/tests/carried_engine_agreement.rs`: heavy lane `both_engines_read_every_carried_document_alike` (`#[ignore]`, release): 14 documents mirroring `setup_carry`, `rest_across_setups` and `carried_verify`; per document the program verdict, the incoming body, the rest grid, verify's prior, the entered body and verify's bounds are read on both engines. **0 findings, max |delta| 0 on every read, 54 s in release.** A mutation check (field tops raised 1e-3) made it fail on every document, so the lane is not vacuous. Plus `the_engine_switch_is_scoped_and_defaults_to_the_column_engine` in the default lane.
- The carried suites run whole on the field arm (`CAMCRAFT_CARRY_ENGINE=field`): `setup_carry` 9/9, `rest_across_setups` 7/7, `carried_verify` 8/8, `carried_fixtures_cache` 6/6.
- Gates on head 68d317b7 (Linux): `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` green - sim suites 203 s, motion 11 s, every app suite 1009 s, 0 failed (it covers `setup_carry`, `rest_across_setups`, `carried_verify`, `carried_fixtures_cache`, `stock_sim_document`, `remachining`, `suppressed_rest`, `top_stock`, `setup_stock_source`, `stock_engine_agreement`). `cargo clippy -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean. Release heavy lanes: `carried_engine_agreement -- --ignored` 1/1 (54 s), `stock_engine_agreement -- --ignored` 3/3 (37 s).

## Not exercised / known limits

- Field arm only (not the shipped default): a cylinder stock is refused; a from-model stock is built (`FieldBody::mesh`) but no lane document uses one; ball, taper and bull-nose tools are not in the lane's documents (all flat end mills, which is why the deltas are exactly 0).
- On a cut-through column the field arm reports the gouge depth to the stock's floor, not the tool's depth below it (the column engine's number). Same class, different magnitude; the sim pin states both. No lane document cuts through.
- The field arm is slow in debug (the carried suites take 15-50 s each against under 1 s on the column arm); release is about 4 s per document.
- The operation priors (`drill_prior`, `top_stock`, `carried_stock`) still receive the read-back tops as a `Dexel` through `Columns::of_grid`; removing `Dexel` from the app is #586's remaining work, and the default flip is #589.
- No golden moved. No snapshot PNG touched. Windows and macOS not run.

Changelog: none (refactor; the column engine remains the default and every shipped verdict is unchanged).

Effort: max (not escalated). Fork synced at v0.18.0.

Refs #637

title: feat(post): generic ISO wire EDM post - codes as machine data
body:
Stacked on #1123 (on #560, #551). #551 and #560 are in rework, so this stack may need a `git merge` of the updated base later. This PR does not edit their files (`edm.rs` is untouched: the codes live on `Machine.edm_codes`).

Fork synced at v0.18.0.

## What changed

- **`assets/posts/wire-iso.cps`** ("Generic ISO Wire EDM", #290 D5). It posts the 2-axis Wire Contour in RS-274 / ISO 6983 words: `%`, G21/G20, G90, G17, the work offset, G0/G1/G2/G3 (incremental I J), M00/M01, M30. Every EDM-specific code comes from the machine's `.mch` `edm.codes`: `condition` (a template holding `{id}`), `comp_off`, and, when `edm.awt: true`, `thread`, `cut` and `tip_disposal`. Each missing code refuses the post as "machine <m> states no edm.codes.<x>". Without AWT the post writes M00 so the operator can thread the wire at the start and cut it at the end.
- **Kerf vs pre-offset path (#532's decision):** the op's moves are already the wire-centre path. The post therefore cancels compensation before every cut and never engages it, so the kerf is applied only once. The post writes no F word, because the condition sets the cutting rate.
- **Refusals by name:** a machine that is not `kind: wire_edm`, a rapid while the wire is threaded, a Z change, a posed move, an arc off the XY plane, a cycle, a tool change, a spindle speed, and a section that is not wire work.
- **post crate:**
  - `machine/edm_codes.rs` parses `edm.codes`; a garbled entry refuses the file by name.
  - The mirror and `script_props` expose `machine.kind` and `machine.edm = {codes, awt}` for EDM kinds.
  - New engine door: `PARAM EdmCondition` through a script without the `wireEdm = true` manifest flag is refused by name, so no cutting post can post a wire path.
- **app:**

title: feat(thread): external threads on a boss at the operation level
body:
Stacked on #1045 (on #1005). Fork synced at v0.18.0.

## What changed

The Thread operation cuts external threads on a boss.

- **`external` on the operation.** `OpParams::Thread { external }`: the list then holds bosses (`radius` = major radius, `entry_z` = top, `floor_z` = shoulder). File / MCP key `external`, additive, written only when set; the stamp digests it only when set, so no internal thread goes Stale.
- **Boss recognition.** `drilling::recognize_bosses`: the hole recogniser's weld, circle fit and rim-span law with the facing vote inverted (closed round upright walls facing away from their axis). Stepped walls are never folded. Detect holes (button and MCP `detect_holes`) reads bosses when the operation is external. The Thread page gets "External thread (on a boss)", "Detect bosses" and a per-row Remove (a round base is a boss too).
- **Judging a tool beside a boss, without the silhouette** (`operation::thread_boss`):
  - crest law: tangency against each boss's MINOR circle (major less 0.6134 x pitch), nothing else in the region. The drawn wall is not what the crests answer to, so a matched thread is not convicted on every helix (the #1071 flaw, not repeated);
  - root law: the solid law with the cutter narrowed by the EXTERNAL depth: roots, tip, shank, holder against the whole part, shoulder included;
  - neighbour law (new): the crest ring at full radius over the cutting length against every facet that is not the threaded boss's own wall, gouge tolerance only. The boss a run of feeds threads is read from the helix's own centre, never from nearness.
- **Air law** (`thread_entry::judge_bosses`, #992's external analogue): every position the feeds take the tool through is read in the stock the program ahead leaves; a column under the tool's disc, more than one cell outside the boss, standing above the tip refuses the thread by name (place, heights, how far out and how deep to clear). Unknown prior is refused.
- **Door** (create / edit / retool, again at generate): a boss no thicker than the thread is deep; a thread longer than the mill reaches beside a boss (shank wider than the tooth roots, or the holder); infeed against the external depth.
- **Simulation.** An external thread is swept at its external root radius (`thread_op::sim_radius`); the internal depth read 0.07 x pitch of the boss as cut and the post gate called it a gouge. Internal threads and taps unchanged.
- The kernel ride is used as #1005 pinned it; nothing in #1005 / #1045 was reworked. No bugs found in them.

## Sources

ISO 68-1 / ISO 965-1 / DIN 13 (external design root 17/24 H = 0.6134 P); Machinery's Handbook, "Thread milling"; Smid, "CNC Programming Handbook", thread milling chapter; Sutherland-Hodgman clipping and point-to-polygon distance (O'Rourke). No HSMWorks / Fusion material consulted. Decisions: `docs/decisions/985-external-threads.md`.

## How tested

- `crates/app/tests/thread_boss.rs` (11 tests): `an_external_m8_thread_verifies_clean_and_posts_helical_moves` (generator verdict, post gate and program sim clean; G02 with Z; goldens), `a_single_form_mill_threads_an_m10_boss_one_turn_per_thread`, `left_hand_and_conventional_external_threads_verify_clean_too`, `detect_reads_the_bosses_of_an_external_thread_and_holes_of_an_internal_one`, `a_boss_standing_in_uncut_stock_is_refused_by_name`, `a_part_wall_the_roughing_left_standing_in_the_sweep_is_refused`, `a_wall_inside_the_crest_rings_sweep_is_a_gouge_that_blocks_the_post`, `impossible_bosses_are_refused_when_the_operation_is_made`, `a_hole_list_read_as_bosses_never_passes_silently`, `moving_the_roughing_after_the_thread_marks_it_stale_and_refuses_it`, `the_external_flag_edits_undoes_and_round_trips_the_project_file`.
- Unit: `operation::thread_boss::tests` (7), `operation::thread_entry::tests` (3 new), `operation::thread_op::tests::an_external_thread_narrows_the_roots_by_the_external_depth`, `drilling::boss::tests` (4).
- MCP: `mcp::external_thread_milling_over_the_tools`. UI: `thread_mill_page_tests::the_geometry_tab_switches_between_holes_and_bosses_and_apply_undoes`, `a_listed_feature_can_be_removed_from_the_draft`.
- Goldens: `thread_mill_external_m8_multi_form.cl`, `nc/thread_mill_external_m8_multi_form.nc`, `thread_mill_external_m10_single_form.cl`.
- Gate: `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/issue/992-thread-undrilled` green on the final head ab0f88fa (motion, app - every app suite, since the shared thread fixtures changed - and ui suites; 12.1 min, 0 failed); `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean.

## Not exercised / left open

- No viewport pick of a boss: recognition plus Remove only. Follow-up #1132.
- A near-net or cast stock with nothing machined ahead is refused (as a cored hole is under #992). Posed (3+2) external threads are refused.
- The simulation does not draw the thread form; the boss shows at its drawn diameter.
- The neighbour law walks the facets the path's box reaches with no spatial index; not timed on a large model.
- No real machine run; NC checked by the golden and the Fanuc post only.
- `crates/app/tests/mcp.rs` (already over 400 lines) grew by one test; the camcraft-mcp skill text is not updated (process file).
- MCP: covered by the existing `add_operation` / `edit_operation` / `detect_holes` tools; no new tool.

Changelog: Thread milling cuts external threads on a boss: an External option with boss detection, refusals by name for a boss too thin, a thread past the mill's reach and stock left standing around the boss (#985)
Effort: max (no escalation)

Fixes #985

title: feat(edm): sinker rough and finish with undersize from their conditions
body:
Stacked on #1131 (→ #560 → #551). Fork synced at v0.18.0.

## What changed
- **Sinker Burn passes** (sibling ops, one electrode per op): each Sinker Burn gains `pass` (single / rough / finish; single keeps #541's law unchanged) and the finished cavity `cavity_x` / `cavity_y`.
- **Undersize law** (`motion::sinker_undersize::judge`): a rough or finish reads its condition's `undersize` and `gap` through #531's `Edm::condition` by id, after the sinker-kind check (`sinker_op::condition`, the door the gap and undersize now share). Per axis it refuses by name: electrode + 2×gap wider than the cavity (the wall would be burned past size), a finish that burns short of the cavity ("sinker finish leaves the cavity under size"), and an electrode that is not `cavity - 2×undersize`. The tip stands one undersize above the finished floor (`SinkerParams.stand`), so a rough leaves `undersize - gap` on floor and walls alike.
- **Order law**: a finish looks back (program order, same setup, unsuppressed) for the rough of the same cavity. If its undersize is not smaller, a new advisory `Warning::SinkerFinishOrder` names both numbers. It does not hold the post, because the finish's own size law already holds the cavity to size.
- Stamp digests the undersize and the rough a finish follows. DTO keys are additive and written only for rough or finish. The UI Passes tab gains the pass and the cavity X/Y.
- Decision record: `docs/decisions/543-sinker-undersize.md`.

## How tested
- `sinker_undersize.rs` (new):
  - `a_rough_finish_pair_reaches_the_finished_size_in_the_sim`: the program verdict with the box atom. After the rough, stock stands and nothing is gouged. After the finish, `dev.is_clean()`. Writes golden `sinker_rough_finish_pair.cl`.
  - `a_finish_that_leaves_the_cavity_under_size_is_refused_by_name`: under size, wrong electrode, overburn, no undersize and no cavity are each refused.
  - `a_finish_no_smaller_in_undersize_than_its_rough_is_warned_by_name`
  - `a_rough_finish_pair_round_trips_the_file`
  - `the_rough_finish_pair_is_driven_over_mcp_with_the_gui_commands`: add_operation, edit_operation, generate and undo. No new MCP tool is needed.
- `motion::sinker_undersize::tests::sinker_undersize_judges_rough_and_finish` (unit).
- Quick gate, run locally: sim lib, motion lib, app lib plus sinker_burn, sinker_undersize, mcp, warned_moves, verify, project_roundtrip, operations, edm_conditions, edm_machine, stock_stamp, commands_undo, ribbon and tool_law. Also ui lib and ui operations. All green. `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -D warnings` is clean.

title: fix(motion): the plan's crossing check reads a shared end a rounding apart as a touch
body:
## What changed

The adaptive planner's own self-crossing check (`crates/motion/src/machining2d/adaptive/guard.rs`, the `scan` behind `first_crossing` / `crossing_pairs`) asks a new pair predicate, `crosses`, instead of the exact-sign `proper`.

- `crosses` is the same proper-crossing (orientation) test, with one change. A chord end within `TOUCH` = **1e-9 mm** (1 pm) of the other chord's line counts as *on* it (sign 0), where only an exact zero did before. Two chords cross only when each one's ends stand strictly on opposite sides of the other's line. The test compares `|orient| <= TOUCH * |ab|`, with no division.
- So a shared end point a rounding apart is read the way an exact shared vertex always was: a contact, not a crossing. That covers an orbit closing a ulp off its start (#980's seam), a microlift return landing on a chord end, and a ring starting on the last ring's vertex. A real crossing still crosses.
- A non-finite point (NaN, +-inf) in any walk now reads as a crossing at that point (its walk paired with itself). Before, the length filter dropped NaN chords silently, and the bounds check looked only at x, so an infinite y slipped through.
- `guard::proper` is unchanged: `lift_link` uses it for its own link law, which this PR leaves alone (#1080 touches it).
- Only `guard.rs` changed, plus the new `guard_tests.rs` (pulled in with `#[path]`, so `mod.rs` is untouched), plus the decision file. No overlap with #953 or #1080.

### The tolerance and why
f64 rounding on a 10 m workspace is ~2e-12 mm per coordinate, so 1 pm sits about 1000x above it. Cutting tolerances are microns (the verifier's is 0.005 mm), about 1e6x above it. A chord end within 1 pm of a line can only meet the other chord at that end, so nothing a tool could cut hides inside it. The full reasoning is in `docs/decisions/1048-guard-shared-ends.md`.

### Changed from the brief: contacts are not crossings
The first version excused only shared ends and treated T-touches and collinear overlaps as crossings. That failed the pinned `adaptive::tests::a_channel_is_grown_as_one_spiral_that_never_crosses`: in the lifted plan, pass 197 retraces pass 196's last chords exactly (32 chord pairs on the same line, same direction). The exact-sign law always read that as a contact (orient 0), and so does the verifier's law (a). A stricter check would send a good adaptive plan to Offset rings, the very loss this issue is about. The fix is therefore the old law with its exact zero widened to `TOUCH`. Whatever contact it accepted exactly, it now also accepts a rounding off. This is pinned and recorded in the decision file.

## Tests (pins, `crates/motion/src/machining2d/adaptive/guard_tests.rs`)
- `a_figure_eight_crosses_and_a_spiral_does_not` (moved from guard.rs, unchanged)
- `a_spiral_returning_to_its_seed_within_rounding_does_not_cross`: jitters of 1e-15 and 1e-12 mm in 8 directions
- `a_return_landing_on_a_chord_end_does_not_cross`
- `a_ring_starting_on_the_previous_rings_vertex_does_not_cross`

  Each of these three also asserts that the old exact-sign `proper` tripped on at least one of its jitters, so the knife edge is really exercised.
- `a_real_crossing_near_a_shared_point_still_crosses`: a chord crossing 0.15 mm past a shared vertex, and a vertex a micron through the chord
- `a_contact_is_no_crossing_and_a_micron_past_is`: the decided case. T-touches exactly on the chord, at ±1e-12 and at 5e-10 mm, a collinear overlap and a retraced chord are not crossings. A vertex 1e-6 mm past the chord is.
- `a_non_finite_point_reads_as_a_crossing`: NaN and ±inf in x or y
- `the_bucketed_scan_agrees_with_all_pairs`: 40 rounds of random walks that reuse each other's vertices 1e-12 apart, comparing the grid scan with the all-pairs predicate

## Effect on the planner, goldens
No golden moved. `golden_cl` passes, and no golden file is in the diff. No fixture changed from Offset rings to adaptive or back in the suites run below. `a_channel_is_grown_as_one_spiral_that_never_crosses` still asserts `first_crossing(&pl.passes).is_none()` on its plan.

## Gates (Linux x86_64, final head)
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: ok (motion lib + adaptive_band, adaptive_hsm, adaptive_orbit_seam, pocket3d_hsm), 1.1 min
- By hand, debug: motion lib (197 passed), machining2d 66, rotary_adaptive 2, offset_shells 6, tiny_step 3, adaptive_hsm 1, adaptive_orbit_seam 1, pocket3d_hsm 3. App: golden_cl 25, conformance 6, shoulder_adaptive 3, roughing2d 7, whole_model_pocket 5, pocket3d_hsm 1, pick_agnostic 5. All green.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean
- Heavy pins (release `--ignored`): all green and none moved. motion adaptive_hsm (5, the M11.4 C metric report and the island budget pin included), motion pocket3d_hsm `the_stepped_block_holds_the_planner_laws_level_by_level`, motion rotary_adaptive (3), motion offset_shells (1), and app pocket3d_hsm `the_users_bore_roughs_adaptive_level_by_level_and_verifies_clean` (272 s; its pinned counts and verify-clean hold)

## Not exercised
- Windows and macOS (the predicate is plain f64 arithmetic, the same on every platform. The plan differences of #1010 come from elsewhere)
- The UI and snapshot lanes (nothing in them is touched)

## Left open
- #1129 (filed): the verifier's law (a) (`sim/verify/laws.rs`, `proper_cross`) is still exact-sign. A plan with an end shared a rounding apart, which the planner now accepts, could still read as crossing there and hold the post. Still safe (refused by name), but the two laws should agree.

Changelog: The Adaptive (HSM) planner no longer reads two walks that meet at one point, a rounding apart, as crossing itself, so such a level keeps its adaptive plan instead of falling back to Offset rings (#1048)

Effort: high (no escalation)

Fork synced at v0.18.0

Fixes #1048

title: fix(posting): the index swing judges the swept work against the standing steel
body:
Fork synced at v0.18.0. Not stacked: branched from upstream main (see "Subplate" below).

## What changed
The index-swing clause judged only the tool against the work the rotary sweeps. It now has a second half, `crates/app/src/posting_swing_standing.rs`, which judges the swept work (stock, parts, the fixtures that turn with it) against what stands still:
- **The face the rotary stands on.** The machine file has a new optional key on a work-turning rotary, `axis_to_table`: the rotary's centre height over its own mounting face. `crates/post/src/machine/swing.rs` reads it by the same law as `nose_to_axis`: unstated reads as unstated, garbled input is refused by name. The microARC 4 states 3.15 in (Tormach 4th-axis comparison sheet). If the swept radius plus 5 mm reaches that face, the post is refused, and the message names the op, the index (`A90.000`), the swept radius, the figure and the clearance.
- **Fixed fixtures over the work's X span.** Each is judged by its bounding box's distance from the A line in YZ. A strike is refused as "standing fixture <name>". Steel that sits wholly beside the work in X is clear.
- **What it cannot judge is named, never silent.** A machine with no `axis_to_table`, a fixed fixture with no facets or non-finite facets, and a fixed fixture whose box reaches across the centerline over the work (a tailstock, the rotary's own body) are listed in the gate's not-judged line: `index swing did not judge the work against the standing steel: ...`. That line reaches the status line, the viewer header and the script result through `GateReport::not_judged`.
- `posting_index_swing.rs`: `swept_radius` becomes `swept` (it returns the radius plus the X span). `work_a` and `index_angle` are now shared with the new clause. The tool half's behaviour is unchanged.
- The microARC tester-kit project carries the new figure (80.01 mm). `assets/machines/AGENTS.md` documents the key.
- Decision file: `docs/decisions/1107-swing-work-vs-standing.md`.

**Subplate (#1082).** Not stacked on #1082. A table, plate or subplate under the rotary raises the centerline along with the rotary, so the nearest standing face under the rotary is always its own centre height below the line, whatever the stack. #1082's subplate is covered by this law without reading its stack model. Steel beside the rotary that reaches under the work is judged once it is modelled as a fixed fixture.

## How tested
Pinning tests in `crates/app/tests/index_swing.rs` (13 pass: 9 existing, unchanged, plus 4 new):
- `work_swinging_into_the_face_the_rotary_stands_on_is_refused_by_name`: the bar on a rotary 2 mm inside the margin is refused by name and the post writes nothing. The same bar with 2 mm to spare passes.
- `a_standing_fixture_under_the_work_is_judged_by_its_distance_from_the_line`: a low plate under the bar clears, a block beside the bar in X clears, and a riser 15 mm under the line is refused by name.
- `standing_steel_the_swing_cannot_read_is_named_not_judged`: with no `axis_to_table` the program posts and the gap is named. A tailstock across the line is named too.
- `the_shipped_microarc_states_its_centre_height_over_the_table`.
- Post unit test `nose_to_axis_reads_scaled_or_refuses_by_name` is extended to `axis_to_table`.

Gate: `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` on the head 5716d312: green (post suites and 98 app suites plus lib, 4.1 min, 0 failed). `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-post --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

## Not exercised
- The GUI by hand.
- A real long part on hardware.
- Per-angle swings: the swing is judged over the full turn, like the tool half.
- Fixtures that are not boxes are judged by their bounding box, which is conservative.
- The release lanes.

Changelog: The index swing now refuses a post when the work it sweeps would strike the face the rotary stands on or a standing fixture; machine files state the rotary's centre height as `axis_to_table` (microARC 4: 3.15 in), and steel it cannot judge is named (#1107)

Effort: high (no escalation)

Fixes #1107

title: feat(edm): sinker burn to depth with a single electrode
body:
#560 and #551 are merged into upstream main; this branch merges upstream/main. Fork synced at v0.18.0.

## What changed
- **Electrode as a tool** (`ToolKind::Electrode`, `crates/tools/src/electrode.rs`). It reuses the existing `Tool` fields: `diameter` = face X, `width` = face Y, `flute_len` = length below the holder, `shank_len` = pickup offset. rpm 0 and a sharp face are required by law. A garbled electrode is refused by name at AddTool / ChangeTool / the library reader. `EDM-E10X6` joins the starter catalog, and the project file round-trips the kind.
- **Sinker Burn op** (`OpType::SinkerBurn`, tag 41, `Section::Sinker`, `Family::Sinker`). It is admitted only on a `sinker_edm` machine; on any other machine the family door refuses it by name. Milling ops on a sinker stay refused (#530). Only an electrode mounts it.
- **Depth from a stated datum.** The datum is the work top, the cavity floor (a stand-off) or the electrode tip at the approach plane. A burn past the cavity floor datum, past the model's floor, or deeper than the electrode is long is refused by name (`crates/motion/src/sinker.rs`).
- **Spark gap** (coordinator note from #560's review). The op names a condition id, which is required. The command checks that the setup's machine is a sinker EDM, then asks `Edm::condition` for `ConditionField::Gap` only, never a wire field. Lookup is by id only, never by role. The tip stops one gap above the floor. The op's stamp digests the resolved gap, so a re-stated condition marks the op stale.
- **CL**: an approach rapid, one feed plunge and a rapid retract. Golden: `crates/app/tests/golden/sinker_burn_cavity.cl`.
- **Stock-sim verification** (#290 D7). A new column-engine **box atom** (`crates/sim/src/stock_sim/dexel_box.rs`, `simulate_box`) sweeps the face grown by the gap and is exact per column. The program verdict (`simulate_document`, carry walk) cuts sinker ops with it. The field eye (stock view and playback) refuses an electrode program by name; it has no box atom yet. Rest masks count an electrode as removing nothing, which is the safe side.
- **UI**: a minimal Sinker Burn op page (`sinker_page.rs`) keeps the tab law and edits through `EditOperationParams`. The full sinker pages are #548. The tool editor gains an electrode X/Y row.
- **MCP**: no new tool is needed. `add_tool` (definition), `add_operation` (kind "Sinker Burn"), `edit_operation`, `generate` and `undo` drive the same undoable commands, and a test pins this.
- **Posting**: refused. #542 owns the sinker post (#533 the wire). `post_serves` is only the picker's listing law, so the post door itself refuses: `posting_family::edm_at_post`, called by every writer (`post_setup`/`post_script` via `post_script_body`, the per-mount `post_each` and the per-op writer) right after `op_streams`, refuses any program whose setup's machine is a wire or sinker EDM by name ("Setup1: no post for a sinker EDM machine yet (#542) - Burn0 is not posted and no file is written; ...") before a byte is written. The MCP `post` tool and the script `post` verb ride the same writers. Pinned by `sinker_burn_held::the_post_refuses_a_burn_on_its_sinker_until_an_edm_dialect_ships` and the MCP leg of `sinker_burn::the_sinker_burn_is_driven_over_mcp_with_the_gui_commands`.
- Decisions: `docs/decisions/541-sinker-burn-depth.md`.

## How tested
- Pinning tests in `crates/app/tests/sinker_burn.rs`:

title: feat(edm): 2-axis wire contour op - kerf offset to a stated punch/die side, start hole, corner refusal
body:
**Stacked on #560 (on #551) - this diff shows their commits until they merge; merge #551, #560 first.** This PR adds three commits on top of #560's head (`f5d8c06a`) and two merges of `origin/main` (no conflicts). Not exercised on a real EDM control.

## What changed

The first wire EDM operation (#532, part of #290; decisions D1, D2, D4, D8): **Wire Contour**, a vertical cut of one closed profile.

**Generator** - `crates/motion/src/wire_edm/` (beside the other 2D generators, on the existing offsetter):
- The wire-centre path is the profile's parallel at the **kerf offset = wire radius + the condition's spark gap**, on the **stated** side: inside the profile for a `die`, outside it for a `punch`. The side is never inferred.
- A straight lead-in runs from the stated **start hole / threading point** to the nearest point of the path; the profile is cut counter-clockwise; the lead-out retraces the lead-in.
- **Corner minimum:** an inside corner, slot, notch or neck the wire cannot cut (tighter than wire radius + gap) is refused by name with its spot and the minimum radius. Outside corners are mitred, so the wire never comes nearer than the offset.
- Refused by name, never trimmed: no start hole, a start hole on the product's side or nearer than the offset, an open profile, several profiles, a crossing or area-less ring, a profile smaller than the wire.
- The moves ride the lower programmed plane and state **no pose and no feed** (D2: it posts as XY; the control's generator sets the rate).

**Operation** - `crates/app`:
- `OpType::WireContour` (stored id 41, appended), its own **Wire EDM** section and family, admitted on a `wire_edm` machine only.
- Created and edited through `CreateOperation` / `EditOperationParams` (also paste and retype). At the command door, **a missing condition, gap or wire diameter is refused by name** through #531's `Edm::condition`.
- **A wire cut mounts no library tool.** Its wire diameter and gap come from the machine's condition table, their only source; a wire cut that names a tool is refused. The stamp digests the condition, so an edited table re-marks the cut Stale.
- The machine check on a wire EDM judges X/Y travel and names what it does not judge. The program gate refuses a wire cut by name until a wire post exists (#533).
- The op rides the project file (`wire_contour { top_z, bottom_z, condition, side, start }`). `side` has no default: a file or patch without it is refused.

`crates/ui` gains the match arms the new kind forces and a **minimal page** (`wire_page.rs`: side and start hole on Geometry, the two planes on Heights, the machine's conditions to choose from on Passes; no Feeds tab) - the UI's registry-wide tab law fails a kind whose tabs draw nothing. The ribbon's quick-add names no tool for a kind that mounts none, and its tip names a wire EDM as the machine wire work needs. No new icon; the real page, viewport picking of the start hole and the ribbon on a wire EDM document are #535.

Decisions the umbrella left open are in `docs/decisions/532-wire-contour.md` (no library tool, mitred outside corners, the 2 um cover tolerance, no arc fitting, lead shape, where each refusal stands, no CL format change).

## Readings

Synthetic condition `C110` (from no machine's manual): wire 0.250 mm, gap 0.040 mm. Profile: 40 x 20 mm, 2 mm corners in 3-degree facets.

| | wire-centre path, top side | distance to the profile |
|---|---|---|
| die | y = 9.835 | 0.165 inside |
| punch | y = 10.165 | 0.165 outside |
| apart | 0.330 | = kerf width (0.25 + 2 x 0.04) |

- On the straight sides the paths stand at the offset to 1e-9 mm in the motion test and 1e-6 mm through the commands (the model's silhouette in between). The nearest any path vertex comes to the profile is the offset to 1e-6 mm; the farthest is under 0.2 um past it (a 3-degree facet's mitre).
- A sharp 40 x 20 rectangle as a die: refused, "minimum inside radius is 0.1650 mm (wire radius 0.1250 + spark gap 0.0400)". The same rectangle as a punch: cut, with sharp path corners at (20.165, 10.165). A 0.1 mm fillet as a die: refused; a 0.2 mm fillet: cut.

## How tested

- `camcraft-motion` lib, `wire_edm::tests` (5): `a_die_and_a_punch_on_one_profile_stand_apart_by_exactly_the_kerf`, `a_corner_tighter_than_the_wire_is_refused_by_name`, `a_missing_or_misplaced_start_hole_is_refused_by_name`, `degenerate_profiles_and_numbers_are_refused_by_name`, `the_moves_ride_one_plane_with_no_pose_from_and_to_the_start_hole`.
- `camcraft-app` `wire_contour` (7): the family door both ways and no tool; the condition door at creation and edit; die and punch apart by the kerf through the commands, the machine check and the post's refusal; the corner and start-hole refusals at generation; the stamp reading the condition; undo / redo; the project round trip and the undefaulted side.
- `golden_cl`: `wire_contour_die_and_punch_match_golden` with `tests/golden/wire_contour_die.cl` and `wire_contour_punch.cl` (LF).
- `tool_law`: `every_kind_names_a_tool_set` now states the one exception (the wire family mounts none).
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main` on the final head `13a12a25`: **green** - post, motion (195 passed), app (the whole suite, 285 test results, because a golden changed), ui (lib and 7 suites). The parents' `edm_machine` (7) and `edm_conditions` (6), `operations` (117) and `golden_cl` (26) are in that run.
- The first gate run was red: three registry pins (the kind count, two ribbon rows), the empty-rack tool refusal test, the UI tab law and the UI tip table. All were the new kind meeting laws that walk every kind; fixed in `cded9490`, and the second run is the green one.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

## Not exercised

- **Not exercised on a real EDM control.** The condition is synthetic; nothing here was cut.
- No wire post exists (#533), so no NC was written; the program gate refuses a wire cut by name.
- No verification of the wire against the part, the slug or the start hole's clearance (#534). The generator certifies only its own two laws (no move nearer the profile than the offset; no profile point the kerf misses).
- The page was only drawn by the registry-wide tab law test (every tab draws, one tab per field); no test clicks through it, and it was not looked at in the running app. On a wire EDM document the ribbon's Wire Contour cell creates a draft that the door refuses until a condition is named, and with an empty tool library the cell is disabled ("No tool yet") although the kind needs none - both #535.
- A picked-edge profile (a selection source) is wired the way the plasma profile's is but was only tested from a whole model's silhouette.
- A wire cut on a setup with an aligned part, carried stock or fixtures was not tested.

## Follow-ups filed

- #1108 `MCP: wire contour op` - `add_operation` requires a non-empty `tool`, and no headless way mounts a wire EDM with conditions yet, so the op is not reachable over MCP in this PR.
- #1109 open-profile contour (a cut-off or slot from the stock edge) - refused by name here.
- #1110 program sim, setup sheet and tool list still read a wire cut's empty tool name.

Changelog: Wire EDM: a Wire Contour operation cuts one closed profile at the kerf offset of the machine's condition (wire radius + spark gap), on a stated die or punch side, from a stated start hole; a corner the wire cannot cut and a missing start hole are refused by name (#532)

Effort: max (not escalated)

Fixes #532

title: feat(app): work offsets post as an index bounded by the setup's own post (#931 slice 2)
body:
## What changed (slice 2 of 3: app)

Stacked on #1101 (slice 1), which stacks on #945. Fork synced at v0.18.0. Effort: high.

The app now hands the post the setup's 1-based work-offset index, not a word. The setup's own post sets the limit; core keeps only a sanity bound.

- **The stream carries the index.** `camcraft_post::post::Dump::wcs` is now a `u32`, where 1 is the first offset. `posting::wcs_context` returns `(index, origin)`. The post writes the word.
- **No fallback (triage point 2).** `setup::work_offset` no longer filters the stored pick. If a setup's post cannot express the stored offset, the offset is still never read as offset 1 or G54. That holds for the stream, the travel check, the label and the setup sheet.
- **Post-time gate.** New `setup_offsets::range_problems`, part of `verification_report`, so it applies to the single-file, per-mount and per-op posts. It checks each setup that has an operation against that setup's own post (`setup_mount::post_of`). An offset the post cannot express blocks the post, naming the setup and the post. Slice 1's engine refusal still runs behind it.
- **Command-time check.** `SetSetupWorkOffset::new` checks the pick against the setup's post (`setup_offsets::check`) and refuses by name.
- **Loader.** The six-offset cap is removed from `project/apply.rs`. Only the sanity bound remains (pick 0..=254, the `u8` that the height digest stores).
- **Names.** New `setup::work_offset_names(world, setup)` reads slice 1's `work_offsets(cps)` table. It is cached per (resolved post, script text) in a bounded map. `setup::offset_name`, `setup::wcs_name` and `setup::wcs_label` use it, and so do the setup sheet, the refusal texts, the spindle-law text and the shared-offset clause. The names are for display only and never go into the stream.
- **File format.** Offsets 1-6 are still saved as `G54`..`G59`, so existing files round-trip byte-identical. Offsets 7 and up are saved as their number. **Builds older than this one cannot open a file that uses offset 7 or higher.** The decision file records this for the release notes (point 8).
- **`WCS_SLOTS` is split (point 1).** It is now a crate-private `LEGACY_WCS_NAMES`, used only for legacy entity-name reservations and the pre-v52 and pre-v54 migrations. All of its word uses are gone.
- **`shared_word_problems` (point 7)** compares offset indexes and names the offset by the post's name.
- **UI and MCP** keep working through the app functions. The Setups combo still lists offsets 1-6, now named by the setup's post. MCP still accepts the words G54-G59. Slice 3 changes the combo and adds MCP's `index`.

## How tested

- Pinning tests in `crates/app/tests/wcs_index.rs`:
  - `offset_nine_on_a_six_offset_post_refuses_by_setup_name_and_never_posts_at_offset_one` (the no-fallback pin)
  - `the_command_refuses_an_offset_the_setups_post_cannot_express`
  - `the_setups_post_names_its_offsets`
  - `offset_seven_and_up_saves_as_its_number_and_reloads`
- Unit test: `project::wcs_pick::tests::legacy_words_and_numbers_round_trip`.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` is green on 671ccd19: post suites, about 250 app suites including `wcs_index`, `setup_wcs`, `posting`, `probe_*`, `project_roundtrip` and `conformance`, the ui lib plus 11 ui suites. Wall time 9.6 min.
- I also ran 23 golden and post suites that the quick gate does not pick, including `golden_cl`, `carvera_post`, `heidenhain_*`, `tormach_post` and `lathe_post_*`. All pass, and no golden file changed.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui -p camcraft-post --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean.

## Not exercised

- No GUI hand check and no Hub run. The combo is unchanged apart from where its names come from.
- A user `.cps` file post with extended offsets was not tried by hand. It goes through the same cache path as the built-in posts.

Waits on #1101's Hub run. Like #1101, it merges at the next cut.

Decisions: `docs/decisions/931-wcs-index-app.md`.

Changelog: Work offsets are an index whose limit and names come from each setup's post. An offset the post cannot express is refused by setup name instead of posting at G54. Offsets 7 and up are saved as their number, and older builds cannot open those files. (#931)

Refs #931

title: feat(tools): .camtools carries the tool body; "Import tool holders" toggle
body:
## What changed

- **Format (`crates/app/src/tool_library.rs`)**: a `.camtools` tool's `definition` may carry `body`, the same `ToolBodyDto` a `.camproj` tool stores (a drawn holder profile, a placed mesh, or a lathe holder). The key is additive: `camcraft-tools/1` stays, files without it read unchanged, and older builds ignore it. Export writes the body of every tool that has one. On read, a body is checked the way the project loader checks one: `ToolBodyDto::to_body` re-derives it and `tool_body::fits` must accept it. If either refuses, the whole file is refused and the tool is named. The clean-room note stays as it was.
- **Command (`commands/tool_import.rs`)**: `ImportTools::with_holders(world, library, holders)` is still one undoable command. `ImportTools::new` is the same call with holders on. With holders on, each body is checked again at command creation. With holders off, every tool lands bare (holder cylinder only). The duplicate and rename rules are unchanged. The body counts toward "identical" only when one lands: a bare library tool matches the document's tool on its record alone, as before, and a tool that lands with a body must match the body too, otherwise it arrives as "Name (2)". `ImportReport` gains `holders` and `holders_left_out`, and both appear on the status line.
- **UI (Tool library page)**: an "Import tool holders" checkbox next to Import library, ticked by default. It is passed to the command as its `holders` parameter and remembered per user in the prefs file (`importToolHolders`, written only when off), the same way as #877. It is not project state and not on the history.
- **MCP**: `import_tool_library` takes an optional `holders` boolean (default true). The schema and description are updated, and the reply adds `holders` and `holders_left_out`. The script verb `cam.importTools(path)` keeps its arity (holders on).
- **Process**: the `import_tool_library` line in the camcraft-mcp skill is updated, so `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION` goes 16 -> 17. Other open process PRs also claim 17-20; whichever merges later takes the next number when it merges main.
- Decision file: `docs/decisions/889-camtools-holder-body.md`.

## How tested (local, macOS, debug, sccache; fork synced at v0.18.0)

Pinning tests:
- `crates/app/tests/tool_library_holders.rs` (new, 5 tests):
  - `export_import_with_holders_is_byte_stable` covers a drawn BT30 ER20 body and a mesh body; export -> import -> export gives identical bytes and the bodies are bit-identical.
  - `holders_off_lands_every_tool_bare_and_undo_restores`
  - `a_malformed_or_ill_fitting_body_refuses_the_file_by_name` covers a non-body, a bad outline, a mesh with no placement, and flutes running into the holder; nothing is applied and nothing goes on the history.
  - `a_file_without_bodies_imports_as_before_and_the_skip_reads_bodies_only_when_one_lands`
  - `mcp_import_tool_library_takes_the_holders_flag` covers the schema, off, the default on, the round trip over MCP, and refusal of a non-boolean.
- `crates/app/tests/view_prefs.rs`: `the_tool_holder_import_choice_survives_a_restart`
- `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests/tool_library_import.rs`: `the_toggle_stands_on_the_page_ticked_and_is_remembered_per_user` (AccessKit CheckBox role and toggled state, prefs written, not dirty) and `unticked_imports_bare_ticked_takes_the_holder_and_undo_restores`.

Suites, all green:

|---|---|
| tool_library | 13 |
| tool_library_holders | 5 |
| view_prefs | 7 |
| holder_library | 11 |
| tool_body | 12 |
| tool_body_bands | 13 |
| tool_body_judged | 8 |

title: fix(thread): a matched thread mill verifies clean - the gouge laws read its major circle
body:
#1071: a Thread op's helix runs the thread depth H = 0.5413 x pitch past the declared hole, which is the thread's minor circle (what CAD draws of a tapped hole), by design (`machining2d::thread_mill`). The verify read that hole as a wall the cutter must keep `r` from, so every matched thread mill was blocked.

That covered the stock source too, which the issue thought was unaffected: the same thread from `SrcRef::Stock` had 52 gouges and 21 crossing pairs. `mill2d_c` never asserted the warnings, so no thread mill could post from any source.

Fork synced at v0.18.0, PROCESS_VERSION 29; merged with upstream main at 62a2c93a (head ea76d5df).

## What changed

Three laws convicted a matched thread, and each is fixed narrowly.

- **Law (b), the rim.** The Thread arm now moves each declared hole's rim out to the major circle (declared radius + H), after the region is built (`material_source::major_rims`). This covers every source and the area-controlled region. A loop that is the hole's minor rim (ours, or the model's own for a through hole) gives way to it; every other wall stays.
- **The containment solid law.** It read the model's minor wall, and the face the hole opens through, as part to keep. A new `sim::verify::thread_bore` (and `solid_hits_threaded`) excuses a hit only when both of these hold:
  - the facet is the thread's own material: the minor wall (near-vertical, every vertex on the declared circle within max(2 % r, 0.1 mm)), or a facet with a vertex on that circle lying wholly at or above the hole's entry (the mouth);
  - the swept cutter stays inside the major cylinder: the farther tip end's radius plus the atom's radius is at most the major radius plus the allowance.

  Floors, walls of another radius, other holes and any cut past the major circle still convict. `solid_hits` is unchanged: it calls the threaded form with no bores.

  **Since the review of f122474d:** the band only RECOGNISES the wall. The cap reads the hit facet's own radius about the axis (its nearest on-circle vertex) plus the thread depth plus the allowance, not the declared major circle. A hole declared wider than, or off the centre of, the model's hole by more than the allowance now convicts. `major_rims` likewise grows a through hole's major circle from the model's own rim loop when that stands nearer than the declared circle.
  **Since the review of 434a464a:** the wall is measured at the facet's (or rim loop's) nearest point to the axis, not its nearest vertex. A chord between two on-circle vertices dips inside the circle.
  - That nearest point must itself be on the band, so a D-bore's flat, a coarse polygon's side, or a step reaching inside the mouth is never the thread's material.
  - The wall stands at that point, credited at most `CHORD_CREDIT` (the sim's `DEV_TOL`, 0.01 mm) toward its nearest vertex. That is tessellation of a round hole: the STEP importer meshes at half of it.
  - `major_rims` reads the same way. It moved with `thread_bores` into `operation/thread_rims.rs`, so `material_source.rs` stays at main's 350 lines.
- **Law (a), crossings.** The retract runs the ride backwards at feed. The reversed arcs put their chord joints a last bit off their twins, and `proper_cross` excused a touch only at an exactly zero orientation. So each shared joint, and each collinear overlap, read as a crossing.

  Now chords that only touch (an endpoint within 1 nm of the other chord's line) are no crossing. A real crossing keeps every endpoint off the other line. This is the one change that reaches every operation's verify, so the whole batch tier was run (below). A parallel-only guard was tried first: it removed 5 of the 21 pairs, and the rest were the joint touches.
- Two functions now take eight arguments (`SolidIndex::hits`, `contain_into`). They carry `#[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]` with a reason, as ten others in `sim` already do.
- Decision record: `docs/decisions/1071-thread-mill-rim.md`.

## How it was tested

New pinning tests:
- `crates/app/tests/thread_mill_rim.rs` (a 6 mm Tap-form thread mill, pitch 1, model-sourced unless named):
  - `a_matched_thread_mill_in_air_verifies_clean`: the issue's cavity fixture (#1073's block). Before the fix: 52 gouges and 21 crossing pairs.
  - `a_matched_thread_mill_in_a_drilled_hole_verifies_clean`: a block with a real r 5 blind hole, 96-gon. Before the fix: the gouges came back from the solid law at the wall and the mouth.
  - `a_stock_sourced_thread_mill_verifies_clean_too`.
  - `a_thread_whose_major_circle_reaches_a_wall_convicts`: the major circle is 0.24 mm into the cavity wall; the minor circle is clear of it.
  - `a_thread_declared_wider_than_the_models_hole_convicts`: the model drilled r 4.5, declared r 5.
  - `a_thread_taken_below_the_models_hole_floor_convicts`: floor declared at Z 9, model floor at Z 10.
  - `a_declared_hole_wider_than_the_models_by_a_hair_convicts` (review round): r 5.05 / 5.1 on r 5, r 15.25 on r 15, and a through hole. It failed on f122474d.
  - `a_declared_hole_off_the_models_centre_by_a_hair_convicts` (review round): centres 0.05 / 0.1 / 0.28 mm off, blind and through. It failed on f122474d.
  - `a_matched_thread_stays_clean_at_other_sizes_and_through` (review round): matched r 15, a matched through hole, and a 5 um off-centre declaration.
  - `a_flat_whose_corners_stand_on_the_circle_convicts` (third review): a D-bore (flat from (3, 4) to (-3, 4)), an octagon and a 16-gon on r 5, and a through octagon. The D-bore verified with no warning on 434a464a, which was checked.
  - `a_fine_polygon_bore_still_verifies_clean` (third review): 48 and 96 sides on r 5.
- `sim::verify::thread_bore` unit tests: `a_flat_between_on_circle_corners_is_not_the_wall`, `a_tessellated_round_wall_reads_its_circle_and_a_coarse_one_its_chord`, `a_step_reaching_inside_the_mouth_is_not_the_mouth`.
- `crates/sim/tests/crossing_retrace.rs`:
  - `a_helix_run_back_over_its_own_trace_is_no_crossing`: three ride/retrace shapes, all-pairs and bucketed. It fails with the touch guard removed, which was checked.
  - `a_real_crossing_still_reads_as_one_at_any_angle`: 90 degrees down to 0.001 rad.

Gates:
- On the head ea76d5df (the third review's fix, merged with upstream main 62a2c93a):
  - `cargo test -p camcraft-sim`: every binary green (lib 89).
  - app `thread_mill_rim` 11, `verify` 21 (2 ignored), `mill2d_c` 9, `solid_law` 4, `solid_law_goldens` 5, `golden_cl` 25, `drill_prior` 12, `verify_arc_reading` 7, `bore_entry` 3, `bore_facet_sagitta` 2, `coarse_contain` 1, `ladder_entry_height` 4: all pass.
  - `cargo clippy -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- Review round 2, on the head 434a464a (upstream main 0fc30b65 merged cleanly, plus `turning: None` in the `thread_mill()` fixture for main's new `Tool.turning`, e1fc569a):
  - `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test thread_mill_rim`: 9 passed.
  - `cargo test -p camcraft-sim --test crossing_retrace --test crossing_buckets`: 2 + 3 passed. `cargo test -p camcraft-sim --lib`: 86 passed.
  - `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test verify --test mill2d_c --test solid_law --test solid_law_goldens --test golden_cl --test drill_prior`: 21 (2 ignored) + 9 + 4 + 5 + 25 + 12 passed, 0 failed.
  - `cargo clippy -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- On the head d9b36d6a (the review fix, merged with upstream main c8a1bab1):
  - `cargo xtask gate batch`: geometry, cl, tools, sim, motion and ui green. The post step (`script_tormach_plasma`) and the app and clippy steps fail on main's own breaks, #1146: stale recorded plasma refusals, and the missing `Cutter::neck` field in `rotary_law_tests.rs`, which stops the app lib tests from compiling. This PR touches neither.
  - Because of that, every app integration suite was run separately: `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test '*'`. Result: 297 suites, 2067 passed, 0 failed, 18 ignored.
  - `cargo clippy -p camcraft-sim --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --lib --test '*' -- -D warnings`: clean.
- Before the review round:
  - `cargo xtask gate batch` on c770b35c (18.3 min): every test suite green.
  - geometry, cl, tools, post, sim (with `crossing_buckets`), motion (slow suites included), app (`center_cut_multiaxis` included), ui.
  - clippy failed only on the two eight-argument functions. With the `#[allow]` (head commit), `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean.
- On the head, both pinning suites were rerun: green.
- No snapshot PNG touched.

## Not exercised

- No posted thread program was run on a machine or simulator.
- The thread flanks are not modelled: the whole minor-to-major annulus is read as removable (#986 owns the form).
- A tilted-frame (indexed) thread uses the same code path, but no test pins it.
- #1073's `coarse_rims::a_thread_mill_reads_the_same_near_the_bound_as_at_full_fidelity` lives on that open PR. When both land it can tighten to `== Vec::new()`, as #1071 asks.

Changelog: Thread milling: a thread mill matched to its hole verifies clean and can be posted. The gouge checks now read the thread's major circle, and the retract is no longer read as a crossing (#1071)

Effort: high (the issue's label). Not escalated.

Fixes #1071

title: test(goldens): judge the slot, trace and plasma goldens by their gates
body:
Stacked on #999 (#862): this branch is built on `issue/862-refused-program-goldens`, so until #999 merges, the diff against `main` also shows #999's commit. Fork synced at v0.18.0. Effort: high (no escalation).

## What changed
#862 added the guard `solid_law_goldens::every_posted_golden_is_a_program_the_gate_passes`, which left six posted goldens in `UNJUDGED`. Each one is now run through the gate its kind's post runs, in a new harness `crates/app/tests/posted_gates/mod.rs`. It is a support directory that only `solid_law_goldens` declares, like `area_support/`.

| Golden | Gate | Outcome |
|---|---|---|
| `slot_fullwidth_centerline` | `verify`, `Mode::Area`, the stadium `operation::region_of` builds for a real Slot op, no model (`DepthLaw::None`) | clean, dropped from UNJUDGED |
| `slot_wide_channel_rows` | same | clean, dropped |
| `trochoid_slot_small` | same, for a TrochoidalSlot op | clean, dropped |
| `trace_plate_with_hole` | `verify`, `Mode::Engrave`, the plate section `region_of` builds for a Trace op over the finished plate | clean, dropped |
| `plasma_plate_with_holes` (+ its `_mm` twin, same CL) | the plasma laws, `verify::plasma::judge`, as `posting_plasma::plasma_clause` runs them | no findings at all (no refusals, no warnings), dropped |
| `arc_planes` | none applies: a hand-built posting fixture (`arc_planes.rs`) with no op kind, part, region or tool record | kept, with that reason; gap filed as #1093 |

Each program is first proved byte-identical to its CL golden. **No golden moved and none was regenerated.** No golden turned out to be an unsafe program the gate would refuse. The guard now checks the blocking findings of all three gate families: depth laws, region laws, and plasma refusals (plasma warnings never block a post). Decisions are in `docs/decisions/1000-judge-unjudged-goldens.md`.

## How tested
New pinning tests in `solid_law_goldens`:
- `the_slot_trace_and_plasma_goldens_pass_their_gates`: all five verdicts are empty.
- `the_slot_gate_bites`: the wide slot's program, judged against a stadium 2 mm narrower, gouges, so the harness can fail.
- `every_posted_golden_is_a_program_the_gate_passes`: now judges the five, and `UNJUDGED` holds only `arc_planes`.

I ran these suites locally (debug, the worktree's own target, sccache), all green: solid_law_goldens 5/5, golden_cl 25/25, conformance 6/6, plasma_gate 6/6, plasma_post 5/5, plasma_post_refusals 7/7, plasma_profile 7/7, plasma_machine 6/6, arc_planes 8/8, fanuc_post 11/11, heidenhain_block_form 5/5, trochoid_op 5/5, slot_caps 4/4. `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean.

## Not exercised
- The full `cargo xtask gate quick` plan. xtask reads any new file under `tests/` as shared test input and plans all ~250 app suites, but only `solid_law_goldens` compiles the new module, so I ran the suites listed above instead.
- `plasma_plate_with_holes_control.nc` has no `.cl` golden of its own, so the guard doesn't judge it. That is unchanged by this PR.

Fixes #1000

title: fix(post): an absent rotary takes no angle word (fanuc, doosan-dnm)
body:
**Stacked on #1002** (the #926 per-post script suites, whose recorded `rotary` golden pins this fix). This branch carries #1002's commit plus a merge of upstream `main`; merge #1002 first, then this PR's diff is only the #997 change. Fork synced at v0.18.0.

## What changed

The RTCP path of `assets/posts/fanuc.cps` wrote all three angle words on the arm block whatever the machine stated - on the A+B tilthead, `G00 X0 Y0 Z20 A30 B0 C0`. A control with no C axis alarms on the C address (or, where C is another function, commands it).

- `statesRotary(letter)` reads `machine.rotaries`; `angleWord(letter, v)` writes a word only for a stated rotary. The arm block and the modal changed-letter words both go through it. Arm on the tilthead is now `G00 X0 Y0 Z20 A30 B0`.
- `missingLetter` (now built on `statesRotary`) still runs first, so a **turning** letter of an absent rotary stays refused by name (`tilted move commands C - the machine states no C rotary`). The only letters dropped are stated zeros.
- **Other posts checked:** haas, mazak, sinumerik, heidenhain and carvera refuse a tilted stream outright (no RTCP output); tormach writes A only on its own index path; fanuc-lathe / tormach-lathe refuse posed moves. Only `assets/posts/doosan-dnm.cps` shared the bug (its RTCP path is a copy of fanuc's) - fixed here the same way.
- Decision recorded in `docs/decisions/997-absent-rotary-word.md`.

## Goldens

- New: `crates/post/tests/recorded/golden/fanuc/rotary.nc` (read before commit: G43.4 arm, `A30 B0`, modal `A0 B30`, return `B0`, no C word anywhere); the `("fanuc.cps", "rotary", 997)` line is removed from `KNOWN_BUGS`.
- Every other golden is byte-identical (no `.nc`/`.refusal`/`.cl` file changed). doosan-dnm's recorded `rotary` stays its refusal (no clamp codes declared), unchanged.
- One existing assertion changed: `fanuc_post::rtcp_output_arms_once_and_walks_the_angles` asserted `G00 X10 Y0 Z5 A40 B0 C0` on an **A-only** trunnion - it had pinned the bug. It now asserts `G00 X10 Y0 Z5 A40`.

## How tested

Pinning tests:
- `script_fanuc::rotary` (the #926 recorded golden)
- `fanuc_post::an_absent_rotary_takes_no_angle_word` (tilthead: arm `A30 B0`, modal `A0 B30`, no C word; a turning C refused by name)
- `doosan_dnm_post::doosan_dnm_absent_rotary_takes_no_angle_word`

Gate (macOS, local, worktree target/, sccache):
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: post suites (lib, axis_direction_cli, comp, comp_plane, mch_head_search, post_engine, recorded_streams, every script_*) ok; app doosan_dnm_post, recorded_post_streams ok; fanuc_post failed once on the old word-count assertion below, fixed, then the whole `fanuc_post` suite 12/12 ok.
- App suites, whole: posting 17, golden_cl 25, conformance 6, tilt 8, fanuc_post 12, doosan_dnm_post 8, fourth_axis_pose 9, rotary_verify 9, recorded_post_streams 2 - all ok.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

`rtcp_output_arms_once_and_walks_the_angles` also asserted the modal block had fewer words than the arm block; on an A-only machine both now carry the single A word, so that comparison is dropped (the exact-line asserts still pin both blocks, and the modal law - unchanged angles rest, only the changed letter returns - is pinned by the new `fanuc/rotary.nc` golden: `G01 X20 Y0 Z0 F800`, `G00 X20 Y20 Z50 B0`).

## Not exercised

No hand-post on a real machine; the doosan fix is pinned only by its direct test (its recorded `rotary` case refuses earlier on undeclared clamp codes).

title: feat(sim): draw a turning tool's lathe body at the tool position
body:
**Stacked on #957** (issue #852, `issue/852-necked-tool-envelope`): this branch was cut from #957's head because both change `crates/app/src/sim_tool_body.rs`. Until #957 merges, this PR's diff also shows #957's commit (`54ed3fe7`); the #1038 change is the single commit on top (`feat(sim): draw a turning tool's lathe body at the tool position`). Retarget/merge order per AGENTS.md "Overlapping issues stack".

Fork synced at v0.18.0 (PROCESS_VERSION 16).

## What changed

Before, `sim_tool_body::for_operation` returned `Ok(None)` for every lathe-held kind, so the simulation and viewport showed only the axis marker for a turning tool, whatever body it carried. Now:

- **New `app::sim_lathe_body`.** It holds a pure pose (`posed(facets, tip, &LatheAxes)`), which maps a tool-frame point (x, y, z) to `tip + x*radial + y*(z x x) + z*along`, and a `LatheBodyCache`. The cache fetches the op's tool's lathe-frame body (`ToolBody::facets`, the same mesh `LatheClearance` is derived from) together with the frame it is judged in. It refits that frame only when the op, its path signature or the body (by `Arc` identity) changes, so the fit does not run every frame.
- **The frame is the holder law's own.** `operation::lathe_body_axes` (= `turning_holder::body_axes`) runs `Frame::about` on the op's source facets (`source_facets`, the read the law and the lathe stock sim use) and takes the radial from `SignedMeridian::of` on the cached path (a new `SignedMeridian::axes` accessor). As a result, every drawn vertex sits where the law reads it: sqrt((X + x)^2 + y^2) from the axis, at station S + z.
- **`SimToolCache::posed`** tries the lathe arm first. The ui seam (`world::sim_tool_tris`) is unchanged, so this adds no second drawing path. `for_operation` now also returns `Ok(None)` for a tool that carries a lathe-frame body, which covers a `Bore` with a lathe body: it is drawn as that body, not as the revolved bar stand-in.
- **A turning tool without a lathe body draws as before** (axis marker only). If the frame cannot be fitted, the refusal is logged once by name and nothing is drawn. No pose is guessed.
- **Display only.** No verdict, warning or posted output changes.
- Decision record: `docs/decisions/1038-lathe-body-in-sim.md`.

## Tests

Pinned by the new `crates/app/tests/sim_lathe_body.rs`:
- `an_od_holder_is_drawn_at_the_tip_radially_out_up_the_spindle`: OD finish ride with an OD shank, checked at several moves. Every drawn vertex equals its tool-frame vertex posed at the tip (+x along the path radial, +z up the spindle), matches the law's radius identity, and gives one drawn facet per body facet (not revolved).
- `an_id_bar_is_drawn_toward_the_axis_up_the_bore`: boring ride with a slim bar. Same vertex-by-vertex check; the bar stands inside the tip radius, its near corners at hypot(X - 4, 1.5), and it runs up the bore.
- `a_turning_tool_without_a_lathe_body_draws_as_before`: the bare insert draws nothing and the cache stays empty with no refusal.
- `a_new_body_is_drawn_at_once_and_the_frame_freed_with_the_transport`: reuse, rebuild on a new body, freed on `clear`.
- `the_pose_maps_each_tool_axis_onto_its_world_direction`: the pure pose on explicit axes, plus refusal of zero, non-finite and skew frames.

Also run: `sim_tool_body`, `tool_neck_laws`, `turning_holder`, `turning_insert_zone` and `tool_body` (all green), the full `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` on the final head, and `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`.

## Not exercised

- No live GUI check: nobody has stepped a turning op in the running app to look at the drawn body. The ui call path is unchanged and is covered by the existing `tool_body` ui test for milling only.
- Tinting the body on a `HolderHit` move (the issue's optional "could") is not done. It needs a colour channel on the sim body part; see the decision file.
- No snapshot PNG changed.

Effort: high

Changelog: Simulation and viewport draw a turning tool's imported lathe holder body at the tool position, posed in the frame the holder law judges it in (OD and ID), instead of only the axis marker (#1038)

Fixes #1038

title: test(gate): a motion generator change runs the operations suite
body:
## What

`crates/app/tests/operations.rs` generates every operation through the app layer, so its tests pin
the motion generators end to end — but its Gate map named `app::` modules only. A change under
`crates/motion/src/multiaxis/` therefore selected no suite that drives multiaxis rough end to end,
so `cargo xtask gate quick` could pass while
`multiaxis_rough_refuses_a_slot_the_cone_cannot_clear` sat out. PR #1044 hit exactly that: its gate
came out green and the failure surfaced only when a stacked merge ran the whole app list.

## The fix

- `operations.rs`'s Gate map names the generators its tests drive end to end, on top of main's
  crate-qualified mapping: `motion::machining3d`, `motion::multiaxis`, `motion::plunge_law` added
  (`motion::drilling`, `motion::finishing3d` and `motion::machining2d` are already there since the
  crate split).
- An xtask test in `xtask/src/gate_maps_tests.rs` (the real-checkout selection suite from #922)
  pins both halves: the map names every one of the six generators, and a plan for
  `crates/motion/src/multiaxis/mod.rs` selects `app:operations`. A header that loses a name now
  fails in xtask's own suite instead of in a later PR's gate run.

## Process

`xtask/` is a process file, so `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION` goes 30 → 31.

## How tested

- `cargo test -p xtask` — 56 passed (new test included)
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main` — ok (app operations suite 62 s, xtask 2 s)
- Selection proof: with a one-line probe under `crates/motion/src/multiaxis/`,
  `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main --plan` lists `app suites ... --test operations`;
  before the header change it listed motion suites only.
- `cargo clippy -p xtask -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` — clean

## Merge note

Main moved past this branch twice (the crate split, then further cuts). The branch now carries a
merge of `origin/main` (`6af3a4ca`), so the header keeps main's crate-qualified names and only adds
the three motion names above.

Changelog: none
Fixes #1068

body:
**Stacked on #1020** (#818, `issue/818-swing-any-horizontal`): this branch starts from #1020's head, so until #1020 merges the diff below also shows its commit. Retarget/merge order per AGENTS.md "Overlapping issues stack". Fork synced at v0.18.0.

Works #821 as corrected by its 2026-11-11 comment: the microARC subplate does **not** turn with A - it is a base plate that mounts the rotary on a fixture plate (two pin bores) or on the T-slots. The safety core: the index-swing check (#804/#810/#818) assumed the machine file's `nose_to_axis` (10.6 in, rotary on the bare table), which is unconservative once a plate and subplate raise the A centerline.

## What changed

- **Rotary subplate** = a new built-in accessory kind `rotary_subplate` (`Accessory::RotarySubplate`: length, width, thickness, bore spacing, first bore from -X, bores from -Y, bore diameter). Generic default figures, named generic (10 x 6 x 3/4 in, 1/2 in bores 6 in apart) - no maker's dimensions committed; the user enters theirs. Solid-slab mesh (bores drawn solid). It lands **fixed** (never in the swept radius). Its frame is the first pin bore at the underside, +X toward the second, so `PlaceOnPlate` seats it on a #819 dowel pair by its pins.
- **Pin law:** a subplate goes only on a dowel pair whose spacing equals its bore spacing (0.05 mm); a single hole or another spacing is refused by name - at `PlaceOnPlate`, at a `SetPlate` re-seat, and at a `SetAccessory` resize of the placed subplate (which also keeps its footprint on the plate).
- **Raised centerline** (`app::rotary_stack`): the setup's subplates and every plate under each (through the plate locations) form a stack; the tallest one is used. The swing clause judges with the **effective** `nose_to_axis` = machine figure less the stack, or the setup's **stated** figure, which wins.
- **Refusal law:** a stack whose thickness is unknown (an imported plate under the subplate, a vanished or looped plate, a non-finite figure), a stated figure that is no length, or an effective figure at or under zero refuses the swing **by name** - never judged on the table figure. **No subplate: judged word for word as before** (pinned by the exact message).
- **Per-setup stated figure:** `SetupDef::nose_to_axis`, command `SetSetupNoseToAxis` (finite, > 0, <= 5000 mm; no-op refused; undoable), carried by a datum transfer with the machine.
- **Save/load:** additive setup key `nose_to_axis`; the subplate rides the existing `accessory` key. Old files load unchanged (pinned).
- Decisions: `docs/decisions/821-rotary-on-plate-stack.md`.

## Commands, MCP, UI

- Commands: `InsertAccessory` / `SetAccessory` (new kind), `PlaceOnPlate` (pin law), new `SetSetupNoseToAxis`.
- MCP: `add_accessory` / `set_accessory` take `rotary_subplate`; `place_on_plate` applies the pin law; new `get_rotary_stack` (stack layers, stated figure, machine rotaries, refusal reason) and `set_setup_nose_to_axis` (number or null).
- UI: the Fixtures page's accessory dialog lists "Rotary subplate" (KINDS-driven); the setup's Machine page gets a "Rotary centerline" section (machine figure, the stack readout or the refusal, a checkbox + field for the setup's stated figure, queued as `CommandKind::SetupNoseToAxis`). Drawn only for a machine with a work-turning rotary. No snapshot PNG changed.

## Tests

- `crates/app/tests/rotary_subplate.rs` (new): `a_subplate_lands_fixed_and_seats_on_a_dowel_pair_by_its_pins`, `the_same_program_clears_on_the_table_and_is_refused_on_the_stack`, `a_stack_of_unknown_thickness_is_refused_by_name`, `an_effective_nose_at_or_under_zero_is_refused_by_name`, `the_setup_s_stated_nose_wins_and_is_an_undoable_command`, `no_stack_is_judged_word_for_word_as_before`, `the_subplate_and_the_stated_nose_survive_a_save_and_old_files_load_unchanged`.
- `crates/app/tests/mcp_rotary_stack.rs` (new): `a_subplate_is_pinned_on_a_plate_and_raises_the_rotary_over_mcp`.
- `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests/setup_rotary.rs` (new, AccessKit labels): `the_stated_nose_is_one_undoable_command`, `the_machine_page_shows_the_rotary_rows_and_states_the_figure`, `a_machine_without_a_work_turning_rotary_draws_no_rotary_rows`.
- `builtin_accessory` updated for the sixth kind (KINDS, bounds/volume of the slab, insert order).
- Gate: `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` green on 642cd694 (app suites 365 s, index_swing_horizontal 10 fn, ui suites 44 s; 0 failed). By hand (not mapped by quick, #1021): index_swing 9/9, index_swing_horizontal 10/10, tormach_fourth_axis 12/12, rotary_fixtures 4/4, rotary_verify 9/9; ui lib `setup_rotary`, `accessory`, `fixture`, `structural` filters 51/51; `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean.

## Not exercised

- **The hardware check on the user's own microARC subplate** (#821 "Checked on the user's microARC subplate") - stays with the user; hence `Refs`, not `Fixes`.
- The camcraft-mcp skill's tool table is not updated (a process file; the new tools describe themselves in `tools/list`).
- Posed collision judgement of the subplate itself is the existing fixed-fixture law (unchanged).

Changelog: A rotary subplate (built-in accessory) is placed on a fixture plate's dowel pair by its pin bores, and the A index-swing check judges from the centerline the subplate and plate stack raise - or from the setup's stated nose_to_axis - refusing by name when the stack's thickness is unknown (#821)

Effort: high (no escalation)

Refs #821

title: fix(app,motion): judge probe and plasma on a reduced-fidelity model; cone/engrave rides stay refused
body:
Stacked on #1064 (base it on main once #1064 merges; it carries #1064's commits until then).

Fork synced at v0.18.0.

## What changed, per kind

#904 left five kinds refused outright on any reduced-fidelity model. Same rule as #864/#904: a law gives the model's excess back out of its slack while a positive slack is left (`verify::excess_floor`); past that it reads untightened and the program gate refuses the op by name.

- **Probe - now judged.** Both halves of the protected-move law read `probe_op::stylus_slack(excess)` = `STYLUS_SLACK` less the excess: the ball distance law (`stylus_hits_excess`) and the stem/body solid law (`stylus_reach_hits_excess`). The old functions forward with 0, so existing callers don't change. `generate` passes `material.excess`. Nothing else judges a probe against the model.
- **Plasma - now judged.** The kerf law (part grown by `kerf/2 - tol`, which the lead planner reads too) and the cover law read `PlasmaParams::kerf_tol()` = `KERF_TOL` less the new `PlasmaParams::model_excess`. `plasma_op` fills that field from `material.excess`. The cut-order, crossing and tip-up laws read only the path.
- **`fidelity_law`**: `excess_aware` now accepts Probe and every Plasma kind. `floor_of` also lists each kind's own slack (`own_law_tol_of`). `GOUGE_TOL` stays the base, so plasma is still refused at 0.01 mm of excess, which is stricter than its 0.025 mm law needs.
- **Cone rides (2D chamfer, deburr) and engrave rides (trace, engrave) - still refused, with the reason recorded.** No law holds them to a tolerance against the model: the ride *is* the mesh edge by construction, so there's no tolerance to give back. Deburr also reads bends between coarse facets as creases. Judging them would need a new stated ride accuracy, which is open design, not a tightening. The reason is in `fidelity_law`'s header and the decision file.
- **Cross drill - still refused; #1053 stays open for it (hence `Refs`).** Its part law and `rapids_radial` would each take a one-line tightening. But the chain is also proved by zero-slack readings of the mesh: `cross_stock::standoff` / `rapids_clear`, `cross_entry`, and `drill_reach`'s reach and holder faces. Tightening those means growing each measured standoff by the excess, which moves the kernel's stations. As #904 set, a law isn't tightened for a kind that stays refused.

Decisions: `docs/decisions/1053-fidelity-probe-plasma.md`.

## How tested

New suite `crates/app/tests/coarse_probe_plasma.rs`. Each law is pinned so that a reading between the plain and the tightened slack is convicted only on the coarse model (excess 0.007), and a real hit is convicted on both:
- `a_ball_between_the_slacks_is_a_gouge_only_on_the_coarse_model`: a touch 0.006 mm in; a real gouge at 0.05 mm.
- `a_stem_between_the_slacks_is_a_shank_hit_only_on_the_coarse_model`: an overhang lip 0.006 mm into the stem; a real hit at 0.05 mm.
- `the_probe_op_judges_with_its_models_excess`: the same lip through `GenerateOperation` on an import with no flag and one flagged 0.012 mm. This proves the wiring.
- `a_kerf_between_the_tolerances_is_refused_only_on_the_coarse_model`: the part grown 0.02 mm past the cut outline; the kerf law refuses by name. A real reach at 0.1 mm is refused on both.
- `the_stylus_slack_...` and `the_kerf_tolerance_gives_the_excess_back_and_reads_plain_past_the_bound`: past the bound the laws read their plain slack.
- `probe_and_plasma_are_judged_while_a_tolerance_is_left_and_refused_by_name_past_it`, plus `coarse_laws::every_kind_is_either_judged_or_refused_for_a_stated_reason_on_a_reduced_model`, whose refused list loses Probe and PlasmaProfile: judged at 0.012 mm, refused by name at 0.030 mm.

Quick gate (`cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/issue/904-reduced-fidelity-laws`) and `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-motion --all-targets -- -D warnings` on the final head: green on 2e4058e7 (motion lib 31 s, 52 app suites 156 s, golden_cl plasma 1 s; 0 failed); clippy -D warnings clean.

## Not exercised

- The plasma cover law's tightening has no marginal pin. Its reading compares the path with the contour, and no fixture puts an edge between 0.018 and 0.025 mm past `kerf` on demand.
- There's no document-level plasma fixture. The part region comes from the model's silhouette slice, which can't be grown by a chosen 0.02 mm, so the law is pinned through `plasma_profile`.
- A bore touch on a coarse model: the tightened slack convicts a tangent touch once the excess passes ~0.0025 mm, because the bore's facets stand inside it. That's a false gouge on the safe side, the #1057 shape, and is recorded in the decision file.

No goldens or snapshots moved (`golden_cl::plasma_plate_with_holes_matches_golden` passes with `model_excess: 0.0`).

Changelog: Probe and Plasma Profile operations can now post from a reduced-fidelity model (e.g. a metre-unit STEP file); their collision laws are tightened by the model's excess and refuse by name past it (#1053)

Effort: high (no escalation)

Refs #1053
