title: feat(pick): box-select edge chains and faces into an operation's picks
body:
Fork synced at v0.18.0 (branch cut from upstream/main a6bd69d8).

## What changed

- **Viewport box select** (`crates/ui/src/box_pick.rs`, `egui_app/shell.rs`): Ctrl (or Shift) + left drag in Edge or Face mode, with an operation open and no other pick draft collecting, draws a rubber band instead of orbiting. On release it adds every visible feature edge chain (Edge mode) or welded face (Face mode) in the box to the operation's picks, as **one `SetOperationGeometry`**, so it is one undo step. A drag to the right is a **window** (takes only what lies wholly inside), a drag to the left is a **crossing** box (also takes what it touches). The band is solid for a window and dashed for a crossing box. A plain left drag still orbits.
- **The rule** (`crates/app/src/pick/box_pick.rs`: `box_bodies`, `box_select`, `box_select_top`) follows #692's one pick rule. Only feature chains are candidates (never facet seams). A candidate counts only if part of it is unoccluded from the eye, using the click pick's own sight test (`feature_pick::occluded`, now `pub(super)`, with no behaviour change), at most 16 sight rays per candidate. Pick-through stays off. Only parts are candidates, never stock or fixtures, but stock and fixtures still hide what lies behind them.
- **MCP**: new tool `pick_in_box` (`crates/app/src/mcp/box_pick.rs`). It takes a world X/Y box seen from straight above (the Top view, orthographic), with `mode` window/crossing and `kind` chains/faces. By default it adds to the current picks; `replace: true` replaces them. One undo step. An empty, degenerate or already-picked box is refused with a message that names the reason. `mcp::pick::kind_door` is now `pub(super)` so the new tool can reuse it.
- The Selection row's hover text documents the gesture. Decisions are in `docs/decisions/979-box-select-picks.md`.

## How tested

- `crates/app/tests/box_pick.rs` uses a 100 x 60 x 10 plate with two square through-cutouts:
  - `a_window_around_one_cutout_takes_exactly_its_top_rim`: from the top in ortho, exactly the cutout's 4 top-rim chains. In perspective, straight over the hole, the eye sees into it, so the result is 12 chains, all on that cutout.
  - `a_window_around_everything_takes_every_top_rim_chain_and_no_hidden_one`: 12 top-rim chains (outer + 2 cutouts), all at the top. Pick-through gives 36 (the hidden ones exist). Seen from below, only the bottom rims.
  - `a_crossing_box_takes_what_it_touches_a_window_only_what_it_holds`
  - `faces_box_the_same_way_and_hidden_faces_stay_out`
  - `degenerate_boxes_take_nothing`
  - `mcp_pick_in_box_adds_the_rim_in_one_undo_step`: covers two boxes and two undos, `replace`, and refusals.
- `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests/box_select.rs` drives real egui pointer and modifier events on the seeded shell with the plate imported, Top view, ortho:
  - `a_ctrl_drag_window_around_one_cutout_adds_its_rim_in_one_undo_step`: no orbit, exactly 4 chains appended to Contour1, and one Undo restores the seed's pick.
  - `a_right_to_left_drag_is_a_crossing_box_and_a_plain_drag_still_orbits`
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` on the final head: green on 6716fad1 (app suites 27 s incl. box_pick, feature_pick, mcp_pick; ui lib + 10 suites 17 s)

## Not exercised

- The real-window (winit/wgpu) look of the rubber band. Only the kittest harness drew it. No snapshot PNG changed.
- The user's actual cutouts project from #241. It is not in the repo, so the plate fixture stands in for it.
- Very large meshes: the cost is up to 16 sight rays per in-box candidate, each against every facet. It was not timed on a 1M-facet model.
- The camcraft-mcp skill's tool table is not updated, because it is a process file and would need a PROCESS_VERSION bump. `tools/list` carries the new tool's description and schema.

Changelog: Viewport box select - Ctrl+drag in Edge/Face mode adds every visible edge chain or face in the box to the open operation's picks in one undo step (drag right: window, left: crossing); MCP `pick_in_box` does the same from the Top view (#979)

Effort: high (no escalation)

Fixes #979

title: fix(verify): judge a stock-sourced Bore's entry rapid against the stock
body:
Fork synced at v0.18.0 (branch cut from upstream/main a6bd69d8).

## What reproduced

In #1066 the planar ladder takes its first descent from the top of the cut plus the plunge height (2 mm): Pocket and Contour read their Top height, Bore reads the hole's `entry_z`. The issue suspected a rapid into stock that stands higher than that top. Fixture: a 40 x 40 x 20 part with a 20 x 20 blind hole (mouth Z 20) in a box 5 mm taller (top Z 25), nothing faced ahead. Each op's entry rapid goes from Z 40 to Z 22, 3 mm into uncut stock.

- 2D Pocket, Contour, and a Bore sourced from the part: already convicted by the rapid law (#96, `RapidInStock`), and the post is blocked.
- **A Bore sourced from the stock: no warning, and it posted.** That's a silent rapid into material, so the issue went to P0.

Cause: `sim::verify::rapids_in_stock` asks `Rest::in_stock`, which falls back to the op's region when `VerifyContext::stock` is `None`, and a stock-sourced op leaves it `None`. For Bore and Thread that region is the stock footprint with the holes' rims punched out, so the column inside the hole never counted as stock.

## What changed

- `operation::material_source::judged_stock` (new, about 20 lines): when the source is the stock and the kind is Bore or Thread, verify's column law reads the stock's own facets instead of the punched region. Every other source and kind reads exactly as before.
- `operation::generate`: the upright and 3+2 verify readings both take that stock. No generator or path changes, so no golden moves.
- `docs/decisions/1066-ladder-entry-height.md`: why the law's reading was fixed rather than raising the ladder's top, and the options dropped.

## How tested

- New suite `crates/app/tests/ladder_entry_height.rs`. Each of its 4 tests runs Pocket, Bore and Contour:
  - `a_ladder_entry_rapid_under_a_taller_block_is_named_and_blocks_the_post`: `RapidInStock` at the entry rapid, and the post gate refuses it. It fails on main for Bore and passes with the fix; I checked both.
  - `a_block_standing_inside_the_plunge_height_is_fed_through_silently` (1.5 mm over the mouth)
  - `stock_to_the_mouth_is_silent_and_posts`
  - `a_face_ahead_to_the_mouth_acquits_the_entry_rapid` (`acquit_by_prior` still clears it)
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: green (1 step, 43 app binaries + lib, 148 s)
- I also ran the suites that build Bore or Thread ops: arc_entry, circular_pick, mill2d_b, mill2d_c, operations, refusal_location, level_links, vertical_arc_entry, project_roundtrip, golden_cl and conformance. All green.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean

## Not exercised

- The Thread case is covered by the same `matches!` arm but has no pinning test of its own (its entry is judged by #992's thread-entry law).
- The 3+2 (tilted) reading takes the same stock, but no tilted test was run for it.
- Drill isn't touched: its R-plane law already refuses this case at generate (checked on the same fixture).

Changelog: A milled Bore sourced from the stock now has its entry rapid judged against the stock above the hole's mouth: a rapid into uncut stock is named and blocks the post (#1066)

Effort: high (no escalation)

Fixes #1066

title: feat(import): the STEP facet budget is a setting carried with the import
body:
Fork synced at v0.18.0 (branch cut from upstream/main a6bd69d8).

## What changed

The STEP importer's facet budget (the constant `MAX_FACETS`) becomes a setting that travels with the import (`app::geometry::import::step_budget`):

- **Default and bounds.** The default is today's cap, 30,000,000 facets, so no default import changes and no golden moves. A set budget must be in 1,000..=60,000,000. Outside that range, every door refuses it by name before parsing (`STEP facet budget N is outside 1000..=60000000 facets`). A budget given for an STL or OBJ file is also refused.
- **Doors.**
  - `ImportModel::within(path, budget)` is the one command the GUI, the script and MCP all build.
  - The script verb is `cam.import(path, name?, facetBudget?)`. A null name keeps the file stem. `cam.d.ts` is regenerated to match.
  - MCP `import_model` takes an optional integer `facet_budget`, declared in the schema with its min/max.
  - Script and MCP take whole numbers only. A fraction, a negative or a string is refused, never rounded.
- **Recorded with the model.**
  - A new component, `schema::StepBudget`, holds the budget, but only when it is not the default. `model_fidelity::budget_of` / `set_budget` read and write it.
  - Import, update (re-import), repair (keeps it), delete and their undo all trade it together with the facets.
  - The project file stores it as an optional `facet_budget` key. An absent key means the default, so default documents save byte for byte as before and older files load unchanged. An out-of-bounds value, or one on a non-model row, is refused by name at load.
  - `get_job` and `cam.import` report the budget.
- **Reduced fidelity (#864) is computed exactly as before.** A smaller budget flags the model; a larger one meshes finer and clears the flag on re-import. The refusal text now names a setting that exists: "re-import with a larger STEP facet budget".
- **GUI.** The model page has a "STEP facet budget (next import)" row (type a value, then Enter or Set). An out-of-range value is refused by name on the row and on the status line, and the last good value stays. The row also shows which budget the model was imported under. Every STEP import started from the window (Model button, recent list, drag and drop) reads the setting. A re-import under the same name stays the undoable `UpdateModel`.
- **`step.rs` edits are minimal.** `parse_with_chord_budget` was added, and the thread-local test override now only lowers the requested budget. This should merge additively with #969's log-line change.

Decisions (60M ceiling, a session-scoped GUI setting on the model page rather than a post-picker modal, re-import uses the current setting, no project version bump) are in `docs/decisions/1054-step-facet-budget.md`.

## How tested

- `crates/app/tests/step_budget.rs` (new, 6 tests):
  - `the_default_budget_imports_exactly_as_before`
  - `a_lowered_budget_flags_and_a_raised_one_clears_through_undo_and_delete`
  - `an_out_of_bounds_budget_is_refused_by_name_before_parsing`
  - `the_script_verb_takes_the_budget_and_refuses_one_out_of_bounds`
  - `mcp_import_model_takes_the_budget_and_get_job_reports_it`
  - `the_budget_round_trips_through_the_project_and_an_older_file_reads_the_default`
- `step_budget::tests` unit tests: bounds, JSON whole numbers only, the default records nothing.
- `crates/ui` `egui_app::tests::step_budget::the_model_page_sets_the_budget_the_next_step_import_runs_under`: the row is drawn, an out-of-range value is refused on the row and the status line, a lowered budget's import lands flagged, a raised re-import clears the flag, and undo restores both.
- `crates/app/tests/model_fidelity.rs`: the two refusal-text pins now expect the new wording.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: green on c93c64ef (app suites ok 167 s, ui suites ok 21 s, 3.1 min wall, 0 failed)

## Not exercised

- A real model that needs more than the 30M default to reach full fidelity. No such fixture is committed. "Raised clears" is pinned from 2,000 up to 5,000,000 on `Milling-test.step`.
- The native file picker and typing into the egui field by keyboard. The test drives the setter and the import queue.
- The camcraft-mcp skill doc does not mention `facet_budget` yet. It is a process file, which would need a `PROCESS_VERSION` bump; the tool's schema and description carry the argument.

Changelog: The STEP facet budget is a setting: the model page, `cam.import(path, name?, facetBudget?)` and MCP `import_model`'s `facet_budget` set it (1000..=60000000, default 30000000), and each model records the budget it was imported under (#1054)

Effort: high (no escalation)

Fixes #1054

title: fix(sim,app): read a containment kind's declared rim at the plain gouge tolerance on a reduced-fidelity model
body:
Stacked on #1064 (branch `issue/904-reduced-fidelity-laws`: this uses its `verify/excess.rs` split and its `coarse_contain` fixture). Fork synced at v0.18.0.

## Root cause

A Z drill, bore or thread mill verifies (`Mode::Boundary`) against rim loops that are our own polygons of each hole's declared circle (`material_source::rim_loop`), built to `RIM_SAG_BUDGET` = 0.005 mm, half the 0.01 mm `GOUGE_TOL`. A 2 mm rim (48 sides) stands 0.00428 mm inside its circle, so a matched drill reads `r - 0.00428` off it. #864 had law (b) read **every** loop at `GOUGE_TOL - excess`. Past 0.01 - 0.00428 = 0.00572 mm of excess (a model flagged above ~0.0107 mm; the issue saw 0.0105 clean, 0.011 convicted) the tolerance left no longer covered the rim's own sagitta: `Gouge { at: 1 }` on a matched drill, and on every ring of a matched bore. Past 0.015 mm `excess_floor` reads untightened and the gate refuses by name, which is why 0.03 read clean.

## What changed

- `sim::verify::VerifyContext` gets `rims: &[(Point2, f64)]` (empty by default): the declared circles of a containment kind. `VerifyContext::is_rim` / `loop_tol` (in `verify/excess.rs`) match a loop to one (every vertex within 2 um: the region's 1 um lattice snap).
- Law (b) (`verify/section.rs`), both the law-point reading and the Boundary whole-move wall reading, reads a rim loop at the plain `gouge_tol` and every other loop at `tightened(gouge_tol)` as before. Rims are found once per verify call.
- `app::operation::generate` fills `rims` from the Drill (Z holes), Bore and Thread params when the depth law is `Contain` (`material_source::rims_of`), at both verify sites.
- The solid law against the model's facets (`contain_into`) is untouched and still tightened.

Why the plain tolerance is honest: the excess measures how far a coarse model's facets stand inside its true surface; a rim is not a facet but a circle we draw from the hole's own centre and radius, so the rim's reading is exactly today's full-fidelity verdict. Nothing a full-fidelity model convicts is acquitted. Decision file: `docs/decisions/1057-drill-excess-false-gouge.md` (options dropped: finer rims, exact-circle reading, zeroing the excess for the containment kinds, recognising rims structurally in sim).

## Readings (`coarse_rims` fixture: 40x40x20 block, 20x20 cavity blind at Z 10, DR-0400 to Z 10.2)

| flagged | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| full, 0.008, 0.0105 | clean | clean |
| 0.011, 0.012, 0.0149 | `Gouge { at: 1 }` | clean |
| 0.03 | clean + refused by name | clean + refused by name |

Matched bore (EM-0800-4FL in a 6 mm-radius hole) at 0.011 / 0.0149: before `Gouge { at: 6, 7, 8, 17, ... }`, after clean.

## How tested

Pinning tests (all fail before the fix where they name a false conviction, pass after):
- `coarse_rims::a_matched_drill_is_clean_on_a_model_flagged_anywhere_below_the_refusal_bound` (full, 0.008, 0.0105, 0.011, 0.012, 0.0149)
- `coarse_rims::a_matched_bore_is_clean_near_the_refusal_bound` (+ a bore offset 1 mm into the wall still convicts at 0.0149)
- `coarse_rims::the_real_drill_gouges_still_convict_on_a_model_near_the_refusal_bound` (oversize drill, drill offset into the wall, drill 0.5 mm past the floor - each at full, 0.011 and 0.0149; and 0.005 mm past the floor: clean at full fidelity, a gouge at 0.0149)
- `coarse_rims::a_matched_drill_past_the_bound_is_refused_by_name_not_convicted` (0.03: no warnings, the gate's fidelity line by name)
- `coarse_rims::a_thread_mill_reads_the_same_near_the_bound_as_at_full_fidelity`
- `model_excess::a_declared_rim_is_read_untightened_and_no_other_loop_is` (sim: an undeclared rim convicted near the bound, declared clean, a 2.01 drill still convicted, a declaration that does not trace the loop leaves the coarse boss convicted)

Gate: `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/issue/904-reduced-fidelity-laws` on the final head fe7403bc - sim 9 s, motion 4 s, app 201 s, 0 failed (3.6 min); plus `verify` and `mill2d_c` (rim law and bore/thread from stock) green; `cargo clippy -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean. No goldens or snapshot PNGs moved.

## Not exercised

- The thread mill is **not** clean: on a model-sourced hole it is convicted on every helix move at full fidelity too (its helix runs the thread depth past the declared rim by design). Not a fidelity bug; filed as #1071. The pin here is only that the excess no longer changes its verdict.
- The 3+2 framed verify site passes the same rims; a rim drawn in the local frame that does not match the world-frame circles simply falls back to the tightened reading (today's behaviour). Not exercised by a framed fixture.

Changelog: A drill or bore matched to its hole is no longer falsely convicted of a gouge on a model imported between ~0.0105 mm and the 0.015 mm refusal bound (#1057, PR #1073)

title: fix(post): seat a canned cycle read away from its hole at the section's hop
body:
**Stacked on #1019 (on #1002).** The diff shows their commits until they merge. This PR's own commits are c5e931c6 (posts and tests) and c12b4d16 (conformance synth fixture and goldens).

Closes the two latent seat gaps the high-tier review of #1019 noted (review at 321df394). Neither stream comes from a generator today (the generator always writes the chain plus the rapids that leave it), but a legacy or foreign stream would post an XY traverse lower than the hop.

### What changed (identical in all six canned-cycle mill posts: fanuc, haas, mazak, sinumerik, tormach, doosan-dnm)
- **Back-to-back cycle records** (`cycleSeat`, the away branch). When the cycle is read away from its hole and no stream rapid took the tool there, the seat now traverses at the section's hop:
  - `G0(0) Z<max(RetractPlane, R)>` when the tool is below it, then `X Y`, then `Z<R>`;
  - a tool already above the hop traverses where it stands.

  The hop is the section's own `PARAM RetractPlane`. `onParameter` captures it into `hopZ`, and `onSectionEnd` forgets it, so a section never borrows the previous operation's hop. A section that states no `RetractPlane` is refused by name: "a canned cycle is read away from its hole with no rapid to it, and the section states no RetractPlane to traverse at". The seats that stay over the hole (only up or down to R) are unchanged.
- **Cycle after probing.** `onProbeMove`, `onProbeRetreat` and `onProbeGuard` call a new `probeSeat()`. It sets `seatKnown` the way `chainRapid` / `chainCut` do, and closes an open cycle group with `G80`, because no probe move is part of a hole's chain. The engine already tracks the position through TOUCH / RETREAT / GUARD records, so a cycle read after probing is seated from there.
- Heidenhain and Carvera post the expanded chain and are untouched; their script suites and goldens are unchanged. fanuc-lathe is not touched (#1025/#1042).
- `assets/posts/AGENTS.md` (hop law paragraph) and `docs/decisions/1028-cycle-seat-latent.md` record the decisions. `assets/posts/AGENTS.md` is not a process file, so there is no PROCESS_VERSION bump.

### Tests (`crates/post/tests/cycle_hop.rs`, all six posts through the #994 checker)
- `back_to_back_cycle_records_traverse_at_the_hop`: the recorded `drill_retract` stream with hole 1's hop, traverse and descent cut out (hole 2 re-anchored AT 13). It asserts that no XY traverse runs below the hop and that the exit is at clearance.
- `back_to_back_cycle_records_without_a_hop_are_refused_by_name`: the same stream without `RetractPlane`. Every post refuses it with the named message.
- `a_cycle_read_after_probing_is_seated_at_the_hop`: a section whose first motion is GUARD, TOUCH and a RETREAT to Z1 (below hop Z3), then a cycle at another XY with no rapid to it, then a second hole. Checked from the first known position (`check_from(.., true)`).
- `the_checker_reads_probe_moves_and_incremental_back_offs`: pins the checker additions:
  - G31 / G38.2-G38.5 read as straight moves;
  - G90/G91 incremental back-offs;
  - the `from_start` watch.

**Revert check:**
- With #1019's six `.cps` files restored, all three stream tests fail. Fanuc, for example, gives `G00 X30 Y10` traversing at Z1 below the hop Z3, and the no-hop stream posts instead of being refused.
- With only the `probeSeat()` calls removed, the probe test alone fails (`G73 X30 Y10 ...` moves to the hole at Z-4), so each fix is pinned on its own.

**Goldens.** No generated-stream golden moved: no generator emits these streams. One test-built fixture did:
- `crates/app/tests/conformance.rs`'s `synth_stream_with` had back-to-back cycle records and no `RetractPlane`, so the hop seat now refuses it.
- The manager's decision (option 1) is that the fixture now states `PARAM ClearancePlane 10` and `PARAM RetractPlane 5` (R is 2), placed as in the recorded `drill_retract` stream. No leaving rapids were added.

The six moved goldens were each read line by line:
- `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/synth_fanuc.nc`, `synth_haas.nc`, `synth_mazak.nc`, `synth_tormach.nc`, `synth_doosan-dnm.nc`, `synth_sinumerik.nc`.
- Before each hole the tool now climbs to the hop (`G0(0) Z0`, work frame), traverses XY there, and drops to R (`Z-3`). Before, it traversed at R. Nothing else changed apart from Sinumerik's N numbers shifting.
- `synth_heidenhain.nc` and `synth_carvera.nc` do not move.
- `WRITE_GOLDEN=1` touched no other file.

### Gates (Linux, on the final head)
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` on c12b4d16: **green**. Post suites cover `camcraft-post` lib plus every test binary (`cycle_hop`, `recorded_streams`, all `script_*`, ...). App suites are the full mapped set (the diff includes #1019's shared `inverted_support`), among them posting, conformance, golden_cl, fanuc_post, tormach_post, doosan_dnm_post, probe_dialects, probe_tormach, probe_guard, drill_rplane, drilling_axial, inverted_post and inverted_probe. 2219 passed, 0 failed, 18 ignored, 18.6 min wall.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --test conformance -- -D warnings`: clean.
- The first gate run, before the fixture change, failed only `conformance::the_synthesized_stream_locks_the_tool_and_spindle_words` (the named refusal above).

### Not exercised
- No real control was run. The posted shapes were read by the checker and by eye for tormach and sinumerik.
- Doosan's Renishaw Inspection Plus (G65 P9810/P9811) probe path goes through the same `probeSeat()`, but no test runs it with a machine that enables it.
- Fanuc-lathe face cycles (#1025/#1026) are not covered here.

Changelog: Canned-cycle posts seat a cycle read away from its hole (back-to-back cycle records, or a cycle right after probing) at the section's RetractPlane, or refuse it by name when none is stated (#1028)

Effort: high (no escalation)

Fork synced at v0.18.0.

Fixes #1028

title: test(bore): pin the centre-cutting law on the milled Bore's way in
body:
Fork synced at v0.18.0. Not stacked (branched from upstream main at 3e9b8ae1).

**What reproduced.** #1036 suspected the milled Bore ride plunges a cutter that is not centre-cutting into an undrilled hole unjudged. It does not. On a solid 60 x 60 x 20 block, a 20 mm hole and an 8 mm end mill marked `center_cutting: false`, the Bore arm generates a path whose every rung is entered by a zig-zag ramp along the radial sweep, with the note "entry: the tool is not centre-cutting and may not plunge into solid (the plunge arm) - ramp along the first cut instead"; the ring's re-entry plunges land on columns the sweep already cut. A 9 mm hole (no helix, no ramp run) is refused: "entry refused: the tool is not centre-cutting - the plunge arm, and no helix or ramp fits onto Z 15.000". The law doing it: `operation::generate` lays the tool's `center_cutting` over the generation's links (M11.3 B-D, 874507a8) and every planar-ladder descent asks it (`descent::plan_core`, `plunge_law::guard`, 515525c4). The Bore ride is a planar ladder.

**What changed.** Tests only: `crates/app/tests/bore_entry.rs` pins the law on the Bore ride, and `docs/decisions/1036-bore-entry.md` records why no #992-style prior-stock refusal is added (an end mill without centre teeth may ramp or helix in; a thread mill cannot).

**How tested.** Pinning tests (all pass):
- `a_cutter_that_is_not_centre_cutting_ramps_into_an_undrilled_bore_never_plunges` - `plunge_law::first_solid_plunge` finds no axial plunge into solid; the ramp substitution is named; the ride reaches the floor.
- `a_centre_cutting_cutter_keeps_its_axial_plunge` - the same audit convicts the centre-cutting path (control: it dives on the axis, unchanged).
- `an_undrilled_hole_too_tight_for_a_ramp_or_helix_is_refused_by_name`.

`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: 1 step, 0 failed. `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --tests -- -D warnings`: clean.

**Not exercised.** Verify/post gate on these paths (the generator already substitutes or refuses); stock standing above the hole's mouth (the ladder's top of cut is the hole's `entry_z` - the generic 2D top-of-cut question, not this one); helix transitions other than the planar links.

No goldens moved, no snapshot PNGs touched.

Changelog: none

Effort: high (no escalation)

title: fix(sim,motion,app): judge turning, rotary and 5-axis ball kinds on a reduced-fidelity model; the collision laws read its excess
body:
Fork synced at v0.18.0 (branch cut from upstream/main 3e9b8ae1, the merge of #911, which this work builds on).

## What changed

#864 / PR #911 flagged a STEP model imported coarser than promised, tightened the upright mill kinds' gouge laws by the model's excess, and refused every other kind outright. This PR takes three families off the refused list and makes the collision laws read the excess (the P1 raise from #911's review). The rule is #864's, unchanged: a tolerance gives the excess back while a positive tolerance is left (`verify::excess_floor`); past that the law reads untightened and the program gate refuses the operation by name. With no excess every law reads exactly as before.

**Now judged on a reduced-fidelity model**

| Family | Law that judges it | What reads the excess |
|---|---|---|
| Turning, band kinds (groove rough/finish, part, threading, form) | the meridian scan | its gouge clause (`turning::gouge_tol_on`; `blade_warnings_excess`, `thread_warnings_excess`, `form_warnings_excess`). The rest clause and the silhouette's chord budget keep the op's tolerance |
| A Part's inspection ask | the composed blade scan at the post | `blade_program_warnings_excess` |
| Turning, nose kinds (facing, profile, chamfer, taper, multi-pass, boring) | envelope law (f) | already tightened by #864; they were only refused |
| Every turning kind | meridian rapid, bar-feed and holder scans | their margin (`fidelity_law::tightened(GOUGE_TOL, excess)`) |
| Rotary contour / parallel / offset | law (f) and the radial field law | the field law's band and rapid allowances (`rotary_law::rotary_into`) |
| 5-axis contour and parallel, flow, multi-axis contour and rough | law (f) | nothing new: a posed ball is the same ball about the same centre, so (f) is the cut's whole gouge verdict |

**Collision laws in `verify` (all kinds)**

- (c) shank and holder reach, and its mid-turn sweep (c3): each band grows by the excess (`VerifyContext::band_growth`) and the kerf that excuses the flutes' own cut shrinks by it.
- (d) rapids in stock: the footprint's slack gives the excess back; the posed second reading gives it back out of the depth it lets a leaning stack stand in the part.

**The gate**

- The floor is per kind (`fidelity_law::floor_of`): the smallest of the 0.01 mm laws, the envelope tolerance, the meridian scan's tolerance and a Part's inspection ask. A groove held to 0.004 mm is refused on a metre-unit file while a 0.05 mm groove on the same file is judged.
- The setup's stock counts: an operation is judged with the worse of its source's and its stock's excess (`material::judged_material`, `model_fidelity::op_coarse`), because the collision laws read clearance against the stock.

**Still refused, each for a stated reason** (`fidelity_law`'s header): swarf and advanced swarf (the flank is proved clear only inside the generator; no verify law re-measures it), the cone and engrave rides, probe, the cross drill and plasma.

Structure only, to stay under the 400-line law: the blade judgments moved from `revolve.rs` to `turning/blade_law.rs`, the threading verdicts from `thread.rs` to `turning/thread_law.rs`, the excess readings from `verify/types.rs` to `verify/excess.rs`. The existing `*_warnings` functions keep their signatures and forward with an excess of 0.

Decisions are recorded in `docs/decisions/904-reduced-fidelity-laws.md`.

## How tested

Each pin holds a cut between the tightened and the plain tolerance (silent at full fidelity, convicted on the coarse model), a flush cut (never convicted by the tightening), a real gouge (convicted at every excess) and the reading past the bound (untightened).

- `camcraft-motion` `turning_coarse` (6 tests): blade, thread and form scans, the composed program scan, the rest clause, `gouge_tol_on`.
- `camcraft-sim` `coarse_collision` (5 tests): reach (c), sweep (c3), rapid (d) on a 90-gon boss whose chord error is the excess, the posed rapid reading, `band_growth`.
- `camcraft-sim` `model_excess::the_envelope_laws_gouge_half_answers_to_the_tolerance_less_the_excess`: law (f) in `Mode::Envelope` and `Mode::Rotary` (#904's point 6 for the envelope law).
- `camcraft-app` lib: `rotary_law::tests` (band and rapid allowances move by the excess), `turning_rapids::tests::the_margin_generation_hands_the_law_shrinks_with_a_coarse_models_excess`.
- `camcraft-app` `coarse_laws` (6 tests), through the document: a groove judged at 0.012 mm, refused by name at 0.030 mm, and the per-kind floor on a metre-unit file; a thread asked 0.046 mm too deep convicted only on the reduced model; a probe ask judged at the tightened budget and refused when the excess uses it up; a rotary contour judged, still convicting rapids through stock, refused past the bound; every kind in the registry either judged or refused for its reason; a stock copied from a coarser model.
- `camcraft-app` `coarse_contain`: the containment solid law on a drill run 0.008 mm past a blind floor, on a model flagged 0.0075 mm (#904's point 6 for that law).

Quick gate on the final head `10a31636`: `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` - sim, motion, app and ui suites, 4 steps, 0 failed (12.8 min; it runs every suite mapped to `sim::verify`, `motion::turning` and `app::operation::generate`, `model_fidelity` and the existing turning, rotary and rapid suites included). `cargo clippy -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

## What was not exercised

- No document-level fixture for the turning margin or the rotary allowances: no generator emits a marginal graze on demand. They are pinned at the law with the value `generate` hands it.
- The multi-axis ball kinds are pinned by the registry test and by law (f)'s pin; no 5-axis operation was generated on a flagged model.
- The release tier (heavy lanes, UI snapshots) was not run.
- The excess is taken out along each law's own measure (a field ray, across a lean); on a surface oblique to that measure the mesh can stand further off than its chord error. Not corrected - noted in the decision record.

## Left open (filed)

- #1052 swarf's flank proof reads the excess (swarf stays refused until then).
- #1053 the cone and engrave rides, probe, the cross drill and plasma (with `rapids_radial`).
- #1054 the STEP facet budget as a setting (dialog, script verb, MCP `import_model`).
- #1055 metre-unit STEP scaled to millimetres before meshing.
- #1056 the flag gaps from #911's review (a stock copy after its source is deleted, older projects, the sim's gouge line near the refusal edge) and the display tolerances.
- #1057 **found while pinning, in the code #911 merged, not changed here:** a matched drill is convicted of a false gouge at its first plunge on a model flagged between about 0.0105 mm and the 0.015 mm bound. Law (b)'s 0.01 mm was sized to absorb our own regions' chord error and the excess takes it away. Safe side, but it blocks the post. The turning and rotary fixtures of this PR were run at 0.0105, 0.012, 0.0135 and 0.0149 mm and stay clean.

With these filed, everything #904 listed is either built here or has its own issue, so the umbrella can be closed when this merges.

Changelog: Turning, rotary and 5-axis ball operations are judged on a reduced-fidelity model with laws tightened by its excess (refused by name once nothing is left) instead of refused outright; shank/holder reach and rapid-in-stock checks read the excess too
Effort: max (not escalated)

Refs #904

title: fix(turning): judge a lathe holder body against chuck jaws and standing steel
body:
Stacked on #1043 (branch `issue/361-vendor-tool-models` on the mkinney fork). Upstream cannot base a PR on a fork branch, so this targets `main` and its diff shows #1043's commits as well. Merge #1043 first; after that, this PR's own diff is the single commit c965895f.

Fork synced at v0.18.0.

## What changed

A turning tool's lathe holder body (#369) was judged against the part and the stock only. The fixture laws swept the tool record's holder cylinder, which is 0 x 0 for a turning insert. So an offset holder running into a chuck jaw passed with no finding, while the op had dropped its "holder not judged" note because a body was present (P0: a holder hitting the chuck is a crash).

- **New law, `operation/turning_holder_steel.rs`.** Each move's meridian pieces (the holder law's own `pieces_of`) are read against every fixture box with each of the body's clearance spans (`LatheClearance::spans`). A strike is `FixtureHit { fixture_part: Holder }` on that move ("holder at move N strikes a fixture"), which blocks the post.
  - Steel that turns with the part (a chuck jaw, the fixture default) is read as its revolved envelope.
  - Standing steel (`SetFixtureFixed`: tailstock, steady rest, table) is a box in the machine frame: station, radial in the plane the moves are written in, and across that plane. The band keeps only |y|, so both sides are read.
  - For a straight tip motion each condition is an interval of the piece's parameter, so strikes are found exactly, not sampled. Boxes grow by the gouge tolerance (contact is contact, as in the fixture laws).
- **Same law at the post gate.** `fixture_struck::op_hits` (the live fixture walk and the struck-fixture view) runs it too, reading the op's part as generation does and the steel as it stands now. A part it cannot read is reported unjudged by name.
- **Unreadable steel is named.** A tagged fixture with no readable geometry has no box, and every box law passes over it. A bodied turning op now carries a note naming it (`STEEL_UNREAD_NOTE`, from `fixture::unreadable_for`).
- `turning_holder::pieces_of` is now `pub(super)`. `SignedMeridian` gains `suv` (station, radial, across-plane).

Decisions: `docs/decisions/1037-lathe-holder-steel.md`.

## How tested

Pinning tests, `crates/app/tests/turning_holder_steel.rs`:
- `an_offset_holder_reaching_a_chuck_jaw_blocks_naming_the_move`: an L holder whose leg stands clear of the part reaches a chuck jaw. There is no HolderHit; there is a holder FixtureHit, the post is refused naming the move, and the live gate walk gives the same moves.
- `the_same_holder_short_of_the_jaw_passes_and_posts`
- `a_standing_jaw_is_read_in_the_machine_frame_and_a_spinning_one_about_the_axis`: a jaw beside the tool's plane is struck while it spins and is clear once declared fixed. In the plane, fixed, it is struck.
- `a_fixture_the_law_cannot_read_is_named_on_the_op`
- Unit test: `operation::turning_holder_steel::tests::a_band_meets_a_box_exactly_along_a_straight_tip_motion`.

Quick gate (`cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/issue/361-vendor-tool-models`) green: the app suites (lib plus 120 suites, the new one included, 629 s) and 6 ui suites (116 s), 0 failed. By hand, also green: `turning_insert_zone`, `vendor_tool_body`, `mcp_tool_body`, `carried_fixtures_cache`, `sim_tool_body`, and `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`. After a final prefilter edit (skip steel the body's length cannot reach), `turning_holder_steel`, `turning_holder`, `fixtures`, `vendor_tool_body`, the lib unit tests and clippy were run again: green. No golden or snapshot changed.

## Not exercised

- Real vendor chuck or tailstock models: only box fixtures. A mesh fixture is read by its box (conservative; the mesh acquittal of #339 is not applied to this law).
- A spindle off a world axis: the reading there is conservative by construction, but no test covers it.
- GUI: no new UI. The finding shows through the existing fixture-hit paths.

## Overlap

#904 (reduced-fidelity turning/rotary/multiaxis laws) is in flight on main. This PR adds a module and one call after the holder law in `generate.rs`, and touches `turning_holder.rs` only to make `pieces_of` visible.

Changelog: A lathe holder body is judged against the setup's workholding: a chuck jaw as its revolved envelope, standing steel (tailstock, steady rest) in the machine frame, a strike blocking the post by move; a fixture with no readable geometry is named on the op (#1037)

Effort: high (not escalated)

Fixes #1037

title: feat(tools): tool library import modes - add, update in place, replace
body:
Fork synced at v0.18.0 (branch cut from upstream/main 3e9b8ae1).

## What changed
`ImportTools` gains an explicit `ImportMode` (`ImportTools::with_mode`; `new` = Add, so existing behaviour and tests hold):
- **Add** (default): skip identical, rename a different duplicate to `Name (2)`.
- **Update**: a same-named tool takes the imported definition in place (same entity, controller number kept, operations using it read Stale); identical skipped; unmatched names added.
- **Replace**: Update, and document tools the library lacks are removed. If an operation uses such a tool the whole import is refused by tool and operation name, nothing applied.
Update/Replace run the `ChangeTool` gates (torch, retype stranding an op, body/cutter fit) and refuse a name that is not a tool. One undo unit (removal uses the `DeleteTool` snapshot, so undo restores number/body/cutter). `ImportReport` gains `updated`/`replaced`/`removed`. GUI: a mode combo beside "Import library..."; `cam.importTools(path, mode?)` and MCP `import_tool_library` take `mode` (cam.d.ts updated). Key is the tool name; #898's part number is the intended future key (decision file `docs/decisions/899-tool-import-modes.md`).

## Tested

title: feat(turning): a setup's workholding max rpm caps G96 and refuses G97 above it
body:
**Stacked on #990** (#891, `issue/891-lathe-cutting-data`). Until #990 merges, this diff also shows #990's commits; this PR's own work is the last commit. Retarget to `main` happens before #990 merges (AGENTS.md "Overlapping issues stack").

Fork synced at v0.18.0 (PROCESS_VERSION 16).

## What changed

A lathe setup can now state the rated maximum rpm of its chuck or collet.

- **Model**: `SetupDef::workholding_max_rpm: Option<f64>` (`None` means none is stated, which is the default and what every older file loads as). It is read through the new `camcraft_app::setup_workholding` module.
- **Command**: `SetSetupWorkholdingRpm::new(world, setup, Option<f64>)` is undoable. It refuses a value that is not finite, is under 1 rpm or is over 100 000 rpm, and it refuses a no-op. It also refuses a name that is not a setup.
- **G96**: the per-section CSS ceiling (#891's `PARAM MaxSpindleSpeed`) becomes min(tool, workholding). Both lathe posts already take the lower of that and the machine's maximum, so `G50 S` (Fanuc) and `G96 D` (Tormach) come out as min(machine, tool, workholding). **No post script changed.**
- **G97**: an operation that turns the work (the spindle law's `turns`) at a constant rpm above its setup's limit is **refused by name** at the program gate (`verification_report`). It is never capped. Example line: `F1: turns the work at 2500 rpm (G97), over setup 'Setup1''s workholding maximum of 2000 rpm - ...`. Every post route and `verify` read this same gate.
- **Suggestion**: the turning "Suggest feeds & speeds" is held to the limit, with a note, and keeps the per-rev feed.
- **Datum transfer**: `CreateSetup` with `datum_from` keeps the source setup's rating. Dropping it would quietly lift a safety ceiling.
- **Project file**: a new additive `workholding_max_rpm` key on a setup, with no version step. It is written only when stated. A value no command would accept is a corrupt file and is refused naming the setup.
- **MCP**: a new tool `set_workholding_max_rpm` `{max_rpm: number|null, setup?}` in `crates/app/src/mcp/workholding_tools.rs`. It is one undo step through the same command. `get_job` setups now report `workholding_max_rpm`.
- **UI**: a "Workholding max rpm" row on a setup's Settings page (value, Apply rpm, Clear rpm). It shows on a lathe or mill-turn setup, or on any setup that already states a limit. It queues `CommandKind::SetSetupWorkholdingRpm` and the drain lands the command.
- Decisions: `docs/decisions/1031-workholding-max-rpm.md`.

## Tests (pinning)

- `crates/app/tests/lathe_workholding_rpm.rs`. This is a new sibling suite, because `lathe_post_css` is at 373 lines.
  - `a_2000_rpm_chuck_clamps_g96_under_a_higher_tool_and_machine_in_both_dialects`: `G50 S2000\nG96 S170 M03` and `G96 D2000 S170 M3` on a 12000 rpm machine, with a tool clamp of none or 3000. A tool rated lower (1500) keeps its own clamp.
  - `a_g97_op_over_the_chuck_is_refused_by_name_never_capped`: 2500 rpm against a 2000 rpm chuck is refused at the gate and by `post_script`, naming the op and the setup. Raising the limit clears the refusal, and undo brings it back. With no limit stated, the op posts `G97 S2500` as before.
  - `the_limit_is_one_validated_undoable_command`: insane values, a no-op and a non-setup are refused; undo and redo work; a datum transfer keeps the rating.
  - `the_turning_suggestion_is_held_to_the_chuck`
  - `the_limit_is_additive_in_the_project_file_and_round_trips_byte_identical`: an older file loads with none; a corrupt value is refused by name; an unstated limit writes no key.
- `crates/app/tests/mcp_workholding.rs`: `set_workholding_max_rpm_states_clears_and_undoes_the_chucks_rating`
- `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests/structural.rs`: `setup_page_workholding_rpm_row_structure`, the structural twin. A mill setup has no row; a lathe setup shows it; Apply lands one undo step; Clear shows once a limit is stated.

## Gate

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` on head `ef57929b`: **green**, 5 steps, 0 failed, 24.1 min wall. The base is upstream/main, so it also covers #990's diff, and its plan ran every app suite, lathe_post_css, lathe_post, lathe_post_refusals, lathe_post_tormach, lathe_spindle_law, lathe_spindle_fit, lathe_spindle_keyed, project_roundtrip, setups, mcp_setup, mcp, mcp_workholding and lathe_workholding_rpm among them. The ui lib, structural twin included, passed too.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

## Not exercised

- No real control was run. The posted words are checked against the Fanuc and Tormach scripts in the engine only.
- No new golden was added, and no existing golden or snapshot PNG changed.
- No script verb was added for the command. The MCP tool covers headless use.
- The `camcraft-mcp` skill's tool table (`.claude/skills/`) is not updated. It is a process file, and changing it needs a PROCESS_VERSION bump, so it is left to a process PR.
- The rating is not checked against the machine's spindle minimum. A chuck rated under the machine's minimum is not flagged.

Changelog: Turning: a setup can state its chuck or collet's maximum rpm (Setups page, MCP `set_workholding_max_rpm`); G96 clamps to min(machine, tool, workholding) and a G97 turning op over it is refused by name (#1031)

Effort: high (no escalation)

Fixes #1031

title: fix(thread): refuse a hole the program ahead has not drilled
body:
Stacked on #1005 (base branch content: `issue/894-thread-mill`; this PR targets `main`, so until #1005 merges its diff also shows #1005's commit - the #992 change is the top commit only).

Fork synced at v0.18.0.

## What changed

A thread mill is not centre-cutting, and the #1005 ride feeds it down the hole's axis at plunge feed. Nothing checked that an earlier operation had opened the hole, so a forgotten tap drill posted a thread mill into solid metal. Now:

- **Generate refuses an undrilled hole by name** (`crates/app/src/operation/thread_entry.rs`, called from the Thread arm of `operation::generate`). Each threaded hole is read in the stock the setup's earlier operations leave standing - the same lazily cut prior grid the drilling and rapid laws read (`drill_prior::PriorCell`). The stock over the hole's minor circle (less one grid cell, never narrower than the mill) must stand at or below the lowest point the path takes the mill to in that hole. Otherwise: "the hole at (x, y) is not drilled yet: the stock the program ahead leaves stands at z .. inside it, above the thread mill's lowest point at z .. - a thread mill does not cut at its centre - add a drilling operation of at least the .. mm minor diameter, deep enough for its point, before the thread".
- **Unknown is refused, never read as air**: nothing ahead cut, a program ahead the grid cannot cut, a posed Thread, a distrusted carried prior, a hole off the grid.
- **Reordering**: an unposed op's stamp already digests the program ahead (#109), so moving the Drill after the Thread marks the Thread Stale, and regenerating it refuses. Pinned, no new stamp code.
- Test fixtures: the #894 thread suites' shared fixtures moved to `crates/app/tests/thread_support/mod.rs`. The modelled hole now runs to z 4 (the tap drill's depth), deeper than the thread's floor at z 8, and every thread there has a Drill operation ahead. `mill2d_c`'s R10 thread gets a 20 mm drill ahead. The MCP thread test now pins generate's refusal on the undrilled block.

Decisions: `docs/decisions/992-thread-undrilled.md`.

## How tested

Pinning tests:
- `camcraft-app --test thread_entry` (new, 5): `a_thread_with_nothing_drilled_ahead_is_refused_by_name`, `a_tap_drill_ahead_opens_the_hole_and_the_thread_verifies_clean` (generator verdict, post gate and program sim clean), `a_drill_of_the_mills_own_diameter_opens_the_hole_too`, `a_drill_too_narrow_or_too_shallow_is_refused`, `moving_the_drill_after_the_thread_marks_it_stale_and_refuses_it` (Stale, post gate shut, regeneration refused, undo restores Ok).
- `camcraft-app` (lib): `operation::thread_entry::tests::*` (4): drilled/exact-depth air, solid / shallow / narrow refusals by name, unknown prior and off-grid refusals, a hole the path never enters.
- Updated: `--test thread_mill` (all 8, now drilled first), `--test mill2d_c` `thread_helices_are_timed_by_the_tools_pitch`, `--test mcp` `thread_milling_over_the_tools`.

Quick gate: `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/issue/894-thread-mill` - app suites (every suite: the shared test fixture changed) and the gate-mapped ui suites, 2 steps, 0 failed (14.4 min). After it, a clippy-only type alias went into `tests/mill2d_c.rs`; `--test mill2d_c` re-run green on the final head `58b4c7db`. `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

Goldens: `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/thread_mill_m8_multi_form.nc` moved - the program now carries the Drill operation ahead (`G81 ... Z4 R20`) and the thread mill is T02; the thread's own blocks are byte-identical. No CL golden moved.

## What was not exercised

- A stock that already has the hole cored (a FromModel stock) with nothing ahead is refused, not acquitted (decision 3; cheap to add later).
- Posed (3+2) thread milling is refused by this law (no frame-aware prior reading).
- The milled Bore ride's axis entry has the same gap: filed as #1036.
- The heavy `--ignored` release lanes; posts other than Fanuc.

Changelog: A Thread operation whose hole the program ahead has not drilled (to the minor diameter, below the thread) is refused by name at generate instead of feeding a non-centre-cutting thread mill into solid stock (#992).

Effort: high (no escalation)

Fixes #992

title: feat(app): refusal ghost where a frame map or a merge came first
body:
**Stacked on #1016 and #993** (merge order: #957, #993, #1016, then this). SKULL merged #993's branch in (aeff62af) because both change the cross-drill call lines in `operation/cross_spindle.rs`: kept #993's `cutter` arguments and this PR's ghost `map_err` on every line. Until the parents merge, this diff also shows their commits.

**Stacked on #1016** (issue #871, branch `issue/871-refusal-ghost-rest`). Until #1016 merges, this diff also shows its commits. Only `78fd6e80` belongs to this PR. Retarget/merge order: #1016 first.

Fork synced at v0.18.0 (mkinney/Camcraft, PROCESS_VERSION 16).

## What changed

These are the part-way refusals #871 listed as owed. Each now hands back its partial path in the frame of the path the generator returns, so it lands where the part is once `run_job` maps that frame (none, or a 3+2 tilt through `world_path`). Where a generator plans in a frame of its own and maps out at the end, the ghost takes the same map the path takes. Success paths are untouched. Every change is a `map_err` on an error path, plus one new merge (`GenError::after_moves` / `Ghost::after`).

| Site | Result |
|---|---|
| finishing3d raster: crossing pass, `rings_and_tail` (parallel, blend, radial, spiral, flow, shadow), `swarf_multi` rungs | **ghost in world** (moves built so far, output frame) |
| finishing3d `waterline` (rings) | **ghost adopted**. Today only first-level refusals (non-finite facet, geo error) can reach it, so nothing shows yet |
| Rotary Contour / Parallel: `waterline` / `swarf` on frame-local facets | **ghost in world**, via `rotary::to_world`. It goes through `posed`, the same pose law and world exit the finished path takes. A ghost `posed` refuses is dropped. The spot rides `f.to_world` |
| Rotary links (`radial_relink`) | **ghost in world** (passes linked so far, carried out the same way) |
| Rotary posing (`posed`) itself | **listed**: cycle or empty base (nothing to show), finite-horizon tail |
| 5-axis stamp shank refusal (Multi-Axis Rough, Contour/Parallel/Flow 5D, swarf) | **ghost in world**: the plan before the refused move (world, unposed, so tips are within one ball radius of the posed ones). Posing a prefix is listed as dropped, with the reason |
| Contour/Parallel/Swarf 5D: refusal inside the finishing plan | **ghost in world** (the plan's own, passed up) |
| Swarf link laws (`link_swings`, `guard_turns`) | **ghost in world** (the posed path they judged). No fixture reaches these today |
| Multi-axis curve walk (`contour_curve`) | **ghost in world** (chains walked before the refused one). `curve_walk::walk` itself holds rests, not moves (**listed**) |
| Rotary gate (`stamp_spindle_c`) | **ghost in world** (the kernel path it judged) |
| Rotary letter gate (`rotary_letter`) | **listed**: it runs before any move |
| Fixture route (`plan_links` Unreachable) | **ghost in world** (upright mill, frame None) |
| Cross drill `rapids_clear`, `cross_holder` | **ghost in world**: the spindle-frame chain moved back by the same `(ox, oy)` shift. A chain with arcs gets no ghost |
| Cross drill `part_clear` | **ghost in world** (the world chain it judged) |
| Nested: `pocket3d_air_split` material leg, `run_rest` rest ladder, stitched contour runs | **merged**: `after_moves` puts the outer moves in front of the inner ghost. Rotary Offset, the only air-split caller, still drops the ghost on purpose (development space) |
| `run_rest`'s sim steps between the ladders | **listed** (not in the issue; could take `with_ghost(&coarse)` later) |
| Face under an area turn | **handled by #1023** (`boundary_turn::turn_refusal` / `face_over_back`). `boundary_turn.rs` and the Face call sites are not touched here |

The decisions and reasons are in `docs/decisions/1015-ghost-frames.md`.

## Tests (pinning)

- `motion/tests/refusal_ghost_frames.rs` (new):
  - `the_raster_refused_at_its_rings_hands_back_the_world_raster`: on an off-origin plate, the ghost equals the opening of the successful world path move for move. `parallel5d` hands back the same world plan.
  - `the_rotary_parallel_ghost_rides_the_pose_law_to_the_world_bar`: on a bar laid off-origin, the ghost's cut tips lie on the world bar's skin and coincide (within 1e-6) with tips of the posted path. Nothing of the ghost stands inside the work.
  - `a_refused_drive_curve_hands_back_the_chains_walked_before_it`: the ghost equals the lone first chain's path minus its closing retract. A first-chain refusal has no ghost.
- `motion/tests/multiaxis_avoid.rs::the_shank_refusal_hands_back_the_world_plan_before_its_move`: the ghost is a prefix of the unposed world 3-D ladder.
- `motion` lib: `ghost::tests::the_outer_moves_stand_in_front_and_a_bad_join_is_refused` and `gen_error::tests::a_nested_refusal_shows_the_outer_moves_then_its_own` (the Ghost merge).
- `app` lib: `rotary_gate::tests::a_gate_refusal_hands_back_the_world_path_it_judged` and `cross_spindle::tests::an_app_side_law_refusal_carries_the_chain_to_the_world`.

## Gate

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` on this head: green, all 4 steps (motion suites incl. refusal_ghost, refusal_ghost_frames, rotary, rotary_links, rotary_offset, pivot5d, flow, ruling, swarf_pose_continuity; app suites incl. refusal_ghost, drilling_cross_*, fixture_route, c_axis_*, center_cut_multiaxis; ui lib incl. refusal_ghost).
- Extra: app golden_cl, conformance, solid_law_goldens, rotary_field_parity/fixtures/letter/verify; motion multiaxis, multiaxis_rough, swarf_reentry, multiaxis_avoid; clippy -D warnings on motion + app. all green (golden_cl 25, conformance 6, rotary_verify 9, ...; clippy clean).
- **Goldens byte-identical**: no golden file changed, and golden_cl and conformance pass unchanged. No snapshot PNG touched.

## Not exercised

- `link_swings` / `guard_turns` refusals and `radial_relink`'s part-way lift refusal: no fixture reaches them. The wiring is the same one-liner the pinned sites use, over a path already in world.
- The nested merges at their real sites (air-split material leg, rest ladder, stitched run): pinned by the merge unit tests only. No fixture refuses mid-leg.

Changelog: A refusal that stops part-way through a rotary, 5-axis, curve, cross-drill, fixture-route, C-gate or nested (rest / air-split / stitched) generation now shows the path built so far where the part is (#1015)

Fixes #1015

title: feat(tools): place a lathe holder body from the tool editor and MCP
body:
Makes a lathe holder body reachable: the tool editor and the MCP server can now give a turning tool a holder from a STEP, STL or OBJ file, placed in the turning tool frame. The judging law (#369) and its insert zone (#396) already existed, but nothing a user could reach led to them.

Fork synced at v0.18.0 (branch cut from upstream/main 3e9b8ae1).

## Where #361 stood

The triage split (#368, #369, #370, #371) has all shipped. What was missing is the case the issue names first, asymmetric lathe tooling:

- The tool editor placed every body along a spindle axis, so Apply body on a turning tool was refused with "lathe holders are placed in the turning tool frame" and the GUI had no way to do that.
- The MCP server had no tool-body tool; the camcraft-mcp skill listed it as a known gap.

## What changed

- **Tool editor.** On a lathe-held tool the Body section places the imported file in the turning tool frame: radial and spindle directions (a preset or a picked face normal), the tip (numbers or a picked corner) and an optional insert zone. Apply body queues the existing `SetToolBody::lathe`, one undo step. A boring bar, which serves both machines, gets a frame switch. Milling tools are unchanged.
- **MCP.** Five tools in `crates/app/src/mcp/body_tools.rs`: `get_tool_body`, `set_tool_body` (by numbers, or by a STEP's ISO 13399 coordinate systems), `set_lathe_tool_body`, `set_lathe_insert_zone`, `clear_tool_body`. Each write is one `SetToolBody`.
- **Safety: a reduced-fidelity STEP is refused as a tool body.** Every body-file path used `load_model`, which drops #864's chord error. A coarsely meshed holder reads smaller than the holder is, so its collision checks were too generous with nothing said. All body files now pass one door (`tool_body_file`), which refuses such a file by name and says to simplify the model. This touches only the tool-body readers, not the part laws #904 is working on.
- **Process.** The camcraft-mcp skill lists the new tools and drops the gap; `PROCESS_VERSION` 16 -> 17.
- **Fixture.** `testdata/models/lathe_holder_offset.step` is our own extruded L (an offset holder), written by a small script. No vendor file was read or committed.

No new judging law and no change to posted output for existing documents. Decisions are in `docs/decisions/361-vendor-tool-models.md`.

## How tested

Quick gate (`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`) green on 1a6d4017: 26 app suites and the ui lib plus 10 ui suites, 0 failed. Also run and green: `tool_body`, `turning_holder`, `tool_csys`, `turning_insert_zone`, `holder_library`, `tool_body_judged`, `tool_body_bands`, and `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`.

Pinning tests:

- `crates/app/tests/vendor_tool_body.rs`
  - `a_step_lathe_holder_placed_off_its_model_frame_is_judged_and_its_mirror_stands_clear`: the STEP holder rubs the part's shoulder (3.2 mm short, post blocked); the same file with the spindle direction reversed is clear.
  - `a_step_meshed_coarser_than_promised_is_refused_as_a_tool_body_by_name`: all five file doors refuse.
  - `the_lathe_placement_preview_is_the_commands_own_reading`
- `crates/app/tests/mcp_tool_body.rs` (5 tests): both frames, the insert zone, undo/redo, and every refusal by name.
- `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests/tool_body_lathe.rs` (6 tests): Apply body lands one undoable command, a non-square placement and an oversized zone are refused by name, picks fill only the draft, the boring bar's frame switch, the coarse-STEP refusal at import.

I also rendered the editor once at 1280x720 to check the lathe section fits; no snapshot PNG is changed.

## Not exercised

- No real vendor STEP was tried (none may be committed, and none was used); the fixture is eight planar faces.
- The picks were tested through the state calls, not by clicking the 3D preview.
- No hands-on run of the GUI beyond the one rendered frame.
- Inch documents: the lathe fields use the same unit lens as the other fields, but no test types an inch value into them.

## Still owed on #361

- #1037 (P1): the lathe holder body is judged against part and stock only, not workholding or fixtures.
- #1038: the lathe body is not drawn in the simulation or viewport.
- #1039: a lathe placement from a file's ISO 13399 coordinate systems.
- #1040: a tool assembled from several vendor bodies (the ISO 26622 / 26623 interfaces the issue names).
- #1041: judge a reduced-fidelity body grown by its chord error instead of refusing it.
- Imported bodies in `.camtools` library files ride #889.

Changelog: Lathe holder bodies from the tool editor and MCP: a turning tool's STEP holder is placed in the turning tool frame (directions, tip, insert zone); MCP `get_tool_body`, `set_tool_body`, `set_lathe_tool_body`, `set_lathe_insert_zone`, `clear_tool_body`; a STEP too detailed to mesh at full fidelity is refused as a tool body (#361)

title: fix(post): the Fanuc lathe seats an off-seat face cycle by the hop law
body:
**Stacked on #1025 (on #975, #964).** This branch was cut from `issue/1011-lathe-cycle-exit`, so until those three merge, its diff also shows their commits. Merge order: #964, #975, #1025, then this one. Only the top commit, `fix(post): the Fanuc lathe seats an off-seat face cycle by the hop law`, belongs to this PR.

## What changed

`assets/posts/fanuc-lathe.cps` now uses #994's `cycleSeat`. A face cycle (G83/G84/G85) is read with the tool on centre at R. When the cycle record arrives with the tool somewhere else, the post seats it with the hop law:

1. If the tool is below R, `G00 Z<R>` first (out of the work).
2. If it is off centre, `G00 X0` (onto the centre at the safe level).
3. If it is above R, `G00 Z<R>` (down to the seat).

This replaces the old single `G00 X0 Z<R>`, which was one diagonal X+Z rapid. If a group is still open, `G80` is written before the seat moves.

**Axis assumption.** "Away from the work" is +Z. That is the post's own Z law: Z runs along the spindle axis with the face at the free end, face cycles drill toward -Z from R, and #1011's `onHole` (`Z <= R`) already relies on it. It also matches the usual public lathe G-code convention, where Z+ points away from the chuck and the face. The post does not just assume this: it checks the record's bottom is below its R.

**Refused by name, no cycle written.** These cycles cannot be seated:
- the cycle is its section's first motion, so there is no stream position to seat from ("approach the hole first");
- the record's bottom is not below its R ("cannot tell which way is clear of the face");
- a legacy record has no R and starts off the axis.

**tormach-lathe** is unchanged. It writes no cycle and no positioning block of its own. A new pin shows that every motion line it posts is one of the stream's moves, in order.

Decision record: `docs/decisions/1026-lathe-cycle-seat.md`.

### Before / after

The synthetic stream reads the cycle at radius 15, Z18, with R22, bottom 10 and exit 40.

Before (parent's .cps):
```
G00 X30 Z18
G00 X0 Z22        <- one X+Z rapid, below R toward the face
G83 Z10 F0.1
G80
G00 X0 Z40
```
After:
```
G00 X30 Z18
G00 Z22
G00 X0
G83 Z10 F0.1
G80
G00 X0 Z40
```
From above R (X30 Z30), the order is `G00 X0` then `G00 Z22`.

## Tests

`crates/app/tests/lathe_cycle_exit.rs`:
- The #1011 read-back checker now also reads the seat. Before the hole, a move that changes X from a known position must stay at Z >= R, and the face cycle must be read on X0 at R.
- New tests:
  - `fanuc_lathe_seats_an_off_seat_face_cycle_by_the_hop_law`: below R and above R, both off centre.
  - `fanuc_lathe_refuses_a_face_cycle_it_cannot_seat_by_name`: a first-motion cycle, and R below the bottom.
  - `tormach_lathe_adds_no_positioning_move_to_an_off_seat_face_cycle`.
  - `the_checker_catches_an_off_seat_cycle_reached_by_one_diagonal`.
- The existing `both_lathe_posts_leave_a_face_drilled_hole_at_the_streams_exit` runs with the seat check on both posts and still passes.

`crates/app/tests/lathe_post_refusals.rs`: two synthetic fixtures read the cycle as the section's first motion, which is now refused. They gain the approach rapid that the generator's streams carry, and their assertions are unchanged:
- `a_face_cycle_ends_on_the_rapid_leaving_its_hole_and_refuses_a_cut_that_leaves`
- `a_section_without_surface_speed_posts_g97_after_one_with_it`

**Revert check.** With the parent's `fanuc-lathe.cps` put back, both fanuc tests fail. The seat test fails with ``line 11: `G00 X0 Z22` moves X at Z18, below the seat Z22``, and the refusal test fails because no refusal is raised. The checker and tormach tests pass either way.

**Goldens.** No golden moved. The axial-drill stream approaches R on centre before its cycle, so `golden/nc/fanuc-lathe/axial_drill.nc` is unchanged (`lathe_post` and `golden_cl` are green).

**Gate.** `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` on the final head: green (1 step, every app suite the stack touches, 25.3 min, 0 failed). By hand: lathe_cycle_exit, lathe_post, lathe_post_refusals, lathe_post_g76, lathe_post_tormach, drilling_axial, posting, golden_cl, conformance and c_axis_live, plus the other suites that post on fanuc-lathe (lathe_spindle_law, program_entry, c_axis_unwind, wear_comp, lathe_blade_corner, comment_escape, coolant_followups, control_comp, lathe_nose_tip, inverted_post, turning_face_approach, drill_prior, drill_prior_kinds) and camcraft-post `comp`: all green (23 app binaries + post `comp`); clippy `-D warnings` clean on the two touched test binaries.

## Not exercised

- No real control or simulator run of the seated sequence.
- No G84/G85 off-seat stream. Their seating takes the same path as G83 (the seat code does not depend on the cycle word).
- No stream with an inverted Z machine axis. `invert::apply` mirrors the stream before the post, and no shipped lathe states one.

Changelog: The Fanuc lathe post seats a face cycle read off its hole by the hop law (Z out to R, onto the centre, down), never one diagonal rapid; one it cannot seat is refused by name (#1026)

title: fix(xtask): quick maps a #[path]-included file to its parent's submodule
body:
Stacked on #972 (which stacks on #967 and #965). Fork synced at v0.18.0.

## What changed
`cargo xtask gate quick` now also maps a source file that a sibling includes with `#[path = "x.rs"] mod name;` to `(parent, name)`, the module the compiler sees. This is a union with the file's own name, so it never selects fewer suites. Before, it took the file name as a top-level module. `crates/app/src/posting_index_swing.rs` is `app::posting::index_swing`, and the suites already name it `app::posting (index_swing)` correctly. The plan read it as `app::posting_index_swing`, which no map names, so a change to the index-swing safety law selected no suites.

- New `xtask/src/path_mods.rs` (`included_as`), hooked into `quick::plan`.
- It covers every `#[path]` file in the tree (posting's nine siblings, stock_sim, drill_reach, ui state, ...) without touching any suite header.
- Decision: `docs/decisions/1021-path-included-modules.md`. Fixing the plan rather than renaming the maps, which were right.
- `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION` → 20, because xtask is a process file. A fork needs nothing beyond the normal process sync.

## How tested
- `cargo test -p xtask`: 44 passed. After review, the pin also asserts that posting_sim still selects wall_column_gouge and contour_arc_sim, posting_suppressed selects rest_across_setups, and posting_plasma selects plasma_gate.
- Earlier pin text: The new pin is `gate_maps_tests::a_path_included_file_selects_its_parents_submodule_suites`: a change to `posting_index_swing.rs` selects `index_swing`, narrows below all of `app::posting`, and the other posting siblings select suites.

Not exercised: #1020's `index_swing_horizontal` suite isn't on this branch. Its map uses the same `app::posting (index_swing)` spelling, so it will be selected the same way.

title: feat(fixtures): edit and re-fit a placed mod vise pair
body:
## What changed

This PR covers parts 2-4 of #832: editing a placed mod vise pair, re-fitting it, and the follow-ups from the #833 review. Part 1, the dual-station block, is **not** in it. Why is under "Held back" below.

**New undoable commands** (`crates/app/src/commands/mod_vise_edit.rs`), one undo step each:
- **`SetModJaw`** changes a placed jaw block's figures, its insert, and, on an adjustable block, its slide. It regenerates the block's solid through `UpdateModel`, as `SetVise` does, and swaps the marker in the same step. The block stays on its hole and turn. It is refused by name when:
  - the edit would change the block's side;
  - a figure breaks the block law;
  - a bolt or pin would land off the grid where the block stands (new `modvise::fit::footprint_at`);
  - the block would hang off the plate (the plate seat check);
  - the clamping face would reach into the stock.

  A jaw lifted off the stock is a warning.
- **`RefitModVise`** re-fits the adjustable block to the stock as it stands now. It runs the same `fit_pair` the pair was placed with, with the fixed block where it stands, and re-picks the adjustable block's hole and slide. Every refusal of the fit is passed on by name, and nothing moves.
  - `RefitModVise::to_partner` finds the single fixed jaw block on the same plate. If there are none, or several, it refuses and names them.

**Follow-ups from the #833 review:**
- `SetPlate`'s jaw check now goes through `judge_face`, which `SetModJaw` shares. A face that was not in front of the stock before the edit (`face_gap == None`) counts as clear. The reviewer's probe used to pass with only a warning and is now refused: the stock moved +130 mm in X, then one plate edit (pitch X +10, pitch Y -2) puts the adjustable jaw 16 mm into it.
- `mcp_plate` now asserts the `warning` field that `set_fixture_plate` returns (null when clear). `mcp_mod_vise` pins a non-null warning: a plate edit that lifts the fixed jaw 2 mm off the stock.

**MCP tools** (`crates/app/src/mcp/modvise_tools.rs`):
- `set_mod_jaw {name, figures{..., slide}, insert}` returns the block and its `warning`.
- `refit_mod_vise {adjustable, fixed?}` returns the hole, turn, location, slide, opening, fixed_gap and warning.

**UI:** each jaw block's row on the Fixtures page now has:
- "Edit jaw block…" with body height, jaw height, jaw thickness, face offset, slide (adjustable block only), soft jaw, and a "Set figures" button that queues `SetModJaw`;
- "Re-fit to stock" on the adjustable block, which queues `RefitModVise`.

Warnings go through `with_warning` into the status line.

**Save/load:** no new key. Both commands write only the existing `mod_jaw` and `on_plate` fields, which #830's lenient `fixture_keys` reader already loads (through `modvise_dto`). Old files load unchanged.

**Decision record:** `docs/decisions/832-mod-vise-edit-refit.md`

## Held back: the dual-station block (part 1)
A dual-station block clamps two workpieces. A setup holds one stock, and fixtures are judged per setup (`fixture::tagged`). There are two ways to give the second station a stock, and both break the Prime Directive:
- Take the second station's stock from another setup. That setup's program would never see the vise steel, so a gouge would go unflagged.
- Put a copy of the steel in each setup. The copies then clash with each other.

Leaving the second station empty is not "fitted per station". This needs a multi-stock design decision first (effort:max or research). #832 stays open for it (`Refs #832`).

## How tested
Pinning tests:
- `crates/app/tests/mod_vise_edit.rs` (new):
  - `a_figure_edit_regenerates_the_block_where_it_stands_in_one_undo`
  - `a_figure_edit_is_refused_by_name_and_a_lifted_jaw_warns`
  - `a_refit_after_the_stock_changed_re_picks_the_hole_and_slide_in_one_undo` (three stock depths: H16, J16, I16; face on the stock to 1e-6; undo and redo exact to the bit)
  - `a_refit_that_cannot_fit_is_refused_by_name_and_nothing_moves`
  - `a_plate_edit_that_brings_a_jaw_into_a_stock_it_was_beside_is_refused` (the #833 probe; it fails with the old `None`-skip in place)
  - `an_edited_and_re_fitted_pair_survives_a_save`
- `crates/app/tests/mcp_mod_vise.rs`: `a_placed_pair_is_edited_and_re_fitted_over_mcp`
- `crates/app/tests/mcp_plate.rs`: the `warning` field assertion.
- Structural UI twin, `crates/ui/src/egui_app/fixture_modvise_tests.rs`:
  - `a_jaw_block_row_edits_its_figures_in_one_undoable_step`
  - `the_adjustable_row_re_fits_the_block_to_a_changed_stock`
  - `a_refused_refit_is_named_in_the_status`

Gates on the final head (c4cab3dc), Linux:
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: green (app suites 581 s, mcp_plate, ui suites 60 s; 0 failed). It covered mod_vise, mod_vise_edit, mod_vise_plate, mcp_mod_vise, mcp_plate, fixtures, fixture_plate*, fixture_keys_lenient, project_roundtrip and the ui lib.
- `cargo test --test fixture_law_gaps`: ok (3).
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo xtask gate test a_plate_edit_that_brings_a_jaw_into_a_stock_it_was_beside_is_refused`: ok.

## Not exercised
- The dual-station block (held back, above).
- Re-fitting with `MountAt::Dowels`. Jaw blocks are only ever placed on holes, so that case is refused by name and not fitted.
- Re-fitting a pair turned 90 or 270 degrees is covered only through `fit_pair`'s existing quarter-turn tests, not by its own test.
- No snapshot PNG was changed.

Changelog: Mod vises: a placed jaw block's figures can be edited (`SetModJaw`, MCP `set_mod_jaw`) and the adjustable block re-fitted to a changed stock (`RefitModVise`, MCP `refit_mod_vise`), one undo each; a plate edit that brings a jaw from beside the stock into it is now refused (#832)

title: fix(post): the Fanuc lathe leaves a face-drilled hole at the stream's exit, not at R
body:
**Stacked on #975 (on #964).** This branch starts at #975's head (`issue/966-lathe-c-no-rate`, which sits on #964's `issue/906-c-unwind-rate-cap`), because all three edit `assets/posts/fanuc-lathe.cps`. Until they merge, this diff also shows their commits. This PR's own change is the single commit `fix(post): the Fanuc lathe leaves a face-drilled hole at the stream's exit`. Retarget/merge order follows AGENTS.md "Overlapping issues stack": #964, then #975, then this one, after `git merge origin/main`.

## What changed

`assets/posts/fanuc-lathe.cps` swallowed every move after a face cycle (G83/G84/G85) until the section ended. So the chain's exit rapid up to clearance never posted: the tool left the hole at R, and `G28 U0 W0` (X and Z together) started from below the verified path.

The fix applies #994's hop law (PR #1019, for the mill posts) to the lathe:
- The cycle replaces only the chain that stays on its hole: the hole's XY (on centre), at or below R (`onHole`).
- The first rapid that leaves the hole ends the group with `G80` and is posted as the stream says (`chainRapid`).
- A feed or arc that leaves the hole inside an open group is refused by name: "a cutting move leaves its hole inside a face-cycle group" (`chainCut`).
- A legacy cycle record with no R word keeps the whole on-axis chain swallowed, as before.

`assets/posts/tormach-lathe.cps` doesn't have the bug and is unchanged. It writes no canned cycle and posts the whole chain as plain moves, so its `axial_drill_mm.nc` / `axial_drill_inch.nc` goldens already end with `G0 X0 Z30` before `G30`. The new read-back pin runs on it too.

The decisions (and what was dropped) are in `docs/decisions/1011-lathe-cycle-exit.md`.

## Before / after (`crates/app/tests/golden/nc/fanuc-lathe/axial_drill.nc`, clearance 30, R 20)

```
 G00 X0 Z20
 G83 Z10 Q12000 F0.008
 G80
+G00 X0 Z30
 M9
 M05
 G28 U0 W0
```

## Goldens

Only one golden moved, and I read it: `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/fanuc-lathe/axial_drill.nc`, which gains the exit `G00 X0 Z30`. `WRITE_GOLDEN=1` over `lathe_post`, `lathe_post_tormach` and `lathe_post_refusals` changed nothing else. No other committed program or test text contains a lathe face-cycle word.

## Tests

- New `crates/app/tests/lathe_cycle_exit.rs`:
  - `both_lathe_posts_leave_a_face_drilled_hole_at_the_streams_exit` posts the axial-drill document's stream through both `fanuc-lathe.cps` and `tormach-lathe.cps`. A read-back checker follows each program as a control would: a face cycle returns to the level it was read at, G80 moves nothing, G28/G30 go home. It asserts one hole drilled, no X move below the stream's exit (its `ClearancePlane`, 30) after the hole, and the tool at the exit level or higher when it leaves the cut (at the first home move).
  - `the_checker_catches_the_r_plane_exit` pins the checker itself on the #1011 program, an off-centre move at R, and the two good shapes (cycle and plain moves).
- New `lathe_post_refusals::a_face_cycle_ends_on_the_rapid_leaving_its_hole_and_refuses_a_cut_that_leaves` uses a synthetic stream. The exit rapid posts as `G83 ...` / `G80` / `G00 X0 Z40`, with exactly one group `G80`. A feed off the hole inside the group is refused by name and writes no guess.
- **Revert check:** with the old `fanuc-lathe.cps` restored, `both_lathe_posts_leave_a_face_drilled_hole_at_the_streams_exit` fails (`"the program leaves its hole at Z20, below the exit Z30"`, fanuc-lathe) and the refusals test fails on the missing `G00 X0 Z40`. With the fix, both pass.
- Quick gate: `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` on the final head. The golden change maps it to every app suite, which includes lathe_post, lathe_post_refusals, lathe_post_g76, lathe_post_tormach, lathe_post_tormach_thread, lathe_spindle_law, c_axis_live, c_axis_unwind, posting, golden_cl, conformance, drilling_axial, drill_prior and drill_prior_kinds. Result: green, 1 step, 0 failed, 25.8 min (`gate-logs/quick-20261112-023802`). Clippy on camcraft-app tests: `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --test lathe_cycle_exit --test lathe_post_refusals -- -D warnings` clean.

## Not exercised

- A lathe tap (G84) or bore (G85) document end to end. They share the same `onRapid`/`chainRapid` path as G83, which the synthetic test covers.
- Mill-turn C-axis sections. A cycle there is still refused before any group opens, and that is unchanged.
- The positioning block (`G00 X0 Z<R>`, written only when the stream's approach isn't already there) is not re-seated the way #994's `cycleSeat` does it. A lathe drills one on-axis hole, and the axial-drill stream always arrives on R first. Noted in the decision file.
- `assets/posts/AGENTS.md`'s hop-law paragraph is #1019's, so I didn't edit it here. The lathe post states the rule in its own header.

Changelog: The Fanuc lathe post leaves a face-drilled hole at the stream's exit level (G80, then the exit rapid) instead of homing from the R plane; a cut leaving the hole inside a face cycle is refused by name (#1011)

title: fix(app): a Face refusal under an area turn names its spot where the part is
body:
Stacked on #993 (itself on #957); its diff shows their commits until they merge.

## What changed
A Face under an area turn is generated in the turned frame and turned back (`turn_path(.., -turn)`), but a refusal left `face_over` through `?` with its spot still in the turned frame. New `boundary_turn::face_over_back` runs `face_over` and carries a refusal's spot (and ghost, if any) back through the same `-turn` (`turn_refusal`, built on `GenError::map_location` / `map_ghost`; a ghost that cannot turn is dropped). Both call sites in `generate.rs` (the path and the air-entry re-run) use it. No turn: refusal untouched. Successful output is unchanged (`golden_cl` and `conformance` green).

## Tests
Pinned by `operation::boundary_turn::law::a_refusal_from_the_turned_frame_names_its_spot_where_the_part_is`, `with_no_turn_the_spot_is_unchanged`, `a_ghost_turns_back_with_the_spot_and_a_plain_refusal_passes`. Quick gate `--base upstream/main`: 5 steps, 0 failed; clippy `-D warnings` clean on camcraft-app.

No end-to-end test through `generate`: today a spot refusal cannot arise under a turn (a turn comes only from an open chain, which drops the base's holes, and any surviving hole is forbidden, so `face_band_sane` refuses first without a spot). The unit test uses a real holed region through `face_over_back`. Details in `docs/decisions/1017-face-turn-refusal-spot.md`.
