title: fix(app): generator refusals speak the document's unit (#740)
body:
An inch document's refusals still read millimeters: a bore 25 mm too deep was refused as `25.000 mm deep`, a `Ø14 shank in a Ø12 hole` quoted bare millimeters - while every dialog around it spoke inches (#740).

## The change

The refusal sentences are built deep in the generator, off the worker threads, world-free - that's why they never saw the document's unit. The fix carries the unit to them rather than reaching for the world:

- `GenJob` grows a `unit: Unit` field; `collect_job` fills it from `crate::units::of(world)` while the world is still in hand, and it rides into every refusal builder as one added argument (`too_deep`, `shank_fits`, `axial_reach`, the cross-reach family in `cross_spindle`/`cross_stock`/`cross_holder`, `circle_of_region`, `pocket_region_on_part`/`around_part`, `offset_run`). `AreaCtx` carries it the same way.
- The lens itself: `units::len(v_mm, unit, prec)` prints `{:.prec}` byte-identically in millimeters and the converted value at `prec + 2` in inches; `Unit::suffix()` gives the word. Every pinned number is `{:.3}` in mm, so inch refusals read five decimals. Where the sentence had a literal `" mm"` it now ends `units::len(..) + unit.suffix()`; bare numbers (mouth coordinates, `shank dia. {:.3}`, `Z {:.3}`) become suffixless `units::len(..)`.
- `GenError::At`'s location stays millimeters - the lens is for the sentence, not the geometry marker. Tests pin this.
- Two `#[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]` attrs (`axial_reach`, `shank_fits`), following the existing convention in `generate.rs`/`plunge_solid.rs`.

Millimeter documents change not one byte: the existing suite, which pins these sentences verbatim, passes untouched.

## Pins (red on main, green with the fix)

`crates/app/tests/units_in_refusals.rs` runs five operations twice each, mm then inch, asserting the mm sentence byte-for-byte and the inch sentence converted:

- `an_axial_reach_refusal_speaks_the_document_unit` - through-hole `too_deep`: depth, flute, fix depth cross the lens, ` mm` becomes ` in`.
- `a_cross_reach_refusal_speaks_the_document_unit` - raw-bar cross hole: mouth coords `(10.000, 0.000, 0.000)` -> `(0.39370, 0.00000, 0.00000)`; the `At` location is pinned to stay `(10, 0, 0)` mm.
- `a_shank_fit_refusal_speaks_the_document_unit` - the BR-1000 shank refusal: depth/flute lensed, bare `shank dia. 14.000` -> `0.55118`; location pinned mm.
- `a_circle_fit_refusal_speaks_the_document_unit` - circular-fit deviation and centre point.
- `a_part_fills_the_selection_refusal_speaks_the_document_unit` - the plane named in the area refusal: ` at Z 7.000` -> ` at Z 0.27559`.

## Scope, relative to the claim table

- `material::section()`'s refusal is dead code - dropped.
- The `holder()` raw-`Display` refusal and the pure-crate refusals (`camcraft-tools`, `camcraft-motion`) need their unit plumbed through crate APIs, not job args - a follow-up PR.
- Refusals quoting profile constants (`spun`, `holder_profile`, `lathe_holder`) quote tool definitions, not document measurements - left alone.
- The contour travel *note* (`contour: rides the open boundary 0.400 mm...`) is a note, not a refusal - left for the same follow-up.

## Tested

- Red first: with only the pins committed, `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test units_in_refusals` builds clean and all five fail on the millimeter strings they still see.
- Green: same command, 5 passed, 0 failed.
- The mm byte-identity proof: untouched sentence pins across the drilling/area/pick suites all pass unmodified - lib `drill_reach` (8), `area::` (4), `contour_open` (2), and integration binaries `drill_reach`, `drill_reach_fit`, `drilling_cross_holder`, `drilling_cross_spindle`, `drilling_cross_stock`, `drilling_cross_rapids`, `drilling_axial`, `circular_pick`, `pick_agnostic`, `drilling_cross`, `drilling_cross_box`, `drilling_cross_part`, `drill_prior`, `drill_prior_kinds`, `drill_rplane`, `lathe_cross_drill`, `area_controls`, `area_open`, `area_picks`, `whole_model_pocket`, `boundary_walls`, `probe_pick`, `refusal_location`, `pick`.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` finishes clean.
- Not exercised: the other crates - the fix touches only `camcraft-app`.

Changelog: generator refusals now print their numbers in the document's unit - an inch document reads inches, millimeter documents unchanged (#740)

Fixes #740

title: feat(align): part alignment from two perpendicular edge picks (full 3D frame)
body:
## What changed

Part alignment from two perpendicular edge picks (#769): the picks
define the full 3D frame.

- `pick::align_from_axes` (`crates/app/src/pick/axis.rs`): with both
  +Y and +X picked, their directions - read through the setup's held
  alignment, so it composes after a face lay - define the frame: the
  primary axis lands exactly, the secondary is orthogonalized against
  it (landing within the skew it came with), and +Z lands on the
  picks' cross, the right-hand rule. The part turns about the centre
  of its bounds; the origin is NOT set (the work offset stays where
  it is placed). A left-handed pair is honoured literally (the part
  lands as picked) instead of refused; only (nearly) parallel picks
  refuse, by name. The landing is proved before the command stores
  anything.
- `AlignPartToSetup::align_from_axes` / `check_align`
  (`commands/setup_align.rs`): the command constructors, same
  refusals by name.
- The UI axis panel (`egui_app/setup_axis_pick.rs`, the `CommandKind`
  renamed `TurnPartInPlane` -> `AlignPartFromAxes`): same rows, same
  picks, same flip toggles - the meaning grew. One picked axis keeps
  the in-plane turn (#557 unchanged, `turn_in_plane` kept for its
  callers); the words under Apply say which case applies.

## How tested

- New `crates/app/tests/align_axes.rs` (9 tests): the user's exact
  case (a down-Z edge picked +Y, a -X edge picked +X - full 3D
  landing, the picks' cross up, centre unmoved); a vertical edge as +Y
  lays the part on its side; in-plane picks subsume `turn_in_plane`
  exactly (positions and rotation, pinned); one axis alone keeps the
  in-plane turn; a skewed secondary lands within its own skew;
  parallel picks refused by name; a left-handed pair honoured
  literally (pinned as deliberate); picks compose after a held
  alignment; a face pick still refuses by name.
- New UI pin `two_picks_with_an_upright_edge_align_the_part_in_full_3d`
  (setup_axis_tests): the round that #557 refused - upright edge +
  top edge - leaves Apply on, applies, lands the picks on their axes
  with +Z on their cross, never touches the work offset, and one undo
  restores. Existing surface pins updated for the renamed command and
  the new status words.
- Battery green: align_axes 9, axis_align 10, plane_align 9,
  points_align 8, turn_pivot 5, ui setup_axis 9; clippy clean on
  camcraft-app and camcraft-ui.

## What was not exercised

- The origin is untouched by design (the work-offset flows own it).
- `turn_in_plane` and `in_plane_turn_deg` are unchanged; their callers
  (single-pick panel round, MCP align tools) keep their behavior -
  the MCP surface exposing `turn_in_plane` still turns in-plane only.

title: fix(xtask): test scanner ignores braces in strings, chars and comments
body:
## What changed
`xtask/src/scan.rs` `test_fns` ended each test span by counting every `{`/`}`, including those inside string literals, so `refuse("{", "bad JSON")` in `fixture_library.rs` swallowed the next test and `cargo xtask gate test <next test>` reported "no #[test] fn matches".

The depth count now goes through the new `xtask/src/braces.rs`, which skips braces inside `"..."` (with `\\` and `\"` escapes), raw strings (`r"..."`, `r#"..."#`, any number of `#`), char literals (`'{'`, `'\''`, `'\u{7d}'`; lifetimes like `'a` are left alone) and `//` comments. The lexer state carries across lines, so multi-line strings work. No unwrap/expect/panic.

The quick tier's changed-fn picker uses the same `test_fns` spans, so it is fixed by the same change.

## How tested
- `cargo test -p xtask`: 30 passed (3 new), `cargo clippy -p xtask --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean.
- Pinning tests: `braces_in_string_literals_do_not_swallow_the_next_test`, `braces_in_raw_strings_chars_comments_and_lifetimes_are_ignored`, `a_change_in_the_test_after_a_brace_string_is_attributed_to_it` (quick planner: a hunk in the second test plans `--exact second`).
- Repro commands from the issue, with `--dry-run`: `the_library_folder_is_the_override_else_a_sibling_of_machines` before: "no #[test] fn matches"; after: `app fixture_library  dry run`. `a_bad_library_is_refused_whole_by_name` finds its test as before.

## Not exercised
Block comments (`/* { */`) are not skipped (not in the issue's scope). Full batch/release tiers not run (tooling only).

## Process
`xtask/` is a process file: `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION` bumped 10 -> 11. A fork must do nothing beyond the normal process sync. Fork synced at v0.16.0.

title: test(app): fixture_library folder resolver uses host-absolute paths
body:
## What changed

`crates/app/tests/fixture_library.rs`, test `the_library_folder_is_the_override_else_a_sibling_of_machines` only. No product code.

The test fed Unix-only paths (`/shop/fixtures`, `/Users/me`, `/home/me`). `fixture_library::user_dir_for` (`store.rs`) keeps an override only when `PathBuf::is_absolute()` is true on the host, so on a Windows host those paths were dropped and the assertions failed.

- The override path, the macOS HOME and the linux HOME are now picked per OS with `cfg!(windows)` (`C:\shop\fixtures`, `C:\Users\me`, `C:\home\me` on Windows; the old strings elsewhere), the same pattern as `machine_edit.rs` `the_user_folder_resolves_from_the_override_else_the_platform_data_folder`.
- Expected folders are built with `PathBuf::from(home).join(...)`, so separators are right on both hosts.
- The `env` helper now copies its pairs into owned strings instead of requiring `&'static` literals, so runtime-chosen per-OS strings can be passed.
- Assertions keep their meaning: an absolute override wins; a relative override (`"relative"`) falls back to HOME; the macOS and linux data folders are unchanged; `linux` with no HOME gives `None`. `library_path(&PathBuf::from("/x"))` is unchanged: it only checks the file name suffix, which holds on any host.

## Why it passes on Windows

On Windows the three host-absolute paths are absolute, so `CAMCRAFT_FIXTURES` is kept and the HOME branches resolve under `C:\Users\me` / `C:\home\me`. The relative override stays non-absolute on Windows too, so it falls back to HOME. The expected `PathBuf`s are built from the same strings with `join`, so they compare equal to what `user_dir_for` produces. This is the same construction as `machine_edit.rs`, which already passes in the Windows batch.

## How tested

- macOS: `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test fixture_library -- the_library_folder_is_the_override_else_a_sibling_of_machines --exact` - 1 passed.
- macOS: `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --test fixture_library -- -D warnings` - clean.
- Linux quick gate against upstream main: `app fixture_library (1 fn)` ok.

  - This branch @ ae39b16f: the same command - **6 passed, 0 failed**.
- Pinning test: `fixture_library::the_library_folder_is_the_override_else_a_sibling_of_machines`.

title: fix(app): pocket recognition refuses an inside-out or open mesh by name
body:
## What changed

The blocker from the maintainer's review of #512 reached main when #512 merged at 7e39726.

`recognize::pockets_of` read "up" and "leans into" straight off the facet winding. So an inside-out 10 mm cube came back as `Pocket { kind: Closed, floor_z: 0, depth: 10, boundary: the part's outline }`, and `detect_pockets create` would cut the whole footprint to the base.

`pockets_of` now runs #387's body-winding verdict (`pick::winding::winding_of` / `verdict_for`) over the whole model first. Any body whose outside can't be trusted is refused by name, in recognition's own words: inside-out, open (torn), non-manifold, mixed winding, flat, or no readable facet.

`docs/decisions/718-pocket-winding.md` records the choices: why whole-model and not per-pocket, and why the refusal has its own wording instead of `refusal()`'s "before aligning to it".

## Pinned by

- `pocket_recognition::an_inside_out_mesh_is_refused_never_read_as_a_pocket`. A reversed cube and a reversed pocket block are refused with "inside-out", and the same block wound outward still reads its one pocket. **It fails without the fix:** the reversed cube reads as a 10 mm closed pocket.
- `pocket_recognition::degenerate_input_refuses_cleanly`: the torn half-pocket now expects the "open body" refusal. Before, it only checked for no panic.

## How tested

On upstream main plus this commit:
- `pocket_recognition` 11/11, `mcp_pockets` 3/3, `mcp` 13/13 and `pick` 9/9 pass;
- the ui lib pocket tests pass;
- clippy `-D warnings` is clean on the app lib and `pocket_recognition`.

## Not exercised

No GUI run. Recognition has no UI entry point yet (#511).

The fork is synced at v0.16.0; the branch is cut from upstream/main.

title: feat(post): grblHAL post processor (3-axis mill)
body:
Fork synced at v0.16.0.

## What changed

A new built-in post, **grblHAL** (`assets/posts/grblhal.cps`, 3-axis mill), and a generic machine, **grblHAL 3-axis** (`assets/machines/grblhal-3axis.mch`). The post is specced from the G-code list in grblHAL's public core README and the LinuxCNC G-code reference (behaviour only; grblHAL's GPL source was not read), structured after `tormach.cps`.

- Header `G21|G20 G17 G90 G91.1 G94 G40 G80`; no `%`, O word, N numbers or G64.
- **No tool length word** (no G43 / G43.1 / G49): on grblHAL the offset belongs to the controller's tool-change handling, and a G49 would discard a measured length. This departs from the issue's G43.1 default; reasoning in `docs/decisions/710-grblhal-post.md`.
- `G53 G0 Z<safe>` then `T<n> M6` **alone on its line**; no G28/G30.
- Canned cycles G73/G81/G82/G83/G86/G89 with G98, dwell P in seconds.
- Refused by name: control/wear compensation (G41/G42), tapping (G84), going home after an operation (G28/G30 positions are controller settings), tilted moves, and probing (the engine refuses it, since the post has no probe hooks).
- **Z lift without trusting an unhomed machine Z0.** With `$22=0` grblHAL takes its power-on position as machine zero, so `G53 G0 Z0` could rapid down. `G53 G0 Z<safe>` is written only when the machine file states `safe_retract` (= "it homes"). Otherwise the lift is `G0 Z<h>` in the work offset, where h is the section's `ClearancePlane` or a higher Z already commanded; it is refused by name when h is unknown or not above `StockZTop`. The generic machine states no `safe_retract`.

## How tested

- `conformance`: grblHAL in POSTS / REFUSED (`tap_plate`, "tapping") / EXTENSIONS. Goldens in `golden/nc/grblhal/` (12) and `golden/nc/synth_grblhal.nc`. The synth stream drops only the tap.
- New `grblhal_post.rs` (9 tests): registry and library, grbl program shape with no length/G64/G28/G30/G84 word, Z lift before a lone `T M6`, dwell P1.5 for 1500 ms, one named tap refusal, inch output, a homed machine lifting with G53, the work-offset lift without homing (clearance, a higher commanded Z, origin shift), and the named refusal of an unknown or buried lift height.
- Cross-post lists extended: `comment_escape`, `control_comp`, `wear_comp`, `post/tests/comp`, `fanuc_post` (non-RTCP; the tilt refusal is now looked for among all warnings, since grblHAL also refuses its lift on that bare stream), `inverted_post`, `after_op` (stops plus the home refusal), `coolant`, `coolant_followups`, `machine` (library expectations).

title: feat(ui,app): every picker resolves through the one pick rule (#692 step 2)
body:
#705 (#692 step 1) has merged; this is step 2.

## What changed (step 2 of #692)
Every viewport picker and the MCP pick tools now resolve through #705's one pick rule. No page carries its own pick logic.

### The UI router: `crates/ui/src/feature_click.rs` (new)
- It builds the `PickRay` from the camera, in perspective or ortho.
- It converts the pixel radius to mm by depth.
- It says which kinds the armed tool accepts:

| Tool | Accepts |
|---|---|
| Plane row | faces only (#554) |
| Axis by edge | edges |
| Axis by two points | points |
| Operation geometry | Face, Edge (with the face between edges) or Vertex mode |
| Boundary | faces or edges |

- **Hover** uses exactly the rule its click would.
- **Origin/WCS chips** read the operation picks, so they get the same rule.

### Removed from the UI
- **`interact.rs`:** `pick_face`, `pick_edge`, `hover_feature_at`, `edge_nearest`, `point_seg_dist_px` and `feature_of_facet`. The old edge pick was screen-space, with no depth test, and offered facet seams. The file drops from 1779 to 1542 lines.
- **`vertex_pick.rs`:** its local nearest/sight logic. It drops from 271 to 122 lines.

### App side
- **`pick/feature_sel.rs` (new):** maps a pick to the `FeatureSel` the pages store (`Chain`, run or `Segment`). `check_pickable` refuses a pick by id that a click could never make.
- **MCP `list_features`:** now lists only feature-edge chains and feature points.
- **Graph cache:** cached per facet allocation, so hover never re-hashes a mesh.
- **Occlusion:** capped at 32 sight rays per candidate tier, a choice measured on `sample_ap214`.

### Intended behaviour changes (#692's rule)
- Rim vertices of round holes and bosses are no longer pickable points.
- Facet seams of smooth walls are no longer edges.
- Hidden edges are no longer pickable.
- In the feature modes, the stock-mesh hover triangle gives way to the feature highlight.

Thresholds and trade-offs are in `docs/decisions/692-pick-wire.md`.

## Tested
**New UI tests** (`egui_app::tests::one_pick_rule`, real egui_kittest clicks):
- `a_click_on_a_flat_faces_diagonal_picks_the_face_never_an_edge`
- `a_click_over_a_hidden_edge_takes_the_near_face_or_nothing_never_the_edge`
- `a_box_corner_picks_as_a_point_where_points_are_taken`
- `a_smooth_walls_facet_seam_is_no_edge`

**New app tests** (`feature_pick_wire`, 4, plus an ignored timing lane):
- `a_pick_resolves_to_the_selection_its_page_stores`
- `the_per_depth_radius_holds_at_a_miss`
- `the_shared_graph_cache_answers_the_same_allocation_without_rebuilding`
- `a_pick_by_id_must_be_one_a_click_could_make`

**New MCP test:** `mcp_pick::listed_chains_and_vertices_follow_the_one_pick_rule`.

**Existing tests rewritten to the new rule:** `vertex_pick_tests` (3, same claims through the real State), `law_tests::feature_pick_tests`, and one `plane_face_pick` assertion.

**Gate:**
- ui: all binaries green (lib 427).
- app: lib 103, `feature_pick` 7, `feature_pick_wire` 4, `pick` 9, `mcp_pick` 3, `mcp` 13, `vertex_pick` 4, `plane_align` 8, `plane_align_edges` 5, `axis_align` 10, `wcs_align` 5, `face_origin` 3, `feature` 18, `fixture_ux` 9, `probe_pick` 9, `mcp_setup` 4.
- clippy `-D warnings`: ui lib+tests and the app lib are clean.

**Timing** (release, 400 hover picks, 12 px radius):

| Model | All kinds, mean | Edges+faces, mean |
|---|---|---|
| sample_ap214 (1.5k facets) | 32 µs | |
| Synthetic 100k-facet cylinder | 2.8 ms | 2.8 ms |

## Not exercised / not done
- **Fixture locate (#566):** wired through `feature_click` (merged with main).
- **Pick-through toggle:** not added. `through: false` is set everywhere, and the API keeps the field.
- **Others still owed:**
  - round-edge centres have no `FeatureSel` variant yet;
  - the WCS anchor markers are still overlay picks;
  - the user-docs note for #688 isn't written.
- **Hand check:** passed 2026-11-10 (user, builds of 47a33610 and e5d3b32e): whole faces, whole chains, corner points, no seams; both two-point markers show after the fix.

Changelog: Picking follows one rule everywhere: whole faces, real feature edges and corner points only, the visible one under the cursor first - never a tessellation edge or a hidden edge through the part (#692)

title: feat(machines): Makera Carvera and Carvera Air, with a Carvera post
body:
## What changed

**Machines.** `assets/machines/makera-carvera.mch` and `makera-carvera-air.mch` are new, registered in `posting::MACHINES`. The figures come from the "Specs" tables on Makera's own product pages (read 2026-11-10):

| | Carvera (C1) | Carvera Air |
|---|---|---|
| Work area (mm), as ±stroke | 360 × 240 × 140 | 300 × 200 × 130 |
| Spindle | 200 W, to 15000 rpm | 200 W, to 13000 rpm |
| Axis feed and rapid | 6000 mm/min | 4000 mm/min |
| Tool changer | 6 | none stated (quick changer) |
| Coolant | Air (M7) | Air (M7) |

No `min_speed` is stated, because Makera publishes "0 – 15000 rpm" and the validator refuses 0. The optional 4th-axis module is left out; it's a later step.

**Post.** `assets/posts/carvera.cps` is registered as "Makera Carvera". It writes only words from the firmware's supported-codes tables (Smoothieware-based).

| Area | What it writes |
|---|---|
| Header | `G21 G17 G90 G94`. An inch machine is refused by name, because G20 halts the firmware. |
| Tool change | `M6 Tn`. There's no G43, because the firmware measures tool length itself. Tool 0 (the wireless probe) is refused as a cutter. |
| Spindle and air | `M3 S…`, then the machine's M7 air, off with M9. |
| Arcs | `G2`/`G3` with relative I/J/K, in G17, G18 or G19. |
| Drilling | No canned cycles in the firmware, so drilling posts as its expanded chain, with `G4 P<s>` dwells at the hole bottom. |
| Program end | `M2`, because M30 does nothing on a Carvera. |
| Refused by name | tapping, control cutter compensation, tilted moves and probe operations. |

`docs/decisions/707-carvera.md` records every choice and its source.

## Pinned by

- **`carvera_machines`:** `every_carvera_states_makeras_figures`.
- **`carvera_post`:**
  - `a_two_tool_pocket_posts_in_the_carveras_own_words` locks the golden `golden/nc/carvera/two_tool_pocket.nc` on the shipped C1 file and asserts no G43 / G49 / G40 / G80 / G91.1 / G20 / M8 / M30 / G53;
  - `an_inch_machine_is_refused_by_name`;
  - `tool_zero_is_the_probe_and_refused_as_a_cutter`;
  - `control_cutter_compensation_is_refused_by_name`.
- **`conformance`:** the Carvera on every mill golden (`golden/nc/carvera/`), with `tap_plate` refused by name; the synth stream (`synth_carvera.nc`); and the extension pin.
- **`machine`:** the shipped-machine list.

## How tested

On upstream main plus this branch:
- every `camcraft-app` test suite and `--lib` pass. `lathe_thread_travel` was left out because it doesn't build on main (#686). The `probe_dialects` fix (#700) has already merged.
- clippy `-D warnings` is clean on the app lib and the touched tests.

## Not exercised

There has been no run on a real Carvera or in Carvera Controller. I'm asking a contributor with the machine to run `two_tool_pocket.nc` before the post is trusted on a machine. The fork is synced at v0.16.0; the branch is cut from upstream/main for the current machine registry.

title: feat(app): one feature graph and pick API - welded faces, feature edges and points, visible-first (#692 step 1)
body:
## What changed (step 1 of #692)
This adds one app-layer picking service. Step 2 (a separate PR) moves every UI picker and the MCP pick tools onto it. No picker uses it yet, so app behaviour is unchanged.

### New modules
- **`crates/app/src/pick/feature_graph.rs` (330):** the feature graph of a mesh.
  - Welded faces are the existing `geometry::feature` patches, reused through `model::features_of_local`. `list_features` is unchanged.
  - Feature edges are creases between welded faces, plus open boundary edges. Seams between the strips of a tessellated wall are filtered out.
  - Feature points are corners (3 or more edges meet), turns over 30° and chain ends.
  - The graph has a cap-8 cache keyed by the facets' digest.
- **`crates/app/src/pick/feature_arc.rs` (90):** circle and arc centres of round feature-edge runs.
- **`crates/app/src/pick/feature_pick.rs` (314):** the one pick API, `pick_feature(world, &PickQuery { ray, radius, kinds, through }, skip)`, with `pick_bodies` for world-free callers.
  - It finds the front-most surface, then snaps point → centre → edge → face, only among the accepted kinds.
  - Edges and points must be visible from the eye: a perspective view checks the sight line, an ortho view the parallel view line. `through = true` turns the occlusion check off.
- **`pick.rs`:** registers the new modules; `ray_triangle` becomes `pub(crate)` so the new code shares it.

The thresholds and the alternatives dropped are in `docs/decisions/692-pick-graph.md`.

## Tested
**Pinned by `crates/app/tests/feature_pick.rs` (7/7):**
- `flat_face_triangulation_edges_are_not_pickable`
- `cylinder_facet_edges_are_not_pickable_but_its_rim_is`
- `a_box_corner_is_a_point_but_a_vertex_inside_a_face_is_not`
- `a_far_side_edge_is_not_picked_through_the_near_face` (perspective and ortho)
- `pick_through_does_pick_the_far_side_edge` (perspective and ortho)
- `the_world_pick_honours_placements`
- `degenerate_input_picks_nothing_and_never_panics`

**Also green:**
- app lib 103, `pick` 9, `mcp_pick` 2, `mcp` 13, `face_origin` 3, `vertex_pick` 4, `plane_align` 8, `plane_align_edges` 5, `axis_align` 10, `wcs_align` 5, `feature` 18.
- `cargo check -p camcraft-ui` passes.
- Clippy `-D warnings` on the app lib and `feature_pick` is clean.

The full app test build still fails on main in `lathe_thread_travel` (#686, not this PR), so I ran the suites one by one.

## Not exercised / left for step 2
- **UI and MCP pickers:** none is rewired yet. The UI has to turn its pixel radius into mm at the hit and build the `PickRay` from its camera.
- **Edges to chains:** an edge pick returns one edge, and the UI still maps it to a `FeatureSel::Chain`.

- **Pick through:** there is no "pick through" toggle in the UI yet, and the user-docs note (#688) is still owed.

title: fix(cl): clearance-seeded mill paths always open with an approach rapid
body:
## What changed

Follow-up to #690 / #694. Mill generators seed their `PathBuilder` at (0, 0, clearance) and rapid to their start. When the start is exactly X0 Y0, that rapid has zero length and the builder drops it, so the first posted motion was a feed from the tool-change position (#690's bug through another door).

- **`crates/cl/src/cl/path.rs`:** a new `PathBuilder::approached(seed)`. If a path's first move would not be a rapid, the builder states a zero-length rapid at the seed first.
  - It happens before any move is recorded, so cycle and comp-span indices never shift.
  - It's opt-in: `new()` is unchanged, so drilling, ladders and the lathe keep their openings byte for byte.
- **The 19 motion files** that seeded `PathBuilder::new(Point3::new(0.0, 0.0, p.clearance_z))` now use `approached`. Face's #694-only insert is removed in favour of the shared rule.
- **Decision record:** `docs/decisions/697-approached-builder.md`.

## Pinned by

`crates/motion/tests/origin_approach.rs` (new, 5 tests):
- `a_start_at_the_seed_still_opens_with_a_rapid`
- `an_arc_first_move_is_approached_too`
- `a_path_that_opens_with_its_own_rapid_is_unchanged`
- `a_plain_builder_keeps_its_old_behaviour`
- `no_generator_seeds_the_clearance_plane_without_the_approach_law` (a source scan, so a new generator can't reintroduce it)

`machining2d::a_face_entering_at_the_origin_still_opens_with_its_approach` from #694 still passes through the shared rule.

## How tested

On upstream main 4aec95a9 plus this commit:
- **cl and motion:** every `camcraft-cl` and `camcraft-motion` suite passes, and clippy on both with `--tests` is clean.
- **app:** every `camcraft-app` suite and `--lib` pass, apart from two known breaks on main:
  - `lathe_thread_travel` doesn't build (#686).
  - `probe_dialects` fails 3/13 on main; #700 fixes it.
- **Goldens:** no app golden changed, so no existing fixture starts exactly at X0 Y0. Every existing program is byte-identical.

## Not exercised

The lathe generators (blade, parting, contour door and rides) seed at a clearance radius and station and have their own approach rules, so they're out of scope; noted on the issue. No machine run. The fork is synced at v0.16.0.

Changelog: Mill operations whose start point is exactly X0 Y0 now open with a rapid on the clearance plane instead of a feed from the tool-change position (#697)

Fixes #697

title: fix(motion): Face opens with an approach rapid on the clearance plane
body:
## What changed

Face's posted program had no approach rapid. The facer started its path *at* its entry point in the air, so its first move was the plunge. Posts write only a move's end point, so the first posted motion after the tool call was a **3-axis feed from wherever the tool change left the spindle, straight to cutting depth** (`G01 X-5 Y5 Z-2 F100` in the old Fanuc golden).

- `crates/motion/src/machining2d/face.rs`: Face starts its cursor where the other mill generators do, at (0, 0, clearance), and its first move is a rapid on the clearance plane to the entry. The plunge follows. An entry at exactly X0 Y0 (where the builder would drop a zero-length move) states the approach outright as a zero-length rapid.
- Every dialect now posts `G00 X<entry> Y<entry> Z<clearance>` before the plunge feed.
- The Tormach golden's old `G0 X0 Y0 / G0 Z0` opening (the #131 workaround in the script, which had no start point to use) now goes to the real entry.

The decision record is in `docs/decisions/690-face-approach.md`. A generic post-layer approach rule was considered and dropped as wider than this bug.

## Goldens and tests updated

title: fix(motion): a step too small to ladder is refused by name, never allocated
body:
## What changed
A stepover or stepdown that's too small to ladder is now refused by name at generate. It no longer allocates until the process aborts (#691).

- **The ladders:** `motion::machining2d::band` (Face, zigzag pocket and slot rows) and `cut_levels` (every depth-stepping 2D op and the 3D entry ladders) now return `Result`.
- **The check:** before allocating, `pass_budget` refuses a step that needs more than `MAX_PASSES` (100 000) passes, or one too small to advance the coordinate (`span + step == span`). The message names the parameter: `stepover 1e-9 mm over 4.000 mm needs more than 100000 passes - raise the stepover`.
- **Callers:** face, bore, circular, contour/chain, pocket, troch/HSM pocket, slots and 3D entry propagate the refusal with `?`.
- **Normal steps** produce byte-identical output.

The decision is recorded in `docs/decisions/691-tiny-step.md`.

## Tested
**Pinned by:** `crates/motion/tests/tiny_step.rs`
- `a_face_stepover_too_small_to_ladder_is_refused_by_name`: 1e-9, and 1e-300 (below float resolution).
- `a_stepdown_too_small_to_ladder_is_refused_by_name_on_face_and_contour`: staged Face and 2D Contour at 1e-9.
- `a_small_but_real_step_still_generates`: 0.05 mm still runs.

**Gate (`scripts/gate.sh quick`), on upstream main b57f8d52+:**
- geometry, cl, tools, post, sim, motion (incl. `tiny_step`) and ui suites are green.
- The app suites and the full clippy failed to compile only on `crates/app/tests/lathe_thread_travel.rs:83` (missing `hand`). That break is already on main and is tracked as #686, not this PR.
- So I ran these instead:
  - app lib;
  - app `face_holes`, `face_blend`, `mill2d_b`, `mill2d_c`, `golden_cl`, `roughing2d`, `operations`, `mcp`, `corner_blend`, `control_comp`, `level_links`, `slot_caps`, `whole_model_pocket`: all green;
  - clippy `-D warnings` on motion (all targets) and the app lib: clean.

## Not exercised
- **Offset-ring pockets and 3D stepovers:** these generators have their own loops and don't go through `band`/`cut_levels`. They're not reported crashing, and this PR leaves them alone.
- **Live repro:** I didn't run the MCP repro in the GUI or the CLI live. The refusal reaches it as a normal `GenError` at generate.

Changelog: A stepover or stepdown too small to ladder (over 100 000 passes) is refused by name at generate instead of aborting on a huge allocation (#691)

title: feat(post): a PathPilot plasma post for the Tormach 1300PL
body:
**Stacked on #676** (#670, plasma profile), which is stacked on #674 (#669, plasma kind). Review only this PR's own commit, `2645a023`.

A **PathPilot plasma post for the Tormach 1300PL** (#671). Every word below was checked against UM10720 v1223A ([UM]) or Tormach's PathPilot Post Processor Guidelines, Plasma column ([PG]).

| Word | Meaning | Source |
|---|---|---|
| `G20`/`G21` | units | [PG] |
| `G90 G91.1 G94 G17 G40 G49 G80` | modal reset, once | [PG]; [UM] §6.2.2 |
| `G64 P0.005 Q0.005` | path blending (P in inches even under G21) | [UM] §6.2.1 p.50; [PG] |
| `G54` | work offset | [UM] §6.2.1 |
| `G43 H1` | torch length offset | [PG] ("always H1"); [UM] §6.2.2 |
| `G30` | go to the G30 height | [UM] §6.2.1-6.2.2 |
| `G0 X Y` | rapid to the pierce point, never Z | [UM] §6.2.1 |
| `M200` | AutoFS (feed, THC volts, pierce height and delay, amps) | [UM] §6.3 p.51, §7.2 p.54 |
| `M207`/`M208`/`M209 P` | pierce height / cut height / pierce delay, only when the op states them | [UM] §6.3.1 p.52, §7.2 |
| `G15` | ohmic probe; WCS Z = 0 | [UM] §7.1 p.54 |
| `G16` | rise to pierce height, fire, delay, go to cut height, THC on | [UM] §7.1; [PG] |
| `G1/G2/G3 X Y [I J] [F]` | the cut, XY only | [PG] |
| `G41.1`/`G42.1 D<kerf>` … `G40` | control compensation, each on its own line before a straight lead | [PG] |
| `M205` | torch off, Z to the G30 height | [UM] §7.2 |
| `M30` | end | [PG] |

- **Never written:** S, M3-M9, M6, G95-G99, canned cycles.
- **M6 conflict:** [PG] says M6 is unsupported on plasma, but [UM]'s test program writes `T1 M6`. This follows the issue and [PG]; the conflict is recorded.

## What changed
- **Script:** `assets/posts/tormach-plasma.cps`, registered as "Tormach PathPilot Plasma", the only `PLASMA_POSTS` entry. Milling posts decline a plasma stream, because they lack the torch hooks.
- **Stream:** #676's records are carried into the post stream: `PLASMA …`, `TORCH ON C<id> …` and `TORCH OFF C<id>` (the `.cl` v5 records without `; `).
  - The parser reads both spellings; malformed records are refused by line number.
  - New properties: `PlasmaKerf`, `PlasmaCompensation`, `PierceHeight`, `CutHeight`, `PierceDelay` (absent = AutoFS), `PlasmaFeed`, `PlasmaReversed`, `Contour`, `ContourRole`, `ParentContour`, `SmallHole`.
  - New hooks: `onPlasma`, `onTorchOn`, `onTorchOff`.
  - `machine.kind` is now a script property.
- **Engine torch law** (`cnc_torch.rs`), refused by name:
  - a TORCH with no header, a second header;
  - ON while lit, a wrong or extra OFF, a rapid while lit;
  - a section or stream left lit;
  - a script without both torch hooks.
- **Post refusals:**
  - a non-plasma op, a Plasma Profile path with no plasma record;
  - rpm, coolant (other than off), a rotary or tilted move;
  - Z on a lit move, a canned cycle, a dark feed;
  - comp under a computer offset, wear comp;
  - a machine that isn't `kind: plasma`.
- **AutoFS:** under AUTOFEED, no F is written. A small hole then runs at the AutoFS feed, with an operator comment; refusing it would block every default plate with a hole.
- **Decision record:** `docs/decisions/671-plasma-post.md` (the sources and ten choices). CNC-INTERMEDIATE.md and assets/posts/AGENTS.md are updated.

## Golden (`tormach-plasma/plasma_plate_with_holes.nc`, inch; excerpt)
```
G20
G90 G91.1 G94 G17 G40 G49 G80
G64 P0.005 Q0.005
(T1 PLASMA TORCH - KERF 0.0591)
G54
G43 H1
G30
(C0 INNER IN C4 - SMALL HOLE 65% FEED)
G0 X3.3465 Y0.7874
M200
M207 P0.1496
M209 P0.5
G15
G16
G1 X3.3465 Y0.9547 F63.98
...
M205
G30
```
Siblings: `_mm.nc` and `_control.nc` (`G41.1 D0.0591` … `G40`). The CLI post is byte-identical to the inch golden.

## How tested
- **`plasma_post` (5):**
  - the inch and mm goldens, with structural checks: no Z/S/T/M3-M9/M6, per-contour order, G30 after every M205, ending `G30 M30`;
  - the in-app dump equals the `.cl` golden;
  - the control-comp golden;
  - a stream round-trip, plus malformed-record refusals;
  - an in-app 1300PL document posts through the gate.
- **`plasma_post_refusals` (5):** every refusal, the engine torch law, every milling builtin declining the stream, and the registry.
- **Pins updated:** plasma_machine, machine_library, plasma_profile, golden_cl and conformance.
- **Gate:**
  - those suites plus posting, camcraft-post and camcraft-cl;
  - also tormach_post, control_comp, coolant, after_op, program_comments, fanuc_post, lathe_post, per_op_files and probe_guard;
  - clippy is clean.

## Not exercised (why this is a draft): a PathPilot Hub 1300PL simulator run
It should check:
1. G20 and G21 both load and run, and `G64 P0.005 Q0.005` reads as inches under G21.
2. `G43 H1` without `T1 M6` is accepted.
3. Whether a bare `G30` after `M205` also travels XY (a time cost only).
4. `M207`/`M209` after `M200` override AutoFS.
5. G1 moves with no F take the AutoFS feed.
6. `G41.1 D…` on its own line, a straight lead, then `G40`, with the offset on the right side.
7. G2/G3 under G91.1.
8. Probe and pierce at each G0 point, THC on, M205, and the part matches.

Changelog: A PathPilot plasma post for the Tormach 1300PL: M200 AutoFS, G15 probe, G16 pierce, M205 torch off, G30; G41.1/G42.1 D<kerf> under control compensation; non-plasma work refused by name (#671)

Fixes #671

title: feat(sim): plasma through-cut laws - cut order, kerf crossing, tip-up
body:
## What changed

**#672 step 1** (part of #621's plasma research): `sim::verify::plasma`, the laws that replace the gouge and collision checks for a 2D plasma through-cut. Based on main, with no dependency on #674 or #670.

**What it judges:** a neutral `PlasmaProgram`:
- the kerf;
- the cuts in cut order, each the torch-on polyline with its contour id, inner/outer and parent outer;
- the rapid into each cut.

So it reads the CL's torch records (#670's `TorchOn { contour, inner, parent }` / `TorchOff`) and nothing of the operation's internals.

| Law | Verdict | Source |
|---|---|---|
| **Cut order:** an inner contour cut after the outer that frees its part | **refusal** | plain plasma practice; the part drops before its holes |
| **Kerf crossing:** a cut within one kerf of an earlier cut's centre line | warning | LinuxCNC Plasma Primer §12 (THC dive into an open kerf) |
| **Tip-up:** a rapid across a part already cut free | warning | Tormach 1300PL manual UM10720 §1.4.2, §4.12.8 |
| **Malformed:** a non-positive or non-finite kerf, a NaN point, a cut with no path | **refusal** | Prime Directive |

**Not yet wired.** Step 2 builds the `PlasmaProgram` from the plasma op's CL torch records once #670 lands, blocks the post on a refusal, and updates the machine check's `notes` (#674) to say these laws judge plasma ops.

## How tested

- **New `crates/sim/tests/plasma_laws.rs`, 5/5.** Each law is tripped by one fixture and passed by another:
  - a plate with a hole, hole-first (clean) versus outline-first (refused);
  - two outlines 1 mm apart at a 1.5 mm kerf (warned) versus 5 mm apart (clear);
  - a rapid over a freed part (warned) versus around it (clear);
  - the malformed kerf, point and path cases.
- **`scripts/gate.sh quick`:** the sim suites pass.
- **Clippy** on sim with `-D warnings`: clean.

## Not exercised

The CL reader and verdict wiring (step 2, after #670). The 2D gouge (the kerf band against the part's section) needs the part's 2D section from the op, also step 2.

Changelog: none (internal: plasma laws, not yet wired)

Refs #672
Refs #621

title: feat(machines): a plasma machine kind and the Tormach 1300PL
body:
First slice of the plasma work (#621 research → #669-#672): a **`plasma` machine kind** and the **Tormach 1300PL**.

## What changed
- **`Kind::Plasma`** (`kind: plasma`, "plasma cutting"), declared only and never inferred from the axes. `Kind` moves to `crates/post/src/machine/kind.rs` and is re-exported.
- **File rules,** in one place: `machine/plasma.rs::plasma_refusals`. These are refused by name:
  - any `spindle.*` key, each one separately;
  - `live_tool`;
  - coolant (station or tooling root);
  - any rotary axis.
  - The Machines-pane validator also requires X, Y and Z (Z is the torch lifter).
  - The rules are held at every door: `parse_mch`, the validator, and `Machine::is_sane` for project files and `SetSetupMachine`.
- **Machine check** (`crates/app/src/machine/plasma.rs`):
  - **Judged:** X/Y travel (arc quarter points included), the X/Y share of each feed, and the tool count.
  - **Refused by name:** a non-plasma op ("a Face operation is milling work - a plasma table cuts only plasma operations"), a tool with rpm, and a tilted move.
  - **Skipped:** Z depth and travel, and rpm and spindle power. They are **named, not failed**: a new non-blocking `MachineCheck.notes`, which the status line prints as "not judged: …".
  - The per-move helpers move to `machine/judge.rs`, so `mod.rs` drops from 427 to 370 lines.
- **Command door:** `family_gate` refuses milling and turning ops on a plasma setup, and the ribbon shows no section. **No op can be posted on a plasma table until #670.**
- **Posts:** a new `posting::PLASMA_POSTS`, empty until #671. Every cutting post declines a plasma table, and `post_offer` never offers a post that wouldn't serve the mounted machine.
- **`assets/machines/tormach-1300pl.mch`** (UM10720 v1223A §2.2.1 and the 03/24 spec sheet):
  - inch; X ±48.5, Y ±50, Z ±3.9. The smaller of the two documents' figures (the manual says X 50 / Y 51.5); both are recorded;
  - 1000 IPM on X/Y and 120 IPM on Z; rapid unstated;
  - a torch head with no spindle; `number_of_tools: 1`; no `safe_retract` (the plasma post retracts with G30).
- **UI:** the machine editor's kind combo and the Machines pane's New blank list offer plasma.
- **Docs:** `assets/machines/AGENTS.md`.
- **Decision record:** `docs/decisions/669-plasma-kind.md`.
  - Kerf lives on the torch tool, as its diameter, so the existing offset code works unchanged.
  - Coolant is refused.
  - A second tool, such as a scribe, stays allowed.

**Seams left for the sibling issues:**
- **#670:** add a `Family` arm in the exhaustive `cuts_plasma`, plus a torch tool kind (relax `Tool::is_sane`'s rpm > 0 for torches only).
- **#671:** add a BUILTINS entry and its name to `PLASMA_POSTS`.
- **#672:** owns what the check skips.

## How tested
- **New `plasma_machine` (6):**
  - spindle, coolant and rotary keys and a missing Z are refused by name;
  - an unknown kind is still refused, and undeclared XYZ reads as a mill;
  - the 1300PL spec pin;
  - the check skips depth and rpm with a note and judges XY (a mill-kind copy does report Z);
  - a mill op is refused at the command door and at the verification gate;
  - a 1300PL setup round-trips byte-identical, and a hand-edited rpm refuses to load.
- **Updated:** the machine, machine_library, machine_edit and tormach_safe_retract expectations.
- **Gate:**
  - machine, machine_edit, machine_library, tormach_machines, tormach_safe_retract, sinumerik_safe_retract, axis_direction, posting, conformance, project_roundtrip, ribbon, lathe_post, setup_mounts_post, tormach_post, vmc_stroke and lathe_stroke pass;
  - camcraft-post passes, and the ui machine and ribbon lib tests pass;
  - clippy is clean on post, app and ui.

**MACHINES list:** this PR appends to `posting::MACHINES`, as do #624, #627, #634 and #654. Whichever merges later takes a trivial list merge.

Changelog: A plasma machine kind (`kind: plasma` - X/Y cut, Z torch lifter, no spindle; spindle, coolant and rotary keys refused by name; machine check judges X/Y travel and feed, skips Z depth and rpm with a named note) and the Tormach 1300PL machine (UM10720 / spec sheet 03/24); no op or post serves it yet (#670, #671) (#669)

Fixes #669

title: fix(ui): the setup-pick sweep runs every frame, whatever the dock shows
body:
**Stacked on #666** (#664, setup picks disarm on page change). Review only this PR's own commit, `75c8b710`.

**P2 (#667, found in M5's review of #666):** #666's disarm sweep ran inside `pages::properties`, so only while the Properties tab was drawn. With the tab closed or hidden behind another tab, an armed Setups pick stayed armed and viewport clicks fed the hidden draft.

## What changed
- **`shell_layout`** wraps the dock with the sweep, once per frame.
  - **Before the dock:** if `layout::is_shown(dock, Properties)` is false, `axis_pick::disarm_all` runs. `is_shown` is new: the tab is in the dock, active in its leaf, and the leaf isn't collapsed.
  - **After the dock:** `axis_pick::disarm_hidden` runs.
- **Ordering:** viewport clicks are routed inside the dock, and egui_dock draws leaves by node index, so the viewport can draw before Properties.
  - The before-dock check closes the one-frame gap: a pane hidden by a click in frame N-1 is disarmed before frame N's viewport runs.
  - It also stops a stale `axis_rows_shown` from letting `hint_stray` swallow clicks while the pane is closed.
  - This is documented at the call site and in `docs/decisions/667-sweep-every-frame.md`.
- **`pages::properties`** loses #666's wrapper and is back to a single function. The rows still mark themselves.

## How tested
- **`setup_picks_disarm`, now 5 tests (headless, real clicks through the View door):**
  - `an_axis_pick_disarms_when_the_properties_tab_is_closed`: arm +Y by Edge and pick, close Properties, click the part, and the draft is unchanged. Reopening shows "Pick +Y edge" with the edge kept.
  - `a_plane_pick_disarms_when_another_tab_hides_the_properties_pane`: opening Machines in front of Properties disarms the face pick. Closing Machines shows "Pick a face" with the face kept.
  - Both fail without the fix. #666's three tests still pass.
- **Gate:**
  - ui lib 391 pass. The 1 failure is the known no-GPU `headless_run_succeeds` in the agent sandbox;
  - boundary_picks, edge_loop_pick and operations pass;
  - clippy is clean. No snapshot PNGs changed.

Changelog: A Setups page pick (axis by Edge or Two points, or lay-on-a-plane) now disarms when the Properties tab is closed or hidden behind another tab, so viewport clicks no longer feed the hidden setup draft (#667)

Fixes #667

title: fix(ui): setup picks disarm when their page is left
body:
**Stacked on #573** (#557, part axes by edge or two points). Review only this PR's own commit, `04d8f749`.

**P2 (#664, found in M5's review of #573):** an armed Setups-page pick stayed armed after leaving the page. Edge, vertex and face clicks on an operation page then fed the hidden setup draft instead of the operation's geometry.

## What changed (ephemeral view state, no command)
- **One sweep.** `pages::properties` clears the "rows drawn" markers (`axis_rows_shown`, the new `State::setup_pick_rows`) and draws the page. It then calls `axis_pick::disarm_hidden`, which stops every armed axis or plane pick whose setup rows weren't drawn this frame.
  - That covers a page or tab change, opening an operation, closing the section, and another setup's page.
  - The axis and plane rows record their setup each frame they are drawn.
- **The plane draft is paused, not dropped.** `PlanePick` gains `picking`, `pause()` and `collecting()`.
  - Re-arming resumes it with the face kept, and on return the row shows the picked face and Apply while disarmed.
  - The row's own "Stop picking" still drops the draft.
- **Click routing:** `interact.rs`, `vertex_pick.rs` and `hint_stray` ask `plane_pick::collecting`. The plane outlines draw only while collecting, the same as the axis draft.
- **Decision record:** `docs/decisions/664-disarm-setup-picks.md` (one sweep rather than per-navigation resets; pause rather than drop).

## How tested
- **New `tests/setup_picks_disarm.rs` (headless, real clicks).** Each test arms the pick from its row and picks once, then switches to the Contour1 operation page and clicks the same pixel: Contour1 gets the pick and the setup draft is unchanged. Back on the setup page, the pick is disarmed and kept.
  - `an_axis_edge_pick_disarms_when_its_page_is_left`
  - `an_axis_two_points_pick_disarms_when_its_page_is_left`
  - `a_plane_face_pick_disarms_when_its_page_is_left` (re-arming resumes with the face)
  - With the sweep commented out, all three fail.
- **Updated:** `plane_face_pick`'s existing test armed the plane pick while the operation page was showing, which was the bug. It now opens the setup page first.

body:
**Stacked on #522** (the Haas, Mazak and Siemens probing hooks). Review only this PR's own commit, `8f0a6d1b`.

The Haas part of #392. #465 made the Fanuc post probe on an inverted X/Y behind the manifest flag `probeAxisInversion`, and left Haas until its probing hooks landed.

## What changed
- **`haas.cps` declares `probeAxisInversion = true`.** #522's Haas hooks write the same controller words as Fanuc:
  - G31, the trip read from `#5061-#5063`, and a `#3000=2` no-contact alarm;
  - a `G91 G1` back-off and the deviation into `#190..`;
  - `G10 L2 P.. X[#5221+#190]`.
  - Each reads in the controller's own frame, so #465's mirrored stream gives the **physical** correction with no Haas-specific code. A comment in the probing section says why.
  - The `onProbeGuard` positioning moves mirror correctly too.
- **`invert.rs`:** the refusal text now names "Fanuc and Haas". `assets/posts/AGENTS.md` is updated to match.
- **Decision record:** `docs/decisions/392-haas-probe-inverted.md`. It records the reasoning, what was dropped (a separate Haas macro reader; relying on G101 or the control's axis-direction setting) and the sources.

## How tested
- **`inverted_probe` (9) now runs every case for both posts:**
  - the cases: face −Z / −X, edge −Y, corners +X+Y / −X−Y, bore and boss;
  - each on standard, inverted X, inverted Y and inverted XY machines;
  - G55 lands on the physical datum, and a part where the model says leaves the datum unchanged;
  - no contact alarms `#3000=2`, and out of tolerance alarms `#3000=1`;
  - the converse also holds: the untranslated program misses, and undoing any one translated word breaks it.
- **New tests:**
  - `an_uninverted_program_is_unchanged_by_the_flag`: both posts give byte-identical standard-machine output, and #173's Haas golden is unchanged;
  - `probing_through_an_unverified_script_still_refuses_by_name`: the refusal is pinned on a shipped script with its flag stripped.
- **Gate:** inverted_post 15, probe_dialects 13, conformance, golden_cl, posting, fanuc_post, inverted_equivalence, probe_op, axis_direction and camcraft-post pass. Clippy is clean.

**Sources:** the Haas Mill Operator's Manual (public), as #522 cites: G31, `#5061-#5063`, `#5221+`, `#3000`/`#3006`, `G10 L2`. The inversion adds no new controller semantics.

**Not exercised:** a real Haas control with an inverted axis.

Changelog: Probing posts on a Haas machine with an inverted X/Y axis (the probe records are mirrored like moves; the written work offset is the physical correction) (#392)

Fixes #392

title: feat(setups): part alignment turns about the WCS origin and lays the picked face down
body:
**Stacked on #603** (#330, the face-lay rows, which also carries #593 and #573). Review only this PR's own commit, `e14ee4a2`.

#606 left three items to decide. Each is recorded in `docs/decisions/606-align-pivot.md`, with what was considered and dropped.

## 1. The typed-angle Apply turns about the WCS origin, with a choice
- **Default pivot: the setup's WCS origin.** That is the WCS entity's position, or zero if none is placed, read the same way as `posting::wcs_context`. The part point on the origin stays on it, which answers the maintainer's report that alignment "shifts the model relative to the origin".
- **Angles stay absolute from "as modelled".** Re-applying the same angles is refused ("already holds the part that way") rather than drifting. All-zero means "as modelled".
- **The choice:** an `about [WCS origin | part centre]` combo sits beside Apply, and the tooltip names the pivot. "Part centre" is the old behaviour.
- **Presets (Flip over X, Turn Z 90, …) still turn about the part centre,** and their tooltip says so. About the origin, a flip would put a part sitting on Z 0 under the table.
- **Code:** new `crates/app/src/setup_turn.rs` and `AlignPartToSetup::turn(…, pivot)`. `CommandKind::AlignPart` gains `pivot`. It is still **one undoable command**.

## 2. Lay on a plane defaults to face down (maintainer's call: recommended option taken)
- The face row's "Flip" becomes **"Face down"**, on for a new pick: the picked face sits on the plane with the part on top. The points row's "Flip points" becomes **"Points down"**, also on by default.
- **Only the UI draft default changed.** `PlaneLay::flip` keeps its meaning for the app, MCP and scripts.
- **Saved setups store the resulting transform, so old projects load and post identically.**

## 3. The structural test checks the pane, not the window
- `setup_page_alignment_rows_structure` now asserts every alignment control, including the new combo and Apply, lies inside the **properties pane's tab rect**.
- Putting the face row back on one line (the #330 regression) **fails** the test: `"Face down" … [[1349.8 344] - [1429.4 362]]` against the pane's right edge at x 1264.

## How tested
- **New app suite `turn_pivot` (5):**
  - the origin corner stays fixed, with undo and redo;
  - zero is the pivot when no WCS is placed;
  - after a preset, the point now on the origin stays, and the same angles are refused;
  - the part-centre pivot equals the old behaviour;
  - refusals by name.
- **New UI tests (headless, real clicks):**
  - `setup_align_tests::the_typed_turn_pivots_on_the_wcs_origin_by_real_clicks_and_undoes`: type Z = 90, Apply, Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Y, switch to part centre, Apply;
  - `setup_plane_tests::face_down_is_the_default_and_off_lays_the_face_up`.
- **Updated** for the new defaults: the plane, points and `plane_face_lay` tests, and the structural test.
- **Gate:**
  - app: turn_pivot, setup_align, plane_align(_edges), points_align, axis_align, winding_align, setup_relative, setup_carry, carried_verify, setup_stock_source, rest_across_setups, commands_undo, project_roundtrip, setup_wcs and setup_sheet all pass;
  - ui lib: 387 pass. The 1 failure is the known no-GPU `headless_run_succeeds` in the agent sandbox;
  - clippy is clean. No snapshot PNGs were touched.

**Not exercised:** a hands-on check in a fresh build.

Changelog: Setups page: the Part alignment row's typed angles turn the part about the setup's WCS origin by default, keeping its place relative to the origin; an "about" choice beside Apply offers the part centre, and the presets still turn about the centre. "Lay on a plane" now lays a newly picked face (or three points) face down on the plane, with "Face down" / "Points down" on by default; saved projects are unchanged (#606)

Fixes #606

title: refactor(sim): a carried field reads back as the column body, the same on both engines
body:
## What changed

**Stacked on #651** (#637 step C), which is stacked on #649 and #646. Merge them in order #646, #649, #651, then this. This is **#637 step D**.

**New `CarriedField::column_body(lattice, judged_before) -> Body`** (`crates/sim/src/stock_sim/field_body.rs`) reads the carried, clipped field onto the next setup's lattice (`Lattice { x0, y0, cell, nx, ny }`, new frame).
- **Per column:**
  - the **top** is one down-march (`march`);
  - the **floor** is step B's exact shell floor (`floor_at`);
  - a **flip** swaps them, since the new top is the old floor;
  - the **clip** trims the column, and `Clip::Empty` leaves every column empty;
  - a floor a cut reached, or a column the field cannot read, is **refused by name**.
- **The result** is the same `carry::Body` the column engine makes (new `Body::from_parts`), so `deviate` (the two-sided verdict), `display`, `volume` and `bounds` run **unchanged** on either engine.
- **Plumbing:** `march::world` is now `pub(crate)`.

**A decision, recorded in `docs/decisions/637-carried-field-read-back.md`:** this replaces the planned `Body = Column | Field` enum. The enum needed a second, field-native implementation of every `Body` method, each new verdict code to prove. The read-back reuses the one verdict the column carry already proves, and tops and floors still come from the field, never interpolated.

## How tested

- **New `crates/sim/tests/carry_engine_agreement.rs`, 2/2, about 3 s in debug.** The same 20×12 block, cut by the same slot (shallow at z 3, deep at z 1), is carried through **all 8 lattice turns** (quarter turns and flips) on **both** engines.
  - Per column, `empty_at` matches and the top and floor agree to **1e-6**.
  - The volumes agree to 1e-6, and `floor_judged` matches.
- **`scripts/gate.sh quick`:** the sim suites pass. Named: field_carry 8, field_floor 3, stock_backend_parity 13, stock_columns 3, and app setup_carry 9, carried_verify 8, rest_across_setups 7.
- **Clippy** on sim and app with `-D warnings`: clean. No golden changed.

## Not exercised

- **Step E:** the app holders (#586) taking a field carry. Nothing in the app calls `column_body` yet.
- **A field-native verdict finer than the lattice:** possible later behind the same `Body` API.
- **The two #651 nits** (a `Display` for `ClipRefusal`, and the mod sort order) are left for step E, which touches the same file.

Changelog: none (internal: the carried field reads back as a column body; not yet used)

Refs #637

title: fix(app): the lathe stroke check judges the posted radius, not world X
body:
**Stacked on #640** (#630, control-point posting and the built-in Lathe's X floor of -2.5). Review only this PR's own commit, `dd45a6c4`.

**P1 (#647):** the machine travel check compared each move's **world X** with a lathe's X band. Turning kernels carry their radius on the **Y meridian**, so a lathe radial over-travel was never judged. It also judged the nose-centre cache, not the control point the post writes.

## What changed
- **New `crates/app/src/machine/lathe_stroke.rs`.** On lathe-kind machines only, each op is judged on **`posting::nose::posted_path`**, the exact stream the post gets: the control point for the nose-centre turning ops, and the cache for the others.
  - **X** is the signed offset from the axis on the path's meridian, read as `fanuc-lathe.cps` `radiusOf` reads it, with the same 0.0005 tolerance. Past centre is negative and meets the floor.
  - **Z** is relative to the origin.
  - **Arcs** about the spindle axis are judged on their radius, with arc quarter points included.
  - **Any point off every meridian** is judged three ways: on signed world X, on its radius, and on Y against any Y band. No single reading can clear it.
  - **Refusal wording** is unchanged: "<op>: move i reaches v in X, the stroke is lo..hi".
  - **When the post refuses the orientation**, the check falls back to the nose-centre cache, so the op is still judged.
- **`machine/mod.rs` (+9 lines):** calls the lathe judge first and skips the world-X block for lathe machines. Mill and mill-turn checks are unchanged.
- **Decision record:** `docs/decisions/647-lathe-stroke-radius.md`.

## How tested (`lathe_stroke`, now 10 tests)
- **New:**
  - `a_facing_control_point_below_the_x_floor_is_refused_by_name`: with the floor at -0.5, Face1 on the Y meridian is refused with "reaches -0.800 in X". It fails without the fix.
  - `a_turning_pass_beyond_the_x_ceiling_is_refused_by_name`: X max 9 on an r10 bar refuses Rough1. It fails without the fix.
  - `a_facing_control_point_on_the_x_floor_passes`: a guard at the band edge.
  - Unit test: `machine::lathe_stroke::tests::the_meridian_radius_is_read_signed`.
- **Updated:** `a_clearance_past_the_lathe_carriage_still_refuses_by_name` now expects Rough1 at Z 634.200, the control point (r 0.8 below the nose centre), not 635.000. Mill-turn still expects 635.000.
- **Gate:** conformance, golden_cl, every lathe_* and turning_* suite (including thread), machine, machine_edit, machine_library, posting and tormach_machines pass. Clippy is clean.

## Interactions
- **#643 (#631):** `mod.rs` merges cleanly. After both merge, lathe machines are judged here first, so #643's `spindle_arc` branch goes unused on lathes; a follow-up can remove it.
- **#643 vs #640:** separately from this PR, #643's `lathe_thread_travel` fixture states `"min": 0.0`, and #640 moves the built-in floor to -2.5. Whichever merges second updates that string.
- **#644:** its converted groove and part paths are judged automatically, through the same `posted_path`.

Changelog: On a lathe, the machine travel check now judges the posted radius — the control point, on the path's own meridian, signed past centre — so a turning or facing over-travel in X is refused by name instead of passing unseen (#647)

Fixes #647

title: refactor(sim): a carried field clips to the next setup's block by intersection
body:
## What changed

**Stacked on #649** (#637 step B), which is stacked on #646 (step A). Merge them in that order. This is **#637 step C**, the clip from the design comment on #637.

`CarriedField` gains an optional **clip block** in the new frame.
- **The law:** the carried solid is **intersected** with the later setup's own stock block, `distance = max(d_body, d_block)`, and membership is body **and** block. That's the field's form of the column body's `lower()` clip in `stock_sim_carry`.
- **A second clip** narrows the block; it never widens it.
- **Carrying again** (`then`) carries the clip through the same turn.
- **New `box_signed(lo, hi, p)`:** the exact signed distance to an axis-aligned box (negative inside), re-exported from `stock_sim`.
- **Not yet wired:** nothing uses it yet. That's step D, the `Body` enum and its agreement lane.

It merges step B's review fix: the 3×3×3 near-tool floor refusal.

## How tested

- **`crates/sim/tests/field_carry.rs`, 5/5** (3 from step A plus 2 new):
  - `a_clip_intersects_the_carried_solid_with_the_next_block`: at every sample the clipped distance is exactly `max(body, block)` and membership is `body && block`. A second clip only narrows.
  - `box_signed_is_negative_inside_and_euclidean_outside`: inside (−1), outside (3), a 3-4-5 corner (5) and on a face (0).
- **`scripts/gate.sh quick`:** the sim suites pass. Named: field_floor 3 (after the merge), stock_backend_parity 13, stock_columns 3, and app setup_carry 9, carried_verify 8.
- **Clippy** on sim with `-D warnings`: clean. No golden changed.

title: refactor(sim): a field column's floor reads exactly from the shell, or is refused
body:
## What changed

**Stacked on #646** (#637 step A). Merge #646 first. This is **#637 step B**, option 2 from the design comment on #637.

**New `SdfField::floor_at(x, y) -> FloorRead`** (`crates/sim/src/stock_sim/field_floor.rs`) reads the **lowest face of the stock under a column**.
- **How:** straight from the shell's own lowest crossing on that column. That's a mesh plane, so it's **exact**.
- **Why:** it's the column body's commonest re-clamp, a part flipped onto a face an earlier setup left uncut.
- **What it refuses:** a column whose floor a cut actually removed (a claim > 0 at or next to the floor cell) gets **`FloorRead::CutFromBelow`**, by name. The down-march's exactness rests on `cut_ups`, and no upward companion exists yet, so no bracketed guess is given. A `cut_downs` companion (option 1) can lift this later.
- **Other results:** `NoMaterial` for a column beside the stock, `Unreadable` for an `Open` parity column.
- **Not yet wired:** nothing uses it yet. It's for steps C–D.

**Also folded in, from the review of #646:** the `unapply` doc now says the round trip is exact **to rounding** (exactly for integer shifts, within an ulp of a fractional one), not "bit for bit".

## How tested

- **New `crates/sim/tests/field_floor.rs`, 2/2:**
  - `an_uncut_floor_reads_the_shell_exactly`: a plate's floor is −6.0 exactly. A shallow top slot leaves it −6.0, since a band reaching down isn't a cut floor. Beside the stock reads `NoMaterial`.
  - `a_floor_a_cut_reached_is_refused_by_name`: a slot cut through the plate gives `CutFromBelow` over the slot, and the floor beside it is still exactly −6.0.
- **`scripts/gate.sh quick`:** the sim suites pass. Named: field_carry 3, stock_backend_parity 13, stock_columns 3, and app setup_carry 9, carried_verify 8.
- **Clippy** on sim and app with `-D warnings`: clean. No golden changed.

## Not exercised

Steps C–E (the clip intersection, the body enum with its agreement lane, and the app holders), per #637.

title: fix(turning): facing approaches at rapid and lifts off the face before retracting
body:
**Stacked on #640** (#630, control-point posting, which changes the facing output). Review only this PR's own commit, `39ceb9c2`. The merge `c18542f9` brings in #640's latest tip.

**P2 (#632):** lathe facing had two problems.
1. Its first move after the tool call was a **feed** from wherever the turret was parked.
2. Every pass rapided straight out in X at the Z just cut, **dragging the nose across the fresh face**.

## What changed (`crates/motion/src/turning/face.rs`)
- **Approach:** the path starts on the axis at the clearance plane, the mill kernels' convention. Its first move is a **rapid to the clearance point (rho_clear, clearance)**, then the existing plunge feed.
  - Posted, the first motion after the tool call is `G00 X13 Z25`.
  - The meridian rapid law (#103) judges this rapid. rho_clear sits outside the stock radius, and a clearance plane inside the bar is refused (`RapidInStock`) and not posted.
- **Retract:** every pass lifts **`LIFT` = 0.2 mm (capped at half the stepdown)** up the axis, then rapids out in X at the lifted Z.
  - The cap keeps the lift inside air the pass above already cleared.
- **Profile Rough:** checked and unchanged. It already starts with a G0, and each rung exits radially outward at the top of its window, away from the finished diameter. This is recorded in the decision file.
- **Decision record:** `docs/decisions/632-facing-approach.md`.

## Golden diff (`fanuc-lathe/facing.nc`)
- `G00 X13 Z25` is added before the first plunge.
- Each retract `G00 X13 Z<s>` becomes `G00 X-1.6 Z<s+0.2>` then `G00 X13 Z<s+0.2>`.
- The header's existing envelope-warning move index shifts by one. That fixture faces the part's own end by design, the same as on main.

## How tested
- **motion `turning_face`:**
  - `the_first_move_is_a_rapid_to_the_clearance_point`;
  - `every_pass_lifts_off_its_face_before_it_rapids_out` (3 stepdown/nose combinations, and no rapid slides along a cut face);
  - the stock-allowance test's rapid assertion is updated for the lift.
- **New app `turning_face_approach`:**
  - `the_first_posted_move_is_a_rapid_to_the_clearance_point`;
  - `every_facing_retract_lifts_z_before_it_moves_out_in_x`;
  - `a_clearance_plane_inside_the_bar_is_convicted_not_posted`.
- **Every new test fails on the old `face.rs`.**
- **Gate:**
  - camcraft-motion: 658 passed.
  - app, 31 binaries and 277 tests: conformance, golden_cl, posting, every lathe_* suite, every non-thread turning_* suite, drill_prior* and project_roundtrip.
  - Clippy is clean.
  - After merging #640's tip: lathe_stroke 7, lathe_post 7 and turning_face_approach 3 pass.

Changelog: Lathe facing now rapids to the clearance point before its first plunge and lifts 0.2 mm off each faced pass before retracting, instead of feeding in from the parked turret and dragging the nose across the fresh face (#632)

title: refactor(sim): a field carried between setups is the same field seen through the turn
body:
## What changed

**#637 step A** (M7.3, the carried stock on the field engine). The design is in https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/issues/637 (research comment).

- **New `crates/sim/src/stock_sim/field_carry.rs`:** `CarriedField` views an `SdfField` through a setup change's `LatticeTurn`. `distance(p) = field.distance(T⁻¹ p)`, and the same holds for `mesh_distance` and `inside`.
  - **Why it's exact:** a signed distance is **invariant under rigid motion**, so nothing is re-sampled. That's the field analogue of `carry`'s "re-index, never re-sample".
  - **Scope:** phase 1 stays on carry's eight lattice turns (Z kept on ±Z). Every other turn is still refused upstream by `CARRY_TURN_REFUSAL`.
- **`LatticeTurn` gains:**
  - `unapply`: the exact inverse (`m`'s transpose and Z's sign);
  - `then`: composition, where signed permutations compose into signed permutations.
- **Not yet wired:** nothing in `carry::Body` or the app uses it. That's steps B–D (B's design finding is posted on #637). So this PR is behaviour-neutral, new API plus tests.

## How tested

title: fix(turning): grooving and parting blades post their touched-off corner
body:
**Stacked on #640** (#630, tool orientation and the shared CL → control-point conversion). Review only this PR's own commit, `22658499`.

**P1 (#641):** grooving and parting posted the **middle of the blade's tip edge**, but a blade is touched off on a **corner**. With a left-corner touch-off, a groove landed w/2 off in Z and a part-off left the part w/2 short.
- **Verified on the kernels:** `blade.rs` plunges at band centres; `parting.rs` plunges at the parting plane, with the kerf at ±w/2.
- **Verified on the old golden:** a 3.2 groove from Z-3.6 to Z-6.8 cut with a 2 mm blade posted Z-4.6 and Z-5.8.

## What changed
- **Blades reuse #630's `orientation`,** read on the LinuxCNC chart. There is no new field or file key, and the same editor row and undoable `ChangeTool` apply.
  - **1**: the right corner (+Z).
  - **2**: the left corner (−Z). This is the **default**, from LinuxCNC Lathe User Information §4.2's parting example, a blade touched off on its left side.
  - **6**: the width centre, the old behaviour. **9** is read as 6.
- **Conversion:** `posting_nose.rs` shifts GrooveRough, GrooveFinish and Part paths by (0, ±w/2) through #640's rigid `control_point_path`.
  - X does not move: the CL radius is already the tip line.
  - There is no corner-radius term: a rounded corner's imaginary tip is the sharp corner.
- **Refused by name:** codes 3, 4, 5, 7 and 8 (ID or face), and a blade with no usable width.
- **Unchanged:** the cache, verifier, stock sim and gouge laws keep the true blade. The parting plane still means the kerf centre.
- **Editor:** a Groove tool's row reads "Touched-off corner" and offers only 1, 2 and 6. The tool note prints `ORIENTATION q`.
- **Decision record:** `docs/decisions/641-blade-corner.md`.

**Behaviour change for existing programs:** the left-corner default moves every grooving and parting program by −w/2 in Z. A shop that touched off on the width centre sets its blades to 6.

## Golden diff (`fanuc-lathe/groove_part.nc`)
- **2 mm groove:** Z-5.8/-4.6 → **Z-6.8/-5.6**, the left corners at the walls.
- **3 mm part-off:** Z-10 → **Z-11.5**.
- Clearances move by the same amount; X is unchanged.

## How tested
- **New `lathe_blade_corner` (4 tests, each fails before the fix):**
  - a 3 mm groove at Z-10 posts Z-11.5, Z-8.5 or Z-10 for orientation 2, 1 or 6, and the cache stays at Z-10;
  - a part-off at Z-20 leaves the part's back face at Z-18.5 for every setting (before the fix, a left-corner blade left 17 mm);
  - ID and face codes are refused by name;
  - undo and redo.
- **Units and round-trip:** a tools unit for the blade chart, and `project_roundtrip::a_blade_corner_round_trips_and_old_blades_take_the_left_corner`.
- **Regressions, all green:** lathe_nose_tip, lathe_post, lathe_post_g76, lathe_post_refusals, lathe_field_sim, lathe_field_tools, turning, turning_blade, conformance, golden_cl, posting, project_roundtrip, commands_undo, the tool suites, tools lib, and the ui orientation row. Clippy is clean.

**Not exercised:** a Hub run, which comes with the lathe kit after #626.

Changelog: Grooving and parting blades post their touched-off corner (lathe orientation 1 = right, 2 = left (default), 6 = width centre) instead of the blade's width centre; ID/face codes are refused by name (#641)

title: fix(app): a lathe thread's spindle arcs are judged by radius in the travel check
body:
## What changed

#631: the built-in Lathe (`lathe.mch`, X 0..320) refused **every thread**, with "move 2 reaches -5.600 in X, the stroke is 0.000..320.000".

**Cause:** a thread pass is a chain of arcs **about the spindle axis**. Their far side, and the travel check's added quarter points, read negative X. That's the CL's antipode: the spindle turning the work, never a slide position. The machine check judged that raw signed X.

**Fix** (`crates/app/src/machine/mod.rs`, the travel law in `check_ops`): on a machine of kind lathe, an XY arc **centred on the spindle axis** is judged in X by its **radius** at each extreme. Every other move keeps its signed X, so a real past-centre move is still judged against the band.

**Not changed:** the band itself. `lathe_stroke::lathe_x_stays_a_centreline_band` records that a lathe's X is a one-sided centreline band. Whether a nose-radius face to centre (#630 / PR #640, which ends at X -r) should widen it is #640's call, not this PR's.

Decision record: `docs/decisions/631-lathe-spindle-arc-travel.md`.

## How tested

- **New `crates/app/tests/lathe_thread_travel.rs`, 2/2:**
  - `a_thread_passes_the_built_in_lathe`: **fails without the fix**, with the issue's exact message ("move 2 reaches -5.600 in X…").
  - `a_real_over_travel_on_a_lathe_is_still_refused`: the same thread against an X stroke of 0..2 mm is refused "… in X".
- **`scripts/gate.sh quick`:** the app suites pass.
- **Named:**

  | Suite | Passed |
  |---|---|
  | machine | 32 |
  | machine_library | 11 |
  | turning_thread | 8 |
  | lathe_post | 7 |
  | lathe_post_g76 | 5 |
  | lathe_post_refusals | 5 |
  | tormach_machines | 5 |
  | conformance | 6 |
  | posting | 17 |
  | setup_mounts_post | 5 |
  | lathe_stroke | 5 |

- **`cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -D warnings`:** clean, after the follow-up commit.
- No golden changed. Fork synced at v0.16.0.

## Not exercised

A Hub run on a lathe. The PathPilot lathe post is #626.

Changelog: A thread no longer fails the built-in Lathe's machine check - an arc about the spindle axis is judged by its radius, not its far side's negative X (#631)

Fixes #631

**Stacked on #595** (issue #585, the `Columns` seam). Merge #595 first. This is M7.3 step 3/6 (#26), **in part**.

title: fix(turning): lathe posts write the tool's control point for its orientation, not the nose centre
body:
**P0 (#630):** lathe posts wrote the insert's **nose-centre** path under G40. With normal touch-off, the controlled point is the imaginary tip (LinuxCNC Lathe User Information §7.1), so turned diameters came out **2r oversize** and faces **r long**. Confirmed against the control vendor's own behaviour: PathPilot's conversational posts the orientation's control point with G40, and refuses a tool whose orientation can't make the cut. That sample is used as behaviour reference only.

## What changed
- **Tool orientation** (LinuxCNC 1-9 chart: Lathe User Information §3 figure, §7.1, §4.1):
  - `Tool.orientation: Option<u8>`. Turning inserts default to **2** (OD, cutting toward the chuck), boring bars to **3**.
  - Editable in the tool editor, which shows the default, through the undoable `ChangeTool`.
  - The project key is written only when set, so old files load with the default. 1-9 is enforced at command creation and at file read.
  - Fanuc's tip chart is different, and no post writes either number, so only the LinuxCNC chart is modelled.
- **One shared conversion,** `crates/post/src/post/nose_tip.rs::control_point_path`, called once from `posting::op_streams` (`posting_nose.rs`), not per .cps:
  - Every move, rapids and arc centres included, shifts by r·(ox, oz) for the orientation.
  - This is exact on diameters, faces, tapers and arcs: the cutting path is already the profile offset by r, and the insert is rigid.
  - Refused by name: a path on two meridians or off every meridian, a C angle, an off-plane arc, and paths carrying cycle, thread, compensation or probe records.
  - Converted ops: facing, profile rough/finish, chamfer, taper, multi-pass, boring. Grooving, parting, threading, form and drilling post as before.
- **The cache stays the nose centre.** The verifier, stock sim, gouge laws and CL goldens are unchanged. Orientation is not part of the op stamp, so editing it never stales an op.
- **Orientation fit, refused by name at post:** a corner tip reaches within 45° of its direction, an axis tip within 90°, and 9 fits anything.
  - Facing needs −Z and −X (2, 6, 7 fit), OD turning −X, boring +X.
  - A cut needing −X and +Z gives exactly [1, 5, 6], matching PathPilot's own refusal.
- **fanuc-lathe.cps:** the header states the control-point rule (G40). The tool note adds `ORIENTATION q` from a new commentary parameter `PARAM ToolOrientation`, documented in CNC-INTERMEDIATE.md.
- **Decision record:** `docs/decisions/630-nose-tip.md`.

## Golden diffs (Fanuc Lathe; r = 0.8, orientation 2)
- **`facing.nc`:** every changed line shifts X −1.6 (diameter) and Z −0.8. The last pass now posts the facing plane (Z14, was Z14.8).
  - Passes end at **X-1.6**: the nose centre still reaches the axis, so the control point stands r past centre. This is a normal facing overtravel, but a machine with a 0 X limit would need #631.
- **`profile_rough_finish.nc`:** shifts by X −1.6 / Z −0.8. The Ø12 flange posts **X12** (was X13.6), the shoulder Z2 (was Z2.8), and the Ø7 neck X7 (was X8.6). Three points differ by 0.001 from a pure shift because of 1 µm grid rounding.
- **Unchanged:** groove/part, axial drill, thread G76 and C-axis goldens. In `lathe_post.rs`, the facing assertion now expects `X-1.6 Z14` and `ORIENTATION 2`.

## How tested
- **`nose_tip` units (7):**
  - the OD finish posts the finished diameter, and a face posts Z0;
  - every orientation's offset;
  - a 30° taper is exact;
  - arcs keep their radius and move their centre;
  - the X-meridian case;
  - refusals;
  - orientation 9 is identity.
- **`orientation` units (3),** including PathPilot's [1, 5, 6].
- **App `lathe_nose_tip` (6):**
  - a Ø19.05 neck posts X19.05 and the shoulder Z0, while the cache stays nose-centre;
  - facing reaches the axis;
  - every fitting orientation equals cache + r·offset, and editing never stales the op;
  - mismatched orientations are refused;
  - ChangeTool undo/redo, and code 10 is refused;
  - a boring bar defaults to 3.
- **Round-trip and UI:** `project_roundtrip::a_lathe_orientation_round_trips_and_old_tools_take_the_default`, and the UI orientation row.
- **Gate:**
  - the non-thread turning and lathe suites, `lathe_post_g76`, conformance, golden_cl, posting, project_roundtrip and commands_undo;
  - the tool suites, c_axis_live, control_comp, wear_comp, program_entry, inverted_post and coolant_followups;
  - camcraft-post and camcraft-tools.
  - Clippy is clean on 5 crates.

## Follow-ups
- **Grooving and parting blades:** they post the centre of the blade's width, but a blade is touched off on a corner (LinuxCNC §4.2), so a width/2 Z offset is likely owed. Filed separately.
- **Refusal rule:** checking the leading direction would need insert lead angles, which the tool library doesn't model.
- **#626 (PathPilot lathe post):** consumes the converted stream once merged; its goldens need regenerating.
- **#639 (#629):** may hit small conflicts in test `Tool` literals.

Changelog: Lathe posts write the turning tool's control point for its orientation (LinuxCNC 1-9, editable per tool; default 2 for turning inserts, 3 for boring bars) instead of the nose-centre path: a Ø19.05 finish now posts X19.05 and a face at Z0 posts Z0; an orientation that cannot cut the operation is refused by name (#630)

Fixes #630
