title: feat(ui): Machines pane "Use for this setup" assigns the selected machine
body:
**Replaces #426** (opened from the old fork, which can no longer take pushes). Same head commit; nothing else changed.

**Stacked on #382** (Machines pane, browse + validate): this branch carries #382's commits plus a merge of current main. Merge #382 first; this PR's own diff is then the last two commits (`cb293f30`, `35cfa074`) plus the merge.

## What changed
- The Machines pane's detail view gets a **"Use for this setup"** button under the validation verdict. Clicking it queues `CommandKind::UseCatalogueMachine(MachineSource)`.
- It follows main's per-setup machine route (#343): `State::mount_catalogue` -> `route_machine(MachineVerb::Mount(..))`. If the active setup owns its machine, the selected machine replaces it (`SetSetupMachine`); otherwise the document's machine changes (`LoadMachine`). One undo step either way.
- Validation is re-run at assignment: `machine::library::read_for_assign` re-reads the built-in text or file, runs `validate_text`, and refuses with the first refusal, so a refused machine never mounts even if the command is queued directly. Shared by `LoadMachine::from_catalogue`, the new `SetSetupMachine::from_catalogue` and the UI route.
- The button is disabled with the reason shown under it and on hover: "fails validation - <first refusal> (and N more)" or "it is already this setup's machine" (reads `machine::of`, the active setup's effective machine).
- `MachineSource::mount_path()` mounts built-ins at `built-in: <name>`, the path the Setup pane's Library list already uses.
- Decision only (no code): the `machine_editor.rs` window becomes the pane's edit mode when the editing slice (#383) lands.

## Readings
Debug, M5 Mac. `scripts/gate.sh quick` (all camcraft-app + camcraft-ui suites): 1734 passed, 4 failed - all known reds on main (`setup_stock_source::a_new_block_after_a_flip…` #415; GPU headless trio). Clippy `-D warnings` clean on app + ui.

## Pinning tests
- App `crates/app/tests/machine_assign.rs`: `assigning_a_catalogue_machine_does_undoes_and_redoes`, `a_refused_machine_cannot_be_assigned_and_says_why`, `a_setup_with_its_own_machine_takes_the_catalogue_machine`.
- UI lib `egui_app::tests::machines_pane`: `use_for_this_setup_assigns_the_selected_machine_and_undo_restores_it`, `a_refused_machine_cannot_be_assigned_and_names_why`, `use_for_this_setup_replaces_an_own_machine_and_leaves_the_document_alone`.

No hand GUI run yet (**draft until the GUI check**); Ctrl+Y redo only at app level; disabled-hover text not asserted. Posted G-code unchanged (machines mount through the existing commands).

Decisions: `docs/decisions/384-machines-use-for-setup.md`.

Changelog: The Machines pane's "Use for this setup" assigns the selected machine to the active setup (its own machine or the document's), undoable; a machine that fails validation can't be assigned and says why

title: feat(ui): preview the incoming stock in the viewport on the setup page
body:
**Replaces #429** (opened from the old fork, which can no longer take pushes). Same head commit; nothing else changed.

## What changed
While a setup's settings page is open and its stock source is "What <previous setup> leaves behind", the viewport draws the incoming body as a translucent **teal** closed block, in the active setup's frame, distinct from the setup's own Stock node.

- App: new `setup_stock_view::incoming_shape(world, setup)` calls `stock_sim::incoming_body` once and returns the box/volume plus `body.display().surface(&[])` as triangles mapped into the viewport's frame (`A_active * inverse(A_setup)`; identity when the setup is active). An empty body or sheet is an error naming the setup; a bad index is skipped, never a panic.
- UI: `incoming_view::IncomingView` caches it keyed by (setup, active setup, `doc_version`) - measured once per document version, never per frame - refreshed at the end of `drain_actions` and cleared the moment the page closes, another page opens, or the setup switches to its own stock. A failed measurement is logged once and draws nothing.
- Drawing: `collect_parts` adds a stock-type part with vertex class 4; `fs_stock` paints class 4 as teal rgb (0.12, 0.66, 0.74) at alpha 0.45 in the existing translucent stock pass.
- **Closed block** (after the GUI check of 2026-11-09 showed nothing teal): `setup_stock_shell::floor_and_walls` closes the incoming body (floor, walls and top), so the preview shows even where the top sheet would sit inside the part.
- **Drawn after the traced stock:** the preview is an overlay part (`viewport::is_overlay`) that `viewport::draw_order` sorts after the stock parts the traced whole-program view replaces, so it stays visible over it.
- The page's incoming box/volume text reuses the viewport's measurement, so there is one program sim per version instead of two.
- Display only: no command, nothing undoable (ephemeral view state per AGENTS.md). No files #412 touches were edited (`stock_sim*.rs`, `operation/*`, `rest/*`).

## Readings
Debug, M5 Mac. `scripts/gate.sh quick` (camcraft-app + camcraft-ui suites): 1718 passed, 4 failed - all known reds on main (`setup_stock_source::a_new_block_after_a_flip…` #415; GPU headless trio). Clippy `-D warnings` clean. The changed WGSL shader was validated offline with naga 30.0.1; the `gpu_render` tests skip here (no adapter in the sandbox).

## Pinning tests
- UI lib `egui_app::incoming_view_tests`: `the_incoming_stock_shows_while_the_carried_setups_page_is_open` (real properties pane via egui_kittest: one class-4 part with Setup2's page open, top at Z 16 where Setup1 faced to; measured once, three more frames measure nothing, a `doc_version` bump measures once more; Close removes it), `no_incoming_stock_for_own_stock_or_another_page`.
- App `crates/app/tests/setup_stock_view.rs`: `the_sheet_stands_in_the_active_setups_frame`, `the_first_setup_draws_its_own_block_and_an_unknown_setup_is_named`, `the_incoming_stock_is_a_closed_block`.
- UI lib `incoming_view_tests::the_incoming_part_sorts_after_the_stock_the_traced_view_replaces`.

## Not exercised
**Hand GUI check passed** (the user, 2026-11-10, build from 1ab3fc88 on `test-519-520.camproj`): the teal block stands from Z −2 to 12, shows with the part hidden or shown, and goes away when the page closes or the setup takes its own stock. Posted G-code unchanged.

title: feat(turning): optional repeat pass at each threading depth
body:
**Replaces #437** (opened from the old fork, which can no longer take pushes). Same head commit; nothing else changed.

**Stacked on #433** (#417), which is on #432 (#416). Part of #363. The #418 work is bf3b0d58.

## What changed
- **The option:** `ThreadInfeed.repeat_each_depth`, off by default. Every pass above the root is followed by an identical copy: same tip depth, same lattice shift, same helix phase. So a repeat can never cut deeper or move. The finishing and spring passes at the root are not repeated.
- **Alternating infeed:** the side flips once per depth, not per cut, so a repeat keeps its flank.
- **G76 refuses it by name.** The record carries a `repeat_each_depth` flag, written to the stream as `REP 1` only when set, plus a `RepeatEachDepth` post property. `fanuc-lathe.cps` refuses with "repeat each roughing depth is not a G76 cycle (the cycle cuts each depth once)".
- **Defaults are byte-identical:** the stamp adds one byte only when the flag is on, and no project key or stream word is written when it's off. No version rung.
- **UI:** a "Repeat each depth" checkbox on the Passes tab, after Spring passes. Its tooltip says G32 only, that G76 refuses it, and that tooling makers recommend against routine spring passes.
- `docs/decisions/418-thread-repeat-pass.md`

## How tested
- motion `turning_thread_infeed`, 10/10, including two new tests:
  - every roughing depth is cut twice (0.4, 0.4, 0.8, 0.8, 1.1, 1.1, 1.2, 1.2) and the default is unchanged move for move;
  - a repeat is the same pass under every method × schedule, and the verdict stays silent.
- app:
  - `turning_thread_infeed` 5/5: the toggle goes stale and back to OK, takes 3 then 5 plunges, with undo and redo; round-trip writes the key only when set;
  - `lathe_post_g76_schedule` 5/5: G76 refuses the repeat; `REP 1` rides the stream; G32 posts 5 passes.
- `turning_thread`, `lathe_post_g76`, `inverted_post`, `project_roundtrip` and the app lib pass. No golden changed.
- `clippy --all-targets -D warnings` on cl, post, motion, app and ui is clean.
- The only failure is the headless-GPU ui test (no adapter on this Mac).

## Not exercised (draft)
GUI check and a lathe sim or machine run. There is a combined test kit for #416, #417 and #418.

Changelog: Threading op: optional repeat of each roughing depth (G32 output; G76 refuses it by name) (#418)

Fixes #418

title: fix(post): G76 words state the thread passes that were verified
body:
**Replaces #433** (opened from the old fork, which can no longer take pushes). Same head commit; nothing else changed.

**Stacked on #432 (#416).** Part of #363.

## What changed
**With the G76 cycle post option, the G76 words now describe the passes the verdict judged.**
- The record maps 1:1: `G76 P(m)(r)(a) Q(dmin) R(d)` / `G76 X Z P(k) Q(dd) F`, where:
  - dd = the first pass's depth;
  - dmin = the step (constant depth) or the plan's minimum (constant area);
  - d = the finishing pass's own depth;
  - m = 1 + spring passes;
  - a = twice the flank angle.
- **Control model** (GSK988TA, Fanuc-compatible G76):
  - each roughing pass goes to `max(dd·√n, previous + dmin)`, up to k − d;
  - the first finishing pass cuts d, and m − 1 more repeat at k;
  - each pass starts `depth·tan(a/2)` along Z.
- **Refused by name with G76 chosen:** alternating infeed (the CL carries a new `alternating` flag; `ALT 1` is written to the stream only when set), a doubled angle outside 0/29/30/55/60/80 (so 29.5° is refused), and a one-pass thread.

**⚠ This changes posted output for the default G76 thread: `R0` becomes `R0.4`.** The golden `fanuc-lathe/thread_g76.nc` changes on one line: `G76 P010000 Q400 R0` → `G76 P010000 Q400 R0.4`.
- Why: with `R0` the control roughs 0.4, 0.8 and 1.2, then cuts its finishing pass at the root again. That is a fourth full-depth pass the verdict never judged. It's not a gouge, but it isn't what was verified.
- With `R0.4` it roughs 0.4 and 0.8 and finishes at 1.2: exactly the three passes we judge.
- Making `R0` true instead would have meant changing G32 output and the judged passes.
- Note: the #363 research said Q = infeed made the control cut a decreasing ladder. That isn't so, because dmin = infeed clamps every step equal. The real gap was R.

`docs/decisions/417-g76-matches-verified.md`

## How tested
- New app `lathe_post_g76_schedule` (4 tests):
  - a new flank, constant-area golden `thread_g76_area.nc` (`G76 P020055 Q100 R0.05` / `G76 X9.6 Z14 P1200 Q400 F2`): the control's schedule computed from the posted words matches the laid depths and stations within 1 µm;
  - the default (`R0.4`) and a 0.5 step (`Q500 R0.2`) also match;
  - one refusal per unexpressible option;
  - `ALT` survives the stream and the project file.
- Existing post, cl, inverted_post, lathe_post, golden_cl, project_roundtrip, tool_law, tool_gate and commands_undo suites are green.
- `clippy --tests -D warnings` (cl, post, motion, app, ui) is clean.
- The gate escalated to batch (cl changed). It fails only on tests already red on main: headless GPU, #415, and `swarf_pose_continuity` (PR #351).

## Not exercised / not confirmed by sources (draft until a lathe sim or machine run)
1. Which way Fanuc shifts Z per pass for flank infeed. This follows LinuxCNC's sign; either sign is gouge-safe.
2. Whether the control also shifts each pass's end Z. If not, early passes end up to k·tan θ off at the runout, shallower than the root.
3. How the minimum-depth clamp applies (read as a per-pass minimum, per the manual's definition).
4. Micron rounding of the words: the control's ladder can differ by under 1 µm.

None of these moves the finished thread form.

Changelog: G76 threading output states the passes that were verified: the finish allowance R is posted (default threads now post R0.4 instead of R0), and options G76 cannot express are refused by name (#417)

Fixes #417

title: feat(turning): threading infeed method and decreasing-depth pass schedule
body:
**Replaces #432** (opened from the old fork, which can no longer take pushes). Same head commit; nothing else changed.

Part of #363 (peck threading; the research comment there has the sources). Follow-up #417 (PR stacked on this one) makes the G76 output match these passes.

## What changed
**New threading op param `infeed_plan` (`turning::ThreadInfeed`).**
- **Infeed method:** radial, modified flank at an angle θ, or alternating flank.
- **Depth schedule:** constant depth, or constant area (first depth × √n).
- **Minimum depth per pass, finish allowance, and spring passes** (default 0, capped at 98).
- The existing `infeed` is the first-pass depth.
- It's shown as rows on the op's Passes tab (`thread_infeed_page.rs`).

**Kernel.** `crates/motion/src/turning/infeed.rs` lays the passes from the plan. `thread_in` calls `thread_planned_in` with the default plan.
- **Flank:** each pass starts shifted by −(tip − root)·tan θ along its travel. Finishing and spring passes sit on the pitch lattice, so lead and spindle phase never change.
- **Safety:** every pass stays inside the finished V exactly when θ ≤ half the insert's included angle. A larger angle is refused by name at the command (create, paste, edit, retype via `thread_gate`) and again at Generate.
- **Alternating:** flips the side each pass.

**The verdict judges the laid passes.** `the_verdict_reads_the_shifted_pass` pins a past-half-angle pass being convicted. `attach_cycle` moved to `thread_cycle.rs`.

**Defaults are byte-identical.** The default plan makes the same `blade::rungs(root, ref_top, infeed, 0)` call at the same stations.
- The op stamp includes the plan only when it isn't the default, so cached threads stay fresh.
- The project key is written only when non-default, so there's no version rung. An older build drops a non-default plan and cuts the radial ladder; that's not a gouge.
- No existing golden changed.

`docs/decisions/416-thread-infeed.md`

## How tested
- New motion `turning_thread_infeed` (8 tests):
  - √n depths with the minimum-depth clamp;
  - allowance plus spring-pass count;
  - flank shift, including the full 30°;
  - alternating flip;
  - verdict silent for every method × schedule on the thread fixture;
  - a shifted pass is convicted;
  - refusals by name.
- New app `turning_thread_infeed` (4/4, plus 1 after the merge): the plan runs in a document; refusals at create and edit; undo/redo (op goes stale); project round-trip with no key for the default plan.
- Existing suites unchanged and green: motion `turning_thread` and `turning_thread_cycle`; app `turning_thread`, `lathe_post_g76`, `lathe_field_tools` and `project_roundtrip`.
- `clippy --tests -D warnings` is clean.
- `scripts/gate.sh quick` passes except tests that already fail on main:
  - the headless-GPU ui tests;
  - `setup_stock_source::a_new_block_after_a_flip…` (#415);
  - `swarf_pose_continuity` (2 tests; red on main, fixed by PR #351).

## Not exercised (draft)
- GUI check of the new Passes-tab rows.
- **Posted G-code for non-default plans** (flank, constant area, allowance, spring passes) is new. It needs a lathe simulator or machine run before ready. Default plans post exactly as before.

Changelog: Threading op: infeed method (radial / modified flank / alternating), decreasing-depth schedule, minimum depth, finish allowance and spring passes (#416)

Fixes #416

title: feat(setup): per-setup post options and the setup's own tool-list export
body:
> Replaces #423, moved to the new fork (the old fork left NeoTech's network, and a push there closes the PR). Main is merged in. The two conflicts were module lists in `ui/src/state.rs` and `egui_app/tests.rs`, where both sides are kept (#371's tool_body). `setup_post_options` passes 8/8, the ui lib tests 11/11, and clippy for app and ui is clean. The hands-on GUI check is done (see the PR comments); since then main was merged again with a semantic per-op skip merge (#155 / #388).

## What changed
**Post options per setup** (same own / follow-the-document law #343 gave the post itself):
- `SetupDef.post_options: Option<PostOptions>`; `None` follows the document (every older file and every new setup).
- New undoable command `SetSetupPostOptions`; a no-op request is refused by name. A datum transfer copies the source setup's options with its post.
- `posting::post_options` returns the active setup's own options, else the document's (mirrors `post_of`). "Skip pauses and homes" is read per operation from that op's setup, so one setup can skip its stops while another keeps them. Output (one file per op) and thread output are program-wide: setups that disagree are refused by name, next to #343's one-mount check.
- Project file: an additive setup key `post_options` (`{"threading":"g32"|"g76","skip_stops":..,"per_op_files":..}`), omitted when `None`; no version step (stays v57), so a document that never sets it saves byte-identically. An unknown threading word is a corrupt-file refusal naming the setup.
- UI: the setup's **Post** page ends with a "Post options" group - radios "Use the document's post options" / "This setup has its own post options" and a note saying whose options the widgets above edit. The existing option widgets route to the active setup's own options when it has them.

**Setup tool-list export**
- `app::tool_list_export` (pure read): rows in first-use order from `tool_list::for_setup` - T number, name, diameter (mm), kind, holder (`D x L` or `none`), ops using it. `.csv` -> RFC 4180 CSV (CRLF, quoted fields); any other extension -> fixed-column text.
- The setup's **Tool list** page gets an "Export tool list…" button (save dialog, CSV/Text filters, default `<Setup>-tools.csv`). A command-free file write like the setup sheet: nothing enters the history.

## Readings
Debug, M5 Mac. `scripts/gate.sh quick` (all camcraft-app + camcraft-ui suites): 1725 passed, 4 failed - all known reds on main: `setup_stock_source::a_new_block_after_a_flip…` (#415) and the GPU headless trio (`headless_run_succeeds`, `headless_cli_exit_code_is_zero`, `egui_headless_cli_exit_code_is_zero`). Goldens (`golden_cl` 23, posts) and `project_roundtrip` (69) unchanged. Clippy `-D warnings` clean on app + ui.

- App `crates/app/tests/setup_post_options.rs`: `a_setups_own_post_options_do_undo_redo`, `a_setup_that_skips_posts_without_its_stops_while_the_other_follows_the_document`, `setups_disagreeing_on_the_output_are_refused_by_name`, `a_single_setup_document_posts_byte_identically`, `own_post_options_round_trip_and_old_files_follow_the_document`, `a_datum_transfer_keeps_the_source_setups_post_options`, `the_tool_list_exports_as_csv_and_text`, `a_tool_list_field_with_a_comma_is_quoted`.
- UI lib `egui_app::tests::setup_post_options`: `the_option_switches_land_on_the_active_setups_own_options`, `the_post_page_radio_gives_the_setup_its_own_options`, `the_tool_list_page_exports_the_setups_tools`.

title: fix(app): a typed Slot's caps no longer read as a gouge
body:
## What changed

A typed Slot whose cutter reaches its round caps was reported as a Gouge on every plunge and feed, so it never posted (#510). The cause was the region the verifier checks a Slot against, `operation::material::stadium`. It drew each cap as 16 chords **inscribed** in the true arc. A chord sits up to `h(1 - cos 5.625°)` inside the arc, and the slot generator's passes follow the true arc exactly, so the gouge check (`d(centre, boundary) >= r - GOUGE_TOL`) flagged a cutter that only touched the cap.

The caps are now the polygon **circumscribed** about the arc. Every chord is tangent to the arc, and the corners sit at `h / cos(phi/2)`. The chord count is set per slot (`cap_segments`) so a corner stands at most `CAP_SAG_BUDGET = 0.001 mm` outside the arc, with 16 to 2048 chords per cap. The first and last corner of each cap lie on the lines of the straight sides, so the sides stay exact. `GOUGE_TOL` is unchanged.

**Posted G-code: unchanged.** The generator is untouched. Only the gouge verdict changes, plus the drawn region outline, which moves by at most 1 µm.

## Readings (80×60×20 stock, EM-0600-4FL, a=(-15,0), b=(15,0), Top 20, Bottom 10, stepdown 5)

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| width 6 (centreline pass) | `Gouge` at moves 2, 3, 7, 8, 12, 13; post blocked | no warnings; posts |
| width 10 (rings at ±2) | `Gouge` on all 18 plunges/feeds; post blocked | no warnings; posts |
| cap-centre distance to boundary (r = 3) | 2.9855 (needs ≥ 2.99) | ≥ 3.0 (tangent) |
| path pushed +0.05 mm in X past the cap | (already convicted) | still convicted |

## Top-Z pass

The issue also reports that a Slot makes a feed pass at its Top before stepping down. The other 2D ladders do the same: `cut_levels(top, bottom, step)` starts at Top for pocket, contour, circular, trace, face and the 3D entries. It is an air pass, never a gouge. This PR pins the current behaviour rather than changing one op on its own. The decision file explains why and recommends a separate issue if the first level should be `top - stepdown` for every ladder.

## Tests

New `crates/app/tests/slot_caps.rs`:
- `a_slot_riding_its_round_caps_verifies_clean_and_posts`: widths 6 and 10, each run with stock as the source and with a slotted part model as the source. Each run has no Gouge, no warning that blocks posting, and `post_setup` writes the program.
- `a_slot_driven_past_its_cap_is_still_a_gouge`: the generated path, shifted 0.05 mm past the cap and checked against the op's own `region_of`, is convicted. The unshifted path checks clean.
- `the_stadium_region_hugs_the_true_caps`: at 721 angles on both caps, the true arc is inside the region and a point 2 µm past it is outside.
- `the_slot_ladder_starts_at_the_authored_top`: the cut levels are [20, 15, 10].

Before the fix, the first three fail and the fourth passes.

Gate (debug): camcraft-app lib (101), slot_caps, operations, area_controls, cutting_data, project_roundtrip, golden_cl, verify and blind_floor all pass. `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean.

## Not exercised

- The release `--ignored` lanes. No goldens move, because the generator output is unchanged.
- The UI region-outline drawing (the outline moves by at most 1 µm).
- Hand-run in the GUI or on a real machine.

Decision file: `docs/decisions/510-slot-cap-region.md`.

Changelog: A typed Slot whose cutter reaches its round ends is no longer falsely reported as a gouge, so it posts again (#510)

Fixes #510

title: feat(app): recognise pockets and slots and turn them into operations
body:
## What changed

Pocket and slot recognition, headless (app layer and MCP; no GUI changes).

- **`camcraft_app::recognize`** (new module: `mod`, `walls`, `shape`, `op`):
  - `pockets_of(world, model)` reads the model's planar-face topology (`geometry::feature`, the same B-rep `list_features` and the pick tools use).
  - A level, up-facing face is a **floor** when the facets across its outer ring rise from it and lean into it (a concave edge), and those walls face each other across the floor.
  - Walled all round, it is a **closed pocket**. With wall-less spans it is an **open pocket**. A straight channel (at least 2 widths long, both long sides walled, each end wholly walled or wholly open, area within 3% of the shape) is a **slot**, with each end open, round or square.
  - Each result carries:
    - the outer ring (world XY, counter-clockwise), island count and area;
    - floor Z, top Z (highest wall point) and depth;
    - the **tightest inside corner radius** (0 = sharp, `None` where no two walls meet) and the **open spans**;
    - for a slot: centreline ends, **width**, length and end kinds.
  - Shoulders, corner steps, top faces and a plate around a boss are not pockets.
- **`recognize::operation_for`** maps a feature onto `CreateOperation`'s inputs, so creating it is one undoable History step with every field editable:
  - a pocket (or a slot with a square closed end, which a round cap would leave standing) becomes a **2D Pocket** on a pick of the floor face, with `bottom_z` at the selection bottom and `top_z` at the selection bottom + depth;
  - a slot with round or open ends becomes a **Slot** along its centreline: width, fixed heights, source stock, open ends running full width out to the floor's edge.
- **MCP `detect_pockets {model, create?, tool?, name?}`** lists the features, each with the floor's `face:0x…` id (the id `list_features` prints) and the operation kind it would create. With `create` it adds that operation, one undo step.
- Decision record: `docs/decisions/35-pocket-slot-recognition.md`.

Provenance: the concave-edge depression rule follows Joshi & Chang (CAD 20(2), 1988). The minimum-area rectangle follows Freeman & Shapira (CACM 18(7), 1975). No vendor material was consulted.

## How tested

Quick gate, debug: `pocket_recognition` 10/10, `mcp_pockets` 3/3, `mcp` 13/13, `mcp_pick` 7/7, `mcp_setup` 18/18, `cli` 2/2, `feature` 3/3. `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean.

Pinning tests, on watertight meshes built in code (`crates/app/tests/pocket_support`):
- `a_rectangular_pocket_is_closed_with_sharp_corners`
- `a_pocket_with_corner_radii_reports_its_tightest_corner` (r 4)
- `a_round_ended_closed_slot_is_a_slot_between_its_cap_centres`
- `a_through_slot_is_open_at_both_ends`
- `an_open_slot_with_a_square_end_machines_as_a_pocket`
- `parts_without_pockets_list_none` (plain block, shoulder, corner step, boss)
- `degenerate_input_refuses_cleanly` (unknown model; NaN, infinite and zero-area facets; a torn half mesh)
- `a_recognised_pocket_becomes_an_undoable_pocket_that_cuts_to_its_floor`: generates with no Gouge, reaches the floor, stays inside the ring; undo removes it
- `an_open_slot_machined_as_a_pocket_cuts_its_floor_without_a_gouge`
- `a_recognised_slot_becomes_a_slot_cut_along_its_centreline`: checks the path geometry exactly; undo removes it
- MCP: `detect_pockets_lists_a_rounded_pocket_and_creates_its_pocket` (generate + verify ok; undo/redo), `detect_pockets_creates_a_slot_for_a_through_slot`, `detect_pockets_refuses_bad_arguments_by_name`

## Not exercised / known gaps

- **#510 (filed):** every typed Slot whose cutter rides its round cap is reported as a gouge today, recognised or not. The likely cause is the stadium region's chorded caps measured against `GOUGE_TOL`. Until #510 lands, a recognised slot's Slot op refuses to post. Its test checks the path geometry, not the verifier's verdict.
- **Not recognised:**
  - through pockets / windows (no floor face);
  - non-level floors and tilted setup frames (the read is world +Z);
  - curved slots, T-slots and undercuts.
  - Each level of a stepped pocket is its own feature.
- An open pocket's open side is not written into the area controls' open boundary. The tool's corner radius stays uncut where a wall meets an open edge.
- **GUI entry point:** #511. Not exercised on real STEP parts or by hand. The release-tier heavy lanes were not run.

Changelog: Pocket and slot recognition - `detect_pockets` (MCP) lists a model's closed/open pockets and slots (depth, corner radius, slot width, open sides) and creates the Pocket or Slot that machines one, one undo step (#35)

Fixes #35

title: fix(sim): judge spindle-C moves at the station pose and fixed steel in the machine frame
body:
Fixes a missed fixture hit under a spindle-C turn (#486). Two causes, both reproduced on main first.

## What was wrong
1. **Fixed steel was judged in the part frame only.** For a C move the live tool never leaves its station (+X), so steel there is hit at every C. The part-frame reading only saw it near C 0; `posed_steel::upright_turn` answers Unjudged for that pose, so the part-frame verdict stood. End to end: a Rotary Contour on the mill-turn C bar with a fixed steady at the station had no hit on the far side of the bar (C≈180), and the post gate was silent too.
2. **Steel riding the part was judged at the wrong pose.** `cl::stamp_c` gave every piece of a split move the move's end axis, while mid-turn the tool points along the diagonal. A chuck jaw on the diagonal at holder radius was silent.

## What changed
- `crates/cl/src/cl/rotary.rs`: `split` stamps each piece with the station pose at its own C (the move's axis turned by the turn left in the move). The last piece keeps the move's axis bit for bit. The post writes only C for C moves, so the stream and the `c_axis_helix.nc` golden are unchanged.
- New `crates/sim/src/verify/c_steel.rs`:
  - `station_poses` reads each C move's pose from its C, so toolpaths cached before this fix are judged right at the gate without regenerating.
  - `fixed_hits` judges fixed steel in the machine frame along the station ray.
  - The spindle line is recovered from the stamped tips, then from the op's rotary axis, and used only if every tip sits on its ray within 1e-4 mm. With no line, or an arc or non-finite C move, a C move against fixed steel is a hit (fails closed).
- `crates/sim/src/verify/workholding.rs`: both `_held` wrappers judge the station-posed path, then add the machine-frame fixed-steel hits. Add-only: no existing verdict loosens.
- Decision record: `docs/decisions/486-stamp-c-axis.md`.

## How tested
- sim `c_axis_fixture` (8). Fail on main: `the_machine_meets_fixed_steel_at_the_station_mid_turn` (line given and line unknown), `a_rapid_turn_past_fixed_steel_convicts_as_a_rapid`, `steel_riding_the_part_meets_the_pose_the_turn_passes_through`, `every_stamped_piece_states_the_station_pose_at_its_own_c`. Also `a_path_stamped_before_486_is_read_at_the_pose_its_c_states`, plus clear and fail-closed controls.
- app `c_axis_fixture` (2): `fixed_steel_at_the_station_convicts_cuts_on_the_far_side_of_the_bar` (fails on main; checks generation and `posting::fixture_findings`) and an off-station control.
- Unit tests in `cl::rotary` and `verify::c_steel`.
- Quick gate (escalated to batch because `cl` changed): every suite green except the known headless-GPU ui tests (no adapter on this Mac). After merging main (#491's `arc_bulge`, a `mod` line conflict): sim `c_axis_fixture`, `posed_fixture`, `fixture_stack_span`, app `c_axis_fixture`, `fixtures` and `c_axis_live` pass; clippy `-D warnings` is clean on cl, sim and app.
- Verdicts in existing suites are unchanged; the only new verdicts are the newly caught hits.

## Not exercised
No posted G-code changes (C-only output and goldens unchanged), so no machine run is needed. May touch the same `verify/mod.rs` area as #488 (a `mod` line at most).

Changelog: Fixture checks under a spindle-C turn judge the tool at its machine station pose: fixed steel at the live-tool station and part-riding steel mid-turn are now caught instead of passing the post gate (#486)

Fixes #486

title: fix(post): the Siemens 840D safe retract comes from the machine file
body:
Stacked on #501 (which is stacked on #477) — merge those first. Until then this PR's diff against `main` also shows their commits; this PR's own change is commit acbc6b6c.

## What changed

`sinumerik.cps` lifted Z with `G53 Z0` in two places: the after-operation home move and the program end. That assumes machine Z0 is the top of Z travel. Siemens' public documentation leaves the reference point and machine zero to the machine builder, so the post now reads #495's `machine.safeRetractZ`, the same way #501 does for the Tormach post:

- **Stated value** (0 included) posts `G0 G53 Z<v>` + `G0 G53 X0 Y0` for a home move, and `G53 Z<v>` at the end. The value is in mm, which is the unit this dialect writes. A non-zero value also adds the header comment `; SAFE RETRACT G53 Z<v> - STATED BY THE MACHINE`.
- **No machine** (null or unnamed) keeps today's `G53 Z0`, byte-identical.
- **A named machine that states no value** gets one counted `message()` naming the machine and the `safe_retract` key, and no retract is written. The XY half of the home move is dropped too, so XY never moves without the Z lift first. The in-app gate blocks the write.
- **No name exemption.** #501 exempts Tormach because PathPilot defines the top-of-travel convention. Siemens documents no such rule, so a model named "Siemens …" is refused like any other.

Docs: `assets/posts/AGENTS.md`, `assets/machines/AGENTS.md`, and the decision file `docs/decisions/503-sinumerik-safe-retract.md`.

**Output change:** none for anything shipped. Every shipped mill file and the default `3axis-vmc.mch` (the conformance goldens' machine) state 0, and the goldens are byte-exact. A user machine without the key, `millturn.mch`, or a document saved before #495 with a mounted machine is now refused by name through this post.

## How tested

New suite `crates/app/tests/sinumerik_safe_retract.rs`:
- `a_stated_z0_and_no_machine_post_byte_identical`: null machine and default VMC keep `G53 Z0`. Every shipped Z0 machine posts the same program as the no-machine path, apart from the name line.
- `a_stated_safe_z_posts_that_z`: covers both the mirror and the raw-file door. Z290 is posted at the home move and at the end, with the header comment. An inch file's 11.5 is posted as Z292.1.
- `a_machine_without_a_safe_z_is_refused_by_name`: covers both doors, and a "Siemens"-named model as well. The machine is refused once and no G53 is written.

Two fixture updates: `coolant.rs` and `coolant_followups.rs` built a bare `Machine` that they post through every mill post. They now state `safe_retract_z: Some(0.0)`.

Gate:
- `cargo test -p camcraft-post`: all green.
- Every `camcraft-app` debug test binary (172) is green, including conformance (goldens byte-exact), tormach_safe_retract, after_op, posting, coolant, and program_comments. The only one not run is the slow `center_cut_multiaxis` lane, which does not post.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --tests -- -D warnings` is clean.

## Not exercised

- No real machine and no Hub sim.
- The `G75` fixed-point form (Siemens' documented tool-change position move) was considered and not adopted. See the decision file.
- The UI machine sheet still does not show the key (same as #501).

Changelog: Siemens 840D post retracts to the machine's stated safe Z (`safe_retract`, machine coordinates) and refuses a machine that states none, instead of assuming machine Z0 is the top of travel

Fixes #503

title: fix(sim): a chamfer or deburr owns its declared edge break
body:
## What changed

A 2D Chamfer or a Deburr generated with no warnings, but the post gate then refused it as a gouge. The program sim judged the bevel the op exists to cut against the model's sharp edge. This PR makes the op own its break, the issue's option 1. The bevel comes from the op's **stated** parameters, not from its moves.

- **`cl::EdgeBreak`** (new, `crates/cl/src/cl/edge_break.rs`): a record of the break the op was asked to cut. It holds the edge as a polyline at its own height, the bevel depth at the edge, and the slope. `floor_at(x, y)` gives the cone swept along the edge, limited to the stated plan width. It is carried on `cl::Toolpath::breaks` and is empty for every other kind.
- **Generators declare their breaks:**
  - `machining2d::chamfer` declares the picked loops at `top_z`, with depth `width*tan(angle)` and slope `tan(angle)`.
  - `finishing3d::deburr` declares its edge runs, with depth `drop` and slope `cot(half-angle)`.
  - Neither reads the declaration back off the moves.
- **Sim credit** (new, `crates/sim/src/stock_sim/edge_break.rs`, `credit_breaks`): this runs after `deviate`, from `simulate_document`. A gouge column inside a declared break's width, under a model top no higher than the edge, is re-judged against the bevel:
  - Cut down to the bevel (within `DEV_TOL`): clean.
  - Cut below the bevel: still a gouge, charged at its depth under the bevel.
  - Rest is untouched.
  - An edge nobody declared, or a boss standing above the edge, keeps the model's verdict.
  - `deviate` and `deviate_field` are not touched, so this stays clear of #481's `wall_slack.rs`.
- **Deburr skips steep edges** (generator fix, found while reproducing). The issue said the deburr's deeper gouge columns were link rapids. They were the vertical corner edges. A vertical cone riding a vertical edge, apex `drop` under each point, countersinks the corner down to the window floor. With the default window that is 9.8 mm on the 10 mm brick, a real gouge. The kernel now skips any edge that climbs steeper than the cone's flank, and says so in a path note.
- **Persistence:** the cached path gets an additive `breaks` key (`project/break_dto.rs`). Absent means none, so an old cache is judged against the sharp model until it regenerates (stricter, never looser).
- **Tilted (3+2) frames:** `TiltedFrame::world_path` translates the breaks when the frame is upright and drops them when it is tilted. A posed program is refused by the verdict anyway.
- **Multi-setup programs:** when the program spans setups that hold the part differently, only the final frame's ops' breaks are credited.
- **Decision record:** `docs/decisions/303-op-owns-its-break.md`.

## Readings (upstream/main b2659dbe, brick 40x20x10, stock = brick, CM-0600-90)

| Job | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| 2D Chamfer, kind defaults | `gouge: ... 624 cell(s), worst 0.74 mm` | gate clean, posts |
| Deburr, kind defaults (w 0.5, window = model) | `gouge: ... 495 cell(s), worst 9.80 mm at (19.94, -9.81, z 0.20)`: the vertical-corner countersink | gate clean, posts (4 vertical edges skipped, with a note) |
| Deburr, the issue's ride (w 2, tips z 6..8) | `gouge: ... 1544 cell(s), worst 3.80 mm` | gate clean, posts |
| Default chamfer, moves lowered 0.3 mm | - | `gouge: ... worst 0.30 mm` |
| Chamfer picks brick A, moves carried onto brick B | - | `gouge: ... worst 0.7x mm` |

## Tests

- `crates/app/tests/edge_break_gate.rs` (new, 5 tests):
  - `a_default_2d_chamfer_on_a_finished_brick_posts` (fails on main)
  - `a_default_deburr_on_a_finished_brick_posts` (fails on main)
  - `a_chamfer_ridden_deeper_than_its_stated_break_still_refuses`
  - `a_chamfer_on_an_edge_it_was_not_asked_to_break_still_refuses`
  - `the_declared_break_survives_save_and_load`
- `crates/sim/tests/edge_break_credit.rs` (new, 5 tests):
  - the declared chamfer is clean
  - over-deep is charged exactly 0.3
  - an undeclared edge keeps its full verdict
  - a boss above the edge is never credited
  - a sloped edge's bevel matches a brute-force swept cone
- `crates/motion/tests/chamfer_circular.rs`: `the_chamfer_declares_the_break_it_was_asked_to_cut` (new).
- `crates/app/tests/deburr_links.rs`: the #304 link test now rides a model with two blocks. The single brick, with its vertical edges skipped, is one run and has no link left to test.
- `crates/motion/tests/deburr.rs`:
  - `a_vertical_edge_is_skipped_out_loud_never_countersunk` (new).
  - `convex_creases_all_ride_a_closed_box_breaks_every_edge` renamed to `..._every_level_edge`. The box's level creases ride and its 4 vertical corners are skipped with a note.
  - `the_window_clips_along_the_edges_own_line` re-pinned on a sloped (1 in 2) rim, because the old curtain's vertical sides are now skipped.
- Test-literal updates for the new `Toolpath` field, with no behaviour change: sim rapids/pose tests, motion `one_descent`, app `turning_rapids_tests`.
- Gate results (debug):
  - `cargo test --no-fail-fast -p camcraft-cl -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-app`: 282 binaries, all green.
  - `cargo clippy -p camcraft-cl -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- Release `--ignored` lanes:
  - all of `camcraft-sim`, plus app `operations`, `stock_sim_document` and `posting`: green.
  - app `stock_engine_agreement`: its 2 known-red tests (#494) fail as they do on main. That suite calls `deviate` directly, not `simulate_document`, so this change does not reach it.
- No golden changed. No chamfer or deburr goldens exist.

## Not exercised

- GUI Deviate view, by eye. A real cut.
- A chamfer on a 3+2 tilted frame: its breaks are dropped, and the posed verdict refuses it as before.
- Deburr edges that are shallower than the flank but whose adjacent face rises above the edge (a bottom rim ridden from above). The window keeps the default off them. If one is ridden, the sim still convicts it, correctly.

Changelog: A 2D Chamfer or Deburr on a finished part now posts: the program sim judges the op's declared edge break against its stated width and angle instead of the sharp model edge, while a deeper or undeclared break still refuses as a gouge; the deburr no longer rides vertical edges (it countersank the corners) and says so (#303)

Fixes #303

title: fix(post): the Tormach safe retract comes from the machine file
body:
## What changed

The Tormach post's safe retract `G53 G0 Z0` assumed machine Z0 is the top of Z travel. That holds on a Tormach, but on a LinuxCNC machine homed with Z0 at the bottom it rapids down into the part (reported on #435).

- **Machine file:** an optional `safe_retract` on the linear Z part gives the retract Z in MACHINE coordinates, in the file's length unit (scaled like travel). Zero counts as a stated value. A non-number, or the key on any other axis, refuses the file and names the axis. The mirror carries it as `safeRetractZ` (mm). The script sees `machine.safeRetractZ` (or `null`) and `machine.model`, the model name through either door (app mirror or CLI raw file).
- **Shipped machines:** every Tormach `.mch` states `0.0`. So do `vmc.mch`, `tilthead.mch` and the default `3axis-vmc.mch` (`"safeRetractZ": 0.0`).
- **tormach.cps:**
  - A stated safe Z posts `G53 G0 Z<that>`.
  - With no machine, or a model named "Tormach..." that states no safe Z, the output is unchanged (`G53 G0 Z0` + `G30`).
  - Any other machine that states no safe Z gets one counted `message()` that names the machine and the key, and no retract line is written. The in-app gate blocks the write.
  - A non-zero safe Z drops `G30`, because an unset G30 position on LinuxCNC is the machine origin. The header then says `(SAFE RETRACT G53 Z<v> - STATED BY THE MACHINE)`.
- **Docs:** `assets/machines/AGENTS.md`, `assets/posts/AGENTS.md`, `docs/CNC-INTERMEDIATE.md`, and the decision file `docs/decisions/495-safe-retract.md` (alternatives considered, plus notes on the other posts).

## How tested

New `crates/app/tests/tormach_safe_retract.rs`:
- `the_shipped_tormach_machines_post_byte_identical`: every library Tormach posts byte-identical with and without the key. A null machine and the default VMC also keep `G53 G0 Z0` / `G30`.
- `a_stated_safe_z_posts_that_z`: covers the mirror and the raw door. An inch file scales, there is no G30, and the header comment is written.
- `a_non_tormach_machine_without_a_safe_z_is_refused_by_name`: covers the mirror and the raw door, and checks that a Tormach-named file without the key still posts Z0.
- `a_garbled_safe_retract_refuses_the_file`

Gate: `cargo test -p camcraft-post` (all), plus 64 camcraft-app suites touching posts and machines, all green. These include conformance (every golden byte-exact), tormach_post, tormach_machines, machine, machine_library, posting, fanuc_post, inverted_post, program_comments, project_roundtrip, wear_comp and control_comp. `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-app --tests -- -D warnings` is clean.

## Not exercised

- No real machine cut and no Hub sim.
- The UI machine sheet does not show the new key yet.
- The CLI `post` binary was not smoke-run by hand. Its raw-door path is covered by the tests.
- Behaviour change: a document saved before this change with a mounted non-Tormach machine (for example the library "VMC 3-axis") stores that machine without the key. Posting it through the Tormach post is now refused by name until the machine is re-mounted.

Changelog: Tormach post retracts to the machine's stated safe Z (`safe_retract`, machine coordinates) and refuses a non-Tormach machine that states none, instead of assuming machine Z0 is the top of travel

Fixes #495

title: feat(post): probe positioning moves post as protected stop-on-contact moves
body:
## What changed

The positioning feeds of a probe cycle (the descent from the rapid / safe plane to each touch's start, the bore entry to its centre, the rise back to the safe plane) were plain G01. They now post as protected moves: stop on contact and alarm if the stylus trips on the way.

- **Stream:** `post::dump` marks every non-rapid straight move of a path that carries probing touches, other than the touches and their incremental back-offs, as a new `GUARD x y z F feed` record (`Record::Guard`, `probe_rec::GuardRec`, documented in `docs/CNC-INTERMEDIATE.md`). An arc or a feed with no rate in a probe path is refused with a WARN. The safe-plane rapids stay rapids.
- **Engine:** the new `onProbeGuard` hook (properties `X Y Z Feed`, `StartX/Y/Z`). A script without it is refused by name, once per operation. There is no PRELUDE default, because a plain feed would be the silent wrong answer.
- **Fanuc (`fanuc.cps`):** `G31 X.. Y.. Z.. F..`, then for each moving axis `IF[ABS[#506n-<end>]GT0.001]THEN#3000=3(PROBE HIT ON POSITIONING)`. This works because, with no skip signal, the skip position is the block end.
- **Tormach PathPilot (`tormach.cps`):** `G38.3 X.. Y.. Z.. F..`, then `oN if [#5070 EQ 1]` / `(MSG, PROBE HIT ON POSITIONING)` / `M2` / `oN endif`, with O-words from 5001.
- **Inverted axes (`invert.rs`):** a GUARD is mirrored like an absolute move.
- **Viewer map (`posting.rs`):** a GUARD counts as one motion record.

Sources (behaviour only): Fanuc's published custom macro B / G31 skip documentation (#5061-#5063, #3000); the LinuxCNC G-code reference (G38.3, #5070, O-code conditionals, MSG); Tormach's PathPilot machine-code reference (G38.2-G38.5 and M2 supported).

## Tests

- New `crates/app/tests/probe_guard.rs`:
  - `the_positioning_feeds_of_a_probe_path_are_marked_protected`: every mode; no plain feed left; GUARD count per mode; one record per move.
  - `the_guard_record_round_trips_and_refuses_malformed_lines`
  - `fanuc_writes_protected_moves_as_g31_with_a_contact_alarm`: new golden `nc/fanuc/probe_corner.nc`.
  - `tormach_writes_protected_moves_as_g38_3_with_a_trip_test`: new golden `nc/tormach/probe_guard_moves.nc`. It pins the guard blocks only, because Tormach's touches are #362 / PR #376.
  - `a_probing_post_without_on_probe_guard_is_refused_by_name`
- Regenerated Fanuc goldens: `probe_bore_centre`, `probe_corner_negative`, `probe_edge_negative_x`. The only change is G01 → G31 + the alarm line.
- `probe_op::the_posted_g31_z_is_the_tip_at_the_expected_contact` now tells touches from guards.
- Gate: these camcraft-app binaries are green, all run on the final head: conformance, fanuc_post, inverted_axis_display, inverted_equivalence, inverted_post, per_op_files, post_not_judged, posting, probe_guard, probe_op, probe_pick, probe_reach, project_roundtrip, scripting, tormach_machines, tormach_post. All camcraft-post tests are green. `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-app --tests -- -D warnings` is clean.

title: fix(sim): fixture laws pad each arc chord by its sagitta
body:
Found while gating #339 slice 2 (PR #492): the fixture box laws judged an arc by its **inscribed** chords at the bare band radius, so steel within the arc's sagitta (about 0.01 mm on R30) was missed. This applied to every fixture.

## What changed
New `crates/sim/src/verify/arc_bulge.rs` (`Bulge`, `ARC_PAD` = 1e-3).

**The pad.** For each chord, with ψ = |θ|/2 and θ = sweep/n (the same equal steps `arc_chords` cuts):
- **Across the chord:** r(1 − cos ψ), the sagitta.
- **Along the chord:** r(ψ − sin ψ).

These bound the true point against the chord point at the same sweep fraction for ψ ≤ π/2. Past a half turn, 2r is used for both. Every arc chord adds `ARC_PAD`, because arc centres sit on the 1 µm lattice.

**XY arcs (box laws, `stack_span`):** the band radius grows by `hypot(across, along) + ARC_PAD`. A helix's z between joints is already exact.

**XZ/YZ arcs:**
- The radius grows by `along·|t_h| + across·|n_h| + ARC_PAD`.
- The z window is the arc's true range between joints. Builder-split arcs are Z-monotone, so the strict-dip silence for a lead arc landing tangent on a face is kept.
- An arc that turns past its circle's top or bottom inside a chord gets that piece's window carried to the extremum ± ARC_PAD.

**Posed sweep (`posed_steel`):** an arc move's capsules grow by `Bulge::deviation()`. The interval travel already covered all but about 1e-4 mm; the pad makes the bound hold for any interval length.

**Straight moves get a pad of exactly 0.0,** so every straight verdict is bit-identical.

**Bad arcs fail closed:** a non-finite centre or radius gives a NaN pad, which the predicates read as a hit.

`docs/decisions/491-arc-sagitta.md`

## How tested
New sim `fixture_arc_sagitta` (10 tests). These four fail on main and pass now:
- **The issue's repro:** R30 arc, r3 flute, 3 chords, sagitta 0.00937, box half a sagitta inside the true reach → Flute. The same arc as a rapid → Rapid.
- The holder band is padded too.
- An XZ arc bulging sideways reports.
- An unsplit XZ arc dipping past its chords reports.

These also pass, as pins:
- Steel 0.002 mm beyond the true reach stays clean.
- A YZ arc bulging sideways reports.
- An XZ arc landing tangent on a face stays silent, while 0.001 deeper hits.
- A posed arc within its sagitta reports.
- Straight moves keep their verdicts.
- The apex sits mid-chord.

**Gates:**
- `scripts/gate.sh quick upstream/main` (all sim suites) is green.
- The full camcraft-app suite, all 170 binaries, is green with **no existing verdict changed**. After the final syntax-only edit, sim in full and the app fixture, rotary, carried, posed-contact, arc-entry and posting suites were re-run, all green.
- `clippy -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-app --tests -D warnings` is clean.

**Note:** #476's `mesh_steel` has its own `ARC_PAD` and can read `Bulge::deviation` once both land. #413 is the same family in the field engine and envelope scan, and stays its own issue.

Changelog: Fixture collision laws pad each arc chord by its sagitta, so steel within an arc's bulge is no longer missed (#491)

Fixes #491

title: fix(app): a saved machine file keeps its key order
body:
**Stacked on #478** (#383, the Machines pane edits and saves `.mch` files). The #480 work is a95093c0.

## What changed
A `.mch` saved from the Machines pane keeps the key order it was read in. Keys the file didn't have go at the end of their object. Project files are untouched.

- **New `crates/app/src/machine/order.rs`** (with provenance).
  - It reads the source text once and records the key order of every object and array as a `KeyOrder` tree. A duplicated key keeps its first position and takes its last value, like `serde_json::Value`.
  - `to_pretty(value, order)` writes the same layout as `to_string_pretty` (2-space indent, `": "`), with keys in the recorded order, then any unknown keys sorted.
- **`MachineDraft`** gains `order: KeyOrder`. `open` and `from_template` fill it from the source, `blank` leaves it empty, and `text()` writes through `to_pretty`. Edits still act on the plain `serde_json::Value`, so `fields.rs` is unchanged.
- **No new dependency, and `serde_json/preserve_order` is not turned on workspace-wide.** That would change every JSON writer, project files included. `indexmap` is already in the lock file, but using it directly would still be a dependency change, and the order visitor is about 60 lines.
- The `docs/decisions/383-machines-edit.md` "key order" entry is replaced by this decision.

## How tested
- `machine_edit::a_saved_file_keeps_its_key_order_and_new_keys_go_last`: a hand-written file in deliberately unsorted order, with unknown keys, gets an edit plus a new `spindle`/`max_speed` block. The saved file's exact key list is checked.
- `machine_edit::a_new_machine_writes_the_same_text_serde_json_would`: with no recorded order, the output matches `to_string_pretty` byte for byte.
- `machine_edit`, `machine_library`, `machine` and `project_roundtrip` (69) pass. Project files are byte-identical; no project writer changed.
- `clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --tests -D warnings` is clean.

## Limitation
Only the key order is kept. A hand-written file's inline arrays (e.g. `[0, 0, 1]` on one line) still come out multi-line.

Changelog: A machine file saved from the Machines pane keeps its key order (new keys go last) (#480)

title: fix(machine): built-in lathe and mill-turn Z stroke in program coordinates
body:
## What changed

The built-in **Lathe** (`assets/machines/lathe.mch`) and **Mill-turn** (`assets/machines/millturn.mch`) stated a machine-frame Z stroke (`-615..0`, `-620..0`). The limit checker (`app::machine::check_document`) reads travel bands in **program coordinates through the work offset** (#457). With Z0 on the face, every move in front of it was out of stroke: clearance, approach, and facing allowance. No turning program posted on either built-in.

**Reproduced on main before the fix:** a face-and-turn job (Z0 on the finished face, 1 mm facing allowance, clearance Z 5) was refused on both machines, down to the facing approach (`Face1: move 0 reaches 0.800 in Z, the stroke is -615.000..0.000`).

Fix: Z is restated as the full stroke each way, the convention PR #477 applies to the VMC and tilt-head. Lathe Z is now `-615..615` and Mill-turn Z is `-620..620`. **X stays one-sided** (`0..320`, `0..650`). A lathe X is measured from the spindle centreline, and the centreline is the program's X0, so `0..R` is already a program-frame band. The Mill-turn Y (`-100..100`) was already symmetric. No checker code changed. This branch is off main, not stacked on #477. It leaves `assets/machines/AGENTS.md` and the module doc alone so the two PRs do not conflict; the convention text is in #477. The decision is in `docs/decisions/493-lathe-z-stroke.md`.

## How tested

- New `crates/app/tests/lathe_stroke.rs`:
  - `a_turning_job_on_the_built_in_lathe_clears_the_face_and_posts` and `a_turning_job_on_the_built_in_millturn_clears_the_face_and_posts`: Facing plus Profile Rough on a flanged bar, clearance Z 5. `check_document` is clean, `verification_report` has no problems, and `post_setup` posts. Both failed on main.
  - `a_clearance_past_the_lathe_carriage_still_refuses_by_name` and `a_clearance_past_the_millturn_quill_still_refuses_by_name`: a clearance of L + 20 is refused with `Rough1: move N reaches 635.000 in Z, the stroke is -615.000..615.000` (and the 620 equivalent). There is no X complaint, and the post is refused.
  - `lathe_x_stays_a_centreline_band`: X stays `0..R` on both machines.
- These app suites all passed (debug): lathe_stroke, lathe_post, lathe_post_g76, lathe_post_refusals, lathe_field_sim, lathe_field_tools, lathe_spindle_fit, lathe_spindle_keyed, lathe_spindle_law, lathe_cross_drill, turning, turning_profile, turning_bore, turning_holder, turning_blade, turning_contour, turning_contour_stock, turning_form, turning_thread, turning_axial_rapids, turning_stock_approach, turning_insert_zone, drill_prior, drill_prior_kinds, drilling_axial, c_axis_live, coolant_followups, carried_fixtures_cache, conformance, machine, machine_library, posting, setup_mount.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean.
- Posted G-code is unchanged: no golden NC/CL file changed, and the post scripts read no linear travel.

## Not exercised

- I did not run the ui crate suites. The ui crate is untouched. Its tests mount the built-in Lathe by name for door and route checks, but none of them reads the stroke.
- GUI and the headless MCP path were not run.
- The Mill-turn X `0..650` also judges its milling ops (live tooling). A milled feature in -X would still read as out of stroke. That is a separate question and is noted in the decision file.

title: feat(app): fixture library - save, insert and delete user fixtures
body:
**Stacked on #482** (#339 slice 4, fixture UX), which is on #476. Slice 6 of #339 per the triage on the issue: a fixture library.

## What changed
**The library file.** One `fixtures.camfixtures` in the user fixtures folder: `CAMCRAFT_FIXTURES` (an absolute path), otherwise `<data dir>/camcraft/fixtures`, beside the machines folder.
- Versioned envelope: `{format: "camcraft-fixtures", version: 1, units: "mm", fixtures: [{name, note?, datum: {origin, rot}, facets}]}`. Save → load → save is byte-stable.
- **Refused by name, whole file:** bad JSON; wrong format, version or units; a missing name, datum or facets; a duplicate name; an empty mesh; a malformed facet; a rotation that isn't one; over 2M facets; the reserved `Machine/Table` name.
- A missing file reads as an empty library. A corrupt one is reported in the dialog, never shown as empty, and never overwritten.
- The atomic write mirrors #383's machine store. It's a short copy, to be folded into one helper once both land; see the decisions file.

**The datum.**
- An entry's facets are the fixture's own model-frame mesh, and its datum is a frame in that mesh.
- On insert, the model's pose is `P ∘ D⁻¹`, so the datum lands on the pick.
- The default datum is the model origin, so a fixture saved and re-inserted at its old pose stands exactly where it was. The other choice is "Bottom centre".

**Duplicate names:**
- In the library, saving an existing name asks "Replace …?". There is no silent rename.
- In the document, an inserted name that's taken lands as "Vise (2)", "Vise (3)" and so on.

**`InsertFixture`, one undo unit.** It spawns the model with the entry's facets, sets its pose, and tags it to the Fixtures node's setup. It refuses by name a setup that no longer exists, a non-finite or non-rotation pick, or a bad entry. There is no new project key: inserted fixtures are ordinary tagged models.

**Save and delete edit the library file.** They are save actions with confirmation, not undo entries, like machine files (#383).

**UI.** The setup's Fixtures node menu gains **Save fixture to library…** and **Insert from library…**, each a modal dialog.
- **Save:** the setup's fixtures as checkboxes, the datum choice, and a note.
- **Insert:** the entry list, X/Y/Z in display units, and roll/pitch/yaw. Buttons are Insert, **Delete from library…** (with confirmation) and Close.
- Picking the datum in the viewport is a follow-up.

All assets are user-made; no vendor libraries.

`docs/decisions/339-fixture-library.md`

## How tested
- App `fixture_library` (6 tests):
  - envelope round-trip, and refusals by name;
  - the folder resolver;
  - save, replace and delete file edits;
  - the datum placement maths;
  - insert with undo, redo and the project round-trip.
- UI `egui_app::fixture_library_tests` (4 tests, driven through the real dialog):
  - the menu rows;
  - save, then the replace confirmation;
  - Insert queues one undoable command, and delete happens only after confirmation;
  - a corrupt library is named in the dialog.
- Regressions green: app `fixture_ux` 8, `fixtures` 14, `commands_undo` 32, `fixture_mesh` 3; ui lib 352, ui `tests/fixtures` 7, `tests/models` 4. One #482 test's menu-label list now includes the two new rows.
- Known failures: the headless-GPU test, and the release-lane `tool_editor_snapshot`.
- `clippy -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --tests -D warnings` is clean.

## Not exercised (draft until the contributor's GUI check)
A hands-on check. The test kit is prepared and sandboxed with `CAMCRAFT_FIXTURES`.

title: test(sim): pin that the fixture box laws already convict every mesh penetration
body:
**Stacked on #476** (#339 slice 1, fixture mesh). Slice 2 of #339, answered by tests rather than new law. The full analysis is posted on #339.

## What this is
Slice 2 asked whether the mesh law must also **convict**: catch penetrations the box laws let through.

**Answer: no.**
- A meshed fixture's box is the exact AABB of the same transformed vertices the mesh law reads (`model::entity_world_aabb` / `world_facets`). `mesh_refined` only reads a mesh whose AABB equals the law's box, and non-finite meshes keep the box verdict. So the mesh always sits inside its box, rotated fixtures and overhangs included.
- Every deliberate silence of the box laws allows an overlap of at most `FIXTURE_HIT_TOL` (1e-9) with the box. That covers the strict z overlap in `band_hits_box` (c2, plus #464's d2 upper bands and flute column) and the strict-dip rule in `rapid_hits_box`. An overlap that small with the box can't be more than that with the mesh.
- Everything else is an enclosure, not a silence.

## What changed
New `crates/sim/tests/fixture_mesh_convict.rs` (5 tests, with a gate-map header). Each composes the box laws with `mesh_refined` the way `posting::fixture_problems` does.
- **A mesh top face keeps the strict dip:** a retract off it, a traverse riding it and a cut riding it are silent. The same moves 0.001 lower report Rapid and Flute.
- **A rotated fixture's top edge is its box's top:** a block turned 45° about X, then 30° about Z.
- **An overhanging arm convicts the stack under it:** the Shank under the arm and the Holder rim off its end both hit. Its top stays flush-silent.
- **The #424 and #425 repros convict on a closed mesh** (Holder), from the box law and the mesh alike.
- **No straight move the box laws clear penetrates the mesh:** a seeded sweep of 12,000 moves biased onto flush planes. 7,045 are silent (103 in flush contact), and none penetrates the mesh. Lowering the box top 0.01 mm makes this test fail at once, which shows it catches real gaps.

## Found along the way (filed separately)
**#491:** the box laws judge an XY arc by its **inscribed** chords at the bare band radius, so steel within the arc's sagitta (about 0.01 mm on R30) is missed. This applies to every fixture, not only meshed ones, so the fix belongs in the box law. It is out of this slice's scope.

## How tested
- `fixture_mesh_convict` 5/5, `fixture_mesh` 9 passed (1 ignored), `fixture_stack_span` 8/8.
- `clippy -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-app --tests -D warnings` is clean.
- Test-only: no product code changes.

title: feat(app): raise fixture-striking links and retracts over the steel
body:
Was stacked on #476 (#339 slice 1, fixture mesh), which merged on 2026-11-09; this PR now targets main alone. Slice 5 of #339 per the triage on the issue: link and retract routing around fixtures.

## What changed
New `crates/app/src/operation/fixture_route.rs`, with one hook in `generate.rs` before the verify pass. It runs for upright mill paths only.

**The rule:**
- **What a link is:** the longest run of straight rapids between two non-rapid moves, or a path end.
- **When it counts as struck:** the gate's own fixture laws flag it. That's #464's whole-stack law (d2) plus #476's mesh acquittal, so a routed link is judged exactly as the post gate will judge it.
- **The fix:** a struck link becomes three G0 moves: up at its start XY, across, down to its end. The height is the higher of the link's own top and the highest box top under the traverse plus 5 mm (`ROUTE_GAP`). "Under the traverse" means every box the widest band reaches along the XY segment.
- **The cap:** the machine's stated Z stroke (WCS origin Z plus the top of the stroke), keeping at least 0.5 mm over the steel. Steel taller than that **refuses generation by name**: "the link at moves i..j … cannot clear fixture 'Clamp1': its steel stands to Z …, and the machine's Z stroke tops out at Z …". With no stroke stated there is no cap, as everywhere else.
- **Re-judging:** the re-laid link is judged again. If it's still struck, the steel stands over the link's own end column and no height helps. The link is then left as laid, its `FixtureHit` still blocks the post by name, and a path note says why.
- **Notes:** every raised link gets a path note: how many rose, from where, over which fixture, to what Z.

**Left as today (report-only):**
- **Keep-down feed links.** In the CL stream they look exactly like cuts, so lifting one could silently skip a cut. They're only taken inside the cut area, so if one hits steel the cuts beside it hit too, and the post is refused anyway. A keep-down **rapid** run at depth does become retract, traverse and plunge.
- **Other paths:** posed and rotary paths, lathe tools, paths with canned cycles (a traverse inserted between holes could post as a drill), thread or probe records, and runs inside a compensated span.

**Posted G-code changes only** for documents with a link the fixture laws strike, and only those links' G0 moves. Documents without fixtures return early untouched, and links that already clear are never rewritten, so all goldens are unchanged.

`docs/decisions/339-fixture-routing.md`

## How tested
- **New app `fixture_route`** (6 tests):
  - A Contour around two blocks with a strap clamp to Z 40 between them, at clearance 25. As generated, the gate refuses ("strikes a fixture"). After the fix, the links rise to Z 45, the post is clean, the cuts are identical, and the note names Clamp1.
  - A clamp the links already clear leaves the path byte for byte.
  - A 100 mm Z stroke still routes over the 40 mm clamp, while a 400 mm clamp refuses generation naming 'Clamp1' and "Z 400.000".
  - A stay-down rapid link becomes retract, traverse and plunge. Clear steel and no steel are untouched.
  - Steel over a link's own end is left as laid and said.
  - A ceiling under the steel refuses, and a ceiling over it caps the rise.
- **Existing suites keep their verdicts:** fixtures (14), fixture_mesh (3), fixture_law_gaps (3), posting (17), tool_body (8). All app test binaries passed in the quick gate.
- `clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-app --tests -D warnings` is clean.

## Not exercised (draft)
This changes posted G-code (raised G0 links) for documents with struck fixtures, so it's a draft until a Hub or machine run. It needs a project with a clamp between features.

title: feat(sim): judge posed, rotary and XZ/YZ-arc moves against the fixture mesh
body:
**Stacked on #476** (#339 slice 1, fixture mesh). Slice 3 of #339 per the triage on the issue: posed, rotary and XZ/YZ-arc moves read against the fixture mesh. Slice 1 left those on the box verdict. As before, **the mesh only ever clears a hit the box law flagged; it never adds one.**

## What changed
**Frames.**
- **Path frame:** steel that turns with the part, and any steel when no rotary axis is stated (the box laws' frame).
- **Machine frame, A rotary:** fixed steel under an A rotary op, carried per stretch by `posed_steel::upright_turn`, the same frame `workholding` uses. A pose the rotary alone can't stand upright keeps the box verdict.
- **Machine frame, spindle C:** each move's C line is recovered from its two stated C angles. Fixed steel gets one exact sweep of the machine's straight station run. Steel turning with the part is read along the real spiral, in stretches turned by −C.
- **XZ/YZ arcs:** chorded in their own plane, with the same sagitta pad as XY arcs.
- **Left to the box:**
  - a C move whose start C isn't the previous move's;
  - a non-horizontal C pose;
  - a C turn under 1e-4 rad or near 180°;
  - a held C under fixed steel;
  - fixed steel under both a rotary axis and C;
  - an arc on a C move.

**Why a "clear" is safe.**
1. Each posed move is split into stretches by its pose turn (`midpose::turn_intervals`). Over a stretch the tip stays on its segment within the chord pad, and the pose stays within `swing` of the stretch axis, by midpose's existing rate bound.
2. A band point `p(t) + Q(t)y` stays within `swing·hypot(max(|lo|,|hi|), r)` of the unturned band. So the band lies inside segment ⊕ oriented cylinder ⊕ ball(pad), a convex set.
3. GJK sweeps the segment and cylinder exactly, and the ball goes into the margin. "Clear" is returned only with a separating-plane proof. A non-finite input or NaN margin counts as a hit.
4. A turn into another frame adds `dth·ρmax`, with ρmax taken at the stretch's four parallelogram corners plus r + pad. Distance to a line is convex, so that bounds it.
5. Consecutive stretches overlap at their shared instant, so one inside-the-solid point per band decides. Using an oriented cylinder rather than a capsule means a tilted tool isn't falsely convicted on a vise floor below its tip.

**Labels.** A mesh-kept rapid hit names a band above the flute by its part (Shank, Holder, Spindle), like #464's law (d2). This now applies on the posed and C paths too.

`docs/decisions/339-mesh-posed.md`, including a finding filed as **#486**: `cl::stamp_c` pieces keep the whole move's tool axis, so the box laws may misjudge fixed steel on C turns. The mesh can't fix that, since it only clears hits.

## How tested
- **New sim `fixture_mesh_posed`** (9 tests, plus 1 heavy-lane):
  - a tilted pass, an in-place index and a tilted rapid down a vise gap are cleared, while the same index into a jaw and a rapid swung into the other jaw still convict;
  - A-rotary fixed and turning steel, each with a clear case and a convicting case;
  - C turns with turning and fixed steel; a move with no prior C, and an axial tool, keep the box verdict;
  - XZ arcs, one clear and one dipping 0.21 mm into the base; a YZ arc in the gap is clear;
  - a posed rapid kept by the mesh names its band;
  - both turn signs (A and C) pinned by mutation.
- **New app `fixture_mesh_posed`** (2 tests): a 3+2 face indexed B 10° between closed jaws. The box law alone convicts every move, yet the post and generation are clean. With the jaws 1 mm into reach, the post is blocked and generation warns.
- **One slice-1 pin renamed** (`unpaired_boxes_keep_the_box_verdict_and_posed_moves_are_read`): a posed gap pass is now cleared.
- **Existing suites keep their verdicts:** posed_fixture, posed_fixture_midpose, posed_rapids, midmove_pose, fixture_stack_span, sim lib; app fixtures, rotary_fixtures, fixture_mesh, fixture_law_gaps. Their fixtures are box-only or open, so the mesh never judges them.
- **Performance:**
  - debug, 29.7k facets and 80 posed moves: 0.07 s;
  - release heavy lane, 203k facets and 2000 posed moves: 0.33 s.
- `clippy -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-app --tests -D warnings` is clean.

## Not exercised
No GUI or G-code change. More 4/5-axis and rotary programs now post: those whose only "hit" was a box around empty space between jaws.

Changelog: Fixture collisions on tilted, rotary and spindle-C moves and XZ/YZ arcs are judged against the fixture's real mesh too, so a tilted pass between vise jaws no longer refuses the post (#339)

title: fix(sim): sweep XY arcs on the true circle in the field engine and envelope scan
body:
## What changed
This is the follow-up to #402 / PR #414. Two more places drew XY arcs (G2/G3 in G17) as chords inside the arc: the **field engine** (`field_cut::chords`) and the **envelope scan** that runs while toolpaths are generated (`stock_sim/scan.rs`). Both now read the true circle.

**Field engine:** new `crates/sim/src/stock_sim/field_arc.rs`, 284 lines, with a provenance header.
- An upright mill tool's XY arc is now cut as `Sweep::Arc` pieces.
- Pieces follow the old chord budget, capped at a quarter turn. So the lattice windows and the `MAX_CELLS_PER_MOVE` limit refuse exactly what they refused before. Each window grows by its piece's sagitta.
- **Level piece:** solved exactly in closed form. The nearest tool pose is at the point's own bearing, clamped to the piece. It uses the column engine's tie rules (`flat_tie`, `bull_tie`), and `field_ray` gets the exact floor plane from it.
- **Helical piece:** searched with `dexel_arc::piece_min`, #414's search (samples, then a golden section). Every result is a real distance evaluation plus the usual 1e-12 margin, so the field never shows material removed that the tool did not cut. Its `residual` is a proven bound: half a sample step of tool travel.
- Tilted tools, lathe tools and XZ/YZ arcs keep their chords.

**Envelope scan:** new `crates/sim/src/stock_sim/scan_arc.rs`, 146 lines.
- Each arc piece keeps the chord `arc_chords` drew. That chord is now only used for indexing (bins, boxes, ring ids, the ridge law's pass counting), so all of that is unchanged.
- Every distance the verdict uses is now measured to the arc:
  - point distances for rest, flank and hidden rest (exact for level arcs);
  - facet distances for gouge, searched only when the chord is within the piece's bulge of the ball.
- The gouge bin walk, the ridge boxes and the `SegGrid` ring prune each grow by the bulge (`sag + |dz|`), so no contact the chords caught can be missed.

**Tests tightened:** `stock_bull_nose::both_engines_cut_a_bull_nose_alike` now holds the helix arc to the same 1e-5 engine parity as straight moves, and the `arc_parity` relaxation is removed.

The decisions and the dropped alternatives (straddling chords, finer chords, one whole-arc sweep) are in `docs/decisions/413-arc-chords-field.md`.

## Pinning tests
- **New `sim/tests/field_arc_sweep.rs`** (5 tests; 4 fail on the old code):
  - `the_field_cuts_every_tool_on_the_true_arc_like_the_column`: flat, ball, cone and bull tools on level and helical arcs, CW and CCW, including a sweep past half a turn and one with a radius smaller than the tool. The field's top matches the column engine's to 1e-5.
  - `the_bull_helix_rim_is_cut_on_the_field_too`: the #414 helix (bull r 2, corner 0.75). Rim columns are cut more than 2 mm deep, matching the column engine to 1e-5.
  - `a_clean_convex_corner_arc_reads_no_gouge_on_the_field`: a column 0.06 mm inside a riser corner. The old chords cut it 10 mm deep, top 28 → 15. Now it is untouched and reads no gouge.
  - `a_convex_corner_arc_cut_too_tight_is_still_a_gouge_on_the_field`: a planted twin that is still convicted at 10 mm.
  - `a_concave_fillet_wall_loses_exactly_the_columns_the_true_arc_reaches`: a fillet over-cut by 0.06 mm. Exactly the wall columns the true arc reaches are cut.
- **New `sim/tests/scan_arc.rs`** (2 tests; both fail on the old code):
  - `a_ball_rolled_round_an_outside_corner_reads_no_gouge`: the old code read 0.0092 mm of phantom gouge.
  - `a_wall_the_true_arc_dips_into_reads_the_dip`: the old code read 0, the true value is 0.0045 mm.
- `stock_bull_nose::both_engines_cut_a_bull_nose_alike`: back to 1e-5 parity on the arc.

## Readings
- **Debug:** all `camcraft-sim` suites pass. All `camcraft-app` and `camcraft-motion` suites pass, including the slow finish3d, pivot5d, flow and center_cut_multiaxis: 2028 passed, 0 failed.
- **Release heavy lanes** (`--ignored`, sim + motion + app): 64 passed, 0 failed.
- **No golden changed.**
- **clippy:** `-p camcraft-sim --all-targets -D warnings` is clean.

## Not exercised
- The GPU and headless UI tests: `camcraft-ui` was not touched, and its GPU headless tests are known to fail on this machine.
- A hand check of the displayed stock in the GUI.
- The rotary field (`field_rotary`), which has its own chord law and is untouched.
- **Cost:** a helical piece costs about the same as the old golden-section chord (8 samples plus a 32-round golden section, against 32 rounds). A level piece costs one evaluation. Cost was not benchmarked beyond the suite times, which did not move noticeably.

Changelog: The field-engine stock view and the generator-time envelope scan cut XY arcs on the true circle instead of inscribed chords, so a convex corner no longer shows a false cut and a concave corner or bull-nose helix no longer hides a real one (#413)

Fixes #413
Fixes #494 (the `stock_engine_agreement` heavy lane: 6465 findings on main, 0 on this head, see the comment on #494)

title: feat(ui): fixture UX - mark/import from the browser, mesh state, struck tint
body:
**Stacked on #476** (#339 slice 1, fixture mesh). Slice 4 of #339 per the triage on the issue: fixture UX.

## What changed
1. **Browser.**
   - A model row's context menu (under Models or a setup's Fixtures) offers **Use as fixture (<active setup>)** and **Stop using as fixture**. They reuse the existing `TagFixture` / `UntagFixture` commands, so undo and redo work.
   - A setup's Fixtures node offers **Import fixture…**, which reuses the existing dialog and activates that setup.
2. **Mesh state per fixture.**
   - Each Fixtures row ends in `mesh`, or `box only: <reason>`: open mesh, non-finite, collapsed, over the facet cap, no facets, or shared box. The reasons come from #476's `FixtureMesh::build`.
   - A mesh refusal is reported ahead of a shared box, since the user can fix it.
   - The Fixtures page shows the full sentence as a `Collision:` label.
   - The app helper is `fixture_view::mesh_states`, cached per document version.
3. **Highlight.** `FixtureHit` names the op, move and band, but not the fixture.
   - For the selected op, `fixture_struck::struck_by` re-runs the gate's own law against each fixture alone and keeps the ones that reproduce a warned move.
   - Those fixtures are tinted in the gouge colour, and the op banner names them ("Strikes fixture: …").
   - A warned move no fixture reproduces (e.g. a jaw moved without regenerating) says "Fixture not resolved for move N … regenerate to re-check" and tints nothing, rather than guessing.
   - Display only, cached per document version, op and path.

**Behaviour changes to note:**
- **Import as fixture is now one undo unit.** The new `ImportFixture` command applies and inverts the import, or the update of an existing name, together with the fixture marker. `crates/ui/tests/fixtures.rs::import_as_fixture_lands_as_two_undo_units` became `…_one_undo_unit`; the test count is unchanged.
- **A refused import now clears the pending fixture binding**, so it can't tag the next, unrelated import.
- **`posting::fixture_problems`'s per-op workholding check now calls `fixture_struck::op_hits`**, the same function the highlight uses, so the gate and the viewport can't disagree. Same logic, and app suites green.

`docs/decisions/339-fixture-ux.md`

## How tested
- App `fixture_ux` (8 tests):
  - closed, open and NaN mesh states, the shared box, and the version cache;
  - mark and unmark with undo;
  - `ImportFixture` fresh and as an update, with undo, redo and refusals;
  - the struck jaw is named and the clear one isn't;
  - a moved jaw is reported unresolved, not guessed;
  - no warnings resolves to nothing.
- UI `egui_app::fixture_ux_tests` (6 tests):
  - the menu rows and their commands, through the queue and undo;
  - the row suffixes;
  - the tint flag (exactly one part carries `STRUCK_CLASS`) and the banner line;
  - the unresolved banner;
  - the Fixtures page's refusal text.
- **No snapshot PNG touched.**
- App suites green. In ui, only the three headless-GPU tests fail (no adapter on this Mac), as on main. `clippy -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --tests -D warnings` is clean.

## Not exercised (draft until the contributor's GUI check)
A hands-on check. A test kit is prepared: a project with a struck jaw, a clear jaw, an open-mesh jaw, and a plain model to mark.

Changelog: Fixtures: mark or import a fixture from the browser, see whether each fixture is judged by its mesh or only its box (and why), and see which fixture a warned move strikes (#339)

Refs #339
